children.title: Simulation–Experiment Transfer
children.top_down_role: Use of simulation knowledge across optimization involving physical experiments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Suboptimality transfer under one-sided global discrepancy bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_e(x)\leq f_s(x)+\beta\) and \(f_s(x)\leq f_e(x)+\alpha\) for all \(x\in X\), and \(f_s(\widehat x)\leq\inf_Xf_s+\varepsilon\). Then \[f_e(\widehat x)\leq\inf_Xf_e+\varepsilon+\alpha+\beta.\] The symmetric condition \(|f_s-f_e|\leq\eta\) gives the specialization \(\varepsilon+2\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simulation suboptimality transfers to experiment with an additive penalty equal to the two one-sided discrepancy bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Transfer Suboptimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Validation Does Not Ensure Global Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-validation identifiability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subsetneq X\) be finite. For any discrepancy values observed on \(V\) and any \(M>0\), discrepancy functions can agree on \(V\) while differing by more than \(M\) at some \(x_0\in X\setminus V\). Finite paired validation therefore cannot alone certify uniform transfer accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agreement at finitely many validation designs does not control discrepancy at unvalidated designs.
assumptions_latex: No regularity or global discrepancy bound is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Agreement on \(V\) does not certify transfer accuracy on \(X\setminus V\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Validation Does Not Ensure Global Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive model-form discrepancy on a common design domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For simulation and experimental objectives on \(X\), define \(\delta(x):=f_e(x)-f_s(x)\). Then \(f_e(x)=f_s(x)+\delta(x)\). Uncorrected transfer assumes that \(\delta\) is decision-negligible; calibrated transfer estimates or bounds it using paired information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Experimental performance equals simulated performance plus a design-dependent discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.title: Simulation–Experiment Discrepancy Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ranking Preservation by a Transfer Margin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise transfer certificate under bounded discrepancy variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_e=f_s+\delta\). If \(|\delta(x)-\delta(y)|\leq\kappa\) and \(f_s(x)+\kappa<f_s(y)\), then \(f_e(x)<f_e(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simulated ranking transfers when its margin exceeds the possible pairwise discrepancy variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Ranking Preservation by a Transfer Margin
Simulation–Experiment Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-discrepancy guarantee for transferring a simulation solution to a physical experiment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty feasible set, and let \(f_s,f_e:X\to\mathbb{R}\) denote simulation and experimental objectives. If \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_s(x)-f_e(x)|\leq\eta\), and \(\widehat{x}\in X\) satisfies \(f_s(\widehat{x})\leq\inf_{x\in X}f_s(x)+\varepsilon\), then \[f_e(\widehat{x})\leq\inf_{x\in X}f_e(x)+\varepsilon+2\eta.\] Thus transfer quality is controlled jointly by simulation optimization error and simulation–experiment discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simulation solution that is epsilon-optimal is at most epsilon plus twice the uniform simulation–experiment discrepancy from experimental optimality.

children.title: High-Cost Replication Regimes
children.top_down_role: Evaluation settings where replication competes directly with exploration for limited resources.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Cost Replication Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replication–precision tradeoff for independent noisy black-box evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one evaluation at \(x\) returns \(Y_i(x)=f(x)+\xi_i\), where the independent errors have mean zero and variance \(\sigma^2(x)\), and each replication costs \(c(x)>0\). The average of \(r\) replications has variance \(\sigma^2(x)/r\) and root-mean-square error \(\sigma(x)/\sqrt r\). Under a budget \(B\), at most \(\lfloor B/c(x)\rfloor\) replications are possible; hence the smallest attainable root-mean-square error using simple replication is \(\sigma(x)/\sqrt{\lfloor B/c(x)\rfloor}\), provided the denominator is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent averaging reduces standard error only as the inverse square root of replication count, while high evaluation cost caps the attainable precision.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Introduction: Tools and Challenges in Derivative-Free and Blackbox Optimization p. 3

review_flags: Locator is provisional for the noisy-evaluation context; the variance calculation is elementary.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 1. Introduction: Tools and Challenges in Derivative-Free and Blackbox Optimization p. 3

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between variance reduction and persistent systematic error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_i(x)=f(x)+b(x)+\xi_i\), where \(b(x)\) is fixed and \(\mathbb{E}[\xi_i]=0\), then \(\mathbb{E}[\overline Y_r(x)]-f(x)=b(x)\) for every \(r\). Independent averaging reduces the centered variance as \(1/r\), but its mean-square error converges to \(b(x)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication reduces independent zero-mean noise but cannot remove fixed systematic bias.
assumptions_latex: The \(\xi_i\) are independent with zero mean and finite variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Systematic-Bias Floor Under Replication

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous optimal allocation across fixed designs with nonzero contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{i:|w_i|\sigma_i>0\}\). For independent sample means with \(\operatorname{Var}(\overline Y_i)=\sigma_i^2/r_i\), minimize \(\sum_{i\in I}w_i^2\sigma_i^2/r_i\) over \(r_i>0\) subject to \(\sum_{i\in I}c_ir_i\leq B\). If \(I\neq\varnothing\), then \[r_i^*=B\frac{|w_i|\sigma_i/\sqrt{c_i}}{\sum_{j\in I}|w_j|\sigma_j\sqrt{c_j}},\qquad i\in I,\] and the minimum variance is \(B^{-1}(\sum_{i\in I}|w_i|\sigma_i\sqrt{c_i})^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous replication increases with statistical importance and noise and decreases with the square root of run cost.
assumptions_latex: The observations are independent across designs and replications.

notation.meaning: continuous replication allocation at design i
cost per replication at design i

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Aware Optimal Replication Allocation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget-feasible black-box optimization policy with incumbent output.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonempty feasible set \(X\), an evaluation oracle \(O\), and an integer budget \(N\geq1\), a fixed-budget derivative-free policy selects \(x_1\in X\) and then, for \(k=2,\ldots,N\), selects \(x_k\) as a function of the history \(H_{k-1}=\{(x_i,O(x_i)):i<k\}\) and internal randomness. After exactly \(N\) oracle calls, it returns an incumbent \(\widehat{x}_N\in\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\), commonly one having the smallest observed value. Performance is assessed at budget \(N\), rather than by evaluations needed to reach a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method adaptively spends exactly N black-box evaluations and returns an incumbent among its sampled points; quality is measured after that fixed budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Evaluation-Budget Optimization

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simple Regret at a Fixed Budget
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal solution-quality criterion for a fixed evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization of \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) with \(f_*:=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)>-\infty\), the simple regret of the recommendation \(\widehat{x}_N\) after exactly \(N\) evaluations is \(r_N:=f(\widehat{x}_N)-f_*\). For a randomized policy, the reported risk functional—such as \(\mathbb{E}[r_N]\), a quantile, or \(\mathbb{P}(r_N>\varepsilon)\)—must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple regret is the true objective gap of the recommendation returned after the fixed evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Simple Regret at a Fixed Budget

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-query boundary for unrestricted objectives when the output must be sampled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(|X|=M>N\), let the admissible objectives include \(f_z(z)=0\) and \(f_z(x)=1\) for \(x\neq z\), and require the recommendation to be one of the queried points. Every deterministic policy using at most \(N\) queries has worst-case simple regret \(1\). Every randomized policy has some \(f_z\) for which \(\mathbb{E}[r_N]\geq1-N/M\). Thus a finite budget alone gives no nontrivial uniform global-accuracy guarantee over unrestricted objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsampled point can hide the unique optimum; randomization cannot remove this obstruction without regularity assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The objective class contains every one-hidden-minimizer function \(f_z:X\to\{0,1\}\).
At most \(N\) points are queried and the recommendation is queried.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_f r_N=1\) for deterministic policies, and \(\sup_f\mathbb{E}[r_N]\geq1-N/M\) for randomized policies.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Budget Indistinguishability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anytime behavior of best-observed recommendations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nested run \(x_1,x_2,\ldots\) that retains the best observation, \(f_N^{\mathrm{inc}}:=\min_{1\leq i\leq N}f(x_i)\) satisfies \(f_N^{\mathrm{inc}}\leq f_{N-1}^{\mathrm{inc}}\) for \(N\geq2\). This does not imply convergence to \(\inf_Xf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining the best sampled point makes incumbent values monotone with budget, but does not ensure global convergence.
assumptions_latex: The recommendation is a best observed point.

notation.meaning: best value observed through evaluation N

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Budget Incumbent Monotonicity

children.title: Parallel Evaluation Batches
children.top_down_role: Concurrent objective evaluations issued in synchronized groups.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(B_{t+1}\) depends only on results completed through the batch barrier at round \(t\).

notation.meaning: ordered batch dispatched at round t

review_flags: The source is provisional and not specific to black-box batching.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous batched black-box evaluation with a batch barrier.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a nonempty feasible set and let \(q\geq1\) workers be available. At round \(t\), a synchronous batched policy uses the completed history \(H_t\) to choose an ordered batch \(B_t=(x_{t,1},\ldots,x_{t,m_t})\in X^{m_t}\), where \(1\leq m_t\leq q\). It dispatches all oracle calls \(O(x_{t,j})\) concurrently and does not construct \(B_{t+1}\) until every result in \(B_t\) has returned. The history is then updated with the complete batch. After a prescribed number of calls or rounds, the policy returns an incumbent among the evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous batch policy launches up to q evaluations concurrently and waits for the entire batch before selecting the next points.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Evaluation Batches

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

assumptions_latex: Every completed evaluation belongs to exactly one of the \(R\) batches.
Each batch contains at most \(q\) evaluations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp oracle-call and synchronization-round accounting for synchronous batches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a synchronous policy completes \(N\) evaluations in \(R\) batches and each batch contains at most \(q\) evaluations, then \(N\leq qR\) and therefore \(R\geq\lceil N/q\rceil\). Equality is attainable by filling every batch except possibly the last. Batching can consequently reduce synchronization depth by at most a factor of \(q\), while the oracle-call count remains \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completing N calls in batches of size at most q requires at least ceiling(N/q) synchronized rounds, and full batches attain the bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Round Lower Bound

children.title: Asynchronous Evaluation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Concurrent evaluations processed as individual results become available.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Evaluation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven black-box evaluation without global batch barriers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\geq1\) workers evaluate a black-box oracle. Initialize by dispatching at most \(q\) feasible points. Whenever any worker completes an evaluation at event time \(t\), append its result to the completed history \(H_t\), select a new feasible point using only \(H_t\) and internal randomness, and immediately dispatch it to an available worker. Outstanding evaluations need not finish before this update. Stop when the evaluation budget or wall-clock deadline is reached, cancel or record outstanding work according to a fixed convention, and return an incumbent from the completed evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asynchronous policy launches a new evaluation whenever a worker becomes free, using completed results without waiting for all outstanding calls.
assumptions_latex: Point selection uses only completed information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No global synchronization barrier is required between successive dispatches.

notation.meaning: results completed by event time t

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting for completed, outstanding, and cancelled asynchronous work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At time \(t\), \[N_{\mathrm{launch}}(t)=N_{\mathrm{done}}(t)+N_{\mathrm{out}}(t)+N_{\mathrm{cancel}}(t).\] A launch budget stops before dispatch would exceed its limit; a completion budget may temporarily have more launched than completed calls; and a charged-cost budget must declare how cancelled or partially executed calls are charged. These conventions are not interchangeable at a deadline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous accounting must distinguish launched, completed, outstanding, cancelled, and charged work.
assumptions_latex: Every launch is completed, remains outstanding, or is cancelled.
The stopping and charging conventions are fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Budget Accounting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Informative-censoring boundary for deadline-truncated histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If response \(Y\) and duration \(T\) are dependent, conditioning on completion before deadline \(\tau\) can change the response law: \(P(Y\in A\mid T\leq\tau)\neq P(Y\in A)\). Treating completed results as an unselected sample may therefore bias estimation or selection unless duration is noninformative or censoring is modeled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When duration depends on outcome, deadline-completed evaluations can be a biased subset of launched work.
assumptions_latex: Evaluation duration may depend on the response or feasibility outcome.
Only calls completed by deadline \(\tau\) are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The completed observations need not follow the launched-observation distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Informative Completion Bias

children.title: Latency-Dominated Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Evaluation management when turnaround time dominates computational overhead.

assumptions_latex: Evaluations are nonpreemptive on \(q\) identical workers.
Local computation time is negligible relative to evaluation time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For known durations, the relevant wall-clock objective is \(\min_a C_{\max}(a)\); for random durations and an admissible scheduling policy \(\pi\), it is \(\min_\pi\mathbb{E}[C_{\max}(\pi)]\).

notation.meaning: admissible scheduling policy for random or initially unknown durations

review_flags: The supplied source is general parallel-computing context rather than a specific black-box scheduling result.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Makespan criterion when evaluation latency dominates local optimization overhead.

source_refs.locator: 4 Parallel computing p. 99
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(m\geq1\) black-box evaluations have processing times \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\geq0\) and must be assigned nonpreemptively to \(q\geq1\) identical workers. For an assignment \(a:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to\{1,\ldots,q\}\), define the makespan by \[C_{\max}(a)=\max_{1\leq j\leq q}\sum_{i:a(i)=j}T_i.\] When model fitting and point-selection costs are negligible, minimizing wall-clock completion time for known durations means minimizing \(C_{\max}(a)\). For random or initially unknown durations, an admissible scheduling policy \(\pi\) may instead minimize \(\mathbb{E}[C_{\max}(\pi)]\), subject to the optimizer's information constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When evaluation time dominates overhead, scheduling minimizes the maximum worker load for known durations, or expected makespan under an admissible policy for random or unknown durations.
knowledge_statements.title: Latency-Dominated Scheduling

source_witnesses.locator: 4 Parallel computing p. 99
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duration-ordered list scheduling and its sharper guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If known durations are sorted in nonincreasing order and then list scheduled on \(q\geq2\) identical workers, the resulting LPT schedule satisfies \[C_{\mathrm{LPT}}\leq\left(\frac43-\frac{1}{3q}\right)C_{\max}^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sorting evaluations from longest to shortest before greedy assignment improves the worst-case makespan guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Durations are known and jobs are nonpreemptive.
All jobs are available before assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Longest-Processing-Time Scheduling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arbitrary-order greedy scheduling on identical workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: List scheduling assigns each next evaluation in a fixed order to a currently least-loaded worker. Its makespan satisfies \[C_{\mathrm{LS}}\leq\left(2-\frac1q\right)C_{\max}^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-loaded-worker list scheduling has approximation ratio two minus one over the worker count.
assumptions_latex: All jobs are available for nonpreemptive assignment.
A fixed processing order is used.
knowledge_statements.title: List Scheduling Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal lower bounds for identical-worker schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonpreemptive durations \(T_1,\ldots,T_m\) assigned to \(q\) identical workers, \[C_{\max}\geq\max\left\{\frac1q\sum_{i=1}^mT_i,\max_iT_i\right\}.\] A schedule attaining this lower bound is makespan optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completion time is at least average work per worker and at least the longest evaluation.
knowledge_statements.title: Makespan Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary for exact identical-worker assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With integer processing times, exact makespan minimization on two identical workers is weakly NP-hard by the Partition problem. When the number of workers is part of the input, the problem is strongly NP-hard. Thus exact assignment is not generally expected to have a polynomial-time algorithm, while approximation guarantees remain available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact identical-worker makespan scheduling is NP-hard, motivating approximation algorithms such as list scheduling and LPT.
assumptions_latex: Processing times are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact \(P||C_{\max}\) scheduling is weakly NP-hard for \(q=2\) and strongly NP-hard when \(q\) is input.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Makespan Scheduling Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tight family for the list-scheduling approximation ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\geq2\), place \(q(q-1)\) unit-duration jobs before one duration-\(q\) job. List scheduling gives every worker load \(q-1\) before assigning the final job, so its makespan is \(2q-1\). An optimal assignment has makespan \(q\), giving ratio \(2-1/q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A long job arriving after balanced unit jobs makes the list-scheduling bound exactly tight.
assumptions_latex: The stated fixed job order is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharpness of Arbitrary-Order List Scheduling

children.title: Straggler-Prone Evaluation Pools
children.top_down_role: Parallel settings with highly variable or exceptionally delayed evaluation completion.

assumptions_latex: For \(A_q\), all individual means are finite and \(\max_i\mathbb E[T_i]>0\).

notation.meaning: distribution function of completion time i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact order-statistic representation and dimensionless measure of straggler amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M_q=\max_{1\leq i\leq q}T_i\), independence gives \[\Pr(M_q>t)=1-\prod_{i=1}^qF_i(t),\qquad \mathbb E[M_q]=\int_0^\infty\left(1-\prod_{i=1}^qF_i(t)\right)dt,\] where the integral may be infinite. When the individual means are finite and not all zero, \[A_q=\frac{\mathbb E[M_q]}{\max_i\mathbb E[T_i]}\geq1\] measures mean barrier amplification. Large or growing \(A_q\), or an infinite barrier expectation, is a precise indication that the synchronous pool is straggler-sensitive; the numerical threshold for calling amplification operationally material is application-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous pool finishes at its maximum completion time; its tail integral gives expected barrier latency, and the ratio to the largest individual mean measures straggler amplification.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Time Distribution and Amplification
Straggler-Prone Evaluation Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous batch slowdown caused by the slowest evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a synchronous batch of \(q\) evaluations with completion times \(T_1,\ldots,T_q\), the barrier time is \(M_q=\max_iT_i\). Consequently \(\mathbb{E}[M_q]\geq\max_i\mathbb{E}[T_i]\), so one slow call delays the entire batch. In the concrete case of independent exponential times with common rate \(\lambda>0\), \[\mathbb{E}[M_q]=\frac{1}{\lambda}\sum_{k=1}^{q}\frac{1}{k}.\] Hence synchronous completion time grows like \((\log q)/\lambda\), even though each individual evaluation has mean \(1/\lambda\); this is the straggler amplification boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous batch finishes at its slowest call; for exponential durations, expected barrier time grows as the harmonic number times the individual mean.
assumptions_latex: For the displayed formula, the times are independent and exponentially distributed with rate \(\lambda>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Driven Sampling Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolation-set growth for full linear and quadratic derivative-free models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(n\) variables, a full affine interpolation model has \(n+1\) coefficients and therefore requires at least \(n+1\) suitably poised sample values for unique determination. A full quadratic model has \((n+1)(n+2)/2\) coefficients and requires at least that many suitably poised values. Thus the sampling and storage burden is \(\Theta(n)\) for full linear interpolation and \(\Theta(n^2)\) for full quadratic interpolation. When evaluations are expensive, this dimension growth can exhaust the available budget before a reliable local model is constructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full linear models require n+1 poised samples, while full quadratic models require order n-squared samples, creating a dimension-driven DFO burden.
assumptions_latex: The model contains all affine or all quadratic monomials in \(n\) variables.
The interpolation set is poised for the selected polynomial space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The required sample counts are \(n+1\) and \((n+1)(n+2)/2\), respectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy Floors from Evaluation Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability floor under adversarially bounded deterministic evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an oracle \(O_f(x)=f(x)+e(x)\) with unknown error satisfying \(|e(x)|\leq\delta\). The objectives \(f_0(x)=0\) and \(f_1(x)=2\delta\) on any nonempty domain generate the identical transcript \(O(x)=\delta\) by choosing errors \(e_0(x)=\delta\) and \(e_1(x)=-\delta\). Their optimal values differ by \(2\delta\). Therefore no procedure using only this oracle can guarantee worst-case error strictly below \(\delta\) when estimating the optimal value over this class; claims below the noise scale require additional error structure or repeated-information assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With unknown bounded error delta, indistinguishable objectives can have optimal values two delta apart, preventing guaranteed value accuracy below delta.
assumptions_latex: Oracle errors may be arbitrary subject only to \(|e(x)|\leq\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every optimal-value estimator has worst-case absolute error at least \(\delta\) on this class.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite noiseless observations cannot identify the optimum of an unrestricted continuous objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) contain a nonempty open ball, and run any deterministic method for finitely many noiseless value queries against \(f_0\equiv0\), producing the finite query set \(Q\). There is an open ball \(U\subset X\) disjoint from \(Q\) and a continuous function \(b:X\to[0,1]\) supported in \(U\) with \(\max_X b=1\). For \(f_1=-b\), every response at the adaptively generated queries is again zero, so determinism yields the same transcript as for \(f_0\), although \(\inf_Xf_0=0\) and \(\inf_Xf_1=-1\). Thus no finite deterministic value transcript identifies the optimal value or certifies the absence of an unseen improving region over this class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After any finite deterministic noiseless transcript, an unseen continuous negative bump can leave all observations unchanged while lowering the optimum by one.

The algorithm is deterministic and makes finitely many noiseless value queries.
The objective class contains arbitrary continuous functions on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite deterministic value-query transcript identifies \(\inf_X f\) over the stated class.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite noiseless observations cannot identify an unrestricted continuous objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) contain a nonempty open ball, and let a deterministic method query only the finite set \(Q=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\). children.title: Derivative-Available Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where reliable derivative information changes the case for derivative-free optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Available Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle condition defining full first-derivative availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and let \(f\) be differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(X\). A full derivative-available regime holds when every admissible query \(x\in X\) can return both \(f(x)\) and the complete gradient \(\nabla f(x)\in\mathbb{R}^n\), with declared accuracy and finite resource cost compatible with the optimization budget. If exact gradients are claimed, the returned vector must equal \(\nabla f(x)\); if inexact gradients are claimed, an explicit error model must accompany the oracle. Such a regime is not intrinsically derivative-free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full derivative access means each feasible query can provide the entire gradient, exactly or under an explicit error model and usable cost.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle exposes \((f(x),\nabla f(x))\) for every admissible \(x\in X\).

children.title: Partial-Derivative Access
children.top_down_role: Problems exposing derivatives for only selected variables, components, or evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Derivative Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-subset form of partial first-derivative access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(f\) possess the relevant partial derivatives. A partial-derivative oracle queried at \(x\in X\) returns \(f(x)\) together with \((\partial_i f(x))_{i\in S(x)}\), where \(S(x)\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a declared coordinate subset that may depend on the query or oracle interface. Derivatives outside \(S(x)\) are unavailable at that query. The access pattern is fixed when \(S(x)=S\) for all \(x\), and adaptive when the method may select \(S(x)\) subject to a stated derivative-query cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial access returns function values and derivatives only for a proper subset of coordinates, with fixed or adaptively chosen access patterns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At query \(x\), derivative information is available exactly on \(S(x)\), not on every coordinate.

notation.meaning: coordinates whose partial derivatives are accessible at x
partial derivative with respect to coordinate i

children.title: Hybrid Derivative-Free Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Optimization frameworks combining derivative-free components with derivative-informed components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structurally mixed interface combining derivative-informed and value-only objective components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=g(x)+h(x)\) on a query domain \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A hybrid derivative-free interface exposes \(g(x)\), a declared exact or inexact derivative of \(g\), and the value \(h(x)\), while assuming no derivative oracle for \(h\). A hybrid method may therefore combine a derivative-based local representation of \(g\) with interpolation, regression, direct search, or directional evaluations for \(h\). The interface must declare the component decomposition and the accuracy convention for every returned derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid interface exposes derivatives for declared objective components while other components remain value-only, allowing derivative-informed and derivative-free models to be combined.
assumptions_latex: The decomposition \(F=g+h\) and the information returned for each component are declared.
Any inexact derivative of \(g\) has an explicit error convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization interface is derivative-informed on \(g\) and derivative-free on \(h\).
review_flags: Replaces the deferred component-coordinate oracle formulation to avoid duplicating the Partial-Derivative Access sibling.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Derivative-Free Interface
Hybrid Derivative-Free Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines mixed-access black-box interfaces in which derivative availability varies across components, variables, or evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m):X\to\mathbb{R}^m\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A hybrid derivative-free interface is an oracle \(\mathcal O\) that, for every query \(x\in X\), returns function information \(F(x)\) and may additionally return derivative information indexed by a declared availability set \(A(x)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For \((i,j)\in A(x)\), the oracle supplies \(\partial_jF_i(x)\) or a stated approximation; no derivative value is assumed for indices outside \(A(x)\). An algorithm using \(\mathcal O\) is hybrid derivative-free when its model or search step combines the supplied derivatives with interpolation, regression, or directional evaluations for the unavailable derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid interface supplies function values everywhere but derivatives only for declared components or variables, so an algorithm models the missing derivative information from evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Every returned approximate derivative is accompanied by its declared accuracy convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O\) partitions derivative information into available indices \(A(x)\) and derivative-free indices \(A(x)^{\mathrm c}\) at each query.

notation.meaning: Indices of derivative entries available at the query point.

children.title: DFO Switching Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions governing transitions between derivative-free, hybrid, or derivative-based approaches.

knowledge_statements.title: DFO Switching Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes when a derivative-free mode ceases to dominate an available derivative-based mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an accuracy target \(\varepsilon>0\) and an information state \(s\). For each admissible mode \(a\in\{\mathrm{DFO},\mathrm{DER}\}\), let \(N_a(s,\varepsilon)\) be its predicted number of oracle calls, \(c_a(s)\) its expected cost per call, and \(q_a(s,\varepsilon)\in(0,1]\) its predicted probability of attaining the target. Define the risk-adjusted work \(W_a(s,\varepsilon)=c_a(s)N_a(s,\varepsilon)/q_a(s,\varepsilon)\). The DFO switching boundary is the indifference set \(\{s:W_{\mathrm{DFO}}(s,\varepsilon)=W_{\mathrm{DER}}(s,\varepsilon)\}\). DFO is preferred where its work is smaller and crosses its suitability boundary where the inequality reverses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DFO switching boundary is where derivative-free and derivative-based modes have equal predicted risk-adjusted work for the requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Both modes use the same success criterion at accuracy \(\varepsilon\).
The cost, call-count, and success-probability predictions are finite and positive.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone, strict positive-dependence, and directional characterizations of a finite nonzero linear spanning family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{span}\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}=\mathbb{R}^n\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(\operatorname{pspan}(v_1,\ldots,v_r)=\mathbb{R}^n\); (ii) for every \(i\), \(-v_i\in\operatorname{pspan}\{v_j:j\neq i\}\); (iii) there exist \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r>0\) such that \(\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i v_i=0\); and (iv) for every \(w\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), there exists \(i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\) such that \(w^\top v_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonzero vectors that linearly span R^n, positive spanning is equivalent to every negative generator being positively generated by the others, to a strictly positive dependence summing to zero, and to every nonzero direction having positive inner product with some generator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Dependence, Positive Independence, and Positive Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence and inclusion-minimal positive-spanning structure for finite vector families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite vector family \(V=\{v_1,\ldots,v_r\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is positively dependent if some \(v_i\) belongs to \(\operatorname{pspan}(V\setminus\{v_i\})\), and positively independent otherwise. It is a positive basis for \(\mathbb{R}^n\) if it is positively independent and \(\operatorname{pspan}(V)=\mathbb{R}^n\). Equivalently, a positive basis is a set of nonzero vectors that positively spans \(\mathbb{R}^n\) and has no proper subset with that property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite vector family is positively dependent if one vector is a nonnegative combination of the others, and positively independent otherwise. A positive basis is a positively independent positive spanning set, equivalently an inclusion-minimal set of nonzero vectors positively spanning R^n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V\text{ is a positive basis}\iff\left(\operatorname{pspan}(V)=\mathbb{R}^n\ \land\ \forall V'\subsetneq V,\ \operatorname{pspan}(V')\neq\mathbb{R}^n\right)

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Positive-Basis Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes positive bases having the smallest possible cardinality in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive basis \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is minimal-cardinality exactly when \(|D|=n+1\). Equivalently, after relabeling, there exist a linear basis \(B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\) of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) and coefficients \(\alpha_i>0\) such that \[D=\{b_1,\ldots,b_n,-\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i b_i\}.\] This set positively spans \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and deleting any member destroys positive spanning. Conversely, every positive basis with \(n+1\) members admits such a representation after positive rescaling of its vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every smallest positive basis has n basis vectors and one negative positive combination of them; it contains exactly n+1 directions.
assumptions_latex: Positive spanning uses nonnegative finite linear combinations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|D|=n+1\) and \(D\) has the displayed basis-plus-one representation.

notation.meaning: Finite positive basis in Euclidean space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A normalized regular-simplex construction of a minimal positive basis, conditional on the source-defined matrix A in equation (2.2).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $V=C^\top=[v_1\ \cdots\ v_n]\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, where $A=CC^\top$ and $A$ is the matrix specified in equation (2.2). Define $v_{n+1}=-\sum_{i=1}^n v_i$. Then $[v_1\ \cdots\ v_{n+1}]$ is a minimal positive basis for $\mathbb{R}^n$. Moreover, $v_i^\top v_j=-1/n$ whenever $i\ne j$, and $\lVert v_i\rVert=1$ for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,n+1\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the factorization of the matrix specified in equation (2.2), the columns of the transposed factor, augmented by their negative sum, form a minimal positive basis of n+1 unit vectors. Every pair of distinct vectors has inner product −1/n.
assumptions_latex: A\text{ is the matrix specified in equation (2.2)}

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Positive-Basis Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes positive bases attaining the largest possible cardinality in dimension n.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive basis \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is maximal-cardinality exactly when \(|D|=2n\). Equivalently, there are a linear basis \(B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}\) and positive scalars \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n\) such that, after relabeling, \[D=\{b_1,\ldots,b_n,-\alpha_1b_1,\ldots,-\alpha_nb_n\}.\] Thus a maximal positive basis consists of oppositely oriented pairs along \(n\) linearly independent directions. It positively spans \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and no positive basis in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) contains more than \(2n\) vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A largest positive basis contains 2n vectors arranged as oppositely oriented, positively scaled pairs along a linear basis.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is inclusion-minimal among finite positive spanning sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|D|=2n\) and \(D\) has the displayed paired-basis representation.

notation.meaning: Linear basis determining the paired directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate-Cardinality Positive Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies positive bases whose cardinalities lie strictly between the minimal and maximal classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a finite positive basis, meaning that \(\operatorname{pos}(D)=\mathbb{R}^n\) and no proper subset of \(D\) positively spans \(\mathbb{R}^n\). It is an intermediate-cardinality positive basis when \[n+2\leq |D|\leq 2n-1.\] Consequently this class is nonempty only for \(n\geq3\). Its members interpolate in cardinality between minimal positive bases of size \(n+1\) and maximal positive bases of size \(2n\), while retaining inclusion-minimal positive spanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intermediate positive basis is an inclusion-minimal positive spanning set with between n+2 and 2n−1 directions.
assumptions_latex: Positive hulls are formed using nonnegative coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is intermediate-cardinality if and only if \(n+2\leq|D|\leq2n-1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive existence of intermediate positive bases at each admissible cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge3\) and \(m\in\{n+2,\ldots,2n-1\}\), and put \(k=m-n\). Choose a direct-sum decomposition \(\mathbb R^n=V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_k\) into nonzero subspaces and a minimal positive basis \(D_j\) of each \(V_j\). Then \[D=\bigcup_{j=1}^kD_j\] is a positive basis of \(\mathbb R^n\) with \(|D|=\sum_j(\dim V_j+1)=n+k=m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every cardinality strictly between n+1 and 2n occurs: take minimal positive bases on complementary nonzero subspaces and unite them.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb R^n\) is decomposed as a direct sum of \(m-n\) nonzero subspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists D\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ a positive basis with }|D|=m.

notation.meaning: Minimal positive basis of subspace V_j.

knowledge_statements.title: Existence Across Every Intermediate Cardinality
Generating-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents positive directional coverage through the positive hull and cosine measure of a finite set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite nonzero set \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), its generated cone and cosine measure are \[\operatorname{pos}(D)=\left\{\textstyle\sum_{d\in D}\alpha_d d:\alpha_d\geq0\right\},\qquad \operatorname{cm}(D)=\min_{\|v\|=1}\max_{d\in D}\frac{v^{\mathsf T}d}{\|d\|}.\] The set \(D\) positively spans \(\mathbb{R}^n\) if and only if \(\operatorname{pos}(D)=\mathbb{R}^n\), equivalently if and only if \(\operatorname{cm}(D)>0\). In that case every nonzero vector \(v\) has a generator \(d\in D\) satisfying \(v^{\mathsf T}d\geq\operatorname{cm}(D)\|v\|\|d\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite direction set covers every direction precisely when its positive hull is the whole space, equivalently when its cosine measure is positive.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, nonempty, and contains no zero vector.
The norm and inner product are Euclidean.

notation.meaning: Cone of nonnegative combinations of generators.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Rank Does Not Imply Positive Spanning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating linear spanning from positive spanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D=\{e_1,\ldots,e_n\}\), the generator matrix has rank \(n\), but \[\operatorname{pos}(D)=\mathbb R_+^n\ne\mathbb R^n.\] Thus full linear rank without positive dependence is insufficient for positive spanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinate basis has full rank but generates only the nonnegative orthant, so linear spanning alone is not a positive-spanning certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Rank Does Not Imply Positive Spanning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar Separation Test for Positive Spanning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-cone characterization intrinsic to finite generating-set geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), \[\operatorname{pos}(D)^\circ=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:v^{\mathsf T}d\le0\ \forall d\in D\}.\] Hence \[\operatorname{pos}(D)=\mathbb R^n\iff\operatorname{pos}(D)^\circ=\{0\},\] equivalently there is no nonzero vector having nonpositive inner product with every generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set positively spans precisely when no nonzero separating direction is nonpositive on every generator.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar Separation Test for Positive Spanning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariance under independent positive rescaling of finite generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha_i>0\), then \[\operatorname{pos}\{\alpha_1d_1,\ldots,\alpha_md_m\}=\operatorname{pos}(D).\] Under the normalized cosine-measure convention, the cosine measure is also unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The positive hull and normalized cosine measure depend on generator rays, not on the positive lengths of their representatives.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and contains no zero vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Scaling Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex and algebraic equivalents of positive spanning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) be finite and nonzero, and let \(A=[d_1\ \cdots\ d_m]\). Then \[\operatorname{pos}(D)=\mathbb R^n\iff0\in\operatorname{int}\operatorname{conv}(D)\iff\bigl(\operatorname{rank}(A)=n\ \text{and}\ \exists\lambda\in\mathbb R^m_{++}:A\lambda=0\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite set positively spans exactly when the origin is interior to its convex hull, equivalently when its direction matrix has full row rank and a strictly positive null vector.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) is finite and contains no zero vector.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose columns are the generators.
Vectors with all components strictly positive.

children.title: Tangent Direction Sets
children.top_down_role: Local tangent-direction geometry relevant to constrained derivative-free search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp example showing that Bouligand tangent cones need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u,v\in\mathbb R^n\) be noncollinear and \(\Omega=\{tu:t\ge0\}\cup\{tv:t\ge0\}\). Then \[T_\Omega(0)=\{tu:t\ge0\}\cup\{tv:t\ge0\},\] which is not convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The union of two noncollinear rays has, at their common endpoint, a tangent cone equal to that nonconvex union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_\Omega(0)\text{ is a closed, nonconvex cone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Tangent-Cone Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent metric characterization of the Bouligand tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(x\in\Omega\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), \[d\in T_\Omega(x)\iff \liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x+td,\Omega)}{t}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction is tangent exactly when its small positive-ray displacements can approach feasibility with error that is little-o of the step along a sequence.

notation.meaning: Euclidean distance from z to Omega.

knowledge_statements.title: Distance Characterization of Tangent Directions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent Cone of a Convex Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic convex-set specialization; active-constraint formulas remain in the constraint-boundary sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is convex and \(x\in\Omega\), then \[T_\Omega(x)=\overline{\operatorname{cone}(\Omega-x)}.\] If \(\Omega\) is polyhedral, \(\operatorname{cone}(\Omega-x)\) is closed, so the closure is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex set, tangent directions are limits of nonnegative multiples of chords from the reference point; for a polyhedron the chord cone is already closed.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative hull of chords from x to points of Omega.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Cone of a Convex Set
Tangent Direction Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the Bouligand tangent cone appropriate for local feasible sampling near constrained points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x\in\Omega\). The Bouligand tangent direction set to \(\Omega\) at \(x\) is \[T_\Omega(x)=\left\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists\,x_k\in\Omega,\ t_k>0\text{ with }x_k\to x,\ t_k\downarrow0,\ \frac{x_k-x}{t_k}\to d\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(d\in T_\Omega(x)\) when arbitrarily small feasible displacements from \(x\), after positive rescaling, approach \(d\). The set is a closed cone, but it need not be convex for a nonconvex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent direction is a limit of positively rescaled feasible displacements approaching the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_\Omega(x)\) is the closed cone defined by feasible displacement limits.

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to the feasible set at x.
Positive displacement scales tending to zero.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bouligand tangent-cone definition and stated closed-cone property fit the leaf, but no inspectable authoritative locator is supplied.

children.title: Feasible-Direction Sets
children.top_down_role: Directions compatible with local feasibility requirements.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex example separating radial feasible directions from tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:b\ge a^2\}\) and \(x=(0,0)\). Then \(\Omega\) is closed and convex and \[T_\Omega(x)=\{(p,q):q\ge0\}.\] The direction \(d=(1,0)\) is tangent, as feasible displacements \((t,t^2)\) approach that direction, but \(x+sd=(s,0)\notin\Omega\) for every \(s>0\). Hence \(d\notin F_\Omega(x)\) and \(F_\Omega(x)\subsetneq T_\Omega(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a parabolic boundary, a horizontal direction is tangent through curved feasible paths although no positive straight segment in that direction is feasible.

notation.meaning: Horizontal tangent direction at the parabolic boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Curved-Boundary Strict Inclusion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radial Cone Representation for Convex Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent displacement-cone representation and closure relation under convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and \(x\in\Omega\). For the radial feasible-direction convention, \[F_\Omega(x)=\operatorname{cone}(\Omega-x):=\{\alpha(y-x):\alpha\ge0,\ y\in\Omega\}.\] Its closure is the Bouligand tangent cone: \[T_\Omega(x)=\overline{F_\Omega(x)}.\] Thus convexity makes radial feasible directions dense in the tangent cone but does not ensure equality unless the radial cone is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex feasible set, radial directions form the cone of feasible displacements, and the tangent cone is its closure.

notation.meaning: Set of feasible displacements from x.
Union of nonnegative rays generated by feasible displacements.

knowledge_statements.title: Radial Cone Representation for Convex Feasible Sets
Feasible-Direction Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directions whose entire sufficiently short ray remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x\in\Omega\). The radial feasible-direction set at \(x\) is \[F_\Omega(x)=\left\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists\,\bar t>0\text{ such that }x+td\in\Omega\text{ for every }t\in[0,\bar t]\right\}.\] Every radial feasible direction is tangent, so \(F_\Omega(x)\subseteq T_\Omega(x)\). The inclusion can be strict because a tangent direction may be realized only by curved feasible sequences rather than by a straight feasible segment from \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction generates a straight feasible segment of positive length from the current point; every such direction is tangent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The radial feasible-direction convention is coherent and distinct from the tangent cone, but terminology varies across sources. An authoritative locator is needed to support this exact straight-segment convention and inclusion claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Qualification Failure at a Degenerate Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of active-gradient boundary formulas without a constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\le0\}=\{0\}\) and \(x=0\). The active gradient is \(g'(0)=0\), so the linearized cone is \(\mathbb R\) and the cone generated by the active gradient is \(\{0\}\). However, \(T_\Omega(0)=\{0\}\) and, under the polar convention, \(N_\Omega(0)=\mathbb R\). Thus both the tangent linearization equality and active-gradient normal representation can fail without MFCQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the degenerate constraint x squared at most zero, the active gradient contains no boundary information, showing why a constraint qualification is essential.

abla h_j(x)^{\mathsf T}d=0\  orall j,\ 
abla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d\le0\  orall i\in I(x)\}.\] For the convention \(N_\Omega(x)=T_\Omega(x)^\circ\), \[N_\Omega(x)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j
abla h_j(x)+\sum_{i\in I(x)}\lambda_i
abla g_i(x):\mu_j\in\mathbb R,\ \lambda_i\ge0ight\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, active equalities impose tangent hyperplanes and unrestricted normal multipliers, while active inequalities impose tangent halfspaces and nonnegative normal multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \exists w:\nabla h_j(x)^{\mathsf T}w=0\ \forall j,\ \nabla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}w<0\ \forall i\in I(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_\Omega(x)\text{ equals the mixed linearization cone, and }N_\Omega(x)=T_\Omega(x)^\circ\text{ has the displayed multiplier representation.}
review_flags: Uses the explicitly stated polar-normal convention.

Constraint-Boundary Direction Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes first-order tangent and normal geometry at a smooth inequality-constrained boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where every \(g_i\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(I(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\). If the Mangasarian--Fromovitz condition holds, namely some \(w\) satisfies \(
abla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}w<0\) for all \(i\in I(x)\), then \[T_\Omega(x)=\{d:
abla g_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d\leq0\  orall i\in I(x)\},\qquad N_\Omega(x)=\operatorname{cone}\{
abla g_i(x):i\in I(x)\}.\] Thus boundary-compatible sampling directions lie in the linearized tangent cone, while active gradients generate its polar normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a standard constraint qualification, active gradients determine the boundary’s tangent halfspaces and generate its normal cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangent cone equals the active linearization cone, and its polar normal cone is generated by active gradients.

notation.meaning: Set of active inequality constraints at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary separating ordinary set density from recurrent coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=1\), \(\mathbb S^0=\{-1,1\}\). Let \(u_0=1\) and \(u_k=-1\) for every \(k\ge1\). Then \(\{u_k:k\ge0\}=\mathbb S^0\) is dense in \(\mathbb S^0\), but no subsequence with strictly increasing indices converges to \(1\). Thus ordinary set density does not imply recurrent directional coverage in dimension one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the two-point unit sphere, one direction may occur only once, so set density need not imply recurrent approximation.

notation.meaning: The two-point unit sphere in the real line.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Density and Recurrent Approximation on Positive-Dimensional Spheres
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional condition under which set density implies recurrent directional approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\), let \(u_k\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\), and suppose \(\{u_k:k\ge0\}\) is dense in \(\mathbb S^{n-1}\). Then every nonempty relatively open spherical neighborhood contains infinitely many sequence terms. Equivalently, for every \(u\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\) there are strictly increasing indices \(k_j\) such that \(u_{k_j}\to u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a positive-dimensional sphere, density of the attained direction set guarantees recurrent visits and a subsequence converging to every unit direction.
review_flags: The equivalence uses that the sphere has no isolated points when n is at least 2.
knowledge_statements.title: Density and Recurrent Approximation on Positive-Dimensional Spheres
Dense Direction Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines asymptotically complete directional coverage by normalized polling or search directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((d_k)_{k\geq0}\) of nonzero vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is directionally dense when its normalized directions \(u_k=d_k/\|d_k\|\) are dense in the unit sphere \(\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\). Equivalently, for every \(u\in\mathbb{S}^{n-1}\) and every \(\eta>0\), infinitely many indices \(k\) satisfy \(\|u_k-u\|<\eta\); equivalently, every \(u\) is the limit of a subsequence \((u_{k_j})\). This property provides asymptotic directional coverage without requiring any finite iteration to use a positive spanning set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction sequence is dense when its normalized vectors approach every unit direction along subsequences.
assumptions_latex: The topology on the unit sphere is induced by the Euclidean norm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Density of the set of normalized directions does not by itself imply infinitely many visits to every neighborhood or a convergent subsequence for every direction. A source is needed to determine whether this leaf intends ordinary set density or the stronger recurrent-direction property.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for a set of nonzero directions in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A set \(V\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) is asymptotically dense if \(\{v/\lVert v\rVert:v\in V\}\) is dense in the unit sphere \(S^{n-1}=\{w\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lVert w\rVert=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set of nonzero directions is asymptotically dense when its normalized directions are dense on the unit sphere.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free gradient representation obtained from values at a nonsingular ordered simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a nonsingular simplex with ordered vertices \(x_1,\ldots,x_{N+1}\), direction matrix \(V(S)=[x_2-x_1,\ldots,x_{N+1}-x_1]\), and difference vector \(\delta(f:S)=(f(x_2)-f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_{N+1})-f(x_1))^T\). The simplex gradient is \(D(f:S)=V(S)^{-T}\delta(f:S)\). The matrices and vectors in this representation depend on the vertex designated as \(x_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonsingular ordered simplex, the simplex gradient is the inverse transpose of the simplex direction matrix applied to the objective-value differences from the distinguished vertex x1. Its representation depends on that vertex designation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational geometry and sampled-value notation for simplex derivative representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For vertices \(x_1,\ldots,x_{N+1}\in\mathbb{R}^N\), let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_{N+1}\}\) and \(V(S)=[x_2-x_1,\ldots,x_{N+1}-x_1]\). The simplex is nonsingular when \(V(S)\) is nonsingular. Define \(\operatorname{diam}(S)=\max_{1\le i,j\le N+1}\|x_i-x_j\|\), the simplex condition as the \(\ell^2\) condition number \(\kappa(V)\), \(\delta(f:S)=(f(x_2)-f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_{N+1})-f(x_1))^T\), and \(\sigma_+(S)=\max_{2\le j\le N+1}\|x_1-x_j\|\), \(\sigma_-(S)=\min_{2\le j\le N+1}\|x_1-x_j\|\). Then \(\sigma_+(S)\le \operatorname{diam}(S)\le 2\sigma_+(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex is the convex hull of N+1 vertices. Relative to the distinguished vertex x1, its direction matrix contains the remaining vertex displacements, and the simplex is nonsingular when that matrix is invertible. The definition also introduces its diameter, Euclidean condition number, sampled objective differences, and maximum and minimum vertex distances from x1; the diameter lies between sigma-plus and twice sigma-plus.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Gradient Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the affine interpolation gradient determined by a poised n-dimensional simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\{y^0,y^1,\ldots,y^n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be affinely independent, define \(S=[y^1-y^0\ \cdots\ y^n-y^0]\), and set \(\delta f=(f(y^1)-f(y^0),\ldots,f(y^n)-f(y^0))^{\mathsf T}\). The simplex gradient of \(f\) on \(Y\) is \[\nabla_S f(Y)=S^{-\mathsf T}\delta f.\] It is the unique vector \(g\) for which the affine model \(m(y)=f(y^0)+g^{\mathsf T}(y-y^0)\) interpolates \(f\) at every point of \(Y\). Affine independence is exactly the condition ensuring that this representation is uniquely defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The simplex gradient solves the affine interpolation equations on n+1 affinely independent sample points.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is defined at every point of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla_S f(Y)=S^{-\mathsf T}\delta f\) is the unique gradient of the affine interpolant on \(Y\).

notation.meaning: Simplex edge matrix based at the first sample point.
Simplex gradient on the sample set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barycentric Representation of the Simplex Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation through the affine barycentric basis of the simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_n\) be the barycentric coordinate functions of an affinely independent simplex \(Y\), so \(\lambda_i(y^j)=\delta_{ij}\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i\equiv1\). Then
\[
m(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(y^i)\lambda_i(x),\qquad
\nabla_S f(Y)=\nabla m=\sum_{i=0}^n f(y^i)\nabla\lambda_i,
\]
with \(\sum_i\nabla\lambda_i=0\). Consequently, the simplex gradient is independent of which vertex is selected as the edge-matrix base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The simplex gradient is the function-value-weighted sum of barycentric-coordinate gradients and is independent of the chosen base vertex.
knowledge_statements.title: Barycentric Representation of the Simplex Gradient

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Simplex-Gradient Formula for Quadratic Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quadratic representation and affine exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=c+a^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx\) with \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\), let \(s_i=y^i-y^0\), and let \(S=[s_1\ \cdots\ s_n]\) be nonsingular. Then
\[
\nabla_S f(Y)=\nabla f(y^0)+\frac12S^{-\mathsf T}
\begin{bmatrix}s_1^{\mathsf T}Hs_1\\ \vdots\\s_n^{\mathsf T}Hs_n\end{bmatrix}.
\]
In particular, the simplex gradient reproduces the exact gradient of every affine function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic objective, the simplex gradient equals the true base-point gradient plus an explicit curvature term; affine functions are reproduced exactly.

notation.meaning: The constant Hessian of the quadratic function.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Simplex-Gradient Formula for Quadratic Functions

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Shape Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines scale-invariant measures of simplex nondegeneracy through its normalized edge matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affinely independent simplex \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(S=[y^1-y^0\ \cdots\ y^n-y^0]\) and \(\Delta=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}\|y^i-y^0\|>0\). With \(\widehat S=S/\Delta\), define the thickness measure \(\tau(Y)=\sigma_{\min}(\widehat S)\) and the inverse shape measure \(\kappa_Y=\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2=1/\tau(Y)\). These quantities are invariant under translation and uniform positive scaling. A family of simplexes is uniformly shape-regular exactly when \(\tau(Y)\) is bounded away from zero, equivalently when \(\kappa_Y\) is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized smallest singular value measures simplex thickness; its reciprocal measures shape ill-conditioning independently of location and scale.
assumptions_latex: The simplex vertices are affinely independent.
The matrix and vector norms are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform shape regularity is equivalent to \(\inf_Y\tau(Y)>0\), or equivalently \(\sup_Y\kappa_Y<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Edge matrix normalized by simplex radius.

source_refs.locator: 6 Ensuring well poisedness and suitable derivative-free models p. 89

source_witnesses.locator: 6 Ensuring well poisedness and suitable derivative-free models p. 89

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-free shape measure based on vertex-to-opposite-face altitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nondegenerate simplex \(Y\), let \(h_i\) be the Euclidean distance from \(y^i\) to the affine hull of its opposite face, let \(h_{\min}(Y)=\min_i h_i\), and let \(d(Y)\) be the diameter. Then
\[
q_{\mathrm{alt}}(Y)=\frac{h_{\min}(Y)}{d(Y)}
\]
is invariant under rigid motions and uniform positive scaling. It is positive for every nondegenerate simplex and tends to zero whenever a fixed-diameter family develops a vanishing altitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum altitude divided by diameter is a scale-free aspect measure that detects simplex flattening.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{\mathrm{alt}}(Y)=h_{\min}(Y)/d(Y)>0\), and it vanishes along fixed-diameter families with vanishing minimum altitude.

notation.meaning: Altitude from vertex i to its opposite face.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Altitude Aspect Measure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-free volume quality of a full-dimensional simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^n\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(S=[y^1-y^0\ \cdots\ y^n-y^0]\) and \(d(Y)=\max_{i,j}\|y^i-y^j\|_2>0\). Define
\[
q_{\mathrm{vol}}(Y)=\frac{n!\operatorname{vol}_n(\operatorname{conv}Y)}{d(Y)^n}=\frac{|\det S|}{d(Y)^n}.
\]
This measure is invariant under translations, orthogonal transformations, and uniform positive scaling, and it is positive exactly when \(Y\) is affinely independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Determinant divided by diameter to the dimension is a scale-free volume measure that is positive exactly for a nondegenerate simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_{\mathrm{vol}}(Y)=|\det S|/d(Y)^n\), and \(q_{\mathrm{vol}}(Y)>0\iff Y\) is affinely independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Simplex Volume Measure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized simplex shape measure formed from volume and diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If $\mathbb{Y}=\{y^0,\ldots,y^n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ forms a simplex, define $\operatorname{von}(\operatorname{conv}(\mathbb{Y})):=\operatorname{vol}(\mathbb{Y})/\operatorname{diam}(\mathbb{Y})^n$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{von}(\operatorname{conv}(\mathbb{Y}))=\operatorname{vol}(\mathbb{Y}/\operatorname{diam}(\mathbb{Y}))$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized volume of a simplex is its volume divided by the nth power of its diameter. Equivalently, it is the volume of the simplex after scaling its diameter to one.

children.title: Simplex Conditioning Measures
children.top_down_role: Numerical conditioning characteristics of simplex-based representations.

assumptions_latex: The displacement matrix \(S=[y^1-y^0\ \cdots\ y^n-y^0]\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantities \(\sigma_{\min}(\widehat S)\), \(\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2\), and \(\kappa_2(\widehat S)\) measure the scale-normalized conditioning of the simplex.

notation.meaning: Matrix of simplex edge vectors based at the first sample point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-normalized spectral conditioning measures for a determined simplex in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Linear interpolation and regression models p. 24
2.4 Error bounds for linear interpolation and regression p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the normalized displacement matrix by \(\widehat S=\Delta^{-1}S\). Its spectral condition number and inverse norm are
\[
\kappa_2(\widehat S)=\|\widehat S\|_2\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(\widehat S)}{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat S)},
\qquad
\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat S)}.
\]
The first quantity measures relative spectral conditioning, while the second is the absolute amplification factor for perturbations passed through \(\widehat S^{-T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After normalizing the simplex edge matrix by the sampling scale, its spectral condition number measures relative conditioning and its inverse norm measures absolute perturbation amplification.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Conditioning Measures

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Linear interpolation and regression models p. 24
2.4 Error bounds for linear interpolation and regression p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of Normalized Simplex Conditioning Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent comparison of inverse norm and spectral condition number under radius normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat S=S/\Delta\), where \(\Delta=\max_i\|Se_i\|_2\), and suppose \(S\) is nonsingular. Then \(1\leq\|\widehat S\|_2\leq\|\widehat S\|_F\leq\sqrt n\), and hence
\[
\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2\leq\kappa_2(\widehat S)\leq\sqrt n\,\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2.
\]
Thus bounded inverse norm and bounded spectral condition number are equivalent normalized conditioning requirements in fixed dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a radius-normalized simplex matrix, inverse norm and spectral condition number differ by at most a factor of the square root of the dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence of Normalized Simplex Conditioning Measures

children.title: Shape-Induced Model Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of local model sensitivity on simplex geometry.

assumptions_latex: The simplex displacement matrix \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
The observed difference vector is perturbed from \(d\) to \(d+e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widetilde g-g\|_2\leq \|S^{-1}\|_2\|e\|_2\), so poorly shaped simplices amplify data errors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of a simplex gradient to additive errors in sampled function differences.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 Error bounds for linear interpolation and regression p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(g=S^{-T}d\) and \(\widetilde g=S^{-T}(d+e)\), then
\[
\widetilde g-g=S^{-T}e,
\qquad
\|\widetilde g-g\|_2\leq \|S^{-1}\|_2\|e\|_2.
\]
Consequently, for fixed sampling scale and data error, decreasing \(\sigma_{\min}(S)\) increases the worst-case sensitivity of the fitted linear model gradient; the bound is attained for a singular-vector-aligned perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Errors in sampled values are amplified in the fitted gradient by the inverse simplex geometry, with worst-case factor equal to the reciprocal smallest singular value.
knowledge_statements.title: Shape-Induced Model Sensitivity

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 Error bounds for linear interpolation and regression p. 26

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Combined Curvature and Noise Sensitivity Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplex-gradient error under smoothness and bounded observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_i=y^i-y^0\), \(S=[s_1\ \cdots\ s_n]\) be nonsingular, and \(\|s_i\|_2\le\Delta\). Suppose \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(\widetilde f(y^i)=f(y^i)+\eta_i\) with \(|\eta_i|\le\varepsilon\). The noisy simplex gradient satisfies \[\|\widetilde g-
abla f(y^0)\|_2\le\|S^{-1}\|_2\sqrt n\left( rac{L\Delta^2}{2}+2\varepsilonight).\] With \(S=\Delta\widehat S\), this becomes \[\|\widetilde g-
abla f(y^0)\|_2\le\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2\sqrt n\left( rac{L\Delta}{2}+ rac{2\varepsilon}{\Delta}ight).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometry amplifies curvature error proportional to the sampling radius and observation-noise error inversely proportional to it.
assumptions_latex: \nabla f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz on the sampled region}.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Curvature and Noise Sensitivity Bound

children.title: Degenerate-Shape Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes where simplex quality becomes inadequate for stable modeling.

assumptions_latex: The matrices \(S_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) are nonsingular for every \(k\).
The sequence satisfies \(S_k\to S_*\), where \(S_*\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(S_*)<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The amplification factors satisfy \(\|S_k^{-1}\|_2\to\infty\), while at \(S_*\) the system \(S_*^Tg=d\) may be inconsistent or nonunique.

notation.meaning: Sequence of nonsingular simplex displacement matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between nonsingular determined simplices and affinely dependent limiting configurations.

source_refs.locator: 6 Ensuring well poisedness and suitable derivative-free models p. 89

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Continuity of singular values gives \(\sigma_{\min}(S_k)\to\sigma_{\min}(S_*)=0\). Hence
\[
\|S_k^{-1}\|_2=\frac{1}{\sigma_{\min}(S_k)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
For each \(k\), the determined simplex gradient is \(g_k=S_k^{-T}d\). At the singular limit, the equations \(S_*^Tg=d\) have no solution when \(d\notin\operatorname{range}(S_*^T)\), and otherwise have multiple solutions because \(\ker(S_*^T)\neq\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When nonsingular simplex matrices converge to a singular matrix, their inverse amplification factors diverge. At the singular limit, the gradient equations are either inconsistent or have multiple solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Shape Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: 6 Ensuring well poisedness and suitable derivative-free models p. 89

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simplex is degenerate exactly when \(\det S=0\), equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(S)<n\).

notation.meaning: Displacement matrix based at the first vertex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine degeneracy of an \(n\)-simplex represented by its edge matrix.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Linear interpolation and regression models p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The simplex generated by \(Y\) is degenerate if its vertices are affinely dependent. Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{rank}(S)<n
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det S=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{vol}_n(Y)=\frac{|\det S|}{n!}=0.
\]
In this case there exists \(v\neq0\) such that \(S^Tv=0\), so sampled affine values cannot uniquely determine every component of a linear model gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex is degenerate precisely when its vertices are affinely dependent, its edge matrix is singular, and its n-dimensional volume is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Degeneracy

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Linear interpolation and regression models p. 24

assumptions_latex: The matrix with rows \((1,(y^i)^T)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique affine model \(m(x)=\alpha+g^Tx\) satisfying \(m(y^i)=f(y^i)\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique affine interpolation from exactly \(n+1\) poised points.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Linear interpolation and regression models p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{(n+1)\times(n+1)}\) by row \(i\) equal to \((1,(y^i)^T)\), and define \(b=(f(y^0),\ldots,f(y^n))^T\). The determined affine interpolant is
\[
m(x)=\alpha+g^Tx,
\qquad
\begin{bmatrix}\alpha\\g\end{bmatrix}=M^{-1}b.
\]
Nonsingularity of \(M\), equivalently affine independence of \(Y\), gives existence and uniqueness and ensures \(m(y^i)=f(y^i)\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly n+1 affinely independent samples uniquely determine an affine model by solving the square interpolation system.
knowledge_statements.title: Determined Linear Interpolation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Linear interpolation and regression models p. 24

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The unique affine function interpolating a scalar-valued function at a poised set of n+1 points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and let \(\mathbb{Y}=\{y^0,\ldots,y^n\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be poised for linear interpolation. Its linear interpolation function is \(L_Y(x)=\alpha_0+\alpha^\top x\), where \((\alpha_0,\alpha)\) is the unique solution of \(\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf 1&Y^\top\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\alpha_0\\\alpha\end{bmatrix}=f(\mathbb{Y})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a poised set, the linear interpolation function of f is the unique affine function agreeing with f at every point of the set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale Invariance of Poised Linear Interpolation Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of poisedness and normalized geometry under positive homothetic scaling about the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb Y=\{y^0,y^1,\ldots,y^n\}\) be poised for linear interpolation. For \(\gamma>0\), define \(y_\gamma^i=y^0+\gamma(y^i-y^0)\) and \(\mathbb Y_\gamma=\{y_\gamma^0,\ldots,y_\gamma^n\}\). Then \(\mathbb Y_\gamma\) is poised,
\[
\overline{\operatorname{diam}}(\mathbb Y_\gamma)=\gamma\overline{\operatorname{diam}}(\mathbb Y),
\qquad
\|\widehat L_\gamma^{-1}\|=\|\widehat L^{-1}\|,
\]
where the matrices are normalized by their respective sampling diameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let row \(i\) of \(M\) be \((1,(y^i)^T)\), let \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_1,\ldots,w_p)\), and let \(b_i=f(y^i)\). The affine regression coefficients solve
\[
\begin{bmatrix}\alpha\\g\end{bmatrix}
=\operatorname*{argmin}_{c\in\mathbb{R}^{n+1}}\|W^{1/2}(Mc-b)\|_2^2
