knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the unique weighted least-squares coefficient vector \(\widehat c\), let \(r=b-M\widehat c\). Then
\[
M^TWr=0,
\qquad
M\widehat c=P_Wb,
\qquad
P_W=M(M^TWM)^{-1}M^TW.
\]
Thus \(M\widehat c\) is the \(W\)-orthogonal projection of \(b\) onto \(\operatorname{range}(M)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Regression Function on a Poised Sample Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and coefficient representation of the affine least-squares model fitted to a poised sample set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\mathbb{Y}=\{y^0,\ldots,y^m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(m\ge n\), be poised for linear regression. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cost and curvature tradeoff between linear and quadratic DFO interpolation models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation-cost comparison for the model-based DFO scheme in the extract; these bounds are not evaluation-complexity convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A determined quadratic model in n variables uses q=\tfrac12(n+1)(n+2)=O(n^2) interpolation values, so initialization requires O(n^2) function evaluations; even when m_k is updated instead of reconstructed from scratch, constructing the model and computing a step requires O(n^4) operations per iteration. Setting G=0 gives a linear model with n+1 parameters and interpolation points and O(n^3) work per iteration, but it cannot represent curvature and is not rapidly convergent. A hybrid scheme may begin with n+1 points and a linear model and switch to a quadratic model after q function values become available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fully determined quadratic interpolation requires quadratically many initial samples and, for the implementation described, fourth-order arithmetic per iteration. Linear interpolation reduces the sample set to n+1 points and the iteration cost to cubic order, but loses curvature representation and rapid convergence. A hybrid may switch to a quadratic model once enough values have accumulated.
assumptions_latex: q=\tfrac12(n+1)(n+2)\text{ for the determined quadratic model}
\text{the model is updated rather than reconstructed from scratch}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Quadratic: }O(n^2)\text{ initial evaluations and }O(n^4)\text{ work per iteration};\quad \text{linear: }n+1\text{ points and }O(n^3)\text{ work per iteration, without curvature representation.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Supremum Lower Bound for Normalized Natural-Basis Polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coefficient-to-function norm bound for natural-basis polynomial models used in derivative-free interpolation geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)\) be a quadratic polynomial of degree at most \(d\), where \(\bar\phi\) is the natural basis and \(\|v\|_\infty=1\). Then there exists a constant \(\sigma_\infty>0\), independent of \(v\), such that
\[
\max_{x\in B(0;1)}\left|v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)\right|\geq \sigma_\infty.
\]
Moreover, \(\sigma_\infty\geq1\) for \(d=1\), and \(\sigma_\infty\geq\tfrac14\) for \(d=2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a natural-basis quadratic polynomial of degree at most d whose coefficient vector has infinity norm one, the maximum absolute value on the unit ball is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant independent of the coefficient vector. The stated lower bounds are 1 for degree one and 1/4 for degree two.
assumptions_latex: v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)\text{ is a quadratic polynomial of degree at most }d
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\sigma_\infty>0\text{ independent of }v\text{ such that }\max_{x\in B(0;1)}|v^{\top}\bar\phi(x)|\geq\sigma_\infty;\quad d=1\Rightarrow\sigma_\infty\geq1,\quad d=2\Rightarrow\sigma_\infty\geq\tfrac14.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unisolvency criteria for determined linear and quadratic interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The primary conclusion concerns determined quadratic interpolation through its lifted linear-system representation; the linear criterion is retained as the explicit comparison used in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For m_k(x_k+p)=f(x_k)+g^Tp interpolating y^1,\ldots,y^n, let s^l=y^l-x_k. The vector g is unique if and only if \{s^1,\ldots,s^n\} is linearly independent, equivalently the simplex with vertices x_k,y^1,\ldots,y^n is nondegenerate. For a basis \{\phi_i\}_{i=1}^q of the n-variate quadratic polynomials and m_k(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q\alpha_i\phi_i(x), the q-point set Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^q\} uniquely determines \alpha if and only if \delta(Y)=\det[\phi_i(y^j)]_{i,j=1}^q\ne0. The monomial quadratic model is equivalently a linear model in lifted linear and quadratic features. As |\delta(Y)| approaches zero, the interpolation system becomes numerically difficult and may fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear interpolation model is unique exactly when its sample displacements are linearly independent. A quadratic model is unique exactly when the evaluation matrix of a quadratic-polynomial basis at the sample points has nonzero determinant. Quadratic interpolation can therefore be treated as linear interpolation in lifted monomial features, while a determinant near zero signals numerical instability.
assumptions_latex: \{\phi_i\}_{i=1}^q\text{ is a basis of the }n\text{-variate quadratic polynomials}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\text{ is unique}\iff\operatorname{rank}[s^1\ \cdots\ s^n]=n;\qquad \alpha\text{ is unique}\iff\delta(Y)\ne0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Condition-number-dependent error bounds for determined quadratic interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform Hessian, gradient, and function-value error bounds for a poised, fully determined quadratic interpolation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), with \(p+1=(n+1)(n+2)/2\), be poised for quadratic interpolation and contained in \(B(y^0;\Delta)\), where \(\Delta=\Delta(Y)\). Let \(f\in C^2(\Omega)\) on an open set \(\Omega\supset B(y^0;\Delta)\), suppose \(
abla^2f\) is Lipschitz continuous on \(\Omega\) with constant \(v_2>0\), and let \(m\) be the quadratic interpolation model on \(Y\). Then, for every \(y\in B(y^0;\Delta)\), \[\|
abla^2f(y)-
abla^2m(y)\|\le\kappa_{eh}\Delta,\qquad \|
abla f(y)-
abla m(y)\|\le\kappa_{eg}\Delta^2,\qquad |f(y)-m(y)|\le\kappa_{ef}\Delta^3,\] where \[\kappa_{eh}= rac{3\sqrt2}{2}p^{1/2}v_2\|\widehat Q^{-1}\|,\qquad \kappa_{eg}= rac{3(1+\sqrt2)}{2}p^{1/2}v_2\|\widehat Q^{-1}\|,\] and \[\kappa_{ef}= rac{6+9\sqrt2}{4}p^{1/2}v_2\|\widehat Q^{-1}\|+ rac{v_2}{6}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a poised, fully determined quadratic interpolation set and a function with Lipschitz-continuous Hessian, the interpolation model uniformly approximates the Hessian to order Delta, the gradient to order Delta squared, and the function value to order Delta cubed throughout the sampling ball. The constants depend explicitly on the Hessian Lipschitz constant and the inverse normalized interpolation matrix.

\nabla^2f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous on }\Omega\text{ with constant }v_2>0
m\text{ is the quadratic interpolation model determined by }Y

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-Point Univariate Quadratic Interpolation and Its Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Univariate specialization of determined quadratic interpolation; the stationary point is a unique global minimizer only when the interpolant is strictly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(a<b<c\) and values \(y_a,y_b,y_c\), the unique polynomial \(q\) of degree at most two satisfying \(q(a)=y_a\), \(q(b)=y_b\), and \(q(c)=y_c\) is
\[
q(x)=y_a\frac{(x-b)(x-c)}{(a-b)(a-c)}+y_b\frac{(x-a)(x-c)}{(b-a)(b-c)}+y_c\frac{(x-a)(x-b)}{(c-a)(c-b)}.
\]
If \(q\) is strictly convex, then its unique minimizer is
\[
x^*=\frac12\frac{y_a(b^2-c^2)+y_b(c^2-a^2)+y_c(a^2-b^2)}{y_a(b-c)+y_b(c-a)+y_c(a-b)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three distinct scalar sample points determine a unique polynomial interpolant of degree at most two. If this interpolant is strictly convex, its stationary point, given by the displayed formula, is its unique global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: q\text{ is strictly convex for the minimizer conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q\text{ is the unique interpolating polynomial of degree at most two; if }q\text{ is strictly convex, then }x^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R}q(x)\text{ is given by the displayed formula.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique determined quadratic interpolation model and its trust-region use
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Determined quadratic interpolation in deterministic model-based derivative-free optimization; no model-accuracy, convergence, or complexity guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^q\}\subset\mathbb R^n, where x_k\in Y, f(x_k)\le f(y^l) for every y^l\in Y, and q=\tfrac12(n+1)(n+2). For m_k(x_k+p)=c+g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TGp with G=G^T, impose m_k(y^l)=f(y^l), l=1,\ldots,q. If the resulting square interpolation system is nonsingular, then (c,g,G), and hence m_k, are uniquely determined. Once formed, the model is approximately minimized subject to \|p\|_2\le\Delta, and the trial point is assessed using \rho=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k^+)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k^+)}; a sufficiently reducing trial is accepted, while an unsuccessful trial may prompt interpolation-set improvement or trust-region contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic in n variables has one-half (n+1)(n+2) independent coefficients. The same number of interpolation values uniquely determines the model when the square interpolation system is nonsingular. The model can then generate a trust-region trial whose acceptance is assessed by actual versus predicted reduction; failure may trigger sample-geometry repair or a smaller trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_k\text{ is uniquely determined; it may be used in }\min_{\|p\|_2\le\Delta}m_k(x_k+p)\text{ with trial management based on }\rho.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a quadratic model \(m(x)=\phi(x)^Tc\), exact interpolation requires \(Mc=b\). Since \(M\) has full row rank, this system is consistent for every \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\). If \(c_0\in\mathbb{R}^q\) is any particular solution, then
\[
\{c\in\mathbb{R}^q:Mc=b\}=c_0+\ker M,
\qquad
\dim(\ker M)=q-p>0.
\]
Thus interpolation alone does not select a unique quadratic model, and an additional selection criterion is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free quadratic-model update combining function-value interpolation with minimum Frobenius-norm change from the preceding model Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After moving from $x_k$ to $x_{k+1}$, construct the quadratic model $m_{k+1}$ by solving
\[
\min_{f,g,G}\ \|G-G_k\|_F^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
G=G^\top,\qquad m_{f,g,G}(y^l)=f_{\mathrm{obj}}(y^l),\quad l=1,\ldots,\hat q,
\]
where $G_k$ is the Hessian of the preceding model, $f_{\mathrm{obj}}$ denotes the objective function, and $\hat q$ is comparable to $n$. Choosing $\hat q>n+1$ is required to guarantee that the updated Hessian can differ from $G_k$, and $\hat q=2n+1$ is a practical choice stated in the source. If the interpolation equations are solvable for every right-hand side and the interpolation points are not all contained in a hyperplane, this equality-constrained quadratic program has a unique solution. Its KKT conditions form a system of equations; after determining the model, compute the next step by solving the associated trust-region subproblem. The method retains $O(n)$ interpolation points and requires $O(n^3)$ operations per iteration, compared with $O(n^4)$ for the fuller interpolation methods under discussion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method updates an underdetermined quadratic model by interpolating objective values at order-n sample points while minimizing the Frobenius-norm change from the previous model Hessian. Solvability of the interpolation equations for every right-hand side and failure of the sample points to lie in one hyperplane ensure a unique update. The update is obtained through the quadratic program's KKT system and is followed by a trust-region step. It retains order-n interpolation points and uses order-n-cubed work per iteration.
assumptions_latex: m_{k+1}\text{ is a quadratic model and }G_k\text{ is the Hessian of the preceding model}.
\text{The interpolation equations are solvable for every right-hand side.}
\{y^i\}\text{ is not contained in a hyperplane.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{f,g,G}\left\{\|G-G_k\|_F^2:G=G^\top,\ m_{f,g,G}(y^l)=f_{\mathrm{obj}}(y^l),\ l=1,\ldots,\hat q\right\}\text{ is a singleton};\qquad |Y|=O(n),\quad \text{work per iteration}=O(n^3).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A minimum-Frobenius-norm quadratic model is defined by
\[
(\alpha_*,g_*,H_*)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R},\,g\in\mathbb{R}^n,\,H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\,H=H^T}\frac12\|H\|_F^2
\]
subject to
\[
\alpha+g^Ty^i+\frac12(y^i)^THy^i=f(y^i),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,p.
\]
Feasibility gives existence. Strict convexity in \(H\) makes the minimizing Hessian unique, and affine spanning of the sample points makes the corresponding \(\alpha\) and \(g\) unique. The selected model is \(m_*(x)=\alpha_*+g_*^Tx+\tfrac12x^TH_*x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among feasible quadratic interpolants, a minimum-Frobenius-norm model minimizes the Frobenius norm of its Hessian. If the samples affinely span the space, the selected model is unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Certificate for a Minimum-Frobenius-Norm Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient optimality certificate for minimum-Hessian-norm interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the interpolation equations as \(A_Lc_L+A_Hc_H=f\), where \(c_L\) contains affine coefficients and \(c_H\) is an orthonormally scaled vectorization satisfying \(\|c_H\|_2=\|H\|_F\). A feasible pair \((c_L,c_H)\) is minimum-Frobenius-norm if and only if there exists \(\lambda\) such that
\[
A_L^T\lambda=0,
\qquad
c_H+A_H^T\lambda=0,
\qquad
A_Lc_L+A_Hc_H=f.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility plus a multiplier orthogonal to the affine design and balancing the Hessian coefficients certifies minimum Frobenius norm.
assumptions_latex: The symmetric-Hessian basis is scaled so coefficient Euclidean norm equals Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed feasibility and stationarity equations are necessary and sufficient for global optimality.

If the sites fail to affinely span \(\mathbb R^n\), there exists a nonzero affine function \(a(x)=\beta+v^Tx\) vanishing at every site. Then \(m_*+ta\) is feasible for every \(t\in\mathbb R\) and has the same Hessian norm as \(m_*\). Thus affine spanning is required for uniqueness of the complete model, not for uniqueness of its minimizing Hessian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spark Certificate for Unique Sparse Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform uniqueness threshold for sparse polynomial coefficients in a fixed dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(b=Mc_*\) and \(\|c_*\|_0\le s\). If \(\operatorname{spark}(M)>2s\), then \(c_*\) is the unique vector satisfying \(Mc=b\) and \(\|c\|_0\le s\). If \(\operatorname{spark}(M)\le2s\), some two distinct vectors with at most \(s\) nonzeros generate identical sampled values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spark greater than twice the sparsity level guarantees unique sparse interpolation, and the uniform threshold is sharp.

notation.meaning: Smallest number of linearly dependent columns of M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Certificate for a Unique Basis-Pursuit Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-specific uniqueness certificate for sparse polynomial interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_*\) satisfy \(Mc_*=b\), with support \(T\). If \(M_T\) has full column rank and there exists \(y\) such that \[M_T^Ty=\operatorname{sign}(c_{*,T}),\qquad \|M_{T^c}^Ty\|_\infty<1,\] then \(c_*\) is the unique solution of \(\min_c\|c\|_1\) subject to \(Mc=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full rank on the active columns together with a strict dual vector certifies uniqueness of a particular basis-pursuit solution.

notation.meaning: Design submatrix formed from columns indexed by T.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificate for a Unique Basis-Pursuit Solution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-Space Characterization of Uniform Basis-Pursuit Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact uniform recovery condition for sparse coefficients using basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every coefficient vector supported on at most \(s\) indices is the unique solution of \[\min_c\|c\|_1\quad\text{subject to }Mc=Mc_*\] if and only if every nonzero \(h\in\ker M\) and every set \(T\) with \(|T|\le s\) satisfy \[\|h_T\|_1<\|h_{T^c}\|_1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform recovery of all s-sparse coefficients by basis pursuit is equivalent to the strict null-space property of order s.
assumptions_latex: A fixed dictionary and sample design matrix \(M\) are given.

notation.meaning: Restriction of h to indices in T.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis-Pursuit Denoising for Sparse Polynomial Fitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise-tolerant sparse coefficient recovery in a fixed polynomial dictionary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a polynomial design matrix \(M\), observations \(b\), and \(\delta\ge0\), basis-pursuit denoising computes \[\widehat c\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{c\in\mathbb R^q}\|c\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|Mc-b\|_2\le\delta.\] For \(\delta=0\), this reduces to basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis-pursuit denoising selects the smallest-l1 coefficient vector fitting the sampled values to the declared tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A fixed polynomial dictionary and design matrix \(M\) are given.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Pursuit Denoising for Sparse Polynomial Fitting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable Recovery Under a Robust Null-Space Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise and approximate-sparsity guarantee for basis-pursuit denoising.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(M\) satisfies the \(\ell_2\)-robust null-space property of order \(s\): for every \(h\) and \(|T|\le s\), \[\|h_T\|_2\le \frac{\rho}{\sqrt{s}}\|h_{T^c}\|_1+\tau\|Mh\|_2,\qquad 0<\rho<1.\] If \(b=Mc_*+e\), \(\|e\|_2\le\delta\), and \(\widehat c\) solves basis-pursuit denoising with tolerance \(\delta\), then constants depending only on \(\rho,\tau\) satisfy \[\|\widehat c-c_*\|_1\le C_1\sigma_s(c_*)_1+C_2\sqrt{s}\,\delta,\qquad \|\widehat c-c_*\|_2\le D_1\frac{\sigma_s(c_*)_1}{\sqrt{s}}+D_2\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust null-space condition makes noisy sparse polynomial recovery stable to measurement error and coefficient tails.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) has the stated robust null-space property.

notation.meaning: Best s-term approximation error of c in the l1 norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable Recovery Under a Robust Null-Space Property

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basis-Pursuit Duality for Sparse Polynomial Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual formulation and optimality condition for exact l1 sparse polynomial fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible sampled system \(Mc=b\), basis pursuit and its dual are \[\min_{c\in\mathbb R^q}\|c\|_1\quad\text{subject to }Mc=b,\qquad \max_{y\in\mathbb R^m}b^Ty\quad\text{subject to }\|M^Ty\|_\infty\le1.\] Strong duality holds. Primal-feasible \(c_*\) and dual-feasible \(y_*\) are optimal if and only if \(M^Ty_*\in\partial\|c_*\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact l1 sparse polynomial fitting has an infinity-norm-constrained dual, and an l1-subgradient match certifies primal-dual optimality.

notation.meaning: Dual variable for the sampled interpolation equality.
Subdifferential of the coefficient l1 norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Pursuit Duality for Sparse Polynomial Interpolation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Certificate for Penalized Sparse Polynomial Fitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality test for an l1-penalized polynomial least-squares fit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L(c)=\tfrac12\|Mc-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|c\|_1\) with \(\lambda>0\), a vector \(c_*\) is globally optimal if and only if there exists \(z\in\mathbb R^q\) such that \[M^T(Mc_*-b)+\lambda z=0,\qquad z_j=\operatorname{sign}(c_{*,j})\ \text{if }c_{*,j}\ne0,\qquad |z_j|\le1\ \text{if }c_{*,j}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient vector solves the l1-penalized polynomial fit exactly when its residual correlations satisfy the lasso subgradient conditions.

notation.meaning: Subgradient of the coefficient l1 norm at the candidate solution.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Certificate for Penalized Sparse Polynomial Fitting

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polynomial model \(m(x)=\sum_{j=1}^q c_j\phi_j(x)\) is \(s\)-sparse when
\[
\|c\|_0=|\{j:c_j\neq0\}|\leq s.
\]
Given sample values \(b\), a convex sparsity-promoting surrogate may select coefficients by
\[
c_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{c\in\mathbb{R}^q}\frac12\|Mc-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|c\|_1.
\]
The definition depends on the chosen dictionary because coefficient sparsity is not invariant under arbitrary basis changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse polynomial uses few nonzero coefficients in a fixed dictionary; an l1-regularized fit is a standard convex way to promote such sparsity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear Residuals Need Not Give a Convex Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of the affine-residual convexity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar residual model \(m_1(x)=x^2-1\), the composite model is \[m_f(x)=\tfrac12(x^2-1)^2,\qquad m_f''(x)=6x^2-2.\] Hence \(m_f''(0)=-2<0\), so a squared nonlinear residual model need not be convex despite being nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squaring a nonlinear residual preserves nonnegativity but not convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Residuals Need Not Give a Convex Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential structure of a least-squares model assembled from residual surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_F=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)^T\) be twice differentiable and define \(m_f(x)=	frac12\|m_F(x)\|_2^2\). Then \[
abla m_f(x)=J_m(x)^Tm_F(x),\qquad 
abla^2m_f(x)=J_m(x)^TJ_m(x)+\sum_{i=1}^rm_i(x)
abla^2m_i(x).\] If every residual model is affine, the second sum vanishes and \(m_f\) is a convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual composition has the standard least-squares derivative decomposition; affine residual models give a convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Composite Gradient and Hessian

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic conversion of residual-vector model error into least-squares objective-model error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\) and \(m_f(x)=\tfrac12\|m_F(x)\|_2^2\). Then \[|m_f(x)-f(x)|\le\tfrac12\|m_F(x)-F(x)\|_2\bigl(\|m_F(x)\|_2+\|F(x)\|_2\bigr).\] In particular, if \(\|m_F-F\|_2\le\varepsilon\) and \(\|F\|_2\le M\), then \(|m_f-f|\le M\varepsilon+\varepsilon^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-vector accuracy transfers to objective-model accuracy, with a bound controlled by residual magnitude and residual-model error.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Objective Error Propagation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Gauss–Newton Curvature at a Zero Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature simplification of a residual-composite model where every modeled residual vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m_f(x)=\tfrac12\|m_F(x)\|_2^2\) with twice-differentiable residual models, if \(m_F(x_*)=0\), then \(\nabla m_f(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla^2m_f(x_*)=J_m(x_*)^TJ_m(x_*)\succeq0\). This Hessian is positive definite if and only if \(J_m(x_*)\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero modeled residual, Gauss–Newton curvature is the exact Hessian and is positive definite exactly under full Jacobian column rank.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the residual-model vector at the zero-residual point.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Gauss–Newton Curvature at a Zero Residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global-optimality certificate for a residual-composite objective model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_f(x)=\tfrac12\|m_F(x)\|_2^2\) on a domain \(D\). If \(x_*\in D\) satisfies \(m_F(x_*)=0\), then \(m_f(x_*)=0\le m_f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\); hence \(x_*\) is a global minimizer. Conversely, \(m_f(x_*)=0\) if and only if every modeled residual vanishes at \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing of every modeled residual certifies global minimality with objective value zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Residual Global-Minimum Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of residual-vector and Jacobian errors to a least-squares objective-model gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=	frac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\) and \(m_f(x)=	frac12\|m_F(x)\|_2^2\). Wherever both residual maps are differentiable, \[
abla m_f(x)-
abla f(x)=J_m(x)^T igl(m_F(x)-F(x) igr)+ igl(J_m(x)-J_F(x) igr)^TF(x).\] Consequently, \[\|
abla m_f(x)-
abla f(x)\|_2\le \|J_m(x)\|_2\|m_F(x)-F(x)\|_2+\|J_m(x)-J_F(x)\|_2\|F(x)\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-value and residual-Jacobian errors jointly control the gradient error of the composed least-squares model.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(m_F\) are differentiable at the point considered.

notation.meaning: Jacobians of the true and modeled residual vectors.

assumptions_latex: The objective has nonlinear least-squares form \(f(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^r F_i(x)^2\).
Local surrogate residuals \(m_i(x)\) are constructed from sampled residual values.
Each \(m_i\) is defined on the model region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual-based objective model is \(m_f(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^r m_i(x)^2\) and is nonnegative.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|F(x)\|_2^2\), construct separate local models \(m_i(x)\) of the residual components \(F_i(x)\). The induced structured model is
\[
m_f(x)=\frac12\|m_F(x)\|_2^2
=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^r m_i(x)^2,
\qquad
m_F=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)^T.
\]
If the residual models interpolate at a sample point, then the composed objective model also interpolates there and remains nonnegative throughout its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model each least-squares residual separately and sum their squared models; this preserves nonnegativity and objective interpolation wherever every residual model interpolates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by an element family that omits a genuine variable interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every element model depends only on a declared variable subset \(E_i\). If variables \(j\) and \(k\) never occur together in any \(E_i\), then every twice-differentiable model \(m(x)=\sum_i m_i(x_{E_i})\) satisfies \(\partial_{jk}^2m(x)=0\). Consequently, the polynomial \(f(x)=x_jx_k\) cannot be represented by that element family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An element pattern that never couples two variables cannot represent their cross interaction; the monomial x_j x_k is a concrete obstruction.
assumptions_latex: Each element depends only on coordinates indexed by \(E_i\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate incidence set of element i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative structure induced by a known partially separable decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q m_i(U_ix)\) and every \(m_i\) is twice differentiable, then \[
abla m(x)=\sum_iU_i^T
abla m_i(U_ix),\qquad 
abla^2m(x)=\sum_iU_i^T
abla^2m_i(U_ix)U_i.\] Hence variables \(j\) and \(k\) can interact in the model Hessian only if some element map \(U_i\) has nonzero dependence on both variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient and Hessian assemble from element derivatives, with possible Hessian interactions limited by the element incidences.
knowledge_statements.title: Elementwise Derivative Assembly

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter count induced by low-dimensional element structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A total-degree-at-most-\(d\) polynomial element in \(n_i\) variables has \(p_i=\binom{n_i+d}{d}\) monomial coefficients. Consequently, an elementwise parameterization has \(\sum_{i=1}^q p_i\) coefficient slots and effective dimension at most this sum after accounting for overlap-induced redundancy, whereas an unrestricted degree-\(d\) polynomial in \(n\) variables has \(\binom{n+d}{d}\) coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partially separable models replace ambient polynomial dimension by a sum of element dimensions, possibly with redundancy from overlapping elements.
assumptions_latex: Each element model has total degree at most \(d\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness boundary for coefficients in an overlapping partially separable polynomial parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each element model be linear in coefficients \(a_i\), and let \(A(a_1,\ldots,a_q)=\sum_{i=1}^q m_i(U_i\cdot;a_i)\) be the induced global polynomial. Element coefficients are identifiable from the global model if and only if \(\ker A=\{0\}\). If \(h\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}\), then \((a_i)\) and \((a_i+h_i)\) define the same global polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping element coefficients are uniquely identifiable exactly when the linear assembly map is injective.
assumptions_latex: Each element model is linear in its coefficient vector.
The element maps and polynomial dictionaries are fixed.

notation.meaning: Linear assembly map from element coefficients to the global polynomial.

Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(U_i x)\) and \(m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q m_i(U_i x)\). Suppose that, for every \(x\in B\), \(|f_i(U_i x)-m_i(U_i x)|\le \kappa_{f,i}\Delta^2\) and \(\|
abla f_i(U_i x)-
abla m_i(U_i x)\|_2\le \kappa_{g,i}\Delta\). Then \[|f(x)-m(x)|\le\Bigl(\sum_i\kappa_{f,i}\Bigr)\Delta^2,\qquad \|
abla f(x)-
abla m(x)\|_2\le\Bigl(\sum_i\|U_i\|_2\kappa_{g,i}\Bigr)\Delta.\]

The stated elementwise bounds hold uniformly on \(B\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines polynomial models assembled from low-dimensional element functions with known variable incidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have the partially separable form \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(U_i x)\), where each \(U_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n}\) selects or linearly combines variables and \(n_i\ll n\). A partially separable polynomial model of degree at most \(d\) is \(m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q m_i(U_i x)\), where every \(m_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to\mathbb{R}\) is a polynomial of degree at most \(d\). Thus model construction and evaluation may be performed elementwise while preserving the incidence structure of \(f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrange-Polynomial Poisedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the classical interpolation definition of bounded Lagrange-polynomial geometry on a region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a polynomial space of dimension \(p\), let \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^p\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\). The set \(Y\) is \(\Lambda\)-poised in \(B\) for \(\mathcal P\) if interpolation on \(Y\) is uniquely solvable and its Lagrange basis \(\{\ell_j\}_{j=1}^p\subset\mathcal P\), defined by \(\ell_j(y^i)=\delta_{ij}\), satisfies \(\max_{1\le j\le p}\sup_{x\in B}|\ell_j(x)|\le\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A determined interpolation set is Lambda-poised when interpolation is unique and every associated Lagrange polynomial is uniformly bounded on the model region.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb R^n\) is the region on which geometry is assessed.

notation.meaning: Lagrange polynomial associated with sample point j.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lebesgue Constant of a Lagrange-Poised Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolation-operator stability implied by bounded cardinal Lagrange polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \((I_Yv)(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p v(y^j)\ell_j(x)\) on \(B\), the operator norm from the maximum norm on sample data to \(L^\infty(B)\) is \(\|I_Y\|=\sup_{x\in B}\sum_{j=1}^p|\ell_j(x)|\). If \(\sup_{x\in B}|\ell_j(x)|\le\Lambda\) for every \(j\), then \(\|I_Y\|\le p\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of the absolute Lagrange polynomials is the interpolation amplification factor, and pointwise Lambda-poisedness bounds it by p Lambda.
assumptions_latex: Interpolation on \(Y\) is uniquely solvable in the p-dimensional polynomial space.
The output norm is uniform on \(B\), and sample data use the maximum norm.

notation.meaning: Polynomial interpolation operator on the sample set.
Lebesgue constant on the model region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of the Lagrange basis for a prescribed interpolation set, including detection of nonpoisedness through a zero pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\ell_i=\bar\phi_i\) for \(i=0,\ldots,p\). For each \(i\), choose \(j_i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\le j\le p}|\ell_i(y^j)|\). If \(\ell_i(y^{j_i})=0\), stop: \(Y\) is not poised. Otherwise exchange \(y^i\) and \(y^{j_i}\), set \(\ell_i\leftarrow\ell_i/\ell_i(y^i)\), and, for every \(j\ne i\), set \(\ell_j\leftarrow\ell_j-\ell_j(y^i)\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a polynomial basis, pivot successively on the remaining sample point where the current polynomial has largest absolute value. A zero pivot detects that the set is not poised; otherwise the algorithm swaps, normalizes, and eliminates to construct the Lagrange basis.
assumptions_latex: \{\bar\phi_0,�ldots,\bar\phi_p\}\text{ is the chosen initial polynomial basis}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Either a zero pivot detects nonpoisedness, or the completed basis satisfies }\ell_j(y^i)=\delta_{ij}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative improvement of an already poised interpolation set until a prescribed Lagrange-polynomial bound is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\Lambda>1\) and begin with a poised interpolation set \(Y\) and its Lagrange polynomials. At iteration \(k\), determine \(\Lambda_{k-1}=\max_{0\le i\le p}\max_{x\in B}|\ell_i(x)|\), exactly or through bounds sufficiently accurate to decide whether \(\Lambda_{k-1}>\Lambda\). If \(\Lambda_{k-1}\le\Lambda\), stop. Otherwise choose \(i_k\) such that \(\max_{x\in B}|\ell_{i_k}(x)|>\Lambda\), choose \(y_*^{i_k}\in B\) by the maximization used in the estimate, replace \(y^{i_k}\) by \(y_*^{i_k}\), update all Lagrange-polynomial coefficients, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate or bound the largest absolute Lagrange-polynomial value over B accurately enough to compare it with Λ. Stop when the value is at most Λ; otherwise replace the point associated with a violating polynomial by a maximizing point in B, update the basis, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: Y\text{ is a poised interpolation set; if necessary it is first generated by Algorithm 6.2}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Completion of a nonpoised set using Lagrange polynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion or repair of an initial sample set inside a region to obtain a full poised interpolation set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\ell_i=\bar\phi_i\), \(i=0,\ldots,p\), and let the initial set contain \(p_{\mathrm{ini}}+1\) points. At stage \(i\), choose \(j_i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i\le j\le p_{\mathrm{ini}}}|\ell_i(y^j)|\). If \(|\ell_i(y^{j_i})|>0\) and \(i\le p_{\mathrm{ini}}\), exchange \(y^i\) and \(y^{j_i}\); otherwise compute or recompute \(y^i\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in B}|\ell_i(x)|\). Then set \(\ell_i\leftarrow\ell_i/\ell_i(y^i)\) and, for every \(j\ne i\), set \(\ell_j\leftarrow\ell_j-\ell_j(y^i)\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each stage, reuse a remaining initial point when it supplies a nonzero pivot. Otherwise choose or replace the point by maximizing the current polynomial over B. Normalize the pivot polynomial and eliminate its value from all other basis polynomials.
assumptions_latex: p_{\mathrm{ini}}+1\text{ initial points are given in }Y
\{\bar\phi_0,�ldots,\bar\phi_p\}\text{ is the chosen initial polynomial basis}
\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in B}|\ell_i(x)|\text{ can be selected whenever a new or replacement point is required}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{On completion, }Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\text{ has a Lagrange basis satisfying }\ell_j(y^i)=\delta_{ij}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolation poisedness characterized by Lagrange-polynomial bounds, bounded representation coefficients, and feature-space volume growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda>0\), let \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\phi=\{\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_p\}\) be a basis of \(\mathcal P_n^d\), and let \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\) be poised, with associated Lagrange polynomials \(\ell_0,\ldots,\ell_p\). Then \(Y\) is \(\Lambda\)-poised in \(B\) in the interpolation sense if and only if any, equivalently all, of the following hold: \(\max_{0\le i\le p}\max_{x\in B}|\ell_i(x)|\le\Lambda\); for every \(x\in B\), there exists \(\lambda(x)\in\mathbb R^{p+1}\) such that \(\sum_{i=0}^p\lambda_i(x)\phi(y^i)=\phi(x)\) and \(\|\lambda(x)\|_\infty\le\Lambda\); replacing any one point of \(Y\) by any \(x\in B\) increases the volume of \(\{\phi(y^0),\ldots,\phi(y^p)\}\) by at most a factor \(\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poised interpolation set is Λ-poised on B exactly when all associated Lagrange polynomials are bounded in magnitude by Λ on B. Equivalently, each feature vector over B has interpolation coefficients bounded by Λ in infinity norm, or any single-point replacement from B increases the feature-space volume by at most Λ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\text{ is }\Lambda\text{-poised in }B\iff\text{the Lagrange-bound, coefficient-bound, and volume-growth conditions hold}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Four elementary properties, with the partition-of-unity clause independent of the poisedness hypotheses used by the first three clauses.

knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Based Poisedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses sample geometry through the spectral conditioning of a scaled polynomial design matrix with full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix integers \(m\ge p\), a polynomial basis \(\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_p)\), a center \(x_c\in\mathbb R^n\), a radius \(\Delta>0\), and samples \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^m\}\subset\mathbb R^n\). Define the scaled design matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) by \(A_{ij}=\phi_j((y^i-x_c)/\Delta)\). For a prescribed \(\kappa\ge1\), the set \(Y\) is condition-poised for this basis and scaling when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=p\) and \(\kappa_2(A):=\|A\|_2\|A^\dagger\|_2=\sigma_{\max}(A)/\sigma_{\min}(A)\le\kappa\). In the square case \(m=p\), this criterion becomes \(A\) nonsingular with \(\kappa_2(A)=\|A\|_2\|A^{-1}\|_2\le\kappa\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scaled sample set is condition-poised when its full-column-rank polynomial design matrix has spectral condition number at most the prescribed bound; for a square matrix, the pseudoinverse reduces to the inverse.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial basis, coordinate scaling, and spectral norm are fixed.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the design matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Regression-Set Poisedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines stable overdetermined polynomial regression through a scaled design matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge p\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) be the scaled design matrix for a fixed polynomial basis, and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) contain sampled values. The regression set is \(\Lambda\)-poised when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=p\) and \(\|A^\dagger\|_2\le\Lambda\), under the chosen row normalization. Then the unique least-squares coefficient vector is \(c=A^\dagger b\), and perturbations satisfy \(\|\delta c\|_2\le\Lambda\|\delta b\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overdetermined sample set is regression-poised when its scaled design matrix has full column rank and a bounded pseudoinverse.
assumptions_latex: The scaling, basis, and row normalization are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c=A^\dagger b\) is unique and \(\|\delta c\|_2\le\Lambda\|\delta b\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of coefficient identifiability when an overdetermined polynomial design lacks full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(m\ge p\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<p\), every least-squares minimizer \(c_0\) generates the family \(c_0+\ker A\); the fitted vector \(Ac\) is unique, but the coefficients are not. Along full-column-rank matrices with \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\downarrow0\), \(\|A^\dagger\|_2=1/\sigma_{\min}(A)\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank loss makes regression coefficients nonidentifiable, while approaching rank loss makes coefficient sensitivity unbounded even though fitted sample values remain unique.
assumptions_latex: Coefficient stability is measured in a fixed scaled basis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines geometric adequacy of an overdetermined polynomial-regression sample set. The region B need not contain the sample set Y.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda>0\), \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\phi=\{\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_q\}\) be a basis of \(\mathcal P_n^d\), \(p>q\), and \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\) be poised. children.title: Underdetermined-Set Poisedness
children.top_down_role: Geometric adequacy of sample sets supporting underdetermined local models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank condition distinguishing sample sets that interpolate every possible data vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) with \(m<p\). The equations \(Ac=b\) are solvable for every \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). Under this condition, every solution set is \(c_0+\ker A\), with \(\dim\ker A=p-m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An underdetermined design fits arbitrary sample values exactly precisely when it has full row rank; its remaining coefficient freedom is the null space.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial basis and scaling defining \(A\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Universal Feasibility of Underdetermined Interpolation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Row Rank Does Not Ensure Uniform Selection Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerating underdetermined sample family with an unbounded minimum-norm right inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the fixed quadratic basis \((1,x,x^2)\), let \(Y_\varepsilon=\{0,\varepsilon\}\) and \[A_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\1&\varepsilon&\varepsilon^2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \varepsilon>0.\] Every \(A_\varepsilon\) has full row rank and therefore interpolates every two-vector of data. However, \(\sigma_{\min}(A_\varepsilon)=\Theta(\varepsilon)\), so \(\|A_\varepsilon^\dagger\|_2=\Theta(\varepsilon^{-1})\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct samples make the underdetermined equations feasible, but coalescing samples make minimum-norm coefficient selection arbitrarily sensitive in the fixed coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The displayed polynomial basis and coordinate scaling remain fixed.
Selection uses the Moore-Penrose right inverse.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Row Rank Does Not Ensure Uniform Selection Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stability certificate for the Euclidean minimum-norm selector in fixed scaled coefficient coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(m<p\), have full row rank. The unique minimum-Euclidean-norm interpolant is \[c_*(b)=A^\dagger b=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}b.\] Its worst-case data amplification is \(\|A^\dagger\|_2=1/\sigma_{\min}(A)\). Thus, in the declared scaled basis, \(\sigma_{\min}(A)\ge\Lambda^{-1}\) is equivalent to \(\|c_*(b+e)-c_*(b)\|_2\le\Lambda\|e\|_2\) for every \(b,e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the minimum-norm selector, stability is equivalent to a lower bound on the smallest nonzero singular value of the scaled design matrix.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial basis, coefficient norm, and trust-region scaling are fixed.

notation.meaning: smallest nonzero singular value of the full-row-rank design matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Norm Underdetermined Stability Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware stability condition for the minimum-Hessian-Frobenius selector rather than the ordinary minimum-coefficient-norm selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In declared scaled polynomial coordinates, partition the interpolation matrix as \(A=[A_L\ A_Q]\), where \(A_L\) contains constant-linear terms and \(W_Q\succ0\) represents the Hessian Frobenius norm on quadratic coefficients. Define \[K=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&A_L^T\\0&W_Q&A_Q^T\\A_L&A_Q&0\end{bmatrix}.\] The sample set is \(\Lambda\)-poised for minimum-Frobenius interpolation when \(K\) is nonsingular and the coefficient solution block \(S\) mapping data \(b\) to \((c_L,c_Q)\) satisfies \(\|S\|_2\le\Lambda\). The selected interpolant then exists uniquely for every \(b\) and obeys \[\|(c_L,c_Q)(b+e)-(c_L,c_Q)(b)\|_2\le\Lambda\|e\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-Frobenius selector stability is certified by a uniformly invertible, correctly weighted saddle-point system in scaled polynomial coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The sample region, polynomial scaling, and coefficient norms are fixed.
Physical derivative rescaling is stated separately from the coefficient-block norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ nonsingular and }\|S\|_2\le\Lambda\Longrightarrow\text{unique stable minimum-Frobenius interpolation}.

notation.meaning: quadratic coefficient weighting representing the Hessian Frobenius norm
data-to-selected-coefficient block of the saddle-point inverse

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Frobenius Saddle-Point Poisedness Certificate
Underdetermined-Set Poisedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines stable underdetermined interpolation relative to a specified model-selection operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m<p\) and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) be a scaled polynomial design matrix. Fix a linear model-selection rule \(R:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^p\). The sample set is \(\Lambda\)-poised for that rule when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\), \(AR=I_m\), and \(\|R\|_2\le\Lambda\). Hence every data vector \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) has the selected interpolating coefficients \(c=Rb\), satisfying \(Ac=b\) and \(\|\delta c\|_2\le\Lambda\|\delta b\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An underdetermined set is poised relative to a chosen right inverse when interpolation is feasible and the selected coefficient map is bounded.
assumptions_latex: The basis, scaling, and selection rule \(R\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c=Rb\) interpolates the data stably, with amplification at most \(\Lambda\).

notation.meaning: Chosen right inverse or model-selection operator.
Stability bound for the selection operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Norm Lagrange Polynomials and Underdetermined Poisedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines minimum-norm Lagrange polynomials for an underdetermined polynomial interpolation system and the associated full-row-rank poisedness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}, with p<q and q+1=\dim\mathcal P_n^d, and let \bar\phi=(\bar\phi_0,\ldots,\bar\phi_q). For j=0,\ldots,p, a polynomial \ell_j(x)=\sum_{k=0}^q(\alpha_j)_k\bar\phi_k(x) is a minimum-norm Lagrange polynomial if \alpha_j is a minimum-norm solution of M(\bar\phi,Y)\alpha_j=e_{j+1}, equivalently \ell_j(y^i)=\delta_{ij}. If M(\bar\phi,Y) has full row rank, these polynomials exist uniquely, and Y is called poised. The polynomials generally depend on the basis, whereas the rank-based poisedness of Y does not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an underdetermined interpolation system, each minimum-norm Lagrange polynomial has minimum-norm coefficients among polynomials equal to one at its associated point and zero at the other sample points. Full row rank of the interpolation matrix guarantees existence and uniqueness and defines poisedness. The polynomials may depend on the basis, but poisedness does not.
assumptions_latex: M(\bar\phi,Y)\text{ has full row rank for the existence-and-uniqueness conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{M(\bar\phi,Y)\alpha=e_{j+1}}\|\alpha\|,\quad \ell_j(y^i)=\delta_{ij};\qquad \operatorname{rank}M(\bar\phi,Y)=p+1\Longrightarrow Y\text{ is poised and each }\ell_j\text{ exists uniquely}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Minimum-Frobenius-Norm Poised-Set Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform iteration bound for constructing poised geometry for minimum-Frobenius-norm models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\Lambda>1\), every closed ball \(B\), and every fixed polynomial basis \(\phi\), Algorithm 6.3 for minimum-Frobenius-norm Lagrange polynomials terminates with a \(\Lambda\)-poised set \(Y\) after at most \(N(\Lambda,\phi)\) iterations, where \(N(\Lambda,\phi)\) is a finite constant depending on \(\Lambda\) and \(\phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any Lambda greater than one, closed ball, and fixed polynomial basis, the minimum-Frobenius-norm Lagrange-polynomial procedure produces a Lambda-poised set within a finite iteration bound depending on Lambda and the basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists N=N(\Lambda,\phi)<\infty\text{ such that Algorithm 6.3 returns a }\Lambda\text{-poised set }Y\text{ in at most }N\text{ iterations.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines quantitative poisedness for underdetermined polynomial interpolation and records the equivalent bounded least-squares and point-replacement characterizations stated by the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \Lambda>0, let B\subset\mathbb R^n, let \bar\phi be the natural monomial basis of \mathcal P_n^d, and let Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\} be poised, with p<q and q+1=\dim\mathcal P_n^d. The set Y is \Lambda\text{-poised in }B in the minimum-norm sense if and only if \[\max_{0\le i\le p}\max_{x\in B}|\ell_i(x)|\le\Lambda.\] Equivalently, for every x\in B there exists \lambda(x)\in\mathbb R^{p+1} giving the stated least-squares representation of \bar\phi(x) from \{\bar\phi(y^i)\}_{i=0}^p and satisfying \|\lambda(x)\|_\infty\le\Lambda. The extract also states the equivalent geometric condition that replacing any one point of Y by any x\in B increases the specified transformed volume by at most a factor \Lambda.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poised underdetermined sample set is Lambda-poised on a region when every associated minimum-norm Lagrange polynomial is uniformly bounded there by Lambda. This is equivalent to bounded least-squares representation coefficients and, as stated in the extract, to a bounded increase in transformed volume after any single-point replacement.
assumptions_latex: \bar\phi\text{ is the natural monomial basis of }\mathcal P_n^d
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Y\text{ is }\Lambda\text{-poised in }B\Longleftrightarrow\max_{0\le i\le p}\max_{x\in B}|\ell_i(x)|\le\Lambda\Longleftrightarrow\forall x\in B\;\exists\lambda(x)\text{ satisfying the stated least-squares relation and }\|\lambda(x)\|_\infty\le\Lambda,\text{ with the stated equivalent point-replacement volume bound}.

children.title: Regularization-Dependent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Interaction between sample geometry plus regularized model selection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness Condition for Quadratically Regularized Fits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compatibility condition between sample geometry and a quadratic penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(L\in\mathbb R^{r\times p}\), and \(\lambda>0\), the objective \(\|Ac-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|Lc\|_2^2\) has a unique minimizer for every \(b\) if and only if \(\ker A\cap\ker L=\{0\}\). Equivalently, \(A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization gives a unique fit exactly when no nonzero coefficient direction is invisible to both the samples and the penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(L\) use the same fixed coefficient coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness Condition for Quadratically Regularized Fits

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ridge Spectral Stability and Bias Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value description of identity regularization's effect on geometry sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=U\Sigma V^\top\) and \(\lambda>0\). The ridge map \(R_\lambda=(A^\top A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^\top\) has singular filter factors \(\sigma_i/(\sigma_i^2+\lambda)\). Hence \(\|R_\lambda\|_2\le1/(2\sqrt\lambda)\); coefficient components in \(\ker A\) are set to zero, and small-singular-value components are attenuated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge regularization caps data sensitivity but shrinks coefficient components, especially in sample-poor directions.
assumptions_latex: The penalty is the identity in the fixed coefficient basis.

notation.meaning: Singular values of the scaled design matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Ridge Spectral Stability and Bias Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable Ridge Fits Can Have Nonvanishing Derivative Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates bounded regularized coefficient sensitivity from DFO approximation accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In one dimension use \(z=x/\Delta\), samples \(x=\pm\Delta\), affine models \(m(x)=c_0+c_1z\), and \(f(x)=x\). Minimize the sum of squared sample residuals plus \(\lambda c_1^2\), where fixed \(\lambda>0\). The selected coefficients are \(c_0=0\) and \(c_1=2\Delta/(2+\lambda)\), so \[m'(x)=\frac{2}{2+\lambda},\qquad |f'(x)-m'(x)|=\frac{\lambda}{2+\lambda}.\] The ridge data map is uniformly bounded, but the derivative error does not vanish as \(\Delta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed ridge penalty can stabilize coefficient recovery while producing persistent derivative bias on shrinking model regions.
assumptions_latex: The slope coefficient is expressed in the scaled coordinate \(z=x/\Delta\).
The sample residual is the unweighted sum over \(x=\pm\Delta\).

notation.meaning: trust-region-scaled coordinate x divided by Delta
fixed ridge penalty on the scaled slope coefficient

knowledge_statements.title: Stable Ridge Fits Can Have Nonvanishing Derivative Bias

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of data amplification, model-class residual, and penalty-induced bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_\lambda=(A^TA+\lambda L^TL)^{-1}A^Tb\), suppose \(b=Ac_*+r+e\), and set \(H_\lambda=A^TA+\lambda L^TL\succ0\). Then \[c_\lambda-c_*=H_\lambda^{-1}A^T(r+e)-\lambda H_\lambda^{-1}L^TLc_*.\] Consequently, \[\|c_\lambda-c_*\|\le\|H_\lambda^{-1}A^T\|(\|r\|+\|e\|)+\lambda\|H_\lambda^{-1}L^T\|\,\|Lc_*\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized coefficient error consists of amplified sampling and approximation errors plus explicit penalty bias.
assumptions_latex: \(b=Ac_*+r+e\), with declared approximation residual \(r\) and data error \(e\).
All norms and coefficient scaling are fixed.

notation.meaning: model-class approximation residual at the samples

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Fit Error Decomposition
Regularization-Dependent Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures geometry through the stability of the regularized fitting operator rather than the design matrix alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), let \(L\in\mathbb R^{r\times p}\), and let \(\lambda>0\). Assume \(A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\) is positive definite. The Tikhonov-selected model is \(c_\lambda=R_\lambda b\), where \(R_\lambda=(A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L)^{-1}A^\top\). For a prescribed \(\Lambda\), the sample geometry is \((L,\lambda,\Lambda)\)-adequate when \(\|R_\lambda\|_2\le\Lambda\); consequently data perturbations obey \(\|\delta c_\lambda\|_2\le\Lambda\|\delta b\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized geometry is adequate when the coefficient map induced by the samples, penalty, and regularization parameter has bounded data sensitivity.
assumptions_latex: \(A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L\) is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Regime Poisedness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unifies determined, regression, underdetermined, and regularized poisedness through stability of the selected fitting map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed scaled design matrix \(A\), let \(S\) denote the data-to-coefficient map specified by the fitting regime: \(S=A^{-1}\) for determined interpolation, \(S=A^\dagger\) for full-column-rank regression, a bounded right inverse for underdetermined interpolation, or \(S=(A^\top A+\lambda L^\top L)^{-1}A^\top\) for Tikhonov fitting. A cross-regime poisedness certificate is the pair of checks that the regime's feasibility or uniqueness rank condition holds and \(\|S\|_2\le\Lambda\). In every regime, \(\|\delta c\|_2\le\Lambda\|\delta b\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across fitting regimes, poisedness consists of the appropriate rank condition plus a bounded data-to-model solution operator.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial basis, scaling, fitting regime, and coefficient norm are fixed.
The displayed solution operator exists for the selected regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|S\|_2\le\Lambda\) yields the common stability bound \(\|\delta c\|_2\le\Lambda\|\delta b\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interpolation-poised subset of a regression-poised set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates regression poisedness of an overdetermined set to interpolation poisedness of a square subset, with an explicit degradation factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\) be \(\Lambda\)-poised in the regression sense for a polynomial basis containing \(q+1\) functions. Then there exists a subset \(Y'\subseteq Y\) of \(q+1\) points that is \((p-q+1)\Lambda\)-poised in the interpolation sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regression-Lambda-poised set of p+1 points contains a square subset of q+1 points that is interpolation-poised with constant (p−q+1)Lambda.

q+1\text{ is the number of polynomial basis functions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists Y'\subseteq Y:\ |Y'|=q+1\ \text{and }Y'\text{ is }(p-q+1)\Lambda\text{-poised in the interpolation sense}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extension of full linearity to larger concentric balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions under which a fully linear derivative-free model on one ball remains fully linear on every admissible larger concentric ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) satisfy Assumption 6.1, and let \(m\) be fully linear on \(B(x;\bar\Delta)\) with respect to \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},v_1^m\), where \(x\in L(x_0)\) and \(\bar\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\). If \(\kappa_{eg}\geq v_1^m+L_{\nabla f}\) and \(\kappa_{ef}\geq\tfrac12\kappa_{eg}\), then for every \(\Delta\in[\bar\Delta,\Delta_{\max}]\), \(m\) is fully linear on \(B(x;\Delta)\) with respect to the same constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},v_1^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let f satisfy Assumption 6.1, and suppose m is fully linear on the ball of radius bar-Delta centered at x, where x belongs to L(x0) and bar-Delta does not exceed Delta-max. If kappa-eg is at least v1-m plus the Lipschitz constant of the gradient of f, and kappa-ef is at least one half of kappa-eg, then m is fully linear with the same constants on every concentric ball with radius between bar-Delta and Delta-max.
assumptions_latex: m\text{ is fully linear on }B(x;\bar\Delta)\text{ with respect to }\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},v_1^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\Delta\in[\bar\Delta,\Delta_{\max}],\quad m\text{ is fully linear on }B(x;\Delta)\text{ with respect to the same }\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},v_1^m.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fully Linear Models and Center-Independent Constants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the pointwise definition to every center and maximum radius and distinguishes center-dependent from center-independent accuracy constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathcal C^1\). Models \(\widetilde f_\Delta\) are fully linear models of \(f\) if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and every \(\bar\Delta>0\), there exists a class \(\{\widetilde f_\Delta\}_{\Delta\in(0,\bar\Delta]}\) of fully linear models of \(f\) at \(x\). They are fully linear with constants \(\kappa_f\) and \(\kappa_g\) if, for every such \(x\) and \(\bar\Delta\), the class can be chosen with the constants in the pointwise definition satisfying \(\kappa_f(x)=\kappa_f\) and \(\kappa_g(x)=\kappa_g\), independently of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Models are fully linear for a continuously differentiable function when a fully linear radius-parameterized class exists at every center and for every positive maximum radius. They have fixed constants when the function-value and gradient accuracy constants can be chosen independently of the center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathbb R^n\;\forall\bar\Delta>0\;\exists\{\widetilde f_\Delta\}_{\Delta\in(0,\bar\Delta]}\text{ fully linear at }x;\quad \text{fixed constants mean }\exists\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\;\forall x:\ \kappa_f(x)=\kappa_f,\ \kappa_g(x)=\kappa_g

u_1^m>0\) such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\), there exists \(m\in\mathcal M\) whose gradient is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant at most \(

abla f(y)-

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Class of Fully Linear Models at a Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic local model-accuracy definition for a radius-parameterized family at a fixed center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathcal C^1\), \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\bar\Delta>0\). A family \(\{\widetilde f_\Delta\}_{\Delta\in(0,\bar\Delta]}\) is a class of fully linear models of \(f\) at \(x\) if there exist \(\kappa_f(x)>0\) and \(\kappa_g(x)>0\) such that, for every \(\Delta\in(0,\bar\Delta]\) and every \(y\in B_\Delta(x)\), \[|f(y)-\widetilde f_\Delta(y)|\le \kappa_f(x)\Delta^2,\qquad \|\nabla f(y)-\widetilde g_\Delta(y)\|\le \kappa_g(x)\Delta,\] where \(\widetilde g_\Delta=\nabla\widetilde f_\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable function and a fixed center, a radius-parameterized model family is fully linear when its function-value error is bounded by a constant times the squared radius and its gradient error is bounded by a constant times the radius throughout each corresponding ball; the constants may depend on the center.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Poised Linear Interpolation Is Fully Linear
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-value component of the fully linear certificate for a determined linear interpolant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(f\in C^{1+}\) on \(B_{\bar\Delta}(x)\) with constant \(K\), and let \(\mathbb Y\) be poised for linear interpolation with \(y^0=x\) and \(\Delta=\overline{\operatorname{diam}}(\mathbb Y)\leq\bar\Delta\). If \(L_Y\) is the linear interpolant of \(f\) over \(\mathbb Y\), then
\[
|f(y)-L_Y(y)|\leq\frac12K\left(1+\sqrt n\,\|\widehat L^{-1}\|\right)\Delta^2
\quad\text{for every }y\in B_\Delta(x).
\]
Together with the corresponding simplex-gradient estimate, this certifies that \(L_Y\) is fully linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poised determined linear interpolant has uniformly quadratic function-value error on the sampling ball; combined with its simplex-gradient estimate, it is fully linear.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb Y\text{ is poised for linear interpolation}
L_Y\text{ is the linear interpolant of }f\text{ over }\mathbb Y

assumptions_latex: \(m\ge n+1\), and the scaled affine design matrix has full column rank and uniformly bounded normalized pseudoinverse.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Poised Linear Regression Model Is Fully Linear
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform function-value and gradient error bounds for regression-based affine models in derivative-free optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f\in\mathcal C^{1+}\) on \(B_{\bar\Delta}(x)\) with constant \(K\), and let \(\mathbb{Y}=\{y^0,\ldots,y^m\}\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), \(m\ge n\), be poised for linear regression, with \(y^0=x\) and \(\Delta=\overline{\operatorname{diam}}(\mathbb{Y})\le\bar\Delta\). Define \(\widehat L=\Delta^{-1}[y^1-y^0\ \cdots\ y^m-y^0]\) and \(\widehat R=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\\mathbf 1&\widehat L^\top\end{bmatrix}\). If \((\alpha_0,\alpha)\) are the linear-regression coefficients, then, for every \(y\in B_\Delta(x)\), \[|f(y)-\alpha_0-\alpha^\top y|\le K\bigl(3+\sqrt m\,\|\widehat R^\dagger\|\bigr)\Delta^2\] and \[\|\nabla f(y)-\alpha\|\le K\left(1+\tfrac12\sqrt m\,\|\widehat R^\dagger\|\right)\Delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If f is C^{1+} on the containing ball and the poised regression sample set contains the ball center, then the fitted affine model has uniformly quadratic function-value error and linear gradient error on the radius-Delta ball. The constants depend on K, the sample count, and the pseudoinverse norm of the scaled regression geometry matrix.
assumptions_latex: (\alpha_0,\alpha)\text{ are the coefficients given by the linear-regression solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall y\in B_\Delta(x):\quad |f(y)-\alpha_0-\alpha^\top y|\le K(3+\sqrt m\|\widehat R^\dagger\|)\Delta^2,\quad \|\nabla f(y)-\alpha\|\le K\left(1+\tfrac12\sqrt m\|\widehat R^\dagger\|\right)\Delta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extension of full quadraticity to larger concentric balls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions under which a fully quadratic derivative-free model on one ball remains fully quadratic on every admissible larger concentric ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) satisfy Assumption 6.2, and let \(m\) be fully quadratic on \(B(x;\bar\Delta)\) with respect to \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},\kappa_{eh},v_2^m\), where \(x\in L(x_0)\) and \(\bar\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Solution Space of Underdetermined Quadratic Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation of all complete quadratic interpolants when value equations do not determine every coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_n\) be the \(q=(n+1)(n+2)/2\)-dimensional space of real polynomials of degree at most two, let \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^{p-1}\}\), and define \(E_Y:\mathcal Q_n\to\mathbb R^p\) by \((E_Ym)_i=m(y^i)\). If \(E_Ym=b\) is consistent, then for any particular solution \(m_0\), \(\{m\in\mathcal Q_n:E_Ym=b\}=m_0+\ker E_Y\). If \(p<q\), then \(\dim\ker E_Y\ge q-p>0\), so the values do not uniquely determine a complete quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistent underdetermined quadratic interpolation gives one interpolant plus every quadratic vanishing on the sample set, and therefore is nonunique.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

abla^2m\|_F\) among quadratic interpolants selects the unique affine interpolant \(m\equiv0\). Nevertheless, \(\|
abla^2f-
abla^2m\|_2=1\) for every \(\Delta>0\), which cannot satisfy a uniform bound \(\kappa_H\Delta\) as \(\Delta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affinely spanning sample set and minimum-Frobenius selection can completely miss mixed curvature, so underdetermined values alone do not ensure a fully quadratic model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Block System for Minimum-Frobenius Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates unpenalized affine coefficients from selected quadratic coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the coefficient vector as \((c_L,c_Q)\), with constant-linear block \(c_L\) and quadratic block \(c_Q\), and partition \(A=[A_L\ A_Q]\). The problem \[\min_{c_L,c_Q}\frac12\|c_Q\|_2^2\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A_Lc_L+A_Qc_Q=b\] has KKT system \[K\begin{bmatrix}c_L\\c_Q\\\mu\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\b\end{bmatrix},\qquad K=\begin{bmatrix}0&0&A_L^T\\0&I&A_Q^T\\A_L&A_Q&0\end{bmatrix}.\] If \(A\) has full row rank and \(A_L\) has full column rank, then \(K\) is nonsingular; in fixed, appropriately scaled coordinates, \(\|K^{-1}\|_2\) bounds data-to-solution sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-Frobenius interpolation is a saddle-point system exposing the affine part, selected curvature, and coefficient sensitivity.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial basis and trust-region scaling are fixed.
After declared basis weighting, \(\|c_Q\|_2\) represents the Hessian Frobenius penalty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Data-Only Universal Fully Quadratic Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic boundary for underdetermined value interpolation over unrestricted smooth objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_\Delta\subset B(x_c,\Delta)\) be affinely spanning and underdetermined for \(\mathcal Q_n\), and choose nonzero \(h_\Delta\in\ker E_{Y_\Delta}\) with \(\|
abla^2h_\Delta\|_2=1\). Any deterministic selector using only the sampled values returns the same model \(m\) for \(f_0\equiv0\) and \(f_1=h_\Delta\). Therefore \[\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\|
abla^2f_i-
abla^2m\|_2\ge	frac12.\] No uniform \(O(\Delta)\) Hessian-error guarantee can hold for all quadratic objectives as \(\Delta\downarrow0\) without prior-curvature or structural information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underdetermined values cannot distinguish quadratic objectives with different curvature, so no data-only selector is universally fully quadratic.

Underdetermined Fully Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic interpolation with fewer equations than coefficients and a stable minimum-curvature selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have an \(L_H\)-Lipschitz Hessian near \(B(x_c,\Delta)\). Let \(Y\subset B(x_c,\Delta)\) contain fewer than \((n+1)(n+2)/2\) points, and choose among interpolating quadratics the model \(m\) minimizing a prescribed Hessian norm, possibly relative to a prior model. If the associated underdetermined interpolation and model-selection operator is uniformly bounded after scaling by \(\Delta\), and its null-space ambiguity yields uniformly bounded second-order error, then \(m\) is fully quadratic: its value, gradient, and Hessian errors are bounded respectively by \(\kappa_f\Delta^3\), \(\kappa_g\Delta^2\), and \(\kappa_H\Delta\) on the ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected underdetermined quadratic is fully quadratic only when both sample geometry and uncontrolled curvature directions satisfy uniform stability bounds.

The unobserved quadratic component has uniformly bounded second-order error.

\(|f-m|\le\kappa_f\Delta^3\), \(\|
abla f-

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Geometry Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts evaluations needed to determine an unrestricted quadratic model in dimension \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The vector space of real polynomials of degree at most two in \(n\) variables has dimension \(q=1+n+n(n+1)/2=(n+1)(n+2)/2\). Consequently, determining an unrestricted quadratic solely by scalar-value interpolation requires at least \(q\) independent sample equations and hence at least \(q\) function evaluations in the deterministic value-oracle model. This requirement is \(\Theta(n^2)\). Using fewer evaluations leaves quadratic coefficients underdetermined unless additional structure, prior information, or a model-selection regularizer is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete quadratic has (n+1)(n+2)/2 coefficients, so determined value interpolation has quadratic evaluation and geometry cost in the dimension.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle call returns one scalar function value.
No sparsity, separability, derivative information, or other coefficient restrictions are assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q=(n+1)(n+2)/2=\Theta(n^2)\) independent evaluations are necessary for determined complete quadratic interpolation.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrange-Based Geometry Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy repair of a polynomial interpolation set inside a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an interpolation set \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^{p}\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), its Lagrange polynomials \(\ell_0,\ldots,\ell_p\), a center \(x\), radius \(\Delta>0\), and threshold \(\Lambda>1\), compute \(M_i=\max_{z\in B(x,\Delta)}|\ell_i(z)|\). If \(\max_i M_i\leq\Lambda\), return \(Y\). Otherwise choose \(i_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i M_i\), select \(z_*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in B(x,\Delta)}|\ell_{i_*}(z)|\), evaluate the objective at \(z_*\), and replace \(y^{i_*}\) by \(z_*\). Recompute the interpolation basis and repeat until the poisedness test holds or a prescribed repair budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly replace the point whose Lagrange polynomial is largest on the trust region by a maximizing point until the interpolation set is sufficiently well poised.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is poised for the chosen polynomial space.
The maxima of \(|\ell_i|\) over \(B(x,\Delta)\) can be computed or adequately approximated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either satisfies \(\max_i\max_{z\in B(x,\Delta)}|\ell_i(z)|\leq\Lambda\) or records exhaustion of the repair budget.

notation.meaning: Lagrange polynomial associated with sample point i

knowledge_statements.title: Pivotal Geometry Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-building procedure for constructing a poised interpolation set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi=\{\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_p\}\) be a basis of a polynomial space and let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a bounded candidate region. Initialize an empty sample set and set \(q_j=\phi_j\). For \(j=0,\ldots,p\), choose a pivot point \(y^j\in C\) satisfying \(|q_j(y^j)|>0\), scale \(q_j\) so that \(q_j(y^j)=1\), and, for every \(k>j\), replace \(q_k\) by \(q_k-q_k(y^j)q_j\). Return \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\); sufficiently large pivots provide quantitative control of the resulting interpolation geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select points as nonzero pivots and eliminate their values from the remaining polynomial basis, producing a poised interpolation set with geometry controlled by pivot size.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) contains a nonzero pivot for every elimination stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interpolation matrix \((\phi_j(y^i))_{i,j=0}^{p}\) is nonsingular, so \(Y\) is poised for \(\operatorname{span}(\Phi)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Set Replacement Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-point replacement balancing interpolation geometry and trust-region locality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a poised set \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\), center \(x\), radius \(\Delta>0\), Lagrange polynomials \(\ell_i\), and an accepted new point \(z\), assign each removable point the score \(s_i=|\ell_i(z)|w(\|y^i-x\|/\Delta)\), where \(w:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\) is nondecreasing. Protect every mandatory point, such as the current center. If an unprotected index with \(\ell_i(z)\neq0\) exists, choose such an index \(i_*\) maximizing \(s_i\) and replace \(y^{i_*}\) by \(z\). Otherwise reject this replacement and invoke a geometry-repair step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace an unprotected point using a score that favors a nonsingular interpolation update and removal of points remote from the current trust region; if no admissible point exists, invoke geometry repair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If an unprotected \(i_*\) with \(\ell_{i_*}(z)\neq0\) is selected, then \((Y\setminus\{y^{i_*}\})\cup\{z\}\) remains poised for the same interpolation space; otherwise no replacement is made.

children.title: Geometry Repair Triggers
children.top_down_role: Geometric conditions that motivate explicit sample-set repair.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Repair Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational conditions requiring repair of a local interpolation set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a poised interpolation set \(Y\) with Lagrange polynomials \(\ell_i\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\), define \(\Lambda(Y;x,\Delta)=\max_i\max_{z\in B(x,\Delta)}|\ell_i(z)|\). Given thresholds \(\Lambda_{\max}>1\), \(\varepsilon_g\geq0\), and \(\kappa_d\geq1\), trigger geometry repair if \(Y\) is not poised; if \(Y\) is poised and \(\Lambda(Y;x,\Delta)>\Lambda_{\max}\); if a trust-region step is unsuccessful and \(\|\nabla m(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_g\); or, when locality enforcement is enabled, if a required sample point \(y\) satisfies \(\|y-x\|>\kappa_d\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trigger repair after loss of poisedness, excessive Lagrange growth, an unsuccessful iteration with a sufficiently small model gradient, or violation of an enabled sample-locality bound.
assumptions_latex: The interpolation model \(m\), sample set, and current trust region are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If any enabled trigger predicate holds, the next geometry-management action is repair or replacement rather than unconditional trust-region contraction.
