knowledge_statements.title: Point-Retention Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention rule trading reusable evaluations against local model geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be the current sample set, and let \(x\) and \(\Delta>0\) define the new trust region. Retaining a previously evaluated point avoids a new objective evaluation, but it supports a local model only while the retained set remains sufficiently poised and spatially relevant to \(B(x,\Delta)\). For a policy with thresholds \(\Lambda_{\max}>1\) and \(\kappa_r\geq1\), maximize reuse subject to \(\Lambda(Y;x,\Delta)\leq\Lambda_{\max}\) and \(\|y-x\|\leq\kappa_r\Delta\) for every retained, nonprotected point \(y\). Points violating an enabled constraint are candidates for replacement even when their objective values remain valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse saves evaluations, but under the stated retention policy, distant or geometrically harmful points are replacement candidates when they prevent a sufficiently well-poised local model around the new center.
assumptions_latex: Objective values at retained points remain valid.
\(\Lambda(Y;x,\Delta)\) denotes the poisedness constant used by the geometry-management procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under this policy, retention is admissible only while the enabled poisedness and locality constraints are satisfied.

children.title: Geometry Repair Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Cases where sample replacement does not recover adequate model geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Repair Failure Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanisms by which sample replacement fails to restore usable interpolation geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Geometry repair can fail if the admissible candidate region is contained in the zero set of every available pivot function, if evaluation constraints forbid all points needed for linear independence, or if finite precision makes the interpolation matrix numerically singular. Concretely, if candidates lie in a proper affine subspace \(H\subset\mathbb R^n\), no set selected from \(H\) can be poised for full linear interpolation in \(\mathbb R^n\). Likewise, replacing \(y^i\) by \(z\) with \(\ell_i(z)=0\) makes the corresponding interpolation update singular rather than repairing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair fails when admissible points cannot span the model space, a zero pivot is accepted, or numerical conditioning destroys the effective independence of samples.
assumptions_latex: The intended model space contains all affine functions on \(\mathbb R^n\).
Candidate points are restricted to a set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(C\subset H\) for a proper affine subspace \(H\), full-dimensional linear poisedness cannot be restored using points from \(C\).

The coefficient pair with zero radial coefficients and tail \(p\) is then a nonzero null vector of the homogeneous augmented interpolation system, regardless of the radial matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local RBF Interpolation with a Polynomial Tail
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolatory radial-basis surrogate constructed on a local DFO sample set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For distinct sites \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^m\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), let
\[
m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\phi(\|x-y^i\|)+p(x),\qquad p\in\Pi.
\]
Interpolation and polynomial side conditions are
\[
m(y^j)=f(y^j)\quad(j=1,\ldots,m),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_iq(y^i)=0\quad(q\in\Pi).
\]
In matrix form the coefficients solve \(\begin{bmatrix}\Phi&P\\P^T&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\lambda\\c\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}f\\0\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local RBF model combines radial translates at sample sites with a polynomial tail, with interpolation and polynomial orthogonality enforced by one augmented linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is a finite-dimensional polynomial tail space.
The augmented system is formed using a fixed basis of \(\Pi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonsingularity of the augmented matrix yields a unique interpolating coefficient pair \((\lambda,p)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local RBF Interpolation with a Polynomial Tail

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsingularity of Conditionally Positive-Definite RBF Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard existence-and-uniqueness condition for an RBF interpolant with the required polynomial tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi\) be strictly conditionally positive definite of order \(d\), let \(\Pi_{d-1}\) be the polynomials of degree at most \(d-1\), and let the distinct sites be \(\Pi_{d-1}\)-unisolvent. Then the augmented matrix
\[
\begin{bmatrix}\Phi&P\\P^T&0\end{bmatrix}
\]
is nonsingular. Consequently every sample-value vector determines unique coefficients satisfying interpolation and \(P^T\lambda=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly conditionally positive-definite radial kernel and a polynomial-unisolvent site set give a unique RBF interpolant.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is strictly conditionally positive definite of order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented RBF-polynomial interpolation matrix is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: polynomial tail space associated with the kernel order

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity of Conditionally Positive-Definite RBF Interpolation
Radial-Basis Local Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolatory radial-basis surrogate augmented by a polynomial tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct sites \(Y=\{y^1,ldots,y^m\}subset\mathbb R^n\), a radial-basis local model has the form \[m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_iphi(\|x-y^i\|)+p(x),\] where \(\phi:[0,infty)\to\mathbb R\) is a radial kernel and \(p\) belongs to a finite-dimensional polynomial space \(\Pi\). Interpolation imposes \(m(y^j)=f(y^j)\) for every \(j\), together with side conditions \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}\lambda_i q(y^i)=0\) for every \(q\in\Pi\). When the associated augmented interpolation matrix is nonsingular, these equations uniquely determine \(\lambda\) and \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An RBF local model combines radial translates centered at sampled points with a polynomial tail, with interpolation and side conditions determining its coefficients.
assumptions_latex: The augmented kernel-polynomial interpolation matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique model \(m\) satisfying the interpolation equations and polynomial side conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise native-space accuracy certificate for a local kernel interpolant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the kernel-interpolation assumptions, define \(P_Y(x)^2=K(x,x)-k_Y(x)^\top G^{-1}k_Y(x)\). Then \(P_Y(x)\ge0\), and every \(f\in\mathcal H_K\) satisfies \(|f(x)-s_Y(x)|\le P_Y(x)\|f\|_{\mathcal H_K}\). Thus \(\sup_{x\in B}P_Y(x)\) certifies uniform interpolation error on \(B\) for functions with bounded native-space norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The kernel power function is a computable geometry-dependent multiplier bounding pointwise and uniform RKHS interpolation error.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is strictly positive definite on the distinct sample sites.

notation.meaning: Kernel power function of the local sample set.
Region on which local model accuracy is assessed.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Power-Function Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unregularized local kernel interpolant and its minimum-native-norm characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be strictly positive definite and let \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^m\}\) contain distinct sites. With \(G_{ij}=K(y^i,y^j)\), one has \(G\succ0\), and every data vector \(f\) determines the unique interpolant \(s_Y(x)=k_Y(x)^\top G^{-1}f\) in \(\operatorname{span}\{K(\cdot,y^i)\}\). It is also the unique minimum-\(\mathcal H_K\)-norm function among all \(g\in\mathcal H_K\) satisfying \(g(y^i)=f_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct sites under a strictly positive-definite kernel determine a unique finite kernel interpolant, which is the least-native-norm function fitting the data.
assumptions_latex: Point evaluation is taken in \(\mathcal H_K\).

notation.meaning: Kernel Gram matrix on the local sample set.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Positive-Definite Kernel Interpolation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility and Uniqueness for Singular Kernel Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility and coefficient-uniqueness boundary for unregularized kernel interpolation with a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\succeq0\) be the Gram matrix of a positive-semidefinite kernel on sites \(Y\), and seek \(s(x)=k_Y(x)^\top\alpha\) satisfying \(G\alpha=f\). An interpolant exists if and only if \(f\in\operatorname{range}(G)\), equivalently \(z^\top f=0\) for every \(z\in\ker G\). When feasible, the coefficient vector is unique exactly when \(G\) is nonsingular. If \(G\) is singular, all solutions are \(G^\dagger f+z\), \(z\in\ker G\), and they represent the same RKHS function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular kernel system interpolates exactly only when the data lie in the Gram-matrix range; feasible coefficients are nonunique, but all represent the same RKHS function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\alpha=f\text{ is solvable}\iff f\in\operatorname{range}(G),\qquad \alpha=G^\dagger f+z,\ z\in\ker G.

notation.meaning: Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of the Gram matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility and Uniqueness for Singular Kernel Interpolation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit inconsistent data for a singular positive-semidefinite kernel Gram system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take distinct sites \(y^1,y^2\), the positive-semidefinite kernel \(K(x,y)=1\), and data \(f=(0,1)^\top\). Then \(G=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), whose range is \(\operatorname{span}\{(1,1)^\top\}\). Hence \(G\alpha=f\) is inconsistent, and no model in \(\operatorname{span}\{K(\cdot,y^1),K(\cdot,y^2)\}\) interpolates both observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant kernel cannot interpolate two unequal observations, so positive semidefiniteness alone does not ensure interpolation feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Kernel Interpolation Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noninterpolatory local kernel regression with positive locality weights and RKHS norm regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel with RKHS \(\mathcal H_K\), let \(y^1,\ldots,y^m\) be sample sites, let \(w_i>0\), and let \(\lambda>0\). The problem \[\min_{g\in\mathcal H_K}\ \sum_{i=1}^m w_i\bigl(g(y^i)-f_i\bigr)^2+\lambda\|g\|_{\mathcal H_K}^2\] has a unique minimizer. It lies in \(\operatorname{span}\{K(\cdot,y^i)\}_{i=1}^m\), so \(m(x)=k_Y(x)^T\alpha\). With \(G_{ij}=K(y^i,y^j)\) and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_i)\), the canonical coefficient vector is the unique solution of \[(WG+\lambda I)\alpha=Wf.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted regularized kernel local model is the unique RKHS fit balancing local weighted residuals and native-space norm, and it is constructed from a finite regularized Gram system.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is positive semidefinite and defines the RKHS \(\mathcal H_K\).

notation.meaning: diagonal matrix of positive locality weights
kernel Gram matrix on the local sample sites

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Regularized RKHS Local Fit
Kernel Local Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized local regression in a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel on a domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), with reproducing-kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_K\). Given weighted observations \((y^i,f_i,w_i)\) and \(\lambda>0\), define the local model as a minimizer of \[\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\bigl(g(y^i)-f_i\bigr)^2+\lambda\|g\|_{\mathcal H_K}^2.\] The representer theorem yields a minimizer of the form \(m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_iK(x,y^i)\). With \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_i)\) and Gram matrix \(G_{ij}=K(y^i,y^j)\), its coefficients satisfy \((WG+\lambda I)\alpha=Wf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kernel local model is a weighted, regularized RKHS fit whose optimizer is a finite kernel expansion over the sampled points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizing local model admits the finite representation \(m=\sum_i\alpha_iK(\cdot,y^i)\).

notation.meaning: kernel Gram matrix on the sample sites

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The RKHS representation and regularized weighted fit are plausible and the representation kind fits the leaf, but the record has no citation or locator supporting the precise objective, coefficient system, or local weighting specialization.

children.title: Support-Vector Local Models
children.top_down_role: Local surrogate representations based on support-vector constructions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal construction of an epsilon-insensitive kernel surrogate from a local sample set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given local samples \((y^i,f_i)\), a positive-semidefinite kernel \(K\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and \(C>0\), solve
\[
\min_{g\in\mathcal H_K,\,b\in\mathbb R,\,\xi,\xi^*\ge0}
\frac12\|g\|_{\mathcal H_K}^2+C\sum_i(\xi_i+\xi_i^*)
\]
subject to \(f_i-g(y^i)-b\le\varepsilon+\xi_i\) and \(g(y^i)+b-f_i\le\varepsilon+\xi_i^*\). A fitted model has the form \(m(x)=\sum_i(\alpha_i-\alpha_i^*)K(x,y^i)+b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a local kernel surrogate using epsilon-insensitive loss and RKHS regularization; nonzero dual-coefficient differences determine its support vectors.
assumptions_latex: Prediction is restricted to the declared local model region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fitted surrogate admits a finite expansion over samples with \(\alpha_i-\alpha_i^*\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local Epsilon-Insensitive Support-Vector Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT classification of samples relative to the epsilon-insensitive tube.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-dual optimum, \(|f_i-m(y^i)|<\varepsilon\) implies \(\alpha_i=\alpha_i^*=0\). If \(0<\alpha_i<C\), then \(f_i-m(y^i)=\varepsilon\); if \(0<\alpha_i^*<C\), then \(m(y^i)-f_i=\varepsilon\). A multiplier at \(C\) may correspond to positive slack outside the tube.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly in-tube samples have zero multipliers, free multipliers lie on a tube boundary, and saturated multipliers may identify tube violations.
assumptions_latex: A primal-dual optimum of the stated local epsilon-SVR problem is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual-multiplier status certifies each sample's KKT position relative to the insensitive tube.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Vector Tube Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Form of Local Epsilon-Support-Vector Regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample dual of the local epsilon-insensitive SVR problem with an unregularized intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With Gram matrix \(K\), the dual is
\[
\max_{0\le\alpha,\alpha^*\le C}
-\frac12(\alpha-\alpha^*)^TK(\alpha-\alpha^*)
-\varepsilon\mathbf1^T(\alpha+\alpha^*)
+f^T(\alpha-\alpha^*)
\]
subject to \(\mathbf1^T(\alpha-\alpha^*)=0\). The recovered model is \(m(x)=\sum_i(\alpha_i-\alpha_i^*)K(x,y^i)+b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local epsilon-SVR has a box-constrained quadratic dual with one balance equality, and its coefficient differences produce the finite kernel expansion.
assumptions_latex: The primal contains an unregularized intercept \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal and dual optimal values agree, and nonzero coefficient differences identify the represented support vectors.

notation.meaning: multipliers for the two tube constraints

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Form of Local Epsilon-Support-Vector Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of support-vector coefficient identifiability for duplicate observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two samples have identical kernel rows and the same response value, the dual objective depends on their multipliers only through the corresponding aggregate coefficients. Whenever an optimal aggregate multiplier can be split between the duplicate indices without meeting a box boundary, a continuum of such splits is dual-optimal. The represented function is unchanged although the individual support-vector multipliers are not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate observations can produce nonunique optimal SVR multipliers even when every optimal split represents the same fitted function.
assumptions_latex: Two samples have identical kernel rows and equal response values.
An optimal aggregate multiplier admits more than one feasible split within \([0,C]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual coefficient vector and index-level support assignment need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Sample Dual Nonuniqueness
Support-Vector Local Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local epsilon-insensitive support-vector regression surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given local samples \((y^i,f_i)\), kernel \(K\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and penalty \(C>0\), solve \[\min_{g\in\mathcal H_K,\,b\in\mathbb R,\,\xi,\xi^*\geq0}\frac12\|g\|_{mathcal H_K}^2+C\sum_i(\xi_i+\xi_i^*)\] subject to \(f_i-g(y^i)-b\leq\varepsilon+xi_i\) and \(g(y^i)+b-f_i\leq\varepsilon+xi_i^*\). The resulting local model is \(m(x)=\sum_i(\alpha_i-alpha_i^*)K(x,y^i)+b\); samples with \(\alpha_i-alpha_i^*\neq0\) are its support vectors. Output this model for prediction within the prescribed neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit epsilon-insensitive kernel regression locally; only samples with nonzero dual-coefficient differences appear as support vectors in the resulting surrogate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fitted model is a finite kernel expansion supported on samples with \(\alpha_i-alpha_i^*\neq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for the local SVR fitting procedure, but no authoritative source or locator is supplied. Several intended commands in the RKHS norm, slack variables, and dual coefficients are also corrupted, so a source-backed repair is needed.

children.title: Kernel Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Modeling regimes distinguished by kernel family or locality characteristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel choice by smoothness, scale, and conditioning requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a local model on a scaled trust region, choose a kernel family and its parameters before fitting. A finite-smoothness kernel is appropriate when limited regularity is expected; a highly smooth kernel is appropriate only when comparable target smoothness is credible. Select the length scale \(h>0\) relative to the sample diameter, for example by using \(K_h(x,z)=K((x-z)/h)\), and require the regularized Gram matrix to meet a prescribed conditioning bound. Among candidates satisfying that bound, select parameters by a declared local validation criterion, such as weighted leave-one-out error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose kernel smoothness to match expected regularity, scale it to the local sample cloud, and tune only among candidates whose Gram matrices remain acceptably conditioned.
assumptions_latex: Local validation uses only available sampled values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected kernel minimizes the declared validation score subject to the prescribed conditioning constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the selection-regime leaf, but the smoothness-matching, conditioning constraint, and weighted leave-one-out selection rule form a method-dependent policy with no cited source or locator.

children.title: Sparsity-Controlled Local Fits
children.top_down_role: Local fits whose complexity is governed through sparse support representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct sparsity control for a finite local kernel dictionary through coefficient regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given local samples \((y^i,f_i,w_i)_{i=1}^m\), define \(K_{ij}=K(y^i,y^j)\) and compute
\[
\widehat\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^m}
\frac12\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\bigl((K\alpha)_i-f_i\bigr)^2
+\lambda\|\alpha\|_1+\frac\mu2\|\alpha\|_2^2,
\]
where \(w_i>0\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\mu\ge0\). The resulting local model is \(m(x)=\sum_{j:\widehat\alpha_j\ne0}\widehat\alpha_jK(x,y^j)\). If \(K^TWK+\mu I\succ0\), the coefficient minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a finite local kernel expansion using an l1 coefficient penalty, optionally stabilized by an l2 penalty; only nonzero fitted coefficients remain in the active dictionary.
assumptions_latex: The finite weighted least-squares objective is used with the declared kernel dictionary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned model is supported exactly on \(\{y^j:\widehat\alpha_j\ne0\}\), with a unique coefficient vector when \(K^TWK+\mu I\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Net Sparse Local Kernel Fit

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coefficientwise Optimality Certificate for Sparse Kernel Fits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient KKT certificate for the elastic-net sparse kernel fit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L(\alpha)=\tfrac12\|W^{1/2}(K\alpha-f)\|_2^2\). A vector \(\widehat\alpha\) minimizes \(L(\alpha)+\lambda\|\alpha\|_1+\tfrac\mu2\|\alpha\|_2^2\) if and only if, for every \(j\),
\[
\widehat\alpha_j\ne0\Rightarrow [\nabla L(\widehat\alpha)]_j+\mu\widehat\alpha_j=-\lambda\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\alpha_j),
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_j=0\Rightarrow |[\nabla L(\widehat\alpha)]_j|\le\lambda.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active coefficients satisfy signed stationarity, while inactive coefficients have loss-gradient magnitude no greater than the l1 threshold.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is the stated convex weighted least-squares loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinate conditions are necessary and sufficient for global optimality.

notation.meaning: gradient of the smooth weighted loss

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficientwise Optimality Certificate for Sparse Kernel Fits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient and support nonuniqueness without strongly convex stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mu=0\) and two columns of \(W^{1/2}K\) are identical. If an optimum assigns a positive total coefficient \(s\) to those columns, every split \((\alpha_j,\alpha_k)=(t,s-t)\), \(0\le t\le s\), has identical fitted values and the same \(\ell_1\) penalty. Hence the fitted function may be unique while its coefficient vector and active support are not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate kernel atoms can admit many equally optimal coefficient splits, so an l1 penalty alone need not identify a unique support.
assumptions_latex: Two weighted kernel-design columns are identical.
An optimum uses a positive total coefficient on the duplicate columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal coefficient vector and its support need not be unique.

notation.meaning: optimal total coefficient on the duplicate atoms
arbitrary split of the total coefficient

Sparsity-Controlled Local Fits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse kernel fitting through an explicit coefficient penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given local samples \((y^i,f_i,w_i)\), kernel dictionary functions \(K(\cdot,y^j)\), and parameters \(\lambda>0\) and \(\mu\geq0\), compute \[\widehat{alpha}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{alpha\in\mathbb R^m}\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m}alpha_jK(y^i,y^j)-f_i\right)^2+lambda\|\alpha\|_1+frac{mu}{2}\|\alpha\|_2^2.\] Return \(m(x)=\sum_{j:widehat{alpha}_j\neq0}widehat{alpha}_jK(x,y^j)\). The parameter \(\lambda\) controls dictionary sparsity, while \(\mu>0\) supplies strong convexity when uniqueness is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a local kernel expansion with an l1 coefficient penalty, retaining only centers with nonzero fitted coefficients; optional l2 regularization stabilizes the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned model uses exactly the active dictionary \(\{K(\cdot,y^j):widehat{alpha}_j\neq0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nelder-Mead reflection-expansion-contraction iteration without shrink
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{x(i)\}_{i=1}^{N+1}\) be ordered so that \(f(x_{\min})\le f(x_{sl})\le f(x_{\max})\). Define \(x_c=N^{-1}(-x_{\max}+\sum_{i=1}^{N+1}x(i))\) and \(x_r=2x_c-x_{\max}\). If \(f(x_r)<f(x_{\min})\), form \(x_{\exp}=2x_r-x_c\) and choose the better of \(x_{\exp}\) and \(x_r\). If \(f(x_{\min})\le f(x_r)<f(x_{sl})\), accept \(x_r\). If \(f(x_{sl})\le f(x_r)<f(x_{\max})\), accept \(\tfrac12(x_r+x_c)\); otherwise accept \(\tfrac12(x_{\max}+x_c)\). Replace \(x_{\max}\) by the accepted point and repeat until the iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This Nelder-Mead variant orders the simplex, reflects its worst point, and then uses expansion, direct acceptance, outside contraction, or inside contraction according to the sampled objective values. It has neither a shrink step nor a feasibility-repair rule.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P=\{x(i)\}_{i=1}^{N+1}\text{ initially consists of feasible, evaluable points}
f\text{ is minimized and is evaluable at every reflected, expanded, and contracted trial point}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\max}\leftarrow x_{\mathrm{new}}\quad\text{and the iteration repeats until its prescribed limit.}

conclusion.conclusion_latex: x_{\max}\leftarrow x_{\mathrm{new}}\quad\text{and the iteration repeats until its prescribed limit.}

knowledge_statements.title: Directional direct-search success, failure, and polling-evaluation rules
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional direct-search success, failure, and polling-evaluation rules
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\), \(\alpha_0>0\), \(0<\beta_1\le\beta_2<1\), \(\gamma\ge1\), and a collection \(\mathcal D\) of positive bases. At iteration \(k\), conduct a finite optional search for strict decrease. If it fails, choose \(D_k\in\mathcal D\) and poll \(P_k=\{x_k+\alpha_kd:d\in D_k\}\) until a strictly improving point is found. On success, set \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\) and choose \(\alpha_{k+1}\in[\alpha_k,\gamma\alpha_k]\). On failure, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and choose \(\alpha_{k+1}\in[\beta_1\alpha_k,\beta_2\alpha_k]\). The poll uses at most \(|D_k|\) evaluations and exactly \(|D_k|\) on failure, where \(|D_k|\ge n+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directional direct-search iteration first permits a finite search and then polls a positive basis if needed. Successful iterations strictly decrease the objective and maintain or enlarge the step size; unsuccessful iterations retain the iterate and reduce the step size. Polling has the stated per-iteration evaluation bound.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D\text{ is a collection of positive bases}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{cases}f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k),\ \alpha_{k+1}\in[\alpha_k,\gamma\alpha_k],&\text{on success},\\x_{k+1}=x_k,\ \alpha_{k+1}\in[\beta_1\alpha_k,\beta_2\alpha_k],&\text{on failure},\end{cases}\qquad N_k^{\mathrm{poll}}\le|D_k|,\quad N_k^{\mathrm{poll}}=|D_k|\text{ on failure}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact cyclic coordinate minimization monotonicity and local-optimality failure
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(x^{(1)}\in\mathbb R^n\), cyclic coordinate search exactly minimizes \(f\) with respect to one coordinate at a time while retaining the latest values of all other coordinates and visiting \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) in a fixed recurring order. Every coordinate update satisfies \(f(x^{(k+1)})\le f(x^{(k)})\). Insignificant improvement over a complete cycle may be used as a stopping indication, but cyclewise stagnation does not guarantee that the method has found even a local minimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For unconstrained minimization of \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), maintain simplex vertices \(x^0,\ldots,x^n\) and select worst and best vertices \(x^h\) and \(x^l\). knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic opportunistic or complete polling along signed coordinate directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), step size \(\alpha_0>0\), forcing function \(\rho:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\), contraction factor \(\theta\in(0,1)\), and expansion bound \(\gamma\geq1\), iteration \(k\) evaluates trial points \(x_k+\alpha_k d\) for directions \(d\in D=\{\pm e_1,\ldots,\pm e_n\}\), either until success or through the complete set. If some trial satisfies \(f(x_k+\alpha_k d)\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\alpha_k)\), accept such a point as \(x_{k+1}\) and choose \(\alpha_{k+1}\in[\alpha_k,\gamma\alpha_k]\). Otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(\alpha_{k+1}=\theta\alpha_k\). Stop when the evaluation budget is exhausted or \(\alpha_k\) falls below a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poll along positive and negative coordinate axes, opportunistically or completely; accept sufficient decrease and possibly enlarge the step, otherwise retain the iterate and contract the step.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) can be evaluated at the trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration returns either an accepted coordinate step or, after an unsuccessful poll, the unchanged iterate with contracted step size.

An opportunistic successful poll evaluates between one and \(2n\) points, while an unsuccessful poll evaluates exactly \(2n\), provided all trial points are distinct and uncached.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x_1,x_2)=\max\{x_1,x_2\}\) and \(x=(0,0)\). For every \(\alpha>0\) and \(d\in\{\pm e_1,\pm e_2\}\), \[f(x+\alpha d)\geq f(x)=0.\] Thus every strict-decrease coordinate poll fails. Nevertheless, \[f^{\circ}(x;(-1,-1))=-1<0,\qquad 0\notin\partial^{\circ}f(x),\] so \(x\) is not Clarke stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the origin, the maximum of two coordinates has no improving signed-coordinate step but decreases along the negative diagonal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical derivative-free coordinate search using positive and negative coordinate directions, strict-decrease acceptance, and step halving after an unsuccessful poll. With zero stopping tolerance, the stated stopping test does not terminate in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\delta^0>0\), and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\ge 0\), define \(P^k=\{x^k\pm\delta^k e_i:i=1,\ldots,n\}\). If some \(t\in P^k\) satisfies \(f(t)<f(x^k)\), set \(x^{k+1}=t\) and \(\delta^{k+1}=\delta^k\). Otherwise set \(x^{k+1}=x^k\) and \(\delta^{k+1}=\delta^k/2\). Increment \(k\) and repeat exactly when \(\delta^{k+1}\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\); otherwise stop. In particular, when \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}=0\), the stopping inequality is never violated in exact arithmetic because every \(\delta^k\) remains positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poll the points obtained by adding or subtracting the current positive step along each coordinate. Accept any poll point that strictly decreases the objective and retain the step; if none does, retain the current point and halve the step. Repeat when the updated step is at least the stopping tolerance, and otherwise stop. A zero tolerance yields no termination through this test in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^k=\{x^k\pm\delta^k e_i:i=1,\ldots,n\};\quad \bigl(\exists t\in P^k:f(t)<f(x^k)\bigr)\Rightarrow(x^{k+1},\delta^{k+1})=(t,\delta^k),\quad\text{otherwise }(x^{k+1},\delta^{k+1})=(x^k,\delta^k/2),\quad\text{and continuation occurs iff }\delta^{k+1}\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Coordinate Minimization and Its Convergence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic derivative-free search using successive one-dimensional minimizations along coordinate directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an objective $F$ in $n$ variables, cyclic coordinate minimization searches successively for a minimum along each coordinate direction $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. A complete cycle adjusts all $n$ variables, and cycles are repeated. The one-dimensional minimizations may use derivative-free searches. Without additional assumptions, the procedure is not guaranteed to converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cyclic coordinate minimization successively minimizes the objective along every coordinate direction. Each cycle adjusts all variables, and the scalar searches can be derivative-free. In general, however, the procedure has no unconditional convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is an objective in }n\text{ variables}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{One cycle adjusts all }n\text{ coordinates, but convergence is not guaranteed in general.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Coordinate Search and Its Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic exact coordinate minimization, its monotonicity, practical stopping indication, and lack of a local-optimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from $x^{(1)}\in\mathbb{R}^n$, cyclic coordinate search successively minimizes $f$ with respect to one coordinate while holding the other coordinates at their latest values, visiting coordinates in a fixed recurring order. Equivalently, it performs successive line searches along the standard basis directions $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. Each exact coordinate minimization cannot increase the objective. Insignificant improvement after a complete cycle may be used as a convergence indication, but the method can fail to find even a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an initial point, cyclic coordinate search successively minimizes the objective over one coordinate at a time, retaining the latest values of all other coordinates and visiting coordinates in fixed cyclic order. This is equivalent to line searches along the standard basis directions. Each exact coordinate minimization leaves the objective unchanged or decreases it. Little improvement over a full cycle may indicate convergence, but the method can still fail to find a local minimum.
assumptions_latex: \text{Each coordinate subproblem attains a minimizer selected by the method.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x^{(k+1)})\le f(x^{(k)})\ \text{after every coordinate update, while cyclewise stagnation does not imply local minimality.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic coordinate search and its stationarity failure boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cyclic coordinate search and records why exact coordinate line searches alone do not ensure approach to stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Cyclic coordinate search successively searches along the coordinate directions $e_1,\ldots,e_n$, changing only the selected component and repeating the cycle after all coordinates have been visited. In general, even exact line searches do not guarantee that the generated iterates approach a stationary point. More generally, cyclic line search along a fixed linearly independent direction set has no unconditional global-convergence guarantee. With
\[
\cos\theta_k=\frac{-\nabla f(x_k)^Tp_k}{\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\,\|p_k\|},
\]
the failure may occur because $\cos\theta_k\to0$ sufficiently rapidly while $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\not\to0$; consequently, satisfaction of the Zoutendijk summability condition need not force vanishing gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cyclic coordinate search changes one variable at a time by searching along successive coordinate directions, then repeats the cycle. Even exact coordinate line searches do not generally ensure that the iterates approach a stationary point, and cyclic search along an arbitrary fixed linearly independent direction set likewise has no unconditional global-convergence guarantee. The obstruction is that the selected direction can become nearly perpendicular to the negative gradient, allowing the angle factor to approach zero while the gradient norm remains bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is differentiable at the iterates whenever gradients and stationarity are invoked}
p_k\text{ is selected cyclically from the coordinate directions, with a minimizing or objective-reducing line search along the selected coordinate}

ot	o0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement; several displayed formulas are unavailable because they were represented as images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a real-valued function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, an initial base point, and positive coordinate step lengths $d_j$, perform exploratory moves successively along the coordinate axes and retain improving trial points. After a successful exploratory sweep, make a pattern move in the direction determined by successive base points and restart exploration. When the attempted progress fails, return to the relevant base point and reduce the step lengths before repeating the exploration. Stop when the coordinate step lengths are below their predetermined tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hooke–Jeeves pattern search performs coordinate-wise exploratory moves and retains improvements. Successful exploration is followed by a pattern move based on successive base points. Failed progress leads back to a base point and to smaller coordinate step lengths. The stopping rule is reached when the step lengths fall below predetermined tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Stop when every coordinate step length }d_j\text{ is below its predetermined tolerance.}

knowledge_statements.title: Generating-Set Search Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained generating-set search in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generating-set search family is a directional direct-search method in which the poll set at iteration \(k\) has the form \(P_k=\{x_k+\alpha_k d:d\in D_k\}\), where \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is finite and positively spans the space: \(\operatorname{cone}(D_k)=\mathbb{R}^n\). The method may test the points of \(P_k\) opportunistically and stop when a point satisfies its decrease test. If no tested point succeeds, it may declare the poll unsuccessful only after all required points of \(P_k\) have been tested, after which it reduces \(\alpha_k\). The cardinality, ordering, and geometry of \(D_k\) may vary with \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generating-set search polls along a finite positive-spanning set. It may stop early after finding adequate improvement, but it declares failure and reduces its step size only after testing every required poll point.
assumptions_latex: At each iteration \(k\), an incumbent \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a finite positive-spanning set \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and a step size \(\alpha_k>0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Testing the required steps generated by a positive-spanning set defines a directional direct-search family without derivative evaluations.

children.title: Constraint-Compatible Generators
children.top_down_role: Generating sets adapted to local feasibility or constraint geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral specialization giving finite tangent-cone generators and sufficiently-small-step feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\), \(x\in\Omega\), and \(I(x)=\{i:a_i^Tx=b_i\}\). Then \[T_\Omega(x)=\{d:a_i^Td\leq0\ \forall i\in I(x)\}\] is a polyhedral cone and admits a finite set \(D\) satisfying \(\operatorname{cone}(D)=T_\Omega(x)\). The set may contain generators of the extreme rays and both signs of a basis for the lineality space. Moreover, for every finite \(D\subseteq T_\Omega(x)\), some \(\bar\alpha>0\) satisfies \[x+\alpha d\in\Omega\qquad\forall d\in D,\quad0\leq\alpha\leq\bar\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a point of a polyhedron, the tangent cone is finitely generated, and any finite set of its directions produces feasible trials for all sufficiently small step sizes.
assumptions_latex: The set used in the feasibility assertion is finite and contained in \(T_\Omega(x)\).

notation.meaning: Indices of constraints active at x.
Bouligand tangent cone of the polyhedron at x.
Nonnegative hull of the finite generator set.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Polyhedral Tangent-Cone Generator Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite feasible generator construction for linear inequalities near an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Omega=\{x:Ax\le b\}\), \(x_k\in\Omega\), and \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), define \(I_k=\{i:b_i-a_i^Tx_k\le\varepsilon_k\}\) and \(K_k=\{d:a_i^Td\le0\ \forall i\in I_k\}\). Choose finite \(D_k\) with \(\operatorname{cone}(D_k)=K_k\), including both signs of a basis for its lineality space. If the poll radius obeys \[\alpha_k\max_{i,d\in D_k}(a_i^Td)_+\le\varepsilon_k,\] then every trial \(x_k+\alpha_kd\), \(d\in D_k\), is feasible. Otherwise trials must be screened before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate the cone restricted by active and nearby faces; a quantitative slack test certifies feasibility of all resulting poll points.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Active Polyhedral Generator Rule

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Radius Feasibility Does Not Cover the Tangent Cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curved-boundary obstruction to a fixed-radius tangent-generator formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge u^2\}\) and \(x=(0,0)\). Then \(T_\Omega(x)=\{(d_u,d_v):d_v\ge0\}\), so \((1,0)\in T_\Omega(x)\). For every \(\alpha>0\), however, \(x+\alpha(1,0)=(\alpha,0)\notin\Omega\). A direction \(d\) is feasible at radius \(\alpha\) only if \(d_v\ge\alpha d_u^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a curved epigraph, a horizontal direction is tangent although every positive straight step along that fixed direction is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Radius Feasibility Does Not Cover the Tangent Cone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General closed-set compatibility stated through feasible realization of tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be closed, \(x_j\in\Omega\) satisfy \(x_j\to x\), and \(\alpha_j\downarrow0\). Poll sets \(D_j\) are asymptotically constraint-compatible at \(x\) if, for every unit vector \(v\in T_\Omega(x)\), some subsequence and directions \(d_j\in D_j\) satisfy \(x_j+\alpha_jd_j\in\Omega\) and \(d_j/\|d_j\|\to v\). For uniform raw-step feasibility, a direction \(d\) may instead be required to lie in the hypertangent cone: there is \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(y+tw\in\Omega\) for all \(y\in\Omega\cap B(x,\varepsilon)\), \(w\in B(d,\varepsilon)\), and \(0<t<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: General compatibility requires feasible poll directions that asymptotically realize every tangent direction; hypertangent directions provide the stronger uniform nearby-feasibility property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall v\in T_\Omega(x)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1},\ \exists d_j:\ x_j+\alpha_jd_j\in\Omega,\quad d_j/\|d_j\|\to v.

notation.meaning: Hypertangent cone defined by uniform nearby feasibility.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region is a nonempty set \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MADS Mesh and Frame Sizes Become Arbitrarily Fine
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic refinement of the mesh-size and frame-size parameters generated by MADS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\delta^k\}\) and \(\{\Delta^k\}\) be the mesh-size and frame-size sequences produced by MADS applied to \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), and suppose that the level sets of \(f\) are bounded. Then \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\Delta^k=\liminf_{k\to\infty}\delta^k=0\). Moreover, for any subsequence indexed by \(K\), \(\lim_{k\in K}\delta^k=0\) if and only if \(\lim_{k\in K}\Delta^k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For MADS applied to a function with bounded level sets, the mesh and frame sizes each become arbitrarily small. On a given subsequence, the mesh size tends to zero exactly when the corresponding frame size tends to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Random construction of a MADS positive spanning set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of n+1 mesh-compatible MADS polling directions; positive spanning requires the rounded mesh parameter to be nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\alpha>0\) and \(n\ge 1\), set \(\delta=\operatorname{round}(1/\sqrt{\alpha})\). Initialize \(L=\operatorname{Diag}(\delta s_1,\ldots,\delta s_n)\), where each \(s_i\in\{-1,1\}\) is sampled randomly. For \(1\le j<i\le n-1\), sample \(L_{ij}\) from \(\{-\delta+1,\ldots,\delta-1\}\), leaving all other off-diagonal entries zero. Randomly permute the rows and columns of \(L\) to obtain \(D\), and return the columns of \([D,-D\mathbf 1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set delta to round(1/sqrt(alpha)). Form the specified triangular integer matrix with random signed diagonal entries and sampled lower-triangular entries, randomly permute its rows and columns, and append the negative column sum. If delta is nonzero, the resulting n+1 columns form a positive spanning set. If delta is zero, that conclusion fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{D_{:1},\ldots,D_{:n},-D\mathbf 1\}\text{ is a positive spanning set in }\mathbb R^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refining Subsequences, Refined Points, and Refining Directions in MADS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions used in the convergence analysis of constrained MADS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convergent subsequence \(\{x^k\}_{k\in K}\) of mesh local optimizers is a refining subsequence if and only if \(\lim_{k\in K}\delta^k=0\); its limit \(\widehat{x}\) is called a refined point. Given a refining subsequence and its refined point, a direction \(d\) is a refining direction if and only if there exist an infinite set \(L\subseteq K\) and poll directions \(d^k\in\mathbb{D}_\Delta^k\) such that \(x^k+\delta^k d^k\in\Omega\) for \(k\in L\) and \(\lim_{k\in L}d^k/\|d^k\|=d/\|d\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent subsequence of mesh local optimizers is refining when its mesh sizes tend to zero, and its limit is a refined point. A direction is refining when normalized feasible poll directions along an infinite subset converge to that direction after normalization.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\in K}\text{ is a convergent subsequence of mesh local optimizers.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\in K}\text{ is refining}\iff\lim_{k\in K}\delta^k=0;\quad d\text{ is refining}\iff\exists L\subseteq K\text{ infinite satisfying the stated feasibility and normalized-direction conditions.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: MADS iteration comprising a finite mesh search, a positive-spanning poll, and frame expansion or contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}\), \(x^0\in\Omega\), the extreme barrier \(f_\Omega\), \(\Delta^0>0\), a positive-spanning matrix \(D=GZ\), rational \(\tau\in(0,1)\), and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\geq0\), set \(\delta^k=\min\{\Delta^k,(\Delta^k)^2\}\). Search a finite set \(S^k\subseteq M^k\). If some \(t\in S^k\) satisfies \(f_\Omega(t)<f_\Omega(x^k)\), set \(x^{k+1}=t\) and \(\Delta^{k+1}=\tau^{-1}\Delta^k\). Otherwise choose a positive spanning set \(\mathbb D_\Delta^k\) such that \(P^k:=\{x^k+\delta^k d:d\in\mathbb D_\Delta^k\}\subseteq F^k\). If some \(t\in P^k\) improves \(f_\Omega\), set \(x^{k+1}=t\) and \(\Delta^{k+1}=\tau^{-1}\Delta^k\); otherwise set \(x^{k+1}=x^k\) and \(\Delta^{k+1}=\tau\Delta^k\). Increment \(k\) and repeat when \(\Delta^{k+1}\geq\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\); otherwise stop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each MADS iteration, derive the mesh size from the current frame size and search finitely many mesh points. If the search fails, poll frame-contained points generated by a positive-spanning direction set. An improving search or poll point becomes the new incumbent and expands the frame by 1/tau; an unsuccessful poll keeps the incumbent and contracts the frame by tau. Repeat while the updated frame size is at least the stopping tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb D_\Delta^k\text{ is positive spanning and }P^k\subseteq F^k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta^k=\min\{\Delta^k,(\Delta^k)^2\};\quad \Delta^{k+1}=\tau^{-1}\Delta^k\text{ after an improvement};\quad (x^{k+1},\Delta^{k+1})=(x^k,\tau\Delta^k)\text{ after an unsuccessful poll};\quad \text{repeat iff }\Delta^{k+1}\geq\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MADS Frame and Frame Size Parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the bounded mesh frame used in mesh adaptive direct search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be invertible, let \(Z\in\mathbb{Z}^{n\times p}\) have columns forming a positive spanning set for \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and set \(D=GZ\). Choose \(\delta^k>0\) and \(\Delta^k\) such that \(\delta^k\leq\Delta^k\). For an incumbent \(x^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), define \[b:=\max\{\|d'\|_\infty:d'\in\mathbb{D}\},\qquad F^k:=\{x\in M^k:\|x-x^k\|_\infty\leq\Delta^k b\}.\] Then \(F^k\) is the frame of extent \(\Delta^k\), and \(\Delta^k\) is the frame size parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the MADS mesh M^k centered at x^k, choose a frame size Delta^k no smaller than the mesh size delta^k. With b equal to the largest infinity norm of a direction in the stated direction set, the frame consists of mesh points at infinity-norm distance at most Delta^k b from x^k.
assumptions_latex: Z\in\mathbb{Z}^{n\times p}\text{ has columns forming a positive spanning set for }\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F^k=\{x\in M^k:\|x-x^k\|_\infty\leq\Delta^k b\},\qquad \Delta^k\text{ is the frame size parameter}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Householder Construction of a Maximal Positive Basis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Householder-based polling-direction construction used in mesh adaptive direct search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), set \(u=v/\lVert v\rVert\), and define the associated Householder matrix \(H=I-2uu^\top\). For every \(\gamma\ne0\), the columns of the horizontal block matrix \(\gamma H[I\; -I]\), equivalently \(\{\pm\gamma He_i:i=1,\ldots,n\}\), form a maximal positive basis of \(\mathbb{R}^n\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{\pm\gamma He_i:i=1,\ldots,n\}\text{ is a maximal positive basis of }\mathbb{R}^n

assumptions_latex: An incumbent \(x_k\), poll size \(\Delta_k>0\), and feasible domain \(\Omega\) are given.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The poll interface receives \((x_k,\Delta_k,D_k,A_k)\), constructs \(P_k=\{x_k+\Delta_k d:d\in D_k\}\cap\Omega\), and evaluates points in a finite prescribed ordering. It returns success together with the first or best \(y\in P_k\) satisfying \(A_k(y)\), or failure after the required poll points have been tested without acceptance. Opportunistic stopping is permitted only after success. On failure, the returned incumbent is \(x_k\); on success, the returned candidate is eligible to become \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A poll interface evaluates a finite, locally covering set of feasible directions and returns either an acceptable point or a completed-poll failure.

assumptions_latex: The search stage receives the current incumbent, mesh or admissible trial set, and an evaluation budget.
The number of search evaluations at each iteration is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optional search may propose any finitely many admissible trials, but its failure must leave the mandatory poll stage available.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The optional-search interface receives the iteration state and selects an arbitrary finite set \(S_k\subset M_k\) of admissible trial points, possibly using models, heuristics, cached evaluations, or previous history. It evaluates points in \(S_k\) until some \(y\) satisfies \(A_k(y)\) or the finite search terminates. It returns success and such a \(y\), or returns failure without changing \(x_k\). Search success may end the iteration; search failure must invoke the poll interface and must not by itself trigger mesh contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optional search can use any finite admissible trial set; success may finish the iteration, but failure passes control to polling without shrinking the mesh.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of finite termination for an optional search stage that precedes mandatory polling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an optional search is permitted to generate and evaluate an infinite sequence of trials without returning success or failure, then an iteration may remain forever in the search stage and never invoke the mandatory poll. Thus per-iteration finite termination, rather than any particular finite cardinality bound, is required for the optional-search interface to preserve the poll safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optional search that need not terminate can starve mandatory polling forever; finite termination is therefore an essential interface condition.
assumptions_latex: The optional search precedes the mandatory poll.
The search may continue generating rejected trials indefinitely without returning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mandatory poll need not be reached unless the search stage terminates finitely.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Search Starvation Boundary

children.title: Poll–Search Coordination
children.top_down_role: Division of roles between optional exploration plus structured polling.

assumptions_latex: Search and poll use the same incumbent, admissibility rules, and acceptance predicate.
The poll stage satisfies the direction-coverage conditions required by the method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is successful if either stage succeeds, and it is unsuccessful only after both search and poll fail.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential search-then-poll control logic for directional direct search.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run the optional search first. If it returns success, set \(s_k=1\), accept its candidate as \(x_{k+1}\), and omit polling. If it returns failure, set \(s_k=0\) and invoke the mandatory poll. Set \(p_k=1\) and accept the poll candidate when polling succeeds; otherwise set \(p_k=0\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Thus \(u_k=\max\{s_k,p_k\}\). Apply a successful scale update when \(u_k=1\), and apply an unsuccessful refining update only when \(u_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search runs first; only its failure invokes polling. Either stage can make the iteration successful, while refinement occurs only when both fail.
knowledge_statements.title: Poll–Search Coordination

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic directional direct-search framework combining an optional finite search, positive-basis polling, adaptive step-size updates, a poll-evaluation bound, and a step-size stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\), \(\alpha_0>0\), constants \(0<\beta_1\leq\beta_2<1\) and \(\gamma\geq1\), and a collection \(\mathcal D\) of positive bases. At iteration \(k\), first evaluate \(f\) at finitely many search points. If a point \(x\) satisfying \(f(x)<f(x_k)\) is found, set \(x_{k+1}=x\) and declare success. Otherwise choose \(D_k\in\mathcal D\), order \(P_k=\{x_k+\alpha_kd:d\in D_k\}\), and poll until a direction \(d_k\in D_k\) satisfying \(f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)<f(x_k)\) is found; then set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and declare success. If no such poll point exists, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and declare failure. On success choose \(\alpha_{k+1}\in[\alpha_k,\gamma\alpha_k]\); on failure choose \(\alpha_{k+1}\in[\beta_1\alpha_k,\beta_2\alpha_k]\). The poll step makes at most \(|D_k|\) function evaluations and exactly \(|D_k|\) at an unsuccessful iteration, where \(|D_k|\geq n+1\). A natural stopping rule is \(\alpha_k<\alpha_{\mathrm{tol}}\) for prescribed \(\alpha_{\mathrm{tol}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each iteration first performs an optional finite search for strict objective decrease. If that search fails, the method polls an ordered positive basis around the current point and accepts the first strictly improving poll point. If every poll point fails, the iterate remains unchanged. Successful iterations maintain or enlarge the step size, while unsuccessful iterations reduce it. Polling uses at most the number of basis directions in function evaluations and exactly that many at unsuccessful iterations. The run may terminate when the step size falls below a prescribed positive tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D\text{ is a collection of positive bases}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{cases}f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k),\quad \alpha_{k+1}\in[\alpha_k,\gamma\alpha_k],&\text{if the iteration succeeds},\\x_{k+1}=x_k,\quad \alpha_{k+1}\in[\beta_1\alpha_k,\beta_2\alpha_k],&\text{if it fails},\end{cases}\qquad N_k^{\mathrm{poll}}\leq|D_k|,\ \ N_k^{\mathrm{poll}}=|D_k|\text{ on failure}.

children.title: Search-Failure Fallbacks
children.top_down_role: Poll-based safeguards used when optional search does not produce acceptable progress.

assumptions_latex: The optional search has returned no acceptable point.
A valid finite poll set can be constructed at the unchanged incumbent and current scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Search failure falls back to a convergence-enforcing poll; scale contraction is justified only if that poll also fails.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mandatory polling fallback after an unsuccessful optional search.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the optional search finds no point satisfying \(A_k\), the algorithm preserves \((x_k,\Delta_k)\) and evaluates the required poll set \(P_k\). A poll point satisfying \(A_k\) is accepted and the iteration is successful. Only when no required point in \(P_k\) satisfies \(A_k\) may the algorithm declare the iteration unsuccessful, retain \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), and reduce the controlling scale. Consequently, failure of a heuristic or model-based search alone is never a stationarity-relevant failure certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When optional search fails, the method polls at the same incumbent and scale; only failure of that poll permits refinement and carries convergence significance.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Failure Fallbacks

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by treating optional-search failure as sufficient reason to refine without polling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_0=0\), and let the optional search return failure at every iteration. Suppose an invalid fallback retains \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and contracts \(\Delta_k\to0\) without polling. Then \(x_k=0\) for every \(k\), although \(f'(0)=1\neq0\). A valid poll containing direction \(-1\) would produce \(f(x_k-\Delta_k)<f(x_k)\) at every positive scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every failed optional search directly contracts the scale and skips polling, the method can remain forever at a point with nonzero derivative even though the omitted poll always contains an improving direction.
assumptions_latex: The optional search always returns failure.
The implementation contracts the scale without invoking an available poll containing \(-1\).
review_flags: demonstrates necessity of mandatory fallback rather than deficient poll coverage
knowledge_statements.title: Skipped-Poll Nonstationarity Counterexample

children.title: Mesh Management
children.top_down_role: Management of discrete search meshes in directional direct-search methods.

assumptions_latex: Trial points must lie on an iteration-dependent mesh.
Mesh updates use factors from a prescribed discrete set bounded away from zero and infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mesh management preserves mesh membership, refines after unsuccessful iterations, and optionally coarsens or retains the mesh after success.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete mesh construction and success-dependent mesh updates.

source_refs.locator: 7.6 The mesh adaptive direct-search method p. 132
Chapter 8. Mesh Adaptive Direct Search p. 135

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), \(D^m\), and \(\Delta_k^m>0\), define \(M_k=\{x_k+\Delta_k^m D^m z:z\in\mathbb{Z}^{|D^m|}\}\). Restrict search and poll candidates to \(M_k\). After an unsuccessful iteration set \(\Delta_{k+1}^m=\tau_k\Delta_k^m\) with \(0<\tau_k<1\). After success choose \(\Delta_{k+1}^m=\gamma_k\Delta_k^m\) with \(\gamma_k\geq1\), or retain the mesh by taking \(\gamma_k=1\). Stop when the mesh tolerance or evaluation budget is reached, returning the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mesh management keeps trials on a generated lattice, refines that lattice after failure, and retains or coarsens it after success.
knowledge_statements.title: Mesh Management

source_witnesses.locator: 7.6 The mesh adaptive direct-search method p. 132
Chapter 8. Mesh Adaptive Direct Search p. 135

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient algebraic condition under which refinement retains every point of the preceding generated mesh.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k=x_k+\Delta_k^mD^m\mathbb Z^p\). Suppose \(x_{k+1}\in M_k\), \(\Delta_{k+1}^m=\Delta_k^m/q\) for an integer \(q\geq2\), and the generator matrix \(D^m\) is unchanged. Then \(M_k\subseteq M_{k+1}\). Thus reciprocal-integer refinement increases resolution without discarding any previously representable mesh point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed generator and reciprocal-integer refinement, the new mesh contains the old mesh whenever the new center lies on the old mesh.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mesh-membership invariant for generalized pattern search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let G\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n} be invertible, let Z\in\mathbb{Z}^{n\times p} have columns forming a positive spanning set for \mathbb{R}^n, and let D=GZ. If M^k=\{x^k+\delta^kDy:y\in\mathbb{N}^p\} is the mesh centered at x^k with mesh-size parameter \delta^k>0, then x^{k+1}\in M^k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the GPS direction matrix is D = GZ, with G invertible and the integer columns of Z positively spanning the space, the next iterate belongs to the mesh centered at the current iterate.

children.title: Step-Scale Management
children.top_down_role: Management of polling or trial displacement scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Scale Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Success-dependent control of direct-search step or poll radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\alpha_0>0\). If iteration \(k\) is unsuccessful, set \(\alpha_{k+1}=\theta_k\alpha_k\), where \(0<\theta_{\min}\leq\theta_k<1\). If it is successful, set \(\alpha_{k+1}=\gamma_k\alpha_k\), where \(1\leq\gamma_k\leq\gamma_{\max}<\infty\), with \(\gamma_k=1\) representing retention. If an upper scale bound \(\alpha_{\max}>0\) is prescribed, replace the successful update by \(\alpha_{k+1}=\min\{\gamma_k\alpha_k,\alpha_{\max}\}\). Terminate when \(\alpha_k\leq\varepsilon\) or the evaluation budget is exhausted, and return the current incumbent together with its final scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The direct-search scale contracts after failure and is retained or enlarged after success, optionally subject to an upper cap; the method stops at a scale tolerance or evaluation budget.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration \(k\) is classified as successful or unsuccessful by a fixed acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step scale contracts on failure and is retained or enlarged on success, subject to the prescribed factor bounds and stopping tolerance.

notation.meaning: step or poll scale at iteration \(k\)

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition under which repeated unsuccessful step-scale updates force geometric refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every unsuccessful update satisfies \(0<\theta_{\min}\leq\theta_k\leq\theta_{\max}<1\), then any run of \(r\) consecutive unsuccessful iterations beginning at \(k\) satisfies \(\alpha_{k+r}\leq\theta_{\max}^{r}\alpha_k\), and hence \(\alpha_{k+r}\to0\) as \(r\to\infty\). Merely requiring \(\theta_k<1\) separately for each iteration does not ensure this conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform upper bound below one makes consecutive failure contractions drive the scale geometrically to zero. Pointwise contraction factors below one are not sufficient by themselves.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on failure contraction factors

children.title: Mesh–Scale Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coordination between mesh resolution plus active search scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Mesh–Scale Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard MADS coupling between poll and mesh parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_k^m>0\) be the mesh size and \(\Delta_k^p>0\) the poll size at iteration \(k\). Mesh–scale coupling requires \(\Delta_k^m\leq \Delta_k^p\) for every \(k\), together with \(\Delta_k^m\to0\) along every refining subsequence for which \(\Delta_k^p\to0\). A standard realization is \(\Delta_k^m=\min\{\Delta_k^p,(\Delta_k^p)^2\}\), which makes the mesh asymptotically finer than the poll radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mesh is never coarser than the poll scale and becomes asymptotically finer whenever a refining subsequence drives the poll scale to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_k^m\leq\Delta_k^p\), and \(\Delta_k^p\to0\) on a refining subsequence implies \(\Delta_k^m\to0\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. Mesh Adaptive Direct Search p. 135

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. Mesh Adaptive Direct Search p. 135

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stronger MADS coupling condition making mesh resolution negligible relative to poll displacement on refining subsequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_k^m\) and \(\Delta_k^p\) be the mesh and poll parameters. On every refining subsequence \(K\) with \(\Delta_k^p\to0\), asymptotic scale separation requires \(\Delta_k^m/\Delta_k^p\to0\). This condition is stronger than merely requiring \(\Delta_k^m\leq\Delta_k^p\) and \(\Delta_k^m\to0\). The realization \(\Delta_k^m=\min\{\Delta_k^p,(\Delta_k^p)^2\}\) satisfies the separation condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard asymptotic MADS coupling makes the mesh size vanish relative to the poll size, not merely vanish alongside it.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Mesh–Poll Scale Separation

children.title: Scale-Stagnation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where scale control ceases to support meaningful search progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Stagnation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for direct search whose control scale cannot contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be minimized by polling \(x_k+\Delta_k d\) over finite direction sets. If unsuccessful iterations do not force scale contraction, then the method may remain forever at a nonstationary point. For example, with \(f(x)=x\), \(x_0=0\), polling direction \(d=-1\), fixed scale \(\Delta_k=1\), and acceptance requiring \(f(x_k+\Delta_kd)<f(x_k)-2\), every poll is rejected although \(f'(0)=1\ne0\). Thus scale refinement is essential to general stationarity guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without forced scale contraction, an overly demanding acceptance test can reject every fixed-size improving step and leave direct search at a nonstationary point.
assumptions_latex: The acceptance threshold need not vanish with \(\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stationarity cannot generally be inferred unless unsuccessful iterations generate scales approaching zero.

children.title: Opportunistic Polling
children.top_down_role: Polling regimes that may terminate after an acceptable direction is encountered.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is available for evaluation at every poll point.
\(m_k\geq1\), and \(D_k=(d_{k,1},\ldots,d_{k,m_k})\) is an ordered tuple of directions in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(A_k:\mathbb{R}^n\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) is decidable from the available function information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the first accepted trial has index \(J_k\), exactly \(J_k\in\{1,\ldots,m_k\}\) poll evaluations are performed; if no trial is accepted, exactly \(m_k\) poll evaluations are performed.

notation.meaning: index of the first accepted trial

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Early-terminating poll procedure for deterministic direct search.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), let \(D_k=(d_{k,1},\ldots,d_{k,m_k})\) be an ordered finite tuple in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(m_k\geq1\), and let \(A_k\) be an acceptance predicate on trial points. Evaluate \(f(x_k+\Delta_k d_{k,j})\) sequentially for \(j=1,\ldots,m_k\). Stop at the first index \(J_k\) for which \(A_k(x_k+\Delta_k d_{k,J_k})\) is true, declare success, and return \(x_k+\Delta_k d_{k,J_k}\). If no such index exists, declare failure and return \(x_k\). No direction following \(J_k\) is evaluated during that iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the nonempty ordered list of poll points until the first acceptable point is found. Return that point immediately, or return the incumbent after all poll points have been rejected.
knowledge_statements.title: Opportunistic Polling

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

children.title: Complete Polling
children.top_down_role: Polling regimes that evaluate the full prescribed direction set.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is available for evaluation at every poll point.
The rule for selecting among accepted trials is prescribed independently of their evaluation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly \(|D_k|\) poll points are evaluated, and the acceptance status of every direction in \(D_k\) is observed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive poll procedure retaining all current-scale outcomes.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), let \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(A_k\) be an acceptance predicate on trial points. Evaluate \(f(x_k+\Delta_k d)\) for every \(d\in D_k\), irrespective of earlier acceptances, and define \(S_k=\{d\in D_k:A_k(x_k+\Delta_k d)\}\). If \(S_k\neq\varnothing\), declare success and select a point from \(\{x_k+\Delta_k d:d\in S_k\}\) by a prescribed rule. If \(S_k=\varnothing\), declare failure and return \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate every point in the nonempty finite poll set. Then select an acceptable point by a prescribed rule, or retain the incumbent if none is acceptable.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete Polling

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

children.title: Evaluation-Order Effects
children.top_down_role: Influence of poll-point ordering on cost, accepted motion, or observed progress.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and the acceptance predicate \(A_k\) are deterministic.
The same finite poll set \(D_k\), incumbent \(x_k\), and scale \(\Delta_k\) are used under every ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete polling reveals the order-invariant set \(P_k\), while opportunistic polling can return different points when \(|P_k|\geq2\) and can use different evaluation counts when both \(P_k\) and \(D_k\setminus P_k\) are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order dependence of opportunistic, but not exhaustive, poll information.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), let \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be finite, and let \(A_k\) be a deterministic acceptance predicate. Define \(P_k=\{d\in D_k:A_k(x_k+\Delta_k d)\}\). Complete polling reveals the same set \(P_k\) under every permutation of \(D_k\). Opportunistic polling can return different trial points under different permutations when \(|P_k|\geq2\). Its evaluation count can differ between permutations when \(P_k\neq\varnothing\) and \(D_k\setminus P_k\neq\varnothing\), because rejected directions may occur before the first accepted direction. If \(P_k=D_k\), every opportunistic ordering accepts after one evaluation, although the returned point may still depend on the order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reordering directions does not change the accepted set revealed by complete polling. It can change the point returned by opportunistic polling when several points are acceptable, and it can change the evaluation count when both accepted and rejected points are present.
knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Order Effects

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected opportunistic evaluation count under a uniformly random permutation of a fixed deterministic poll set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\geq1\) poll trials contain exactly \(r\) acceptable trials, and order all \(m\) trials by a uniformly random permutation. If \(r\geq1\), the expected position \(J\) of the first acceptable trial, and hence the expected opportunistic evaluation count, is \(\mathbb{E}[J]=(m+1)/(r+1)\). If \(r=0\), opportunistic polling evaluates all \(m\) trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a uniformly random ordering and r acceptable points among m, opportunistic polling uses an expected (m+1)/(r+1) evaluations when r is positive, and m evaluations when none is acceptable.
assumptions_latex: The objective and acceptance predicate are deterministic for the fixed poll set.
The ordering is a uniformly random permutation of \(m\) distinct trials.

notation.meaning: position of the first acceptable trial

knowledge_statements.title: Uniformly Random Poll Ordering Cost

children.title: Early-Acceptance Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Evaluation savings plus directional-information losses associated with early poll acceptance.

assumptions_latex: \(m_k\geq1\), and each poll-point evaluation has the same counted cost.
At least one trial is accepted, and \(J_k\in\{1,\ldots,m_k\}\) is the position of the first accepted trial.
Values of unevaluated trials are not otherwise available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Opportunistic polling saves \(m_k-J_k\) evaluations relative to complete polling, but it does not generally certify that its returned trial minimizes \(f\) over all accepted poll points.

notation.meaning: position of the first accepted direction
objective function used to compare accepted trials

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation-versus-information tradeoff induced by terminating a poll early.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a poll contain \(m_k\geq1\) ordered trial points, and suppose the first accepted trial occurs at position \(J_k\in\{1,ldots,m_k\}\). Opportunistic polling then performs \(J_k\) evaluations, whereas complete polling performs \(m_k\), so the saving is \(m_k-J_k\). Because the remaining \(m_k-J_k\) objective values are not observed, the returned trial cannot in general be certified to minimize \(f\) over all accepted poll points. Such a certificate is available only if independent information guarantees that no unevaluated accepted point has a smaller objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the first acceptable trial is in position J, early acceptance saves the evaluations that complete polling would spend on the remaining directions. Without independent information about those unevaluated trials, it cannot certify that the returned point has the best objective value among all acceptable poll points.
knowledge_statements.title: Early-Acceptance Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Simple-Decrease Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-improvement acceptance rule without a quantitative forcing term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization of \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a trial point \(y_k\) satisfies the simple-decrease acceptance condition at incumbent \(x_k\) precisely when \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\). In a poll step, \(y_k=x_k+\Delta_kd\) for some current direction \(d\). The condition demands strict improvement but imposes no decrease magnitude tied to \(\Delta_k\); therefore arbitrarily small positive reductions are acceptable in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial is accepted exactly when its objective value is strictly below the incumbent’s, with no scale-dependent decrease requirement.
assumptions_latex: The problem is posed as minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_k\) is accepted if and only if \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\).

children.title: Sufficient-Decrease Regimes
children.top_down_role: Direct-search acceptance requiring scale-sensitive progress.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is an objective to be minimized.
