knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forcing-function acceptance rule for directional direct search.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be minimized, let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). A forcing function is a map \(\rho:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\) satisfying \(\rho(t)/t\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). The trial \(y_k=x_k+\Delta_k d\) satisfies sufficient decrease when \(f(y_k)\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\). A standard example is \(\rho(t)=ct^2\) with \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, sufficient decrease accepts a trial only when it lowers the objective by at least a positive forcing amount whose ratio to the step scale tends to zero near zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient-Decrease Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Telescoping consequence of repeated sufficient-decrease acceptance for a lower-bounded incumbent sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the accepted iteration indices. Suppose \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\) for \(k\in S\), while \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) for \(k\notin S\). If \(f(x_k)\geq f_{\inf}>-\infty\), then \(\sum_{k\in S,\,k<N}\rho(\Delta_k)\leq f(x_0)-f_{\inf}\) for every \(N\). Therefore \(\sum_{k\in S}\rho(\Delta_k)<\infty\), and if \(S\) is infinite, \(\rho(\Delta_k)\to0\) along accepted iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-bounded objective, accepted forcing decreases are summable and therefore vanish along every infinite sequence of accepted iterations.
assumptions_latex: Unaccepted iterations leave the incumbent unchanged.

notation.meaning: lower bound on incumbent objective values

knowledge_statements.title: Summability of Accepted Forcing Decreases

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance rule for nontrivial search and poll steps in directional direct-search methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A new point \(x_{k+1}\neq x_k\) is accepted, in either a search or poll step, only if \[f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)-\rho(\alpha_k),\] where the forcing function \(\rho:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is continuous, positive, and nondecreasing, and satisfies \[\lim_{t\to0^+}\frac{\rho(t)}{t}=0.\] Examples are \(\rho(t)=t^2\) and, more generally, \(\rho(t)=t^{1+a}\) for \(a>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nontrivial search or poll point is accepted only when its objective decrease exceeds a scale-dependent forcing term. The forcing function is continuous, positive, nondecreasing, and negligible relative to its argument near zero. Powers t^(1+a), for a>0, are examples.

children.title: Acceptance-Regime Transitions
children.top_down_role: Relationships plus transitions between simple-decrease and sufficient-decrease criteria.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact endpoint convention connecting simple decrease with positive-margin sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau_k\geq0\), define the transition rule by accepting \(y_k\) when \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\) if \(\tau_k=0\), and when \(f(y_k)\leq f(x_k)-\tau_k\) if \(\tau_k>0\). The zero-margin endpoint is exactly simple decrease. Taking \(\tau_k=\rho(\Delta_k)>0\) gives the sufficient-decrease rule. A single non-strict formula with \(\tau_k=0\) is not equivalent to simple decrease because it also accepts ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact transition uses strict comparison at zero margin and a non-strict quantified comparison at positive margin; retaining a non-strict comparison at zero incorrectly accepts ties.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_k=0\) recovers strict simple decrease, whereas \(\tau_k=\rho(\Delta_k)>0\) recovers sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Strictness-Consistent Acceptance Transition
Acceptance-Regime Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-dependent interpolation between sufficient and simple decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau_k\geq0\) be an iteration-dependent acceptance margin. Accept a trial \(y_k\) when \(f(y_k)\leq f(x_k)-\tau_k\). Choosing \(\tau_k=\rho(\Delta_k)>0\) gives a sufficient-decrease regime, while \(\tau_k=0\) with a strict inequality gives simple decrease. A transition rule is asymptotically compatible with first-order direct-search analysis when \(\tau_k/\Delta_k\to0\) along refining subsequences, so the normalized acceptance margin does not obscure directional first-order behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scale-dependent margin interpolates between quantified sufficient decrease and strict simple decrease; its normalized size should vanish along refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transition is first-order compatible when \(\tau_k/\Delta_k\to0\) along refining subsequences.

children.title: Noise-Sensitive Acceptance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of decrease-based acceptance under uncertain objective evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact robust-decrease certificate and sharp ambiguity boundary under uniformly bounded additive evaluation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\widetilde f(z)=f(z)+e(z)\) with \(|e(z)|\leq\varepsilon\). For \(\widetilde\delta=\widetilde f(y)-\widetilde f(x)\) and \(\delta=f(y)-f(x)\), one has \(\delta\in[\widetilde\delta-2\varepsilon,\widetilde\delta+2\varepsilon]\). Hence \(\widetilde f(y)\leq\widetilde f(x)-\tau\) guarantees \(f(y)<f(x)\) when \(\tau>2\varepsilon\), while \(\tau=2\varepsilon\) guarantees only \(f(y)\leq f(x)\). If the true decrease \(a=f(x)-f(y)\) satisfies \(0<a<2\varepsilon\), admissible extremal errors can make \(\widetilde f(y)>\widetilde f(x)\); if \(a=2\varepsilon\), they can make the observations tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two bounded evaluation errors create a two-epsilon uncertainty interval: margins above it certify strict true decrease, equality certifies only nonincrease, and smaller true decreases can have their observed sign reversed.
assumptions_latex: The two evaluation errors may attain opposite extremal signs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde f(y)\leq\widetilde f(x)-\tau\) and \(\tau>2\varepsilon\) imply \(f(y)<f(x)\), and the threshold \(2\varepsilon\) is sharp.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Bounded-Noise Acceptance Boundary
Noise-Sensitive Acceptance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic acceptance limits under uniformly bounded evaluation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose observed values satisfy \(\widetilde f(x)=f(x)+e(x)\) with \(|e(x)|\leq\varepsilon\). From two observations, an asserted decrease \(\widetilde f(y)\leq\widetilde f(x)-\tau\) guarantees true strict decrease only when \(\tau>2\varepsilon\), because \(f(y)-f(x)\leq-\tau+2\varepsilon\). Conversely, if the true decrease has magnitude at most \(2\varepsilon\), admissible errors can reverse its observed sign. Hence simple decrease and forcing margins below the noise-separation threshold cannot reliably distinguish improvement from deterioration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uniformly bounded noise, an observed decrease certifies true improvement only when its margin exceeds twice the error bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for this nontrivial noise boundary. The forward implication with a margin strictly greater than twice the error bound is correct, but the converse is overstated at equality: a true decrease of exactly twice the bound can be erased to a tie by extremal errors, not reversed to a strict observed increase. An authoritative locator and a corrected boundary statement are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable with Lipschitz-continuous gradient on a neighborhood containing the relevant iterates and poll trials. At iteration \(k\), let \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a finite positive-spanning set whose cosine measure is at least \(\kappa>0\), and suppose \(\delta\leq\|d\|\leq M\) for every \(d\in D_k\), where \(0<\delta\leq M<\infty\) are independent of \(k\). A trial is accepted only if \(f(x_k+\Delta_k d)\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\), where \(\rho(t)>0\) and \(\rho(t)/t\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). If an infinite set \(K\) of unsuccessful poll indices satisfies \(\Delta_k\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\) through \(K\), then \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\) through \(K\). Consequently, \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\), and every accumulation point \(x_*\) of \((x_k)_{k\in K}\) is first-order stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth unconstrained direct search, uniformly well-spread poll directions with norms bounded above and away from zero, a vanishing normalized forcing term, and unsuccessful scales tending to zero imply that gradients along those unsuccessful refining iterations tend to zero. Their accumulation points are stationary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nelder–Mead value and vertex convergence under finite shrink regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific asymptotic properties of ordered simplex values and vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the Nelder--Mead method applied to a function \(f\) bounded below on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Then \(\{f_k^0\}\) converges. If only finitely many shrink steps occur, each sequence \(\{f_k^i\}\), \(i=0,\ldots,n\), converges, and its limits satisfy \(f_*^0\leq f_*^1\leq\cdots\leq f_*^n\). Moreover, if \(f_*^j<f_*^{j+1}\) for some \(j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\), then the change index satisfies \(k^*>j\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). If only finitely many nonshrink steps occur, all simplex vertices converge to a single point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Nelder–Mead applied to a function bounded below on R^n, the best ordered simplex value converges. With only finitely many shrink steps, every ordered vertex-value sequence converges in nondecreasing limiting order; a strict gap between consecutive limits eventually places the change index above that gap. With only finitely many nonshrink steps, all simplex vertices converge to one point.
assumptions_latex: \text{The simplex sequence, ordered values }f_k^i\text{, and change index }k^*\text{ are generated by the Nelder--Mead method.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_k^0\text{ converges};\quad \#\{\text{shrink steps}\}<\infty\Rightarrow\left(\forall i\in\{0,\ldots,n\},\ f_k^i\to f_*^i\right),\ f_*^0\leq\cdots\leq f_*^n,\ \left(f_*^j<f_*^{j+1}\Rightarrow k^*>j\text{ eventually}\right);\quad \#\{\text{nonshrink steps}\}<\infty\Rightarrow\text{all simplex vertices converge to one point.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the objective-value-only simplex search principle and its general convergence limitation. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization in \(N\) variables, the Nelder\text{--}Mead method begins with \(N+1\) trial points forming a simplex and selects replacement points using only numerical objective values. Without additional assumptions or safeguards, the method has no general local-convergence guarantee and is therefore heuristic.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplex geometry and search-line representation in Nelder–Mead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation of the Nelder–Mead simplex and its basic iteration principle. The extract calls \(\bar x\) the centroid but its displayed formula omits the required factor \(1/n\); the normalized centroid is used here, with that discrepancy recorded explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For vertices \(z_1,\ldots,z_{n+1}\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{z_1,\ldots,z_{n+1}\}\) and \(V(S)=[z_2-z_1,\ldots,z_{n+1}-z_1]\). Then \(S\) is nondegenerate if and only if \(V(S)\) is nonsingular. In a Nelder–Mead iteration, order the current vertices so that \(f(x_1)\leq\cdots\leq f(x_{n+1})\), form the centroid \(\bar x=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\) of the best \(n\) vertices, and parameterize the line through that centroid and the worst vertex by \(\bar x(t)=\bar x+t(x_{n+1}-\bar x)\). The method seeks a replacement for \(x_{n+1}\) by reflection, expansion, or contraction on this line; if no such replacement is accepted, it retains \(x_1\) and shrinks the other vertices toward \(x_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The edge matrix of n+1 vertices in R^n has columns z_2-z_1 through z_{n+1}-z_1, and their simplex is nondegenerate exactly when this matrix is nonsingular. Nelder–Mead orders the current vertices by function value, forms the centroid of the best n vertices, and searches on the line through that centroid and the worst vertex using reflection, expansion, or contraction. If no candidate is accepted, it keeps the best vertex and shrinks the remaining vertices toward it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is nondegenerate}\iff\det V(S)\neq0,\qquad \bar x=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i,\qquad \bar x(t)=\bar x+t(x_{n+1}-\bar x),\text{ with reflection, expansion, contraction, or a fallback shrink used to update the simplex.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nelder–Mead reflection, expansion, and contraction iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the particular minimization variant in the extract. It includes neither a shrink step nor a feasibility-repair rule, so generated trial points must be evaluable even when affine transformations leave the initial feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{x(i)\}_{i=1}^{N+1}\) and order its points so that \(f(x_{\min})\le f(x_{sl})\le f(x_{\max})\), where \(x_{sl}\) is second worst. Define \(x_c=\frac1N\left(-x_{\max}+\sum_{i=1}^{N+1}x(i)\right)\) and \(x_r=2x_c-x_{\max}\). If \(f(x_r)<f(x_{\min})\), set \(x_{\exp}=2x_r-x_c\) and choose \(x_{\mathrm{new}}\in\{x_{\exp},x_r\}\) with the smaller objective value. If \(f(x_{\min})\le f(x_r)<f(x_{sl})\), set \(x_{\mathrm{new}}=x_r\). If \(f(x_{sl})\le f(x_r)<f(x_{\max})\), set \(x_{\mathrm{new}}=\tfrac12(x_r+x_c)\); otherwise set \(x_{\mathrm{new}}=\tfrac12(x_{\max}+x_c)\). Replace \(x_{\max}\) by \(x_{\mathrm{new}}\) and repeat until the prescribed iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order N+1 simplex points from best to worst, compute the centroid excluding the worst point, and reflect the worst point through that centroid. Use expansion when reflection improves on the best point, accept an intermediate reflection directly, and otherwise use the specified outside or inside contraction. Replace the worst point and repeat to the iteration limit. This extracted variant has no shrink or feasibility-repair step.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P=\{x(i)\}_{i=1}^{N+1}\text{ consists initially of feasible, evaluable points}
f\text{ is evaluable at every reflected, expanded, and contracted trial point}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\max}\leftarrow x_{\mathrm{new}}\quad\text{and the reflection-expansion-contraction iteration repeats.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded description of the reflection, expansion, contraction, and shrink structure. Several displayed point formulas, branch inequalities, and the stopping condition are illegible, so this is not a complete executable specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For unconstrained minimization of \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), maintain simplex vertices \(x^0,\ldots,x^n\) and select \(x^h\) and \(x^l\) attaining the largest and smallest sampled objective values. Generate a reflection using coefficient \(\alpha>0\). If reflection yields a new lowest value, test an expansion with coefficient \(\gamma>1\) and retain the better of the reflected and expanded points. In the extract's intermediate case, accept the reflected point. Otherwise attempt a contraction with coefficient \(0<\beta<1\); if its prescribed comparison fails, halve the distances of the other vertices from \(x^l\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For derivative-free unconstrained minimization, rank the vertices of a current simplex by objective value and try to replace the worst vertex through reflection. A new-best reflection triggers an expansion test; an intermediate reflection is accepted; otherwise contraction is attempted. If contraction fails, the simplex is shrunk halfway toward its best vertex. The corrupted extract does not preserve all point formulas or branch tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The worst simplex vertex is updated by reflection, possible expansion, or contraction; failed contraction triggers a half-shrink toward }x^l\text{.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an affinely independent simplex and order it so that \(f(v_0)\le f(v_1)\le\cdots\le f(v_n)\). With \(c=n^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}v_i\), form the reflection \(r=c+\alpha(c-v_n)\). According to the ordered objective comparisons, accept \(r\), try expansion \(e=c+\gamma(r-c)\), or try an outside or inside contraction toward \(c\). If contraction fails, replace every \(v_i\), \(i\ge 1\), by \(v_0+\sigma(v_i-v_0)\). The classical coefficients are \(\alpha=1\), \(\gamma=2\), \(\rho=1/2\), and \(\sigma=1/2\). Reorder and repeat until the chosen diameter or objective-spread tolerance holds; output the best vertex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume deterministic tie-breaking and decisions based only on objective-value comparisons. For every strictly increasing phi, replacing f by phi composed with f leaves the generated simplex sequence unchanged. If T(x)=Ax+b with nonsingular A, applying the method to f composed with T^{-1} from T(v_0),...,T(v_n) generates T(S_k) whenever the original run generates S_k. These statements need not extend to stopping rules using untransformed numerical diameter or objective-spread tolerances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement. The flattened extract's branch nesting is resolved from the mutually exclusive function-value tests and its outside-contraction, inside-contraction, and shrink annotations. Symbols such as \(x_{-2}\) are normalized to the previously defined points \(\bar x(-2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_i=f(x_i)\), where \(f_1\leq\cdots\leq f_{n+1}\), let \(\bar x=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\), and define \(\bar x(t)=\bar x+t(x_{n+1}-\bar x)\). Evaluate \(f_{-1}=f(\bar x(-1))\). If \(f_1\leq f_{-1}<f_n\), replace \(x_{n+1}\) by \(\bar x(-1)\). If \(f_{-1}<f_1\), evaluate \(f_{-2}=f(\bar x(-2))\) and replace \(x_{n+1}\) by \(\bar x(-2)\) when \(f_{-2}<f_{-1}\), otherwise by \(\bar x(-1)\). If \(f_{-1}\geq f_n\), then when \(f_n\leq f_{-1}<f_{n+1}\), evaluate the outside contraction \(f_{-1/2}=f(\bar x(-1/2))\) and accept \(\bar x(-1/2)\) if \(f_{-1/2}\leq f_{-1}\); when \(f_{-1}\geq f_{n+1}\), evaluate the inside contraction \(f_{1/2}=f(\bar x(1/2))\) and accept \(\bar x(1/2)\) if \(f_{1/2}<f_{n+1}\). If the applicable contraction is not accepted, set \(x_i\leftarrow\tfrac12(x_1+x_i)\) for \(i=2,\ldots,n+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order the simplex vertices from best to worst and reflect the worst vertex through the centroid of the best n vertices. Accept a reflection whose value lies from the best value up to, but not including, the second-worst value. If the reflection is better than the current best, compare it with an expansion and accept the better point. If the reflection is no better than the second-worst point, try the applicable outside or inside contraction with its stated acceptance test. If that contraction fails, halve every edge from the best vertex while leaving the best vertex fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{n+1}\text{ is replaced according to the reflection, expansion, or applicable contraction test; if that contraction fails, }x_i\leftarrow\frac12(x_1+x_i)\quad(i=2,\ldots,n+1).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-scaled coefficient representation commonly associated with adaptive Nelder--Mead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dimension-scaled Nelder--Mead parameterization is
\[
(\alpha_n,\gamma_n,\rho_n,\sigma_n)=\left(1,1+\frac{2}{n},\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{2n},1-\frac{1}{n}\right).
\]
It satisfies \(\gamma_n\in(1,2]\), \(\rho_n\in[1/2,3/4)\), and \(\sigma_n\in[1/2,1)\) for \(n\ge 2\), with limits \(\gamma_n\to 1\), \(\rho_n\to 3/4\), and \(\sigma_n\to 1\). The scaling therefore moderates expansion and shrinkage increasingly with dimension while retaining unit reflection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard dimension-scaled parameterization makes expansion milder, contraction approach three quarters, and shrinkage approach one as dimension increases.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Scaled Nelder–Mead

children.title: Parameter-Scaling Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by fixed, adaptive, or dimension-dependent simplex parameters.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The classical regime is dimension invariant, whereas the adaptive regime changes by terms of order \(n^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of fixed classical and dimension-adaptive coefficient regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For coefficient order \((\alpha,\gamma,\rho,\sigma)\), the classical regime is
\[
p^{\mathrm{cl}}=(1,2,1/2,1/2),
\]
whereas the dimension-adaptive regime is
\[
p^{\mathrm{ad}}_n=\left(1,1+\frac{2}{n},\frac{3}{4}-\frac{1}{2n},1-\frac{1}{n}\right).
\]
The adaptive deviations from their limiting values are exactly \(\gamma_n-1=2/n\), \(3/4-\rho_n=1/(2n)\), and \(1-\sigma_n=1/n\). Hence this regime changes the nonreflection transformations on the scale \(n^{-1}\), while the classical coefficients remain independent of dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical coefficients stay fixed, while adaptive expansion, contraction, and shrink parameters vary from their limiting values by order one over dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Scaling Regimes

children.title: High-Dimensional Nelder–Mead Behavior

assumptions_latex: A shrink maps each nonbest edge vector to \(\sigma_n\) times itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Adaptive shrinkage preserves an asymptotic fraction \(e^{-1}\) of simplex volume, unlike classical shrinkage whose volume fraction vanishes exponentially.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact high-dimensional volume effect of adaptive versus classical simplex shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because shrinkage multiplies all \(n\) edge vectors from the best vertex by \(\sigma_n\), its volume ratio is \(V^+/V=\sigma_n^n\). For adaptive shrinkage,
\[
\frac{V^+}{V}=\left(1-\frac{1}{n}\right)^n\longrightarrow e^{-1}.
\]
For the classical choice \(\sigma=1/2\), the corresponding ratio is \(2^{-n}\to 0\). Thus, in high dimension, a single classical shrink collapses simplex volume exponentially, while the dimension-scaled shrink retains a nonzero limiting volume fraction. This geometric statement alone does not imply convergence or superior objective progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive shrinkage retains about an e-inverse volume fraction in high dimension, whereas classical shrinkage retains only two to the minus dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: High-Dimensional Nelder–Mead Behavior

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=[v_1-v_0,\ldots,v_n-v_0]\), \(\delta=\max_{i,j}\|v_i-v_j\|>0\), and \(q=\sigma_{\min}(E)/\delta\). Under the shrink \(v_i^+=v_0+\sigma(v_i-v_0)\), \(i\ge 1\), with \(0<\sigma<1\), one has \(E^+=\sigma E\), \(\delta^+=\sigma\delta\), and \(q^+=q\). Thus homothetic shrinkage reduces scale but neither improves this normalized shape measure nor repairs exact affine degeneracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For vertices \(v_0,ldots,v_n\), define \(E=[v_1-v_0,ldots,v_n-v_0]\) and \(\delta=\max_{0\le i,j\le n}\|v_i-v_j\|>0\). The scale-invariant flatness ratio is
\[
q=\frac{\sigma_{\min}(E)}{\delta}.
\]
Given a geometric tolerance \(\tau_q>0\), call the simplex \(\tau_q\)-flat when \(q\le\tau_q\). It is exactly degenerate when \(q=0\), equivalently when \(\det(E)=0\), so that its vertices are affinely dependent. A sequence of normalized simplices flattens when \(q_k\to 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex is flat when its smallest edge-matrix singular value is small relative to its diameter, and degenerate when that ratio is zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k\ge m\), define
\[
s_k=\max_{k-m\le j<k}\|x_{j+1}-x_j\|,
\qquad
r_k=\max_{k-m\le j<k}|f(x_{j+1})-f(x_j)|.
\]
The search is window-stagnant at iteration \(k\) when
\[
s_k\le \tau_x(1+\|x_k\|)
\quad\text{and}\quad
r_k\le \tau_f(1+|f(x_k)|).
\]
This predicate records negligible movement and objective change over the selected window. It does not by itself imply \(\nabla f(x_k)=0\), Clarke stationarity, or local optimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free model-based descent using controllably accurate gradient approximations, accuracy-parameter refinement, and an Armijo line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $f\in\mathcal C^1$, $x^0\in\mathbb R^n$, controllably accurate gradient approximations $\widetilde g_\Delta$ of $\nabla f$, $\Delta^0,\mu^0>0$, $\eta,\varepsilon_d\in(0,1)$, and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\ge 0$, set $k=0$ and repeat: construct $\widetilde g^k=\widetilde g_{\Delta^k}(x^k)$ from finitely many points. If $\Delta^k<\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}$ and $\|\widetilde g^k\|<\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}$, declare success and stop. If $\Delta^k>\mu^k\|\widetilde g^k\|$, choose $\Delta^{k+1}\le \Delta^k/2$, set $\mu^{k+1}=\mu^k$ and $x^{k+1}=x^k$, increment $k$, and rebuild the model. If $\Delta^k\le\mu^k\|\widetilde g^k\|$, choose $d^k$ satisfying $\left(d^k/\|d^k\|\right)^\top\left(\widetilde g^k/\|\widetilde g^k\|\right)<-\varepsilon_d$ and seek $t^k$ such that $f(x^k+t^kd^k)<f(x^k)+\eta t^k(d^k)^\top\widetilde g^k$. If such a step is found, choose any $x^{k+1}$ with $f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k+t^kd^k)$ and set $\Delta^{k+1}=\Delta^k$, $\mu^{k+1}=\mu^k$. Otherwise set $x^{k+1}=x^k$, $\Delta^{k+1}=\Delta^k$, and choose $\mu^{k+1}\le\mu^k/2$. Increment $k$ and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, MBD constructs a controllably accurate approximate gradient from finitely many sampled points. It stops when both the model-accuracy parameter and approximate-gradient norm are below tolerance. If the model fails its accuracy test, it retains the iterate and target parameter while reducing the model-accuracy parameter. Otherwise it selects a direction making a sufficiently negative angle with the approximate gradient and seeks an Armijo step. A successful search accepts any point no worse than the trial point; a failed search retains the iterate and model-accuracy parameter while reducing the target-accuracy parameter.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde g_\Delta\text{ is a controllably accurate approximation of }\nabla f\text{ constructed from finitely many points}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{These model-accuracy checks, line-search conditions, and parameter updates define the MBD iteration and its success test.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The interpolation set \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\) is \(\Lambda\)-poised in \(B(x,\Delta)\) when interpolation is uniquely defined and its cardinal Lagrange polynomials satisfy \[\max_{0\le i\le p}\ \max_{z\in B(x,\Delta)}|\ell_i(z)|\le\Lambda.\] Geometry-quality control maintains this inequality with a prescribed finite \(\Lambda\), replacing sample points or adding evaluations when necessary. Uniform boundedness prevents the interpolation map from amplifying sampled-value errors without limit.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity alone does not provide a uniform interpolation-quality bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine interpolation in \(\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(Y_\varepsilon=\{(0,0),(1,0),(1,\varepsilon)\}\) with \(\varepsilon>0\). Every \(Y_\varepsilon\) is poised, but the cardinal polynomial associated with \((1,\varepsilon)\) is \(\ell_2(x)=x_2/\varepsilon\). Hence on any fixed modeling ball containing a point with \(|x_2|\ge c>0\), \[\max_x|\ell_2(x)|\ge c/\varepsilon\to\infty.\] Thus unique interpolation does not imply uniformly controlled geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of nonsingular interpolation simplices may become arbitrarily ill poised, so unique interpolation alone is not an adequate geometry certificate.
assumptions_latex: Affine interpolation is performed on a fixed-scale modeling ball containing the sample sets and a point whose second coordinate has fixed nonzero magnitude.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The poisedness constants diverge although every interpolation system remains uniquely solvable.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Descent and geometry are coordinated by enforcing the invariant that every objective trial uses a sufficiently accurate model built from geometry controlled on the same scale \(\Delta_k\). If geometry is inadequate, a geometry-improving evaluation is performed before relying on model decrease; if model criticality is small while \(\Delta_k\) is too large, the radius is reduced and the model rebuilt. With \(\|\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\), this gives \[\bigl|\|\nabla f(x_k)\|-\|g_k\|\bigr|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Descent uses models whose accuracy and sample geometry are certified at the same radius, with rebuilding triggered before criticality decisions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model-Based Trust-Region Algorithm with Fully Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order derivative-free trust-region scheme using fully linear local models and an actual-to-predicted reduction acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f\in\mathcal C^1\), a starting point \(x^0\), an initial radius \(\Delta^0\), fully linear models \(\widetilde f_\Delta\), a model-accuracy parameter \(\mu\), \(\eta,\gamma\in(0,1)\), and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\ge 0\), proceed as follows at iteration \(k\). If \(\Delta^k>\mu\|\nabla\widetilde f^k(x^k)\|\) or \(\widetilde f^k\) is not fully linear on \(B_{\Delta^k}(x^k)\), set \(x^{k+1}=x^k\), set \(\Delta^{k+1}=\gamma\Delta^k\), construct a fully linear model on \(B_{\Delta^{k+1}}(x^k)\), and continue. Otherwise, declare success if \(\Delta^k<\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\) and \(\|\nabla\widetilde f^k(x^k)\|<\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\). If the stopping test fails, solve or approximately solve the model trust-region subproblem over \(B_{\Delta^k}(x^k)\), obtaining \(x_{\mathrm{tmp}}^k\), and compute \(\rho^k=\frac{f(x^k)-f(x_{\mathrm{tmp}}^k)}{\widetilde f^k(x^k)-\widetilde f^k(x_{\mathrm{tmp}}^k)}\). If \(\rho^k>\eta\), choose \(x^{k+1}\) with \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x_{\mathrm{tmp}}^k)\), set \(\Delta^{k+1}=\gamma^{-1}\Delta^k\), and update the model. If \(\rho^k\le\eta\), set \(x^{k+1}=x^k\), \(\Delta^{k+1}=\gamma\Delta^k\), and \(\widetilde f^{k+1}=\widetilde f^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method first checks whether the current model is fully linear and whether the radius is sufficiently small relative to the model-gradient norm. A failed accuracy check shrinks the radius and rebuilds the model. Otherwise, the method stops only when both the radius and model-gradient norm are below tolerance. It then solves or approximately solves the model subproblem and uses the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio: a ratio strictly above the threshold accepts an equally good or better point and enlarges the radius, while a ratio at or below the threshold rejects the trial point, keeps the iterate and model, and shrinks the radius.
assumptions_latex: \text{Fully linear models are available for the required centers and radii}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure generates accepted or rejected trust-region iterations and declares success when }\Delta^k<\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}\text{ and }\|\nabla\widetilde f^k(x^k)\|<\epsilon_{\mathrm{stop}}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse, revalidation, and rebuilding of a derivative-free model as the active center, radius, or sample set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), associate \(m_k\) with a declared model class, center \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), data set \(Y_k\), and a construction theorem whose hypotheses imply the required fully linear or fully quadratic bounds on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\). The manager may release \(m_k\) for a trial only while those hypotheses remain valid at that exact center and scale. After any change of center, radius, data, or model coefficients, it must revalidate the theorem's hypotheses; if they fail, it requests the separately specified geometry or sampling repair and rebuilds the model before releasing another ordinary trial.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Samples Do Not Certify Trust-Region Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary for uniform model-accuracy certification from sampled values alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\subset B(x,\Delta)\) be finite. Without an independently specified function class and corresponding smoothness bounds, agreement of a model \(m\) with all observed values on \(Y\) does not certify fully linear or fully quadratic error bounds throughout \(B(x,\Delta)\): smooth objectives can agree on \(Y\) while having arbitrarily different values or derivatives away from \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching finitely many sampled values cannot by itself certify uniform trust-region model accuracy.
assumptions_latex: No restrictive function class with independently justified smoothness constants is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{f(y):y\in Y\}\) alone does not certify fully linear or fully quadratic bounds for \(m\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Samples Do Not Certify Trust-Region Accuracy

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a poised interpolation set \(Y_k=\{y_k^0,\ldots,y_k^p\}\), a center \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and a target \(\Lambda_{\max}>0\), evaluate \[\Lambda(Y_k;B(x_k,\Delta_k))=\max_{0\le i\le p}\max_{z\in B(x_k,\Delta_k)}|\ell_{k,i}(z)|.\] If this quantity exceeds \(\Lambda_{\max}\), choose a geometry-improving point using a cardinal polynomial with excessive magnitude, evaluate the objective there, and perform a poised sample replacement according to the geometry-improvement procedure. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A geometry-critical regime occurs when \(\chi_k=\|\nabla m_k(x_k)\|\) is small but \(\Delta_k>\mu\chi_k\), or when the sample set is not certified at radius \(\min\{\Delta_k,\mu\chi_k\}\). In this regime the algorithm does not declare approximate stationarity and does not enlarge the radius. It sets a smaller working radius comparable to \(\chi_k\), repairs the sample geometry, rebuilds a fully linear model, and recomputes criticality. This safeguard makes the gradient-error bound small relative to the quantity being tested.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When model criticality is small relative to the radius, the method shrinks the region and repairs geometry before assessing stationarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free interpolation-based trust-region iteration with adaptive relaxation of the wedge pivot threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\), \(\Delta_{\max}>0\), \(\Delta_0\in(0,\Delta_{\max}]\), an initial sample set \(Y_0\), and an initial model \(m_0\). Let \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\), \(0<\gamma<1<\gamma_{\mathrm{inc}}\), \(\epsilon_c>0\), \(\mu>\beta>0\), \(\xi_0>0\), \(0<\kappa_{fcd}<1\), and \(r\ge1\). At iteration \(k\), perform the criticality step of Algorithm 10.1, apply Algorithm 11.3 to select \(u_{i_k}\), and solve (11.1) for \(s_k\). If \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)<\frac{\kappa_{fcd}}{2}\|g_k\|\min\{\|g_k\|/\|H_k\|,1\}\), set \(\xi_k\leftarrow\xi_k/2\) and repeat the step calculation. Otherwise set \(y^{i_k}=x_k+s_k\), evaluate \(f(x_k+s_k)\), and define \(\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)}\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) if \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), or if \(\rho_k>0\) and \(Y_k\subset B(x_k;r\Delta_k)\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Finally perform the trust-region-radius update of Algorithm 10.1, update the interpolation model from the new sample set, and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The modified wedge method halves its pivot threshold and recomputes the wedge-constrained step until the required fraction of Cauchy decrease holds. knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k,&\rho_k\ge\eta_1\ \text{or}\ (\rho_k>0\ \text{and}\ Y_k\subset B(x_k;r\Delta_k)),\\x_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\quad\text{after the fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease test has been satisfied by relaxing }\xi_k\text{ as necessary.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(p+1\) interpolation equations do not determine every coefficient of a quadratic model, a minimum-norm or minimum-change model is defined by \[m_Y=\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\in\mathcal P_2}\frac12\|c(m)-c_{\mathrm{ref}}\|_{\mathcal M}^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad m(y^i)=f(y^i),\quad i=0,\ldots,p.\] Here \(c(m)\) is the selected coefficient vector, \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}=0\) for a minimum-norm model and is the previous coefficient vector for a minimum-change model. The positive-definite squared norm makes the objective strictly convex on the feasible coefficient set; it is commonly chosen to penalize Hessian coefficients.

Suppose $f\in\mathcal C^1$ is bounded below, $\widetilde f_\Delta$ are fully linear models of $f$ with constants $\kappa_f$ and $\kappa_g$ and have the quadratic form (11.7), there exists $\kappa_H>0$ such that $\lVert H^k\rVert\leq\kappa_H$ for all $k$, $\mu_C\in(0,1)$, and all test points $x_{\mathrm{tmp}}^k$ produced by MBTR satisfy (11.9). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\phi+\eta\), where \(\phi\in C^1\) has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(|\eta(z)|\leq\delta\). If \(F(x\pm h e_i)\geq F(x)\) for every coordinate \(i\), then \[|\partial_i\phi(x)|\leq \frac{Lh}{2}+\frac{2\delta}{h},\qquad \|\nabla\phi(x)\|_2\leq\sqrt n\left(\frac{Lh}{2}+\frac{2\delta}{h}\right).\] For exact evaluations, unsuccessful stencils with \(h\to0\) certify first-order stationarity at any convergent sequence of stencil centers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit filtering with bounded Armijo backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The formal outer-inner implicit-filtering iteration using finite-difference gradients and a difference-scale sequence converging to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\{\epsilon_k\}\downarrow0\), \(c,\rho\in(0,1)\), \(a_{\max}\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), and \(x=x_0\). For each \(k\), repeatedly compute \(f(x)\) and \(g_k=\nabla_{\epsilon_k}f(x)\). If \(\|g_k\|\leq\epsilon_k\), end the inner loop. Otherwise, choose the smallest \(m\in\{0,\ldots,a_{\max}\}\) such that \[f(x-\rho^m g_k)\leq f(x)-c\rho^m\|g_k\|_2^2.\] If such an \(m\) exists, set \(x\leftarrow x-\rho^m g_k\) and continue the inner loop; if none exists, end the inner loop. Then set \(x_k\leftarrow x\), increment \(k\), and continue until the termination test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a difference-scale sequence converging to zero, Armijo constants, a maximum backtracking count, and an initial point. At each outer iteration, stop the inner loop when the finite-difference gradient is small at the current scale. Otherwise take the first geometrically backtracked step satisfying Armijo decrease. If no acceptable step exists within the allowed backtracks, leave the inner loop, record the current outer iterate, and advance to the next difference scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\leftarrow x-\rho^m\nabla_{\epsilon_k}f(x)\text{ for the least acceptable }m,\text{ or advance to the next outer scale when an inner-loop stopping condition holds.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of cubic regularization to control trial steps when a value-built model is required only to interpolate the current center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=0\) on \(\mathbb R\). At center \(x_k=0\), the model \(m_k(s)=-k^2s\) interpolates the available center value, \(m_k(0)=f(0)\), but has uncontrolled gradient. With \(q_k(s)=m_k(s)+\tfrac13|s|^3\), the global minimizer is \(s_k=k\). Hence \(|s_k|\to\infty\), the true reduction is zero, and the model predicts reduction \(k^3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cubic coercivity ensures a subproblem minimizer but cannot prevent arbitrarily large, misleading trials when sampled-model accuracy is uncontrolled.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Global Optimality Conditions for the Cubic Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient certificate for global minimization of an unconstrained cubically regularized quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[q(s)=c+g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}Bs+\tfrac{\sigma}{3}\|s\|^3,\qquad B=B^{\mathsf T},\quad\sigma>0.\] A vector \(s_\star\) is a global minimizer of \(q\) if and only if \[g+Bs_\star+\sigma\|s_\star\|s_\star=0,\qquad B+\sigma\|s_\star\|I\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic-model step is globally optimal exactly when it satisfies regularized stationarity and the shifted quadratic matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Global Optimality Conditions for the Cubic Subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coercivity and unboundedness boundaries for power-regularized polynomial models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a polynomial of degree \(r\geq1\) with leading homogeneous part \(m_r\), and define \[q(s)=m(s)+\frac{\sigma}{p}\|s\|^p,\qquad \sigma>0.\] If \(p>r\), then \(q\) is coercive. If \(p=r\), coercivity holds when \(\sigma/p+\min_{\|u\|=1}m_r(u)>0\). If \(p<r\) and \(m_r(u)<0\) for some unit vector \(u\), then \(q(tu)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\). Thus \(p>1\) alone does not ensure a well-posed regularized polynomial subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A power regularizer automatically dominates a polynomial model when its power exceeds the model degree; a lower power can leave the subproblem unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is a finite polynomial of degree \(r\).
For the unboundedness clause, the leading homogeneous term is negative in some direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p>r\Rightarrow q\text{ is coercive},\qquad p<r\ \&\ \exists u:m_r(u)<0\Rightarrow\inf q=-\infty.

notation.meaning: degree-r homogeneous component of the polynomial model

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\) be an oracle whose effective domain is \(D=\{x\in X:\mathcal O(x)\text{ returns usable numerical outputs}\}\). A hidden-constraint encounter occurs when an algorithm requests \(\mathcal O(x)\) at some \(x\in X\) and observes failure, hence learns only that \(x\notin D\). Because no defining function for \(D\) is supplied, this observation does not reveal which implicit condition failed, its violation magnitude, or a direction leading back into \(D\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given successful samples \(S_k\subset X\) and failed samples \(H_k\subset X\), fit a score \(q_k:X\to\mathbb{R}\) using labels \(0\) on \(S_k\) and \(1\) on \(H_k\). Choose a declared threshold \(\tau_k\) and define the inferred failure region by \[\widehat H_k=\{x\in X:q_k(x)\geq\tau_k\}.\] Use \(\widehat H_k\) to rank, screen, or cautiously explore subsequent trials, while retaining oracle evaluation as the definitive test. After each new request, append the observed label and refit. The construction guarantees consistency with the training labels only when the fitting rule enforces it; it does not certify \(\widehat H_k\) as the true failure region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure-region inference fits a classifier to successful and failed evaluations, then uses its predicted failure set to guide trials without treating predictions as certified feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Region Inference

children.title: Feasibility Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Cases where evaluation failure cannot be reliably attributed to constraint violation.

assumptions_latex: The oracle has an unknown effective domain \(D\subseteq X\).
Only finitely many successful and failed evaluations have been observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outside the observed sample, feasibility cannot generally be identified without additional structural assumptions or new evaluations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the identifiability limit caused by finite binary observations of an otherwise unrestricted hidden domain.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S,H\subset X\) be finite disjoint sets of observed successes and failures. For any unsampled point \(z\in X\setminus(S\cup H)\), there exist two effective domains \(D_1,D_2\subseteq X\) satisfying \(S\subseteq D_j\) and \(H\cap D_j=\varnothing\) for \(j\in\{1,2\}\), while \(z\in D_1\) and \(z\notin D_2\). Hence the same evaluation history is compatible with both feasibility labels at \(z\). Unless regularity, geometry, a probabilistic model, or further oracle information is imposed, no rule based solely on that finite history can certify whether \(z\in D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite success and failure observations cannot determine hidden feasibility at an unsampled point unless additional structure or further oracle information is supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Ambiguity

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

assumptions_latex: The objective is a value-accessible map \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\) on the nonempty box \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell\leq x\leq u\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every evaluated trial belongs to \(B\), and the algorithm returns the best evaluated box-feasible iterate when its declared scale or budget test is met.

notation.meaning: finite poll-direction set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected bound-constrained direct-search template with sufficient decrease, duplicate-trial removal, and explicit scale updates.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118
7.6 The mesh adaptive direct-search method p. 132

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\in B\), \(\alpha_0>0\), an expansion factor \(\gamma_+\geq1\), a contraction factor \(\gamma_-\in(0,1)\), a stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and a finite poll-direction set \(D_k\) at each iteration \(k\). Let \(P_B\) denote Euclidean projection onto \(B\). At iteration \(k\), form the set of distinct projected trials \(Y_k=\{P_B(x_k+\alpha_kd):d\in D_k\}\setminus\{x_k\}\) and evaluate its elements according to the poll rule. If some \(y\in Y_k\) satisfies \(f(y)\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\alpha_k)\), accept one such point as \(x_{k+1}\) and set \(\alpha_{k+1}=\gamma_+\alpha_k\). Otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(\alpha_{k+1}=\gamma_-\alpha_k\). Stop when the evaluation budget is exhausted or \(\alpha_k\leq\varepsilon\), and return the best objective value among the evaluated points in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-constrained direct-search method projects each poll proposal onto the box, removes duplicate and unchanged trials, accepts sufficient objective decrease, and updates the poll size according to success.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained Direct Search

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118
7.6 The mesh adaptive direct-search method p. 132

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when projected poll displacements omit a feasible descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(B=[0,1]^2\) with \(f(x_1,x_2)=-x_2\), polling at \((0,0)\) only with projected directions generated by \(\{(1,0),(-1,0)\}\) finds no decrease. Nevertheless \((0,1)\in T_B(0,0)\) and \(\nabla f(0,0)^T(0,1)=-1\), so \((0,0)\) is not box stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection cannot repair an incomplete poll set: a missing feasible descent direction can cause failure at a nonstationary point.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Projected-Poll Stagnation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refining-Subsequence Stationarity for Box Direct Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order accumulation result for projected or feasible polling over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be continuously differentiable near the visited level set in a nonempty box \(B\). Suppose unsuccessful iterates satisfy \(x_{k_j}\to\bar x\), \(\alpha_{k_j}\to0\), and \(\rho(\alpha_{k_j})/\alpha_{k_j}\to0\), and their normalized nonzero feasible poll displacements uniformly cover the tangent cone \(T_B(x_{k_j})\) in the positive-spanning sense required by the method. Then \[0\in\nabla f(\bar x)+N_B(\bar x),\] equivalently \(\nabla f(\bar x)^Td\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_B(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking unsuccessful polls with vanishing normalized forcing and adequate tangent-cone coverage yield box-constrained first-order stationarity at refining accumulation points.
assumptions_latex: f\in C^1\text{ near the visited level set}

notation.meaning: tangent cone of the box at x
normal cone of the box at x

knowledge_statements.title: Refining-Subsequence Stationarity for Box Direct Search

assumptions_latex: The objective is a value-accessible map \(f:B\to\mathbb{R}\) on a nonempty box \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and derivatives of \(f\) are unavailable.
Sampled feasible objective values can be used to construct a sufficiently poised interpolation or regression model on the current trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All sampled and accepted points belong to \(B\), and the algorithm returns the best evaluated box-feasible point when its declared radius or budget test is met.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-constrained derivative-free trust-region template with an explicit actual-to-predicted reduction test.

source_refs.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173
6 Ensuring well poisedness and suitable derivative-free models p. 89

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an evaluated point \(x_0in B\), a radius \(\Delta_0>0\), an acceptance threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), a stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and declared trust-region radius-update rules. At iteration \(k\), construct a sufficiently poised interpolation or regression sample set in \(B\cap\{x:\|x-x_k\|\leq\Delta_k\}\) and fit a model \(m_k:B\to\mathbb{R}\). Compute an approximate solution \(s_k\) of \[\min_s m_k(x_k+s)\quad\text{subject to }x_k+s\in B,\quad\|s\|\leq\Delta_k.\] When the predicted reduction \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\) is positive, evaluate \(f(x_k+s_k)\) and form \[r_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)}.\] Accept \(x_k+s_k\) when \(r_k\geq\eta\); otherwise retain \(x_k\). Update \(\Delta_k\) using the declared trust-region rules and repair the sample geometry when required. If no positive predicted reduction is obtained, retain \(x_k\), repair the model geometry or reduce the radius, and do not form the ratio. Stop when \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon\) or the evaluation budget is exhausted, and return the best evaluated point in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-constrained model-based method fits a local derivative-free model, approximately minimizes it within the box and trust region, and accepts a feasible trial when its actual-to-predicted reduction ratio passes the declared threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained Model-Based DFO

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Named quadratic-interpolation specialization of bound-constrained model-based DFO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: BOBYQA maintains a quadratic interpolation model using box-feasible sampled points, approximately minimizes that model subject to the box and a trust region, judges the trial by observed versus predicted reduction, and replaces interpolation points to maintain useful geometry without derivative evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BOBYQA is a bound-constrained derivative-free trust-region method using quadratic interpolation and geometry-aware sample replacement.

\text{a box-feasible interpolation set can be maintained}

Then the method can attain \(\chi_f(x_k)\leq\varepsilon\) in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) trust-region iterations and \(O(p\varepsilon^{-2})\) objective evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Criticality from an Unvalidated Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of model-only termination without a gradient-accuracy guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(B=[-1,1]\), let \(f(x)=x\), \(m(x)=0\), and \(x=0\). Then the projected model-criticality measure is zero, whereas the true projected criticality is positive. Thus model criticality alone does not certify stationarity without a model-gradient error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inaccurate constant model can declare stationarity at a nonstationary interior point.
knowledge_statements.title: False Criticality from an Unvalidated Model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected first-order target used by model-based trust-region DFO over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable model \(m_k\) at \(x_k\in B\), define \[\chi_{m_k}(x_k)=\left\|x_k-P_B\bigl(x_k-\nabla m_k(x_k)\bigr)\right\|.\] Define \(\chi_f\) analogously. Then \(\chi_f(x)=0\) exactly when \(0\in\nabla f(x)+N_B(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound-constrained model-based DFO measures criticality by the norm of a projected model-gradient step.

Then \(\chi_f(x_k)\to0\), and every accumulation point is first-order stationary for minimization of \(f\) over \(B\).

children.title: Projection Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Use of projection operators to maintain or restore simple-set feasibility.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is the nonempty box \(B=\{x:\ell\leq x\leq u\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection interface maps every proposed point to a uniquely defined feasible point in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto a closed box, expressed componentwise for derivative-free trial generation.

source_refs.locator: 7 Directional direct-search methods p. 115

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the projection interface returns the unique point \[P_B(z)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{y\in B}\|y-z\|_2,\qquad (P_B(z))_i=\min\{u_i,\max\{\ell_i,z_i\}\}.\] Given a feasible incumbent \(x\in B\), direction \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and step length \(\alpha\geq0\), the projected trial is \(y=P_B(x+\alpha d)\in B\), with realized displacement \(s=y-x\). Projection can shorten a step or make \(s=0\), so the interface returns both \(y\) and \(s\) to the search procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection interface clips each coordinate to its bounds and returns both the resulting feasible trial and its realized displacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Directional direct-search methods p. 115

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition under which projection leaves a feasible incumbent unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B=[\ell,u]\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), \(P_B(x+\alpha d)=x\) if and only if: \(d_i=0\) when \(\ell_i<x_i<u_i\); \(d_i\leq0\) when \(x_i=\ell_i<u_i\); \(d_i\geq0\) when \(\ell_i<x_i=u_i\); and \(d_i\) is arbitrary when \(\ell_i=x_i=u_i\). Equivalently, \(d\in N_B(x)\) for the outward polar normal cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection is immobile exactly for outward-normal proposals, with arbitrary components along fixed coordinates.

notation.meaning: outward polar normal cone of the box

review_flags: Includes the fixed-coordinate case omitted by the builder formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Displacement Projection Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic properties of Euclidean box projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty closed convex box \(B\), \(p=P_B(z)\) is characterized by \[p\in B,\qquad (z-p)^\top(y-p)\leq0\quad\forall y\in B.\] Projection is idempotent and firmly nonexpansive: \[P_B(P_B(z))=P_B(z),\qquad \|P_B(z)-P_B(w)\|_2^2\leq(P_B(z)-P_B(w))^\top(z-w).\] Hence it is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box projection has a variational-inequality characterization, is idempotent, and cannot increase Euclidean distance.
assumptions_latex: B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a nonempty closed box}
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Characterization and Stability

children.title: Feasible-Direction Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Use of locally feasible directions within constrained derivative-free search.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is the box \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell\leq x\leq u\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A direction is locally feasible exactly when its components respect all active lower and upper bounds.

notation.meaning: cone of locally feasible directions at x
active lower-bound and upper-bound index sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the tangent cone of a box as the feasible-direction interface.

source_refs.locator: 7 Directional direct-search methods p. 115

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(I_\ell(x)=\{i:x_i=\ell_i\}\) and \(I_u(x)=\{i:x_i=u_i\}\). A vector \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is a feasible direction at \(x\) precisely when there exists \(\bar\alpha>0\) such that \(x+\alpha d\in B\) for every \(\alpha\in[0,\bar\alpha]\). For a box this condition is equivalent to \[d\in T_B(x)=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:v_i\geq0\text{ for }i\in I_\ell(x),\quad v_i\leq0\text{ for }i\in I_u(x)\}.\] A feasible-direction interface accepts \(x\) and returns directions belonging to this cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an active lower bound a feasible direction cannot point downward, and at an active upper bound it cannot point upward.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Directional direct-search methods p. 115

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum Feasible Step Along a Direction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasible step interval for a box-tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B=[\ell,u]\) and \(d\in T_B(x)\), define \[\alpha_{\max}(x,d)=\min\left\{\min_{i:d_i>0}\frac{u_i-x_i}{d_i},\ \min_{i:d_i<0}\frac{\ell_i-x_i}{d_i}\right\},\] with an empty minimum equal to \(+\infty\). Then \(x+\alpha d\in B\) exactly when \(0\leq\alpha\leq\alpha_{\max}(x,d)\). If \(d\notin T_B(x)\), no positive interval \([0,\bar\alpha]\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction has an explicit maximum step determined by the first bound reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum Feasible Step Along a Direction

children.title: Projection–Direction Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between projected trial points plus feasible-direction geometry.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is a nonempty closed box \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), and the incumbent satisfies \(x\in B\).
The search uses Euclidean projection \(P_B\) and a finite direction set \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility holds when, for every sufficiently small positive step length, the nonzero projected displacements positively span the box tangent cone at the incumbent.

notation.meaning: projected displacement associated with direction d and step length alpha

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility is stated as local tangent-cone coverage by the realized nonzero projection displacements.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d\in D\) and \(\alpha>0\), define the realized displacement \(s_\alpha(d)=P_B(x+\alpha d)-x\). The projection and direction interfaces are locally compatible at \(x\) when there exists \(\bar\alpha>0\) such that, for every \(\alpha\in(0,\bar\alpha]\), \[\operatorname{cone}\{s_\alpha(d):d\in D,\ s_\alpha(d)\neq0\}=T_B(x).\] Equivalently, every vector in the local feasible cone belongs to the positive hull of the nonzero realized projected poll displacements. This condition prevents clipping at active bounds from destroying directional coverage, although individual proposed directions may project to zero or yield collinear displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection and polling are locally compatible when, at every sufficiently small positive step length, their nonzero projected displacements positively span all locally feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection–Direction Compatibility

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 A directional direct-search framework p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection Can Destroy Ambient Directional Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient positive spanning need not survive projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(B=\mathbb R_+^2\) at \(x=(0,0)\), let \(D=\{(-1,0),(0,-1),(1,1)\}\). Although \(\operatorname{cone}(D)=\mathbb R^2\), for every \(\alpha>0\) the first two projected displacements vanish and the third equals \(\alpha(1,1)\). Thus the nonzero projected displacements generate only \(\operatorname{cone}\{(1,1)\}\), strictly smaller than \(T_B(x)=\mathbb R_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ambient positive-spanning set can collapse after projection and fail to cover the feasible tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Can Destroy Ambient Directional Coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical box-compatible direction construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{\pm e_i:i=1,\ldots,n\}\). For every \(x\in B=[\ell,u]\) and \(\alpha>0\), discard zero vectors from \(\{P_B(x+\alpha d)-x:d\in D\}\). The remaining displacements positively span \(T_B(x)\): both signs survive at a free coordinate, only the inward sign survives at a one-sided active bound, and neither sign is needed at a fixed coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Signed-coordinate polling remains compatible with box projection because clipping removes only locally infeasible coordinate signs.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Poll Compatibility for Boxes

children.title: Boundary-Active Search Geometry
children.top_down_role: Search geometry when iterates lie near active simple-set boundaries.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is the box \(B=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ell\leq x\leq u\}\).
The point \(x\in B\) may have active bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Active bounds replace the full-space search geometry by a polyhedral tangent cone and its polar normal cone.

notation.meaning: tangent cone of the box at x
normal cone of the box at x
active lower-bound and upper-bound index sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the local first-order geometry induced by active coordinate bounds.

source_refs.locator: 7 Directional direct-search methods p. 115

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in B\), let \(I_\ell(x)=\{i:x_i=\ell_i\}\) and \(I_u(x)=\{i:x_i=u_i\}\). The local search geometry is the polyhedral tangent cone \[T_B(x)=\{d:d_i\geq0\text{ on }I_\ell(x),\ d_i\leq0\text{ on }I_u(x)\},\] together with its polar normal cone \[N_B(x)=\{v:v_i\leq0\text{ on }I_\ell(x),\ v_i\geq0\text{ on }I_u(x),\ v_i=0\text{ otherwise}\}.\] If no bound is active, then \(T_B(x)=\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(N_B(x)=\{0\}\); each active bound removes one outward local search direction and introduces a corresponding normal generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active bounds restrict local search to a polyhedral tangent cone; their outward coordinate normals generate the associated normal cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Active Search Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Directional direct-search methods p. 115

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct cone representation when a box contains coordinates fixed by equal bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\ell_i=u_i=x_i\), then every \(d\in T_B(x)\) satisfies \(d_i=0\), whereas the corresponding normal component is unrestricted: \(v_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(v\in N_B(x)=T_B(x)^\circ\). Thus the coordinate representation of \(N_B(x)\) is \(v_i=0\) at free coordinates, \(v_i\leq0\) at lower-only active bounds, \(v_i\geq0\) at upper-only active bounds, and arbitrary at fixed coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed coordinate has no tangent motion and admits normals of either sign.

notation.meaning: tangent cone and its polar normal cone

review_flags: The immutable seed's displayed normal-cone formula requires nondegenerate coordinate bounds or this fixed-coordinate case separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Coordinate Tangent–Normal Geometry

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolution-dependent conservative boundary geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in B=[\ell,u]\) and \(\varepsilon\geq0\), let \(I_\ell^\varepsilon(x)=\{i:x_i-\ell_i\leq\varepsilon\}\) and \(I_u^\varepsilon(x)=\{i:u_i-x_i\leq\varepsilon\}\). Define \[T_B^\varepsilon(x)=\{d:d_i\geq0\ (i\in I_\ell^\varepsilon(x)),\ d_i\leq0\ (i\in I_u^\varepsilon(x))\}.\] Then \(T_B^0(x)=T_B(x)\), and \(\varepsilon_2\geq\varepsilon_1\) implies \(T_B^{\varepsilon_2}(x)\subseteq T_B^{\varepsilon_1}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating nearby bounds as active produces a conservative cone that shrinks as the activity tolerance grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Active Bound Cone

assumptions_latex: The objective is an extended-real-valued black-box function on \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
A feasible initial point \(x_0\in\Omega\subseteq X\) and finite polling sets \(D_k\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted iterate belongs to \(\Omega\), and objective decrease is tested only at points where the original evaluation is permitted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic directional direct search with an extreme barrier enforcing an admissible domain.

source_refs.locator: Part 3. Direct Search Methods p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F_\Omega(x)=f(x)\) for \(x\in\Omega\) and \(F_\Omega(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. Initialize with \(x_0\in\Omega\) and \(\Delta_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate trial points \(x_k+\Delta_k d\), with \(d\in D_k\), through \(F_\Omega\). If some trial point has a strictly smaller finite value, accept one such point as \(x_{k+1}\) and maintain or enlarge \(\Delta_k\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and reduce \(\Delta_k\). Stop under a prescribed evaluation budget or when \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct search polls nearby points through an infinite-valued barrier, accepts only feasible objective improvement, and reduces the poll size after failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme-Barrier Direct Search

source_witnesses.locator: Part 3. Direct Search Methods p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Clarke Stationarity of Refining Extreme-Barrier Polls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order directional consequence of unsuccessful feasible polls approaching every feasible tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let unsuccessful iterates satisfy \(x_k\in\Omega\), \(x_k\to x_*\in\Omega\), and \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\). Assume \(f\) is locally Lipschitz near \(x_*\), and unsuccessful polling gives \(f(x_k+\Delta_k v)\geq f(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\) for every evaluated feasible poll displacement \(v\). If \(\rho(t)/t\to0\) and, for every \(d\in T_\Omega^C(x_*)\cap\mathbb S^{n-1}\), some further subsequence contains feasible poll directions \(v_k\to d\), then \[f^\circ(x_*;d)\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in T_\Omega^C(x_*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unsuccessful refining polls that approach every Clarke-tangent direction imply constrained Clarke directional stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Every evaluated feasible poll satisfies the unsuccessful-poll inequality with forcing function \(\rho\).
Every unit Clarke-tangent direction is approached by feasible poll directions along a further subsequence.

notation.meaning: Clarke tangent cone to the admissible set

children.title: Extreme Barriers for Unrelaxable Constraints
children.top_down_role: Extreme-barrier treatment of constraints that must remain satisfied at every accepted evaluation.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set of unrelaxable constraints is \(\Omega_u=\{x\in X:c_i(x)\leq0,\ i\in I_u\}\).
The black-box evaluation is defined only, or is permitted only, on \(\Omega_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing \(F_u\) is equivalent to minimizing \(f\) over \(\Omega_u\), while infeasible trials cannot be accepted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-value treatment of constraints that must hold at every evaluated point.

source_refs.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The extreme-barrier extension associated with the unrelaxable feasible set \(\Omega_u\) is \[F_u(x)=\begin{cases}f(x),&x\in\Omega_u,\\+\infty,&x\notin\Omega_u.\end{cases}\] An algorithm using \(F_u\) rejects every trial outside \(\Omega_u\) without comparing its objective value. Consequently, an accepted iterate must satisfy every unrelaxable constraint, and the finite-valued minimizers of \(F_u\) on \(X\) are exactly the minimizers of \(f\) on \(\Omega_u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrelaxable constraint is enforced by assigning infinite objective value outside its feasible set, so every accepted and evaluated iterate remains admissible.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Barriers for Unrelaxable Constraints

source_witnesses.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

children.title: Extreme Barriers for Hidden Constraints
children.top_down_role: Extreme-barrier treatment of feasibility restrictions revealed only through evaluation outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A simulator evaluation at \(x\in X\) either succeeds with value \(f(x)\) or returns a recognized failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimizer can treat recognized evaluation failure as membership in \(X\setminus\Omega_h\) without requiring an explicit constraint formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hidden feasibility is identified operationally by whether the black-box evaluation succeeds.

source_refs.locator: 1.1. What Are Derivative-Free and Blackbox Optimization? p. 3

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_h=\{x\in X:\text{the black-box evaluation succeeds at }x\}\). The extreme barrier for the hidden constraint is \[F_h(x)=\begin{cases}f(x),&x\in\Omega_h,\\+\infty,&x\notin\Omega_h.\end{cases}\] Membership in \(\Omega_h\) need not be described by known functions: it is observed from the evaluation outcome. A trial producing a recognized failure is therefore rejected as barrier-infeasible, whereas a successful trial may enter the method's ordinary acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hidden constraint is represented by the simulator's success domain; recognized failures receive infinite value and successful evaluations remain eligible for acceptance.
knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Barriers for Hidden Constraints

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1. What Are Derivative-Free and Blackbox Optimization? p. 3

children.title: Failure-as-Infeasibility Semantics
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of failed evaluations as infeasible outcomes within extreme-barrier frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-as-Infeasibility Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational semantics, not a claim that every numerical failure is genuine infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the extended response by \[\widehat f(x)=\begin{cases}f(x),&\mathcal{O}(x)=(\mathrm{success},f(x)),\\+\infty,&\mathcal{O}(x)=\mathrm{failure}.\end{cases}\] Failure-as-infeasibility semantics interprets the second outcome as evidence that \(x\) is inadmissible rather than as an unknown objective value. Consequently, an acceptance rule that requires a finite response, or strict improvement over a finite incumbent, rejects a failed trial because \(\widehat f(x)=+\infty\). This semantic equivalence applies only when the oracle's failure classification is reliable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated oracle convention, a failed evaluation is represented by infinite value and is rejected by rules requiring a finite response or strict improvement over a finite incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle call returns either \((\mathrm{success},f(x))\) or \(\mathrm{failure}\).
Failure is stipulated to mean that \(x\) lies outside the admissible evaluation domain.
The acceptance rule requires a finite response or strict improvement over a finite incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under these conventions, failure and an extreme-barrier value of \(+\infty\) induce the same rejection decision.
