children.title: Constraint-Misclassification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits arising when evaluation failures do not reliably identify hidden infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Misclassification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic boundary separating conservative and unsafe constraint misclassification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\in\widehat\Omega\setminus\Omega\), the classifier declares a point admissible although its evaluation is forbidden or undefined. If \(x\in\Omega\setminus\widehat\Omega\), the classifier declares a genuinely evaluable point inadmissible, so the implemented extreme barrier assigns it \(+\infty\) and may exclude a true minimizer. The condition \(\widehat\Omega\subseteq\Omega\) prevents false-feasible classifications but can still remove feasible points. The implemented and true extreme-barrier representations agree at every point of \(X\) exactly when \(\widehat\Omega=\Omega\); unequal domains may nevertheless have coincident minimizers in a particular problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overestimating the admissible domain permits invalid evaluations, while underestimating it rejects valid points and may remove solutions. Domain equality is exactly what makes the implemented and true barrier representations agree everywhere.
assumptions_latex: The true successful-evaluation domain is \(\Omega\subseteq X\).
An implementation classifies points using an accepted domain \(\widehat\Omega\subseteq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inclusions \(\widehat\Omega\setminus\Omega\) and \(\Omega\setminus\widehat\Omega\) identify false-feasible and false-infeasible classifications, respectively, and pointwise equality of the true and implemented barrier representations requires \(\widehat\Omega=\Omega\).

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

assumptions_latex: Relaxable constraints are represented by a violation function \(h:X\to[0,+\infty]\), with feasibility equivalent to \(h(x)=0\).
A nonnegative threshold sequence \((h_k^{\max})\) is maintained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier admits controlled infeasibility and approaches exact feasibility when \(h_k^{\max}\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based progressive barrier for constraints that may be violated temporarily.

source_refs.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), define \[F_k(x)=\begin{cases}f(x),&h(x)\leq h_k^{\max},\\+\infty,&h(x)>h_k^{\max}.\end{cases}\] Initialize \(h_0^{\max}\geq h(x_0)\). Generate derivative-free trial points and accept only trials satisfying the current threshold and the prescribed objective-or-violation progress test. After sufficient progress, choose \(0\leq h_{k+1}^{\max}\leq h_k^{\max}\); otherwise retain or revise the search scale. Stop at the evaluation budget or when the search scale and feasibility tolerance are met, returning the best point with \(h(x)\leq h_k^{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A progressive barrier admits points below a violation threshold, tightens that threshold as progress occurs, and ultimately targets zero violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxable-Constraint Progression

source_witnesses.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of exact feasibility when the admissible violation does not vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(h_k^{\max}\to\bar h>0\) and some \(x\) satisfies \(0<h(x)<\bar h\), then the constant sequence \(x_k=x\) is eventually threshold-admissible but has the infeasible accumulation point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A threshold bounded away from zero can admit a permanently infeasible sequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonvanishing-Threshold Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact set representation of monotone violation-threshold tightening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_k=\{x:h(x)\leq h_k^{\max}\}\), \(0\leq h_{k+1}^{\max}\leq h_k^{\max}\) implies \(A_{k+1}\subseteq A_k\). If \(h_k^{\max}\downarrow0\), then \[\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}A_k=\{x:h(x)=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progressive-barrier admissible regions are nested, and vanishing thresholds leave exactly the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Progressive-Barrier Domains

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Accumulation Points Under Vanishing Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological feasibility consequence of the progressive threshold rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(h\) is lower semicontinuous, \(h_k^{\max}\to0\), and \(h(x_k)\leq h_k^{\max}\) for every \(k\). Then every accumulation point \(\bar x\) of \((x_k)\) satisfies \(h(\bar x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With lower-semicontinuous violation and thresholds tending to zero, every accumulation point of threshold-admissible iterates is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Accumulation Points Under Vanishing Thresholds

assumptions_latex: Constraints are partitioned into unrelaxable and relaxable classes with admissible set \(\Omega_u\) and violation measure \(h_r\).
A threshold \(h_k^{\max}\geq0\) is maintained for relaxable violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All accepted points satisfy unrelaxable constraints, while relaxable violation is permitted only below the current threshold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme enforcement for unrelaxable constraints combined with progressive enforcement for relaxable constraints.

source_refs.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[F_k(x)=\begin{cases}f(x),&x\in\Omega_u\ \text{and}\ h_r(x)\leq h_k^{\max},\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Initialize at \(x_0\in\Omega_u\) with \(h_r(x_0)\leq h_0^{\max}\). At each iteration, evaluate only trials in \(\Omega_u\), reject those exceeding \(h_k^{\max}\), and accept an admissible trial according to the derivative-free progress test. Tighten \(h_k^{\max}\) after feasibility progress. Stop at the budget or prescribed search-scale and feasibility tolerances, returning the best admissible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed barrier enforces unrelaxable constraints exactly while progressively reducing the tolerated violation of relaxable constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Relaxability Progressive Barriers

source_witnesses.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between the extreme and progressive components of the mixed barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_k=\{x\in\Omega_u:h_r(x)\leq h_k^{\max}\}\), a point outside \(\Omega_u\) belongs to no \(A_k\), irrespective of \(h_r\). Conversely, if \(h_k^{\max}\to\bar h>0\), the threshold conditions need not imply \(h_r(x)=0\); points with \(0<h_r(x)\leq\bar h\) can remain admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Threshold changes cannot legalize an unrelaxable violation, while a nonvanishing threshold need not enforce exact relaxable feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Separate Enforcement Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set structure obtained by tightening only the relaxable-constraint threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k=\{x\in\Omega_u:h_r(x)\leq h_k^{\max}\}\). If \(0\leq h_{k+1}^{\max}\leq h_k^{\max}\), then \(A_{k+1}\subseteq A_k\subseteq\Omega_u\). If \(h_k^{\max}\downarrow0\), then \[\bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}A_k=\{x\in\Omega_u:h_r(x)=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tightening the relaxable threshold creates nested admissible sets that always preserve unrelaxable feasibility and limit to joint feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Mixed-Barrier Admissible Sets

assumptions_latex: Objective and violation values \((f(x),h(x))\) are available at evaluated points.
The filter is a finite set of mutually nondominated objective-violation pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted point is not dominated by the filter and improves at least one coordinate by the prescribed margin.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Biobjective filter acceptance embedded in a directional polling method.

source_refs.locator: Part 3. Direct Search Methods p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\), \(\Delta_0>0\), and a filter \(\mathcal F_0\) of nondominated pairs \((f,h)\). Poll points \(x_k+\Delta_k d\). A trial \(y\) is filter-acceptable if, for every \((f_i,h_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), it satisfies \(f(y)<f_i-\gamma_f h_i\) or \(h(y)<(1-\gamma_h)h_i\), where \(\gamma_f,\gamma_h\in(0,1)\). Accept an acceptable trial, delete pairs it dominates, insert \((f(y),h(y))\), and update \(\Delta_k\); otherwise reduce \(\Delta_k\). Stop at the budget or poll-size tolerance and return a least-violation filter point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct search accepts a poll point when it sufficiently improves objective or violation relative to every stored nondominated pair.
knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Search Filter Methods

source_witnesses.locator: Part 3. Direct Search Methods p. 93

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general direct-search locator does not establish the stated objective-violation filter margin, update rule, or returned-point policy. A method-specific direct-search filter source is required before choosing this exact algorithmic version.

assumptions_latex: Derivative-free models \(m_k^f\) and \(m_k^h\) are constructed in a trust region of radius \(\Delta_k\).
A finite filter stores nondominated objective-violation pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted steps provide filter progress, while rejected steps trigger model improvement, radius contraction, or restoration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free trust-region models coupled to objective-violation filter acceptance.

source_refs.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\), \(\Delta_0>0\), and \(\mathcal F_0\). Construct \(m_k^f\) and \(m_k^h\) from sampled values, and approximately solve a model subproblem over \(\{s:\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\}\). Evaluate \(y=x_k+s_k\). Accept \(y\) only if \((f(y),h(y))\) satisfies the filter margin and the relevant actual-versus-predicted reduction test; then update the filter and possibly enlarge \(\Delta_k\). Otherwise improve the models, contract \(\Delta_k\), or enter restoration. Stop at the evaluation budget or radius and stationarity tolerances, returning an acceptable incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-free trust-region method proposes model-based steps and accepts them only when observed objective or feasibility progress passes the filter and model-agreement tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Filter Methods

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited derivative-free trust-region chapter does not specifically support the combined filter acceptance, actual-versus-predicted reduction, restoration, and stopping policy. A source for a constrained derivative-free trust-region filter method is required.

assumptions_latex: The main filter iteration has failed to produce an acceptable trial.
A restoration procedure can seek lower violation without requiring objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restoration either returns a point acceptable to the filter or reports failure under its stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration phase used when ordinary filter steps cannot obtain acceptable progress.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the main iteration cannot find a filter-acceptable trial, initialize restoration at the current incumbent and apply a derivative-free search to reduce \(h\), without requiring decrease in \(f\). Terminate restoration successfully at a point \(x_k^R\) whose pair \((f(x_k^R),h(x_k^R))\) satisfies the filter margin and any prescribed restoration decrease condition. Insert that pair after removing dominated entries, resume the main phase, and update the search scale. Terminate unsuccessfully if the restoration budget or minimum search scale is reached first.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After ordinary filter failure, restoration temporarily prioritizes violation reduction and returns to the main phase once a filter-acceptable point is found.
knowledge_statements.title: Filter Restoration Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

children.title: Feasibility Restoration Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Derivative-free mechanisms focused on recovering acceptable feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic feasibility-restoration subproblem, independent of objective descent and filter-transition policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an admissible search set \(X\) and a violation measure \(h:X\to[0,+\infty]\) with \(h(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points, restoration seeks to reduce \(h\), canonically through \(\min_{x\in X}h(x)\). It succeeds to tolerance \(\varepsilon_h\geq0\) when it returns \(x^R\in X\) satisfying \(h(x^R)\leq\varepsilon_h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration treats constraint violation as its temporary objective and succeeds when the returned point meets the declared feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Restoration Subproblem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic limitation of locally optimizing a violation measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a local restoration method converges to a stationary point or local minimizer \(\bar x\) of \(h\) on \(X\) with \(h(\bar x)>0\), it has not restored feasibility; stationarity for the restoration subproblem alone is not a feasibility certificate for the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violation search can stagnate at a positive-violation stationary point, so restoration stationarity does not guarantee feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is stationary or locally minimizing for }h\text{ on }X
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Violation Restoration Stationarity

assumptions_latex: A violation measure \(h:X\to[0,+\infty]\) satisfies \(h(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points.
A derivative-free search mechanism can compare sampled violation values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful restoration phase produces a verifiable decrease in violation and may supply a point admissible to the main method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic derivative-free phase for recovering feasibility independently of objective progress.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z_0\) at the current incumbent and \(\delta_0>0\). At restoration iteration \(j\), generate derivative-free trials near \(z_j\) and accept a trial \(y\) when \(h(y)\leq h(z_j)-\sigma_j\), for a prescribed \(\sigma_j>0\); otherwise reduce \(\delta_j\). Stop successfully when \(h(z_j)\leq\varepsilon_h\) or when \(z_j\) satisfies the main method's admissibility test. Stop unsuccessfully at the restoration budget or when \(\delta_j\leq\varepsilon_\delta\), and output the lowest-violation sampled point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility restoration runs a derivative-free search on constraint violation and returns the lowest-violation point when feasibility or the restoration stopping rule is reached.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Restoration Mechanisms

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

children.title: Barrier–Filter–Restoration Transitions
children.top_down_role: Interfaces plus transitions among barrier handling, filter acceptance, plus restoration phases.

assumptions_latex: Unrelaxable feasibility, relaxable violation, and objective values are represented by \(\Omega_u\), \(h\), and \(f\), respectively.
Barrier, filter, and restoration phases use fixed acceptance and switching tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state rules preserve unrelaxable feasibility and assign each evaluated outcome to a determinate next phase.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic state machine connecting extreme barriers, progressive barriers, filters, and restoration.

source_refs.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_k\in\{E,P,F,R\}\) denote extreme-barrier, progressive-barrier, filter, or restoration mode. Every trial outside \(\Omega_u\) is rejected in every mode. Use \(E\) when only strict admissibility is allowed; use \(P\) while enforcing \(h(x)\leq h_k^{\max}\); enter \(F\) when objective-violation tradeoffs are admitted through \(\mathcal F_k\). If the active mode cannot produce acceptable progress, set \(q_{k+1}=R\). After restoration finds a point satisfying the active barrier or filter test, return to \(P\) or \(F\); otherwise stop at the restoration limit and output the best admissible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state rule moves among strict barriers, progressive thresholds, filters, and restoration while always rejecting violations of unrelaxable constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier–Filter–Restoration Transitions

source_witnesses.locator: Further Remarks on Direct Search Methods p. 154

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-mode state machine and its switching rules combine distinct barrier, filter, and restoration mechanisms into a specific algorithm not established by the cited locator. A source explicitly defining these transitions is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic outer penalty sequence with explicitly declared derivative-free inner accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\rho_k\uparrow\infty\) and inner tolerances \(\eta_k\downarrow0\). For each \(k\), use a derivative-free solver to return \(x_k\in X\) satisfying \(Q_{\rho_k}(x_k)\leq\inf_{x\in X}Q_{\rho_k}(x)+\eta_k\). Return a feasible incumbent when the prescribed feasibility and budget rules hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing-penalty DFO approximately minimizes successive exterior-penalty objectives with declared inner errors.
assumptions_latex: The inner solver's guarantee is the displayed global objective-gap condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Exterior-Penalty Template

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexact exterior penalty for relaxable equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Q_\rho(x)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left(\sum_i[g_i(x)]_+^2+\sum_j h_j(x)^2\right),\qquad \rho>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exterior quadratic penalty adds squared constraint violation to the objective and permits infeasible trials.
assumptions_latex: The penalized functions are evaluable at infeasible trial points.
knowledge_statements.title: Exterior Quadratic Penalty

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noninvariance of a common scalar quadratic penalty under equivalent constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(g_i(x)\leq0\) by \(a_i g_i(x)\leq0\), \(a_i>0\), preserves feasibility but changes \([g_i(x)]_+^2\) to \(a_i^2[g_i(x)]_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent constraint scaling changes relative quadratic-penalty weights and may change the search trajectory.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Scaling Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Increasing-Penalty Limit with Inexact Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global limit theorem for continuous penalties and vanishing absolute inner error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f\) and \(v\geq0\) be continuous, and let \(F=\{x\in X:v(x)=0\}\neq\varnothing\). If \(\rho_k\to\infty\), \(\eta_k\to0\), and \(f(x_k)+\rho_kv(x_k)\leq\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+\rho_kv(x)\}+\eta_k\), then every cluster point of \((x_k)\) globally minimizes \(f\) over \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing-error global minimizers of increasingly penalized problems approach globally optimal feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\text{ for every cluster point }\bar x.
knowledge_statements.title: Increasing-Penalty Limit with Inexact Inner Solves
Derivative-Free Penalty Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic derivative-free penalty scheme for inequality- and equality-constrained minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given black-box functions \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), define \(v(x)=\lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert+\lVert h(x)\rVert\). Choose \(x_0\), \(\rho_0>0\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_k\downarrow0\), and a derivative-free unconstrained solver. At iteration \(k\), approximately minimize \(P_{\rho_k}(x)=f(x)+\rho_kv(x)\) to obtain \(x_{k+1}\) satisfying the solver's stopping test at tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\). If feasibility progress is insufficient, choose \(\rho_{k+1}>\rho_k\); otherwise retain \(\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k\). Stop when \(v(x_{k+1})\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) and the derivative-free stationarity test for \(P_{\rho_k}\) is met; output \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly minimize a black-box objective plus weighted constraint violation, increasing the penalty when feasibility fails to improve, and stop at approximate feasibility and penalty stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(g\), and \(h\) can be evaluated without derivatives.
The chosen derivative-free solver supplies a specified approximate-stationarity test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is returned only after meeting the prescribed feasibility and penalty-stationarity tolerances.
review_flags: Exact penalty norm and update safeguards vary by method; a constrained-DFO source with a precise algorithm is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but the penalty norm, feasibility-progress test, update safeguards, and stationarity test are method-dependent and have no cited source with an inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct-Search Augmented Lagrangian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer augmented-Lagrangian updates coupled to a derivative-free direct-search inner solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g(x)\leq0\) and \(h(x)=0\), initialize \(x_0\), multipliers \(\lambda_0\geq0\), \(\mu_0\), and \(\rho_0>0\). At outer iteration \(k\), apply a direct-search method to approximately minimize \(x\mapsto\mathcal{L}_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\), producing \(x_{k+1}\). Update \(\lambda_{k+1}=[\lambda_k+\rho_kg(x_{k+1})]_+\) and \(\mu_{k+1}=\mu_k+\rho_kh(x_{k+1})\). Increase \(\rho_k\) when the prescribed constraint-violation test fails; otherwise retain it. Stop when violation, direct-search stationarity, and multiplier-update residuals satisfy their tolerances, and output \(x_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct-search inner iteration minimizes an augmented Lagrangian; outer iterations update projected inequality multipliers, equality multipliers, and the penalty parameter.
assumptions_latex: Function and constraint values are available, but derivatives need not be available.
\(\mathcal{L}_{\rho}\) is a specified augmented-Lagrangian merit function consistent with the displayed multiplier updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies the algorithm's feasibility, derivative-free stationarity, and multiplier-residual stopping tests.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform composite-model accuracy when the penalty becomes unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Errors in the quadratic constraint term are multiplied by \(\rho_k\). Thus bounded fully-linear constants for component constraint models do not imply uniform constants for \(M_k\) when \(\rho_k\to\infty\), unless the relevant products of \(\rho_k\) and component errors remain bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A growing penalty amplifies constraint-model errors and can destroy uniform model accuracy.
assumptions_latex: No compensating tightening of constraint-model errors is imposed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy Transfer to the Composite Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform first-order model accuracy while penalty, multipliers, residuals, and model Jacobians remain bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose uniformly on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) that \(|f-m_k^f|=O(\Delta_k^2)\), \(\lVert
abla f-
abla m_k^fVert=O(\Delta_k)\), \(\lVert c-m_k^cVert=O(\Delta_k^2)\), and \(\lVert J_c-J_{m_k^c}Vert=O(\Delta_k)\). If \(y_k,ho_k,c,m_k^c,J_c,J_{m_k^c}\) are uniformly bounded, then \(|\mathcal L_{ho_k}-M_k|=O(\Delta_k^2)\) and \(\lVert
abla_x\mathcal L_{ho_k}-

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained augmented-Lagrangian model assembled from local derivative-free component models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), component models \(m_k^f\) and \(m_k^c\) define \(M_k(x;y_k,\rho_k)=m_k^f(x)+y_k^{\mathsf T}m_k^c(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert m_k^c(x)\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local objective and constraint models combine algebraically into an augmented-Lagrangian model.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k^f\) and every component of \(m_k^c\) are defined on the current trust region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori first-order certificate for equality-constrained local models with validated derivative errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c(x)=0\), suppose \(\|
abla f(x)-
abla m^f(x)\|\le\epsilon_f\) and \(\|J_c(x)-J_m(x)\|\le\epsilon_J\). For a multiplier estimate \(y\), let \(r_m=
abla m^f(x)+J_m(x)^{\mathsf T}y\). Then \[\|
abla f(x)+J_c(x)^{\mathsf T}y\|\le\|r_m\|+\epsilon_f+\epsilon_J\|y\|.\] Thus \(\|c(x)\|\le\epsilon_c\) and \(\|r_m\|+\epsilon_f+\epsilon_J\|y\|\le\epsilon_s\) certify the displayed primal-feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated model derivative errors convert feasibility and model stationarity into explicit true KKT-residual bounds.
assumptions_latex: The displayed model-error bounds are valid.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free Powell–Hestenes–Rockafellar model for black-box inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(c_i(x)\le0\), \(y_i\ge0\), and \(\rho>0\), define \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\left[c_i(x)+\frac{y_i}{\rho}\right]_+^2-\left(\frac{y_i}{\rho}\right)^2\right).\] Component models give \[M_k(x)=m_k^f(x)+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\sum_{i=1}^m\left(\left[m_{k,i}^c(x)+\frac{y_{k,i}}{\rho_k}\right]_+^2-\left(\frac{y_{k,i}}{\rho_k}\right)^2\right),\] with compatible update \(y_{k+1}=[y_k+\rho_k c(x_{k+1})]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-part terms and projected multiplier updates give the canonical model-based augmented-Lagrangian form for inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint component models are defined on the current model region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_{k+1}\in\mathbb R_+^m\quad\text{and}\quad M_k\text{ is the component-model analogue of }\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y_k).

Model-Based Augmented Lagrangian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free trust-region models used as inner solvers for an augmented-Lagrangian method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\), multipliers \(y_0\), penalty \(\rho_0>0\), and trust-region radius \(\Delta_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), construct interpolation or regression models of the objective and constraints on a sample set near \(x_k\), combine them into a model \(m_k\) of the augmented Lagrangian \(\mathcal{L}_{\rho_k}(\cdot,y_k)\), and approximately minimize \(m_k(x_k+s)\) subject to \(\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta_k\). Accept or reject the trial point using actual-to-predicted reduction, update \(\Delta_k\), update \(y_k\) from constraint residuals, and increase \(\rho_k\) when feasibility progress is insufficient. Output a point meeting prescribed feasibility and model-criticality tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local interpolation models approximate an augmented Lagrangian inside a trust region, while acceptance, radius, multiplier, and penalty updates use evaluated black-box values.
assumptions_latex: Objective and constraint values are evaluable near each iterate.
Each sample set is sufficiently poised for the selected model class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point meets the specified constraint-violation and model-based criticality tolerances.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way constrained-optimality certificate independent of a multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(v\geq0\), \(F=\{v=0\}\), and a feasible \(\hat x\) locally minimizes \(P_\rho=f+\rho v\), then \(\hat x\) locally minimizes \(f\) over \(F\). The analogous global implication also holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible minimizer of a nonnegative violation penalty is a constrained minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Penalties Are Generally Not Exact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar finite-penalty counterexample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x x\) subject to \(x=0\), the feasible solution is \(x^*=0\), whereas \(P_\rho(x)=x+\frac{\rho}{2}x^2\) has the unique minimizer \(-1/\rho\neq0\) for every finite \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic penalty may approach feasibility only asymptotically and need not be exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Penalties Are Generally Not Exact

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local and global finite-threshold exactness of a penalty family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty family \(P_\rho\) is locally exact at a constrained local solution \(x^*\) if some finite \(\bar\rho\) satisfies \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\mathrm{loc}}P_\rho\) for every \(\rho\geq\bar\rho\). Global exactness is defined analogously with global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact penalty reproduces a constrained solution after a finite penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Exactness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exactness from a Local Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient local exactness theorem avoiding an underspecified multiplier qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x:v(x)=0\}\), where \(v\geq0\). Suppose \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(f\) on \(F\), \(f\) is locally \(L\)-Lipschitz, and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\leq\kappa v(x)\) near \(x^*\). Then for every \(\rho>L\kappa\), \(x^*\) locally minimizes \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local feasibility error bound and Lipschitz objective make the violation penalty exact above a finite threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Exactness from a Local Error Bound
Exact-Penalty Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exactness of an ℓ1 constraint-violation penalty under multiplier and regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and \(h_j(x)=0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,p\). Let \(x^*\) be a local solution satisfying a constraint qualification, with KKT multipliers \(\lambda^*\geq0\) and \(\mu^*\). Define \(P_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m[g_i(x)]_++\sum_{j=1}^p|h_j(x)|\bigr)\). If \(\rho>\max\{\lVert\lambda^*\rVert_\infty,\lVert\mu^*\rVert_\infty\}\), then \(x^*\) is a local minimizer of \(P_\rho\). Thus a derivative-free solver may address the constrained problem through function values of \(P_\rho\), without differentiating its nonsmooth penalty term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Above the largest optimal multiplier magnitude, the standard ℓ1 violation penalty preserves a regular constrained local solution as a local unconstrained minimizer.
assumptions_latex: A constraint qualification yielding KKT multipliers holds at \(x^*\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and approximate stationarity measure for a smooth objective over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(f\) be differentiable at \(x\). For \(\gamma>0\), define \[G_\gamma(x)=\gamma^{-1}\bigl(x-P_\Omega(x-\gamma\nabla f(x))\bigr).\] Then \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+N_\Omega(x)\). The declared test \(\|G_\gamma(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-projected-gradient stationarity certificate relative to \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a closed convex feasible set, the projected-gradient mapping vanishes exactly at first-order stationary points.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Projected-Gradient Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth feasible stationarity using Clarke tangent and normal constructions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(f\) be locally Lipschitz near \(x\). Clarke feasible stationarity is the condition \[f^\circ(x;d)\geq0\qquad\forall d\in T_\Omega^C(x),\] equivalently \[0\in\partial_C f(x)+N_\Omega^C(x),\qquad N_\Omega^C(x)=(T_\Omega^C(x))^\circ.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is Clarke stationary when every Clarke-tangent direction has nonnegative generalized directional derivative.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal stationarity for a differentiable objective on a closed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(f\) be differentiable at \(x\). The point \(x\) is Bouligand stationary when \[\nabla f(x)^\top d\geq0\qquad\forall d\in T_\Omega^B(x),\] where \(T_\Omega^B(x)\) is the contingent tangent cone. Equivalently, \(-\nabla f(x)\in(T_\Omega^B(x))^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is Bouligand stationary when no contingent tangent direction gives first-order descent.
knowledge_statements.title: Bouligand Feasible Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Poll Failure Is Not Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between an iteration outcome and a feasible-stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure to decrease \(f\) over a finite feasible trial set \(\mathcal S\) certifies only that no tested trial met the acceptance rule. It implies no feasible first-order stationarity unless the method additionally supplies vanishing resolution, asymptotically adequate coverage of the relevant tangent directions, and the regularity assumptions needed to pass trial inequalities to directional derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsuccessful finite feasible poll is not a stationarity certificate without vanishing scale and adequate tangent-direction coverage.
assumptions_latex: No accepted decrease is observed on \mathcal S
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Poll Failure Is Not Stationarity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier representation at a regular smooth feasible local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\Omega=\{x:g_i(x)\leq0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\) with continuously differentiable data, let \(x\in\Omega\) be a local minimizer. If MFCQ holds at \(x\), then there are multipliers \(\lambda_i\geq0\) and \(\mu_j\) such that \[
abla f(x)+\sum_i\lambda_i
abla g_i(x)+\sum_j\mu_j
abla h_j(x)=0,\qquad \lambda_i g_i(x)=0.\] Without an appropriate constraint qualification, a normalized KKT representation need not follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular smooth feasible local minimizer admits a KKT multiplier representation.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is a feasible local minimizer}

Feasible Stationarity Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order feasible stationarity expressed through tangent and normal cones without requiring computed derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed, let \(f\) be locally Lipschitz near a feasible point \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(T_\Omega(x)\) be the Clarke tangent cone. The point \(x\) has no Clarke-feasible descent direction precisely when \(f^{\circ}(x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in T_\Omega(x)\), where \(f^{\circ}\) is the Clarke directional derivative. Equivalently, \(0\in\partial_C f(x)+N^C_\Omega(x)\). A derivative-free method certifies approximate feasible stationarity by reporting a feasible \(x\) and a nonnegative criticality measure that bounds the greatest detected feasible descent and tends to zero as the polling or model resolution tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is Clarke stationary when every feasible tangent direction has nonnegative generalized directional derivative, equivalently when objective and constraint normals balance.

notation.meaning: Clarke tangent cone to the feasible set

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Stationarity Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity of a constraint-violation measure at an infeasible accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be locally Lipschitz, and define \(v(x)=\lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert_1+\lVert h(x)\rVert_1\). An infeasible point \(\bar x\) with \(v(\bar x)>0\) is violation-stationary when \(v^{\circ}(\bar x;d)\geq0\) for every \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), equivalently \(0\in\partial_Cv(\bar x)\). Thus the pair consisting of positive residual \(v(\bar x)>0\) and a vanishing derivative-free criticality measure for \(v\) certifies convergence to an infeasible stationary family rather than to a feasible stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive constraint violation together with stationarity of the violation function certifies an infeasible stationary limit, not a feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are locally Lipschitz near \(\bar x\).
The violation criticality measure consistently approximates Clarke stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(\bar x)>0\) and \(0\in\partial_Cv(\bar x)\) certify infeasible violation stationarity.

notation.meaning: Clarke directional derivative of the violation function
Clarke subdifferential of the violation function

children.title: Constraint-Geometry Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Geometric constraint configurations that obstruct reliable local progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificate for degenerate smooth constraint geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible point \(x\), let \(I(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\). MFCQ fails at \(x\) if and only if there exist multipliers \((\lambda,\mu)
eq(0,0)\) such that \[\lambda_i\geq0\quad(i\in I(x)),\qquad \sum_{i\in I(x)}\lambda_i
abla g_i(x)+\sum_{j=1}^p\mu_j
abla h_j(x)=0.\] Inactive-inequality multipliers are zero. This homogeneous certificate contains no objective gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero homogeneous combination of active constraint gradients certifies MFCQ degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Abnormal-Multiplier Certificate of MFCQ Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of constraint degeneracy on first-order multiplier certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a smooth feasible local minimizer, MFCQ excludes a normalized Fritz–John system whose objective multiplier is zero, so Fritz–John multipliers can be rescaled to KKT multipliers. If MFCQ fails, an abnormal system with zero objective multiplier may exist; consequently the Fritz–John relation alone need not yield a KKT certificate, and boundedness or uniqueness of KKT multipliers cannot be inferred from the first-order equations alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate constraint geometry permits abnormal multipliers, so Fritz–John stationarity need not reduce to a regular KKT certificate.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraints are continuously differentiable near a feasible local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{MFCQ}(x)\text{ permits }\lambda_0=0\text{ in a nontrivial Fritz--John system}.

notation.meaning: Fritz–John multiplier of the objective gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Fritz–John to KKT Regularity Boundary
Constraint-Geometry Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of Mangasarian–Fromovitz geometry at a feasible smooth constrained point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the feasible set \(\Omega=\{x:g_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,p\}\), let \(I(x)=\{i:g_i(x)=0\}\). Constraint geometry is MFCQ-degenerate at a feasible point \(x\) if either the vectors \(\{
abla h_j(x)\}_{j=1}^p\) are linearly dependent, or no direction \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies \(
abla h_j(x)^	op d=0\) for all \(j\) and \(
abla g_i(x)^	op d<0\) for every \(i\in I(x)\). Equivalently, the usual MFCQ regularity condition fails at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint geometry is degenerate when equality gradients are dependent or no tangent direction strictly decreases every active inequality while preserving linearized equalities.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) and \(h_j\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\).

children.title: Restoration-Phase Failure
children.top_down_role: Failure modes arising while attempting to recover feasibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-relative certificate for one restoration iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\geq0\) be the declared violation measure, let \(\mathcal S_k\) be the complete finite trial set prescribed at iteration \(k\), and let \(\rho_k>0\) be the declared required decrease. If acceptance requires \(v(s)\leq v(x_k)-\rho_k\), then the evaluated inequalities \[v(s)>v(x_k)-\rho_k\qquad\forall s\in\mathcal S_k\] certify failure of that restoration iteration. They do not certify local stationarity, local infeasibility, or global infeasibility without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Testing the complete declared trial set certifies only that the current restoration iteration failed its stated decrease test.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S_k\text{ is the complete finite trial set prescribed by the method}
v\text{ is evaluated at every }s\in\mathcal S_k
review_flags: The certificate is explicitly conditional on the method's declared trial set and acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Declared-Trial Restoration Failure Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Local Violation Minimum Does Not Prove Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp separation between local restoration failure and global infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[v(x)=(x^2-1)^2\left(x^2+\tfrac14\right).\] Then \(v\geq0\), \(v(\pm1)=0\), and \(x=0\) is a strict local minimizer with \(v(0)=\tfrac14>0\). Thus a local restoration method can stall at positive violation even though feasible points exist elsewhere. Global infeasibility requires an independent certificate such as a verified positive global lower bound on \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive strict local minimum of violation can coexist with feasible points elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: Restoration uses local information about a nonnegative violation measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(0)>0\text{ and local minimality do not imply }\{x:v(x)=0\}=\varnothing.
review_flags: Corrects the builder's polynomial, which did not itself establish the claimed positive strict local minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Local Violation Minimum Does Not Prove Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restoration can stall at a positive stationary value of the violation measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\geq0\) be continuous with \(v(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points. If a restoration sequence converges to \(\bar x\), where \(v(\bar x)>0\) and \(\bar x\) is stationary for minimizing \(v\) over the restoration domain, then restoration has reached an infeasible stationary point. Vanishing restoration criticality certifies stationarity of the violation subproblem only; it certifies neither feasibility nor emptiness of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration may converge to a stationary point of constraint violation that remains infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is an infeasible stationary restoration limit, not a feasibility or infeasibility certificate}.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Stationary Restoration Limit
Restoration-Phase Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tolerance certificate that a restoration phase cannot produce sufficient feasibility improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) be the restoration violation measure, let \(x_k\) be the restoration center, and let \(\mathcal{S}_k\) be the finite set of admissible derivative-free trial points at resolution \(\Delta_k>0\). Given forcing function \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(t)>0\) for \(t>0\), restoration fails at iteration \(k\) when \(v(x)>v(x_k)-\varphi(\Delta_k)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal{S}_k\). The evaluable certificate is the list of trial values together with \(\min_{x\in\mathcal{S}_k}v(x)>v(x_k)-\varphi(\Delta_k)\). It certifies failure of that restoration iteration, not local infeasibility of the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration fails at a given resolution when every admissible evaluated trial point misses the required decrease in constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{S}_k\) is the complete trial set prescribed by the restoration iteration.
\(v\) is evaluable at every point in \(\mathcal{S}_k\).
review_flags: Restoration acceptance tests differ across constrained derivative-free methods; a method-specific source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits, and the claim is carefully limited to iteration-level failure. Nevertheless, the complete trial set, forcing function, and strict sufficient-decrease test are method-specific and unsupported by a cited restoration algorithm.

children.title: Geometry-Induced Restoration Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Interfaces where adverse constraint geometry defeats restoration.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Deficient Restoration Model Can Hide Violation Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-geometry failure independent of a particular acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x_1,x_2)=1-x_2\) near the origin, and fit a linear restoration model using only distinct sample points on \(x_2=0\). The sampled values are constant, so the coefficient of \(x_2\) is unidentifiable and a zero-gradient model is consistent with the data, although \(v'(0;(0,1))=-1\). An unsuccessful step computed from that rank-deficient model therefore cannot certify stationarity of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Samples confined to a line can make a violation model appear stationary while hiding normal descent.
assumptions_latex: The model is inferred only from their violation values
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla m(0)=0\text{ may fit the data while }v'(0;(0,1))=-1.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Restoration Model Can Hide Violation Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Restoration Poll Can Hide Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth polling-geometry failure for a violation objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(x_1,x_2)=1-x_1\) at \(x=(0,0)\), polling only \(D=\{(0,1),(0,-1)\}\) gives \(v(x+\alpha d)=v(x)\) for every \(d\in D\) and \(\alpha>0\), although \(v'(x;(1,0))=-1\). Thus failure on a poll set whose positive hull omits a descent direction does not certify restoration stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vertical-only restoration poll misses horizontal violation descent.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Restoration Poll Can Hide Descent
Geometry-Induced Restoration Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of model or polling geometry prevents a reliable restoration-criticality conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a restoration method models a violation function \(v\) on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) using a sample set \(Y_k\). If the poisedness constant \(\Lambda(Y_k;B(x_k,\Delta_k))\) is unbounded, then interpolation errors need not decrease proportionally to powers of \(\Delta_k\), even when \(v\) is smooth. Consequently, failure to find a restoration step from the resulting model does not certify stationarity of \(v\). Likewise, if normalized polling directions fail to positively span \(\mathbb{R}^n\), absence of decrease along the polled directions does not exclude an untested descent direction. Restoration conclusions therefore require uniformly controlled model poisedness or a uniformly positive-spanning polling geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate sample sets or polling directions can hide violation-reducing directions, so unsuccessful restoration cannot certify stationarity without uniform geometry control.
assumptions_latex: The restoration step is generated from interpolation models or a finite polling set.
Stationarity is inferred from unsuccessful restoration trials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without bounded poisedness or positive-spanning poll geometry, unsuccessful restoration does not imply stationarity of \(v\).

notation.meaning: poisedness constant on the restoration region

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Locality Cannot Test Neighboring Integer Fibers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of ordinary small-neighborhood stationarity on a mixed domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equip \(\mathbb R^{n_c}\times\mathbb Z^{n_i}\) with the ambient Euclidean norm. If \(0<r<1\), then \(\|(u',z')-(u,z)\|_2<r\) implies \(z'=z\). Consequently, sufficiently small Euclidean neighborhoods test only the continuous fiber \(\mathcal X_z\) and do not compare adjacent integer assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small Euclidean neighborhoods freeze all integer coordinates, so continuous local stationarity says nothing about neighboring integer fibers.
knowledge_statements.title: Euclidean Locality Cannot Test Neighboring Integer Fibers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint-fiber representation of a mixed continuous–integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_c}\times\mathbb Z^{n_i}\), define \(Z=\{z\in\mathbb Z^{n_i}:\mathcal X_z\ne\varnothing\}\) and \(\mathcal X_z=\{u\in\mathbb R^{n_c}:(u,z)\in\mathcal X\}\). Then \[\mathcal X=\bigsqcup_{z\in Z}(\mathcal X_z\times\{z\}),\qquad \inf_{(u,z)\in\mathcal X}f(u,z)=\inf_{z\in Z}\inf_{u\in\mathcal X_z}f(u,z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed domain is the disjoint union of continuous feasible fibers indexed by admissible integer assignments.

notation.meaning: Continuous feasible fiber at integer assignment z

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Fiber Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-class definition allowing constraints that couple real and integral blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous–integer feasible domain is a nonempty set \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_c}\times\mathbb Z^{n_i}\), where \(n_c,n_i\ge0\). Its points are written \((u,z)\), with real block \(u\) and integral block \(z\); \(\mathcal X\) need not be a Cartesian product because feasibility constraints may couple the blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous–integer domain contains real and integral coordinate blocks and may impose coupled feasibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Continuous–Integer Feasible Domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes independent block domains from coupled continuous–integer feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_c}\times\mathbb Z^{n_i}\), let \(U=\operatorname{proj}_u\mathcal X\) and \(Z=\operatorname{proj}_z\mathcal X\). The blocks are uncoupled exactly when \(\mathcal X=U\times Z\), equivalently when every \(u\in U\) can be paired feasibly with every \(z\in Z\). Otherwise the continuous fiber \(\mathcal X_z\) depends on the integer assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed domain is a product exactly when every projected continuous value is feasible with every projected integer assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal X=U\times Z\iff(\forall u\in U)(\forall z\in Z)\;(u,z)\in\mathcal X.
knowledge_statements.title: Product and Coupled Mixed-Domain Boundary
Continuous–Integer Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-variable search domains containing Euclidean and integral coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous–integer domain is a set \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_i}\), where \(n_c,n_i\geq0\), whose points are written \(x=(x_c,x_i)\). The continuous block satisfies \(x_c\in X_c\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\), while the integer block satisfies \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{n_i}\); additional coupling constraints may restrict the product \(X_c\times X_i\). A derivative-free problem on this domain minimizes an evaluable function \(f:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) without requiring derivatives with respect to \(x_c\); derivative concepts are inapplicable to integer coordinate changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous–integer domain combines real-valued and integral coordinate blocks, possibly linked by constraints, and supports black-box objectives defined only on admissible mixed points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_c}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_i}\) is the admissible mixed continuous–integer search space.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically addresses mixed continuous–integer derivative-free domains.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and mixed continuous–integer domain description fit the leaf, but no source with a specific locator supports the formal definition or its derivative-free interpretation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invalidity of Ordinal Arithmetic on Nominal Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between nominal categories and ordered discrete variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical code \(r:C\to\mathbb R\) for nominal labels is not intrinsic. Relabeling \(C\) by a bijection can change the order and distances of the codes while leaving the categorical domain unchanged. Therefore interpolation, averaging, or nearest-neighbor rules based only on scalar codes are not invariant under relabeling unless an order or metric is supplied separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar codes create arbitrary order and distance for nominal labels unless that structure is declared as problem data.
assumptions_latex: C\text{ is nominal and has no declared order or metric}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{arithmetic based solely on }r\text{ is not invariant under relabeling}
knowledge_statements.title: Invalidity of Ordinal Arithmetic on Nominal Labels

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cardinality of a Finite Product Categorical Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size of a full finite categorical product and an admissible subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each label set \(C_j\) is finite, then \[\left|\prod_{j=1}^q C_j\right|=\prod_{j=1}^q|C_j|.\] Consequently, every admissible subset \(\mathcal C\subseteq\prod_j C_j\) satisfies \(|\mathcal C|\le\prod_j|C_j|\), with equality exactly when every label combination is admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full finite categorical product has multiplicative cardinality, while coupling restrictions can only remove combinations.
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality of a Finite Product Categorical Domain
Categorical Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite or countable labeled choices without an intrinsic Euclidean metric or ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_j\) be a finite or countable set of labels for \(j=1,\ldots,q\). A categorical domain is a nonempty admissible subset \(\mathcal{C}\subseteq\prod_{j=1}^q C_j\). Distinct labels encode alternatives, but their names impose neither an order nor a numerical distance; any neighborhood relation, dissimilarity, or embedding must be specified separately as problem data. A derivative-free objective on this domain is a function \(f:\mathcal{C}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) accessed through evaluations. Search moves replace one or more labels subject to membership in \(\mathcal{C}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A categorical domain is an admissible product of label sets whose labels have no inherent order or distance unless extra structure is explicitly supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{C}\subseteq\prod_{j=1}^q C_j\) defines the admissible categorical search space.

notation.meaning: label set for categorical coordinate j

review_flags: No supplied source locator gives a formal categorical-domain definition for derivative-free optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but no cited source supports the formal domain definition. In particular, allowing countably infinite categorical label sets and prescribing label-replacement search moves require explicit support rather than being assumed from the usual finite categorical setting.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical embedding of a finite categorical coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}\), the one-hot map \(e(c_i)=e_i\in\mathbb R^m\) is injective and satisfies \(\|e(c_i)-e(c_j)\|_2=\sqrt2\) for \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-hot encoding places all distinct labels at equal Euclidean distance.
review_flags: deferred: numerical encoding is primarily owned by the Discrete Embedding Interfaces sibling branch, not by this domain-classification leaf
knowledge_statements.title: One-Hot Representation and Its Symmetry

children.title: Conditional Activation Structure
children.top_down_role: Domains whose active variables depend on prior choices or states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic evaluation of activation rules on an acyclic dependency graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the activation dependency graph \(G=(V,E)\) is acyclic, process variables in a topological order. After all controlling parents of \(i\) have been processed, evaluate its deterministic activation rule using their states and values. For fixed input values and total deterministic rules, this computes a unique active set in \(O(|V|+|E|+C_a)\) time, where \(C_a\) is the total rule-evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acyclic deterministic activation rules can be evaluated uniquely in topological order with linear graph overhead.
assumptions_latex: \text{activation rules are deterministic and total on admissible processed-parent states}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{the active set is uniquely computed in }O(|V|+|E|+C_a)
knowledge_statements.title: Topological Activation Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for hierarchical parent-controlled activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rooted dependency DAG \(G=(V,E)\), an activation pattern \(A\subseteq V\) is ancestrally closed when \[i\in A\implies\operatorname{anc}(i)\subseteq A.\] Hierarchical activation semantics that require every active variable's controlling ancestors to be active must restrict admissible patterns to ancestrally closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When activation is hierarchical, every active variable must have all of its controlling ancestors active.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a rooted directed acyclic graph}
\text{the declared semantics require active descendants to have active controlling ancestors}
knowledge_statements.title: Ancestral Closure of Activation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of recursive activation semantics without a selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two binary activation indicators satisfy \(b_1=b_2\) and \(b_2=b_1\). Both \((b_1,b_2)=(0,0)\) and \((1,1)\) satisfy the equations. Thus cyclic activation rules need not determine a unique active set unless a fixed-point selection rule or another well-posedness condition is declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cyclic activation equations can admit multiple consistent active sets and therefore require additional semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{cyclic activation equations need not determine a unique active set}

notation.meaning: binary activation indicator for variable i

knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Activation Ambiguity
Conditional Activation Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parent-variable choices determine which subordinate variables belong to the active search domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let variables be indexed by \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with coordinate domains \(X_i\), and let \(a_i:\prod_{j\in\operatorname{pa}(i)}X_j\to\{0,1\}\) be an activation rule for variable \(i\). For an assignment \(x\), its active set is \(A(x)=\{i\in V:a_i(x_{\operatorname{pa}(i)})=1\}\), with root variables assigned constant activation one. A conditionally structured domain contains assignments to the active coordinates only, or total assignments modulo the equivalence relation \(x\sim y\) when \(A(x)=A(y)\) and \(x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\in A(x)\). Hence inactive-coordinate values cannot alter feasibility or the objective value represented by an equivalence class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activation rules map parent-variable choices to the set of meaningful subordinate variables; assignments differing only in inactive coordinates represent the same configuration.
assumptions_latex: The dependency relation \(\operatorname{pa}(i)\) is acyclic or otherwise admits consistent activation evaluation.
Each activation rule \(a_i\) is defined for every admissible parent assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x)=\{i:a_i(x_{\operatorname{pa}(i)})=1\}\), and inactive-coordinate differences are semantically irrelevant under \(\sim\).

notation.meaning: binary activation rule for variable i

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses conditional or hierarchical variable activation semantics.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but no source supports this particular activation-rule and quotient-space formalization. The assertion that inactive coordinates cannot affect feasibility or objective value is a substantive semantic assumption that must be sourced or explicitly built into the domain definition.

children.title: Hierarchical Search-Space Structure
children.top_down_role: Nested variable domains organized across multiple decision levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric underdetermination between configurations with different active-coordinate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Metrics \(d_A\) defined separately on strata \(X_A\) do not determine the distance between \((A,x)\) and \((B,y)\) when \(A\ne B\). A cross-stratum metric must additionally specify the cost of changing activation patterns and the treatment of shared and nonshared coordinates. Without these data, cross-stratum nearest-neighbor and trust-region constructions are not canonically defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within-stratum metrics do not determine distances between configurations having different active variables.
knowledge_statements.title: No Canonical Cross-Stratum Metric

assumptions_latex: Each variable has a prescribed domain and may be conditionally active.
Activation depends only on values assigned at ancestor nodes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible search space is the disjoint union of the leaf-specific active-variable domains.

notation.meaning: active-variable domain associated with leaf ell

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted-tree representation of a conditional mixed-variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a rooted tree whose internal edges encode admissible choices and whose nodes introduce variables active whenever the root-to-node path is selected. For every leaf \(\ell\in L(T)\), let \(X_\ell\) be the Cartesian product of the domains of variables active along its root-to-leaf path, including all path-consistency constraints. The hierarchical search space is the tagged disjoint union \[\mathcal X_T=\bigsqcup_{\ell\in L(T)}\{\ell\}\times X_\ell.\] Thus points on different leaves may have different dimensions and variable domains, while every point retains its activation path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical domain is a disjoint union of path-specific subspaces whose active variables and dimension are determined by a rooted decision tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Search-Space Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the hierarchical-domain leaf, but the specialized tagged-union representation has no cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed neighborhood between hierarchical strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Join activation patterns when one controlling choice changes one pattern into the other, and combine these edges with within-stratum neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed hierarchical neighborhood combines within-stratum moves with activation-changing graph moves.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tagged-union decomposition indexed by fixed active-variable sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be the admissible active-variable sets and \(X_A\) the feasible active-coordinate domain for \(A\). Then \[\mathcal X=\bigsqcup_{A\in\mathcal A}\{A\}\times X_A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical space is a tagged union of components indexed by activation patterns.
assumptions_latex: X_A\text{ is defined for each }A\in\mathcal A

children.title: Inactive-Variable Semantics
children.top_down_role: Treatment of variables excluded by conditional domain structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition under which inactive placeholders may be canonically imputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d:E/{\sim}\to E\) select one valid encoded representative of each active configuration, so \(q\circ d=\operatorname{id}\). Replacing \(x\) by \(d(q(x))\) preserves a response \(F\) exactly when \(F=F\circ d\circ q\), equivalently when \(F\) factors through \(q\). Default imputation preserves an optimization problem exactly when this condition holds for its objective and every constraint response.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Default imputation is harmless exactly when all relevant responses are invariant within each active-configuration class.
assumptions_latex: d\text{ selects a valid representative of every quotient class.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F=F\circ d\circ q\iff F\text{ factors through }q.
knowledge_statements.title: Default-Imputation Preservation Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of inactive-coordinate invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in\{0,1\}\) make \(z\in\mathbb R\) active only when \(a=1\), but define \(F(a,z)=az+(1-a)z^2\). The encodings \((0,0)\) and \((0,1)\) represent the same active configuration, yet \(F(0,0)=0\) and \(F(0,1)=1\). Thus the inactive placeholder leaks into the response and different defaults define different encoded problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A response that uses an inactive placeholder assigns different values to semantically equivalent configurations.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Placeholder Leakage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents meaningful configurations as equivalence classes of encoded configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be an encoded conditional domain and define \(x\sim y\) when \(x\) and \(y\) have the same activation pattern and agree on every active coordinate. A response \(F:E\to S\) ignores inactive coordinates exactly when it factors through the quotient map \(q:E\to E/{\sim}\): there exists a unique \(\bar F:E/{\sim}\to S\) such that \(F=\bar F\circ q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A response ignores inactive placeholders exactly when it depends only on the active-configuration equivalence class.
assumptions_latex: \sim\text{ is induced by equality of activation patterns and their active values.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is constant on each equivalence class}\iff\exists!\bar F\text{ such that }F=\bar F\circ q.
knowledge_statements.title: Quotient by Inactive-Coordinate Equivalence

assumptions_latex: An activation map specifies which coordinates are meaningful at each feasible configuration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective and constraint values must be invariant under changes to inactive coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extensional semantics for ignored coordinates in an encoded hierarchical domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) be an encoded conditional domain and let \(A(x)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) denote the coordinates active at \(x\). Inactive-variable semantics requires that whenever \(x,y\in\mathcal X\) have the same activation structure and satisfy \(x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\in A(x)=A(y)\), then \[F(x)=F(y).\] The same invariance is required of each feasibility constraint. Hence inactive coordinates are semantically absent rather than ordinary coordinates assigned influential default values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inactive coordinates carry no objective or feasibility meaning: configurations agreeing on their common active variables must be observationally equivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Variable Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The invariance condition fits inactive-variable semantics, but no source supports the precise objective-and-constraint formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conclusion from an unsuccessful exhaustive poll at one scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\subseteq\Omega\) be a finite feasible poll set. If every \(y\in P_k\) is evaluated and \[f(y)>f(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\quad\text{for all }y\in P_k,\] then no point in that particular poll set achieves the prescribed sufficient decrease. This does not certify local or global optimality unless \(P_k\) exhausts the declared comparison neighborhood and the acceptance threshold implements the corresponding optimality test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completed failed poll certifies absence of sufficient decrease only among the tested mixed-integer poll points at the current scale.
assumptions_latex: P_k\subseteq\Omega\text{ is finite and exhaustively evaluated}

notation.meaning: feasible poll set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Completed Mixed-Integer Poll Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between refining continuous polls and nonzero lattice moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer coordinate, every nonzero lattice displacement \(s\in\mathbb Z\) satisfies \(|s|\ge1\). Hence a scalar poll radius \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\) cannot make nonzero integer displacements arbitrarily small. A mixed-integer convergence statement must separately specify the continuous refining geometry and the discrete neighborhood or scale-dependent lattice moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer moves have a positive minimum size, so continuous poll-radius refinement cannot by itself describe discrete exploration.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Step Scale Boundary

assumptions_latex: The feasible set contains continuous and integer coordinates.
The objective is available through evaluations but derivatives are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an incumbent for which no tested feasible mixed-integer poll step produces sufficient decrease.
review_flags: mixed-integer extension not supported by supplied pattern-search locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible polling version with lattice-preserving integer moves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\Omega\), \(\Delta_0>0\), forcing function \(\rho(t)>0\), and finite polling sets \(D_k\), form \(P_k=\{x_k+s_k(d):d\in D_k\}\cap\Omega\), where each \(s_k(d)\) scales continuous components by \(\Delta_k\) and maps integer components to admissible nonzero lattice steps. If some \(y_k\in P_k\) satisfies \(f(y_k)\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) and retain or enlarge \(\Delta_k\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and reduce \(\Delta_k\). Stop at the prescribed poll-size or evaluation limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-integer pattern search polls feasible continuous and lattice-preserving steps, accepting sufficient decrease and shrinking the poll size after failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Pattern Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A mixed-integer pattern-search source is required. Moreover, stopping at an evaluation limit does not certify that no feasible poll step gives sufficient decrease.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of discrete local optimality on the selected neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1,2\}\), \(N(0)=\{1\}\), and \(f(0)=0\), \(f(1)=1\), \(f(2)=-1\). Then \(0\) is an \(N\)-local minimum but is not a global minimum on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse neighborhood can exclude a better feasible point, so neighborhood-local optimality need not imply global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Local Need Not Be Global

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local optimality relative to a declared discrete neighborhood map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible set \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and neighborhood map \(N:X\rightrightarrows X\), a point \(x^\star\in X\) is an \(N\)-local minimum if \[f(x^\star)\le f(y)\quad\text{for every }y\in N(x^\star)\cap X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A neighborhood-local minimum is no worse than every feasible point in its declared neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Local Minimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improvement-only neighborhood search on a finite feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite. A search sequence that satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\) at every accepted move cannot revisit a point and therefore makes at most \(|X|-1\) moves. If termination occurs only after every point of \(N(x_K)\cap X\) has been examined and none improves the objective, then \(x_K\) is an \(N\)-local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict descent terminates in at most one fewer moves than feasible points, and exhaustive terminal inspection certifies neighborhood-local optimality.
assumptions_latex: N(x_K)\cap X\text{ is exhaustively examined before termination}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\le |X|-1,\qquad f(x_K)\le f(y)\quad\forall y\in N(x_K)\cap X
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination Under Strict Descent

assumptions_latex: Every incumbent has a finite enumerable neighborhood.
Only feasible neighbors may be evaluated or accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination without improvement certifies local optimality relative to the selected neighborhood map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improvement-based local search on an arbitrary finite neighborhood system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in X\) and a neighborhood map \(N:X\rightrightarrows X\) with finite \(N(x)\), evaluate admissible points in \(N(x_k)\). If a point \(y_k\in N(x_k)\cap X\) satisfies \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\), choose one such point according to a fixed selection rule and set \(x_{k+1}=y_k\). Otherwise stop and return \(x_k\). At termination, the returned point satisfies \[f(x_k)\leq f(y)\quad\text{for every }y\in N(x_k)\cap X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete neighborhood search repeatedly moves to an improving feasible neighbor; failure to find one yields neighborhood-local optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Neighborhood Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local-optimality conclusion requires exhaustive examination of the finite feasible neighborhood; the procedure does not state that requirement unambiguously and cites no source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal extracted update and return behavior; the final nonimproving neighbor is returned, so the procedure can return a point worse than its predecessor and does not by itself certify a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeat \(x'\leftarrow x\) and choose \(x\in\arg\min_{y\in N(x')}f(y)\) until \(f(x)\ge f(x')\); then return the final selected \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the current point by a best neighbor at each iteration. Stop when that selected neighbor is not strictly better than its predecessor and, literally as extracted, return the selected neighbor rather than restoring the predecessor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If the procedure terminates, }f(x)\ge f(x')\text{ and it returns the final selected }x;\text{ no local-minimum or monotonic-return guarantee follows.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-neighbor descent over an ordered finite family of neighborhoods for objective minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a current solution $X$ and ordered neighborhoods $N_1,\ldots,N_{k_{\max}}$, initialize $k\leftarrow1$. For each current $k$, compute $X'\leftarrow\operatorname{BestNeighbor}(N_k(X))$. If $f(X')<f(X)$, set $X\leftarrow X'$ and $k\leftarrow1$; otherwise set $k\leftarrow k+1$. Continue until a complete neighborhood sweep produces no strict improvement or the CPU-time limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inspect the neighborhoods in order. If the best neighbor in the current neighborhood strictly lowers the objective, accept it and restart from the first neighborhood; otherwise advance to the next neighborhood. Stop after a complete sweep without improvement or when the CPU-time limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: N_1,\ldots,N_{k_{\max}}\text{ are an ordered finite family of neighborhoods}
\operatorname{BestNeighbor}(N_k(X))\text{ returns a best candidate from the explored neighborhood}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unless interrupted by the CPU-time limit, the algorithm terminates after a complete sweep in which no returned best neighbor strictly improves }f(X).
