knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded description of the organizing idea of variable neighborhood search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Variable neighborhood search successively explores a prescribed set of neighborhood structures, randomly or systematically, to seek different local optima and escape a current local optimum. Its rationale is that different neighborhoods induce different search landscapes and that a global optimum is locally optimal with respect to a neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable neighborhood search explores several predefined neighborhoods, randomly or systematically, to obtain different local optima and escape local traps. Different neighborhoods induce different landscapes, and a global optimum is locally optimal for a neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: \{N_k\}_{k=1}^{k_{\max}}\text{ is a prescribed family of neighborhoods on }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Explore the neighborhoods successively to seek different local optima and escape local traps; no improvement or global-optimality guarantee is asserted.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pseudo-discrete variables and records the relaxation bound, fixing-and-reoptimization heuristic, and its lack of a global-optimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal F_D\subseteq\mathcal F_C be respectively the discrete feasible set and its continuous relaxation for a minimization problem. A pseudo-discrete variable has meaningful continuously relaxed values but is restricted to a finite admissible set for extraneous reasons. Suppose x^c is the unique global minimizer over \mathcal F_C, x_1\in\{d_1,\ldots,d_r\} on \mathcal F_D, and d_s<x_1^c<d_{s+1}. Then F(x^c)\le F(x) for every x\in\mathcal F_D. A heuristic fixes x_1 to d_s or d_{s+1}, similarly fixes other pseudo-discrete variables, and reoptimizes the remaining continuous variables from x^c. A resulting discrete-feasible restricted solution x^r need not be globally optimal; however, if F_D^*=\min_{x\in\mathcal F_D}F(x), then 0\le F(x^r)-F_D^*\le F(x^r)-F(x^c).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pseudo-discrete variable has meaningful fractional values but is restricted to a finite set by external requirements. The continuous-relaxation optimum lower-bounds every discrete-feasible solution. Nearby admissible values may be fixed and the continuous variables reoptimized, but this heuristic need not find the discrete optimum. For a feasible restricted solution, its gap from the relaxation is an upper bound on its discrete suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \min_{x\in\mathcal F_C}F(x)\text{ has the unique global minimizer }x^c
x^r\in\mathcal F_D\text{ when the restricted-solution gap is evaluated}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x^c)\le F_D^*\le F(x^r),\qquad 0\le F(x^r)-F_D^*\le F(x^r)-F(x^c),\quad\text{but }x^r\text{ need not be globally optimal.}

children.title: Rounding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces mapping continuous proposals onto admissible discrete values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity lost by composing a lattice objective with nearest-integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For componentwise nearest-integer rounding, \(f\circ R\) is constant on the interior of every rounding cell. If two cells sharing a boundary map to lattice points \(u,v\) with \(f(u)\ne f(v)\), then \(f\circ R\) is discontinuous at that boundary, independently of the fixed tie rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rounded response has cellwise plateaus and jumps between adjacent cells whose discrete objective values differ.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is componentwise nearest-integer rounding with a fixed tie rule}
f(u)\ne f(v)\text{ for two lattice images of adjacent cells}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\circ R\text{ is cellwise constant and discontinuous at the shared boundary}
knowledge_statements.title: Discontinuity and Plateaus Under Rounding

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise rounding from Euclidean space to the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For componentwise nearest-integer rounding \(R:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb Z^m\), using any fixed tie rule, \[|R(z)_i-z_i|\le\tfrac12\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad \|R(z)-z\|_2\le\frac{\sqrt m}{2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearest-integer rounding moves each coordinate by at most one half and has Euclidean error at most square-root m over two.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ rounds each coordinate to a nearest integer using a fixed tie rule}
knowledge_statements.title: Nearest-Integer Rounding Error

assumptions_latex: The optimizer operates on a continuous relaxation of a discrete domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The black box is queried through the composite map obtained by rounding relaxed points to discrete points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic interface between a relaxed search space and discrete evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a discrete feasible domain, let \(Z\supseteq X\) be a continuous relaxation, and let \(R:Z\to X\) be a deterministic map satisfying \(R(x)=x\) for every \(x\in X\). A rounding interface presents the relaxed optimizer with the composite response \[\widetilde f(z)=f(R(z)),\qquad z\in Z.\] The reported discrete candidate is \(R(z)\). Because distinct relaxed points may share an image, \(\widetilde f\) is constant on each fiber \(R^{-1}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rounding interface maps each relaxed proposal to a discrete feasible point and returns the black-box value at that mapped point.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches a rounding interface and is internally consistent, but the retraction-like rounding assumptions and fiber claim lack cited support.

children.title: Feasibility-Repair Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces correcting mixed-variable proposals that violate domain restrictions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of proposal distinctions under a noninjective repair map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P(z_1)=P(z_2)\), then \[(f\circ P)(z_1)=(f\circ P)(z_2)\] for every objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Consequently, a noninjective repair makes the effective objective constant on every repair fiber; no preservation of proposal-space distance or descent follows without additional regularity assumptions on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Many-to-one repair creates plateaus on its fibers and supplies no general preservation of proposal-space geometry or descent.
knowledge_statements.title: Plateaus Induced by Many-to-One Repair

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Retraction and Idempotence of Exact Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic structure of a repair map that fixes feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\subseteq Z\) and \(P:Z\to X\) satisfies \(P(x)=x\) for every \(x\in X\), then \[P(P(z))=P(z)\quad\text{for every }z\in Z,\qquad \operatorname{Fix}(P)=X.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair map that fixes every feasible point is an idempotent retraction whose fixed points are exactly the feasible points.

notation.meaning: fixed-point set of the repair map

knowledge_statements.title: Retraction and Idempotence of Exact Repair

assumptions_latex: Candidate points may violate integrality or other discrete feasibility restrictions.
A repair map is defined on every candidate that may be submitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All black-box evaluations and returned candidates are feasible after application of the repair map.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic repair wrapper for black-box evaluation of infeasible proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a proposal \(z_k\in Z\), compute \(x_k=P(z_k)\), where \(P:Z\to X\) satisfies \(P(z)\in X\) for every \(z\in Z\) and preferably \(P(x)=x\) for \(x\in X\). Evaluate and return \(f(x_k)\), not \(f(z_k)\), to the proposing optimizer. If the optimizer terminates at \(z_\star\), output \(P(z_\star)\). Thus the effective objective is \(f\circ P\), and feasibility follows directly from the codomain of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repair interface converts every proposal into a feasible discrete point before evaluation and applies the same repair to the final output.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Repair Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The procedural content appropriately describes a repair wrapper, but no source supports this precise interface specification.

children.title: Discrete Embedding Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Representations that place discrete or categorical variables in searchable spaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lack of geometric invariance under arbitrary injective encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every set \(X\) containing three distinct points \(x,y,z\), there exist injective embeddings \(e_1,e_2:X\to\mathbb R^q\) such that \[\|e_1(x)-e_1(y)\|<\|e_1(x)-e_1(z)\|\quad\text{but}\quad \|e_2(x)-e_2(y)\|>\|e_2(x)-e_2(z)\|.\] Thus injectivity preserves identity but does not supply an encoding-invariant similarity geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two injective encodings can reverse which configurations appear closer, so injectivity alone does not justify latent distance-based search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{injectivity alone does not preserve a canonical neighborhood geometry}
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Dependent Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry Induced by a Discrete Embedding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pullback of latent metric geometry to encoded discrete configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an injective embedding \(e:X\to(Z,d_Z)\), define \[d_e(x,y)=d_Z(e(x),e(y)).\] Then \(d_e\) is a metric on \(X\), and any latent neighborhood rule expressed solely through \(d_Z\) induces a neighborhood rule on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injective embedding pulls a latent metric and its distance-based neighborhoods back to the discrete domain.

notation.meaning: embedding-induced metric on the discrete domain

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Induced by a Discrete Embedding

assumptions_latex: Each discrete configuration has a numerical code in a latent space.
The surrogate or optimizer acts on those numerical codes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Predictions on discrete configurations are obtained by composing a latent-space model with the embedding.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding interface from discrete configurations to a numerical surrogate domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a discrete domain and let \(e:X\to Z\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be an injective encoding. A discrete embedding interface represents each \(x\in X\) by \(e(x)\) and induces the surrogate \[\widehat f_X(x)=g(e(x)),\qquad x\in X,\] for a latent-space model \(g:Z\to\mathbb R\). Any latent proposal \(z\notin e(X)\) must be decoded by an explicitly specified map \(d:Z\to X\); only \(d(z)\) is eligible for discrete black-box evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete embedding assigns numerical codes to configurations, enabling latent-space modeling while requiring explicit decoding of off-code proposals.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Embedding Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the embedding-interface leaf, but the injective encoding and mandatory decoding formulation have no cited evidence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Enumeration and simplex embeddings for intrinsically integer choices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrasts finite enumeration with a continuous proportion embedding and states the limitation of the resulting discrete-choice guidance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An intrinsically integer variable is one for which noninteger values have no meaningful interpretation. For discrete variables with finite domains D_1,\ldots,D_q, exhaustive enumeration considers \prod_{j=1}^q|D_j| assignments before feasibility pruning and reoptimizes any remaining continuous variables for each retained assignment, so its cost grows rapidly with q. A one-of-m choice may instead be relaxed to x\in\Delta_m:=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^m:\sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}. The relaxed proportions may guide selection of a discrete alternative but need not identify the discrete optimum. For \lambda>0, the added term \lambda/(\sum_i x_i^2) is minimized over \Delta_m at its vertices and therefore encourages a one-hot choice, although its addition to another objective does not by itself guarantee a vertex solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intrinsically integer variable has no sensible fractional interpretation. Exhaustive enumeration requires the product of the finite domain sizes before pruning and quickly becomes expensive. A categorical choice can instead be represented by nonnegative proportions summing to one; the relaxed solution can guide the discrete choice but does not guarantee the discrete optimum. A positive reciprocal sum-of-squares term favors one-hot proportions, without guaranteeing them in the combined model.
assumptions_latex: \lambda>0\text{ and }\lambda/(\sum_i x_i^2)\text{ is added to a minimization objective}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \#\text{unpruned assignments}=\prod_{j=1}^q|D_j|,\qquad \frac{\lambda}{\sum_i x_i^2}\ge\lambda\text{ on }\Delta_m\text{ with equality exactly at its vertices; the relaxation supplies guidance but no discrete-optimality or integrality guarantee.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An arbitrary symmetric similarity need not be a valid covariance kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=\{a,b\}\), let \(k(a,a)=k(b,b)=1\) and \(k(a,b)=k(b,a)=2\). Its Gram matrix \[K=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\] has eigenvalues \(3\) and \(-1\), so symmetry and positive diagonal entries do not imply positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric similarity with positive self-similarities can still be indefinite and invalid as a covariance kernel.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Category Similarity Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp validity range for an exchangeable categorical covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(|C|=q\ge2\), with \(k(c,c)=\alpha\) and \(k(c,c')=\beta\) for \(c\ne c'\). Then \(K=(\alpha-\beta)I_q+\beta\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\), and \[K\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha-\beta\ge0\ \text{ and }\ \alpha+(q-1)\beta\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exchangeable categorical kernel is valid exactly when its diagonal and common off-diagonal parameters satisfy two eigenvalue inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Compound-Symmetry Categorical Kernel Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite kernel defined directly on category labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite category set \(C\), a categorical kernel is a symmetric map \(k:C\times C\to\mathbb R\) such that every finite Gram matrix \(K_{ij}=k(c_i,c_j)\) is positive semidefinite, equivalently \(\sum_{i,j}a_i a_jk(c_i,c_j)\ge0\) for all finite category sequences and coefficient vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A categorical kernel is a symmetric positive-semidefinite function of category labels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a^{\mathsf T}Ka\ge0\quad\text{for every finite Gram matrix }K.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Categorical Covariance Kernel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving constructions for categorical covariance models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(k_1,\ldots,k_r\) are positive-semidefinite kernels on the same domain and \(a_j\ge0\), then \(\sum_ja_jk_j\) is positive semidefinite. If \(k_j\) is positive semidefinite on \(C_j\), then \(k(x,x')=\prod_{j=1}^pk_j(x_j,x_j')\) is positive semidefinite on \(\prod_jC_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative sums and coordinatewise products preserve categorical-kernel validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure of Categorical Kernels

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical direct kernels for one or several categorical coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a finite category set, \(k_\delta(c,c')=\mathbf1\{c=c'\}\) is positive semidefinite. For \(x\in\prod_{j=1}^pC_j\), the weighted Hamming kernel \[k_H(x,x')=\exp\!\left(-\sum_{j=1}^p\theta_j\mathbf1\{x_j\ne x'_j\}\right),\qquad\theta_j\ge0,\] is positive semidefinite because it is a product of coordinate kernels having diagonal value \(1\) and off-diagonal value \(e^{-\theta_j}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality indicators define a basic kernel, and coordinatewise products yield the exponential weighted-Hamming kernel.
knowledge_statements.title: Delta and Hamming Categorical Kernels

assumptions_latex: The chosen similarity function is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The kernel defines a valid covariance model and hence a kernel surrogate over categorical inputs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite covariance kernels defined directly on category labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite categorical domain \(C\), a categorical kernel is a symmetric function \(k:C\times C\to\mathbb R\) such that, for every \(m\geq1\), every \(c_1,\ldots,c_m\in C\), and every \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^m a_i a_j k(c_i,c_j)\geq0.\] Equivalently, the Gram matrix \(K_{ij}=k(c_i,c_j)\) is positive semidefinite. Using \(k\) as a covariance function defines a valid kernel or Gaussian-process surrogate on categorical inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A categorical kernel is a symmetric positive-semidefinite similarity function on category labels, usable as a covariance model for surrogate prediction.
knowledge_statements.title: Categorical Kernel Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-semidefinite kernel definition is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary when latent coordinates enter only through pairwise distances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e:C\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(k_e(c,c')=\phi(\|e(c)-e(c')\|_2)\). For every orthogonal matrix \(Q\) and vector \(b\), define \(\widetilde e(c)=Qe(c)+b\). Then \[k_{\widetilde e}(c,c')=k_e(c,c')\quad\text{for all }c,c'\in C.\] Hence data depending on \(e\) only through this kernel cannot identify its absolute translation or orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance-based latent category coordinates are identifiable only up to translations and orthogonal transformations.
knowledge_statements.title: Isometric Nonidentifiability of Distance-Based Embeddings

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed and Jointly Learned Latent Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal fitting interfaces for latent-coordinate categorical surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a fixed-embedding model, a prescribed map \(e\) is held constant while surrogate parameters are fitted to \(\{(e(c_i),y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\). In a jointly learned model, \(e\) and other parameters \(\vartheta\) optimize a declared fitting criterion \(J(e,\vartheta)\). When \(J\) is invariant under transformations of the coordinates, normalization or parameter conventions may select a representative, but they must remove only invariances actually present in the chosen model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latent coordinates may be prescribed or learned jointly with the surrogate, with normalization used for genuine nonidentifiabilities.
assumptions_latex: The latent dimension and fitting criterion are specified.
Any imposed normalization is compatible with an invariance of the selected model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (e,\vartheta)\text{ is fitted under the declared criterion and valid normalization conventions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed and Jointly Learned Latent Embeddings

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of distinguishability when categories share a latent coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(e(c)=e(c')\) for distinct categories, then every predictor \(\widehat f(c)=g(e(c))\) satisfies \(\widehat f(c)=\widehat f(c')\). Every induced kernel \(k_e(c,d)=\kappa(e(c),e(d))\) also has identical rows for \(c\) and \(c'\). A surrogate whose category dependence enters only through \(e\) therefore cannot distinguish them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Categories mapped to the same latent point are indistinguishable to every latent-only surrogate.
assumptions_latex: All category dependence enters through e.
knowledge_statements.title: Noninjective Category-Collapse Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a categorical surrogate by composing category coordinates with a Euclidean predictor or kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e:C\to\mathbb R^q\) assign a latent coordinate to each category. A Euclidean predictor \(g\) induces \(\widehat f(c)=g(e(c))\). If \(\kappa\) is a positive-semidefinite Euclidean kernel, then \(k_e(c,c')=\kappa(e(c),e(c'))\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent model maps categories to Euclidean coordinates and applies an ordinary predictor or kernel in that space.
assumptions_latex: \kappa\text{ is positive semidefinite when the kernel assertion is used}
knowledge_statements.title: Pullback Surrogate Through Category Embeddings

assumptions_latex: Each category is assigned a latent Euclidean coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Euclidean kernel on latent coordinates induces a positive-semidefinite kernel on the original categories.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel surrogate obtained from learned or prescribed category coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a finite categorical domain, let \(e:C\to\mathbb R^q\) assign a latent coordinate to each category, and let \(\kappa:\mathbb R^q\times\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel. The latent embedding model uses \[k_e(c,c')=\kappa(e(c),e(c'))\] as its categorical covariance and predicts through a surrogate fitted on the embedded observations \(\{(e(c_i),y_i)\}\). The composition preserves positive semidefiniteness; injectivity of \(e\) is required only when distinct categories must remain distinguishable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent embedding model maps categories to Euclidean coordinates and applies an ordinary kernel or surrogate in that latent space.
knowledge_statements.title: Latent Embedding Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The induced-kernel construction is standard, but no source is cited and the fitted observations use undeclared symbols c_i and y_i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of nominal-category invariance under scalar threshold encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign distinct scalar codes \(r(c)\) to categories and permit only tests \(r(c)\le t\). A single split selects a prefix of the imposed order. Thus, if \(r(a)<r(b)<r(c)\), no threshold isolates \(\{a,c\}\) from \(\{b\}\). Ordinal coding therefore imposes artificial adjacency and cannot express every nominal subset at the same depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding scalar category codes imposes an artificial order and cannot express every nominal subset in one split.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinal-Encoding Split Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Category-Label Permutation Invariance of Subset Splits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation invariance for trees using arbitrary categorical subset predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every categorical node test has the form \(c\in S\), where \(S\subseteq C\). For a bijection \(\pi:C\to C\), replace each test \(c\in S\) by \(\pi(c)\in\pi(S)\). Inputs follow corresponding root-to-leaf paths, and the relabeled tree satisfies \[\widehat f_{\pi}(\pi(c),u)=\widehat f(c,u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subset-split trees are invariant to permutations of category labels when their split subsets are relabeled accordingly.
knowledge_statements.title: Category-Label Permutation Invariance of Subset Splits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy construction interface for a regression tree with nominal predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node containing observations \(I\), a categorical split chooses a coordinate \(j\) and nontrivial subset \(S\subset C_j\), producing \(I_L=\{i:x_{ij}\in S\}\) and \(I_R=I\setminus I_L\). A greedy squared-error tree selects an admissible split maximizing \[\sum_{i\in I}(y_i-\bar y_I)^2-\sum_{B\in\{I_L,I_R\}}\sum_{i\in B}(y_i-\bar y_B)^2.\] Recursion and terminal fitting follow declared depth, child-size, and improvement rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A categorical regression tree greedily selects nominal subset splits by impurity reduction and recursively fits terminal predictions.
assumptions_latex: Only splits satisfying the declared child-size and feasibility rules are admissible.
Stopping and terminal-fitting rules are specified.

notation.meaning: Category subset routed to the left child

knowledge_statements.title: Categorical Subset-Split Tree Fitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate count for exhaustive binary splitting of one categorical predictor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a categorical predictor having \(K\ge2\) labels present at a node, complementary nontrivial subsets define the same unordered binary partition. Hence exhaustive nominal subset splitting has \(2^{K-1}-1\) distinct candidate partitions before child-size or feasibility pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact enumeration of all binary nominal-category splits is exponential in the number of labels.

notation.meaning: Number of labels represented at the node

knowledge_statements.title: Nominal Subset-Split Enumeration Burden

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Base representation of a regression tree over mixed or categorical inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regression tree recursively partitions its input domain by coordinate predicates. If \(\mathcal L\) is its set of terminal leaves, \(R_\ell\) is the region of leaf \(\ell\), and \(\mu_\ell\) is a constant terminal prediction, then \[\widehat f(x)=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\mu_\ell\mathbf1\{x\in R_\ell\}.\] Categorical predicates may directly test membership in a subset of labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree surrogate recursively partitions the domain and predicts from the terminal region containing the query.
assumptions_latex: The terminal regions form a partition of the represented input domain.

notation.meaning: Region associated with terminal leaf ell

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive-Partition Tree Surrogate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes averaging ensembles from stagewise additive ensembles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bagged surrogate has \(\widehat f_B(x)=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^BT_b(x)\), with trees fitted to resampled data and optionally randomized predictor subsets. A boosted surrogate has \(\widehat f_M(x)=\widehat f_0(x)+\sum_{m=1}^M\eta_mT_m(x)\), where each stage fits a tree to a declared residual or loss-gradient target. Their fitting and weighting rules are distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree ensembles may average randomized trees or add stagewise trees fitted to residual-like targets.
assumptions_latex: The resampling, randomization, loss, and weighting rules are declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Bagged and Additive Tree Ensembles

assumptions_latex: The predictor is constructed from recursive partitions of the mixed-variable input domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fitted surrogate is piecewise constant on leaves for regression trees, or an average of such leafwise predictors for ensembles.

notation.meaning: terminal leaves of a fitted tree

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regression-tree representation allowing direct categorical splits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A regression-tree surrogate recursively partitions the input domain using predicates on continuous, integer, or categorical coordinates. If \(\mathcal L\) is the set of terminal leaves, \(R_\ell\) is the region assigned to leaf \(\ell\), and \(\mu_\ell\) is its fitted response, then \[\widehat f(x)=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\mu_\ell\mathbf 1\{x\in R_\ell\}.\] A tree ensemble with trees \(\widehat f_b\) and nonnegative weights \(w_b\) satisfying \(\sum_b w_b=1\) predicts \(\sum_b w_b\widehat f_b(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree surrogates recursively split mixed-variable inputs, predict within terminal regions, and may be averaged in ensembles.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Structured Surrogates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regression-tree and ensemble representation fits the terminal container, but it has no supporting citation.

children.title: Stochastic Noise DFO Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Derivative-free methods and statistical interfaces for deterministic error, stochastic simulation, and sampling-controlled local optimization.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Simulation Optimization: A Concise Overview and Implementation Guide
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Finite-set selection and continuous simulation-optimization taxonomy
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Simulation Optimization: A Concise Overview and Implementation Guide

assumptions_latex: A uniform error bound is known or postulated on the domain of interest.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reported value lies within a fixed deterministic tolerance of the true objective value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform additive-error model for deterministic black-box evaluations.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be the true objective and let the deterministic oracle return \[\widetilde f(x)=f(x)+e(x),\qquad x\in X.\] The oracle has bounded deterministic evaluation error with level \(\varepsilon\geq0\) when \[\sup_{x\in X}|e(x)|\leq\varepsilon.\] No zero-mean, independence, or distributional assumption is imposed. Consequently, repeated evaluation at the same point returns the same value, and every reported value belongs to \([f(x)-\varepsilon,f(x)+\varepsilon]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic noisy oracle has bounded error when its fixed evaluation bias is uniformly no larger than a specified tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Deterministic Evaluation Error

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Robust Pairwise Ordering Under Bounded Evaluation Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp interval test for certifying the true ordering of two evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(|\widetilde f(x)-f(x)|\leq\varepsilon\) and \(|\widetilde f(y)-f(y)|\leq\varepsilon\). Then
\[
|\{\widetilde f(x)-\widetilde f(y)\}-\{f(x)-f(y)\}|\leq2\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently, \(\widetilde f(x)+\varepsilon<\widetilde f(y)-\varepsilon\), equivalently \(\widetilde f(y)-\widetilde f(x)>2\varepsilon\), certifies \(f(x)<f(y)\). If the two uncertainty intervals overlap, the bounds alone do not determine the true ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An observed gap exceeding twice the deterministic error bound certifies the true pairwise ordering; overlapping error intervals do not.
assumptions_latex: Both evaluations obey the same uniform deterministic error bound \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Pairwise Ordering Under Bounded Evaluation Error

assumptions_latex: Each oracle call is modeled on a probability space.
The evaluation noise is integrable conditional on the queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional expectation of the reported evaluation equals the true objective value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise conditionally unbiased additive-noise oracle model.

source_refs.locator: 7 Stochastic optimization p. 161
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an evaluation at \(x\in X\) return \[Y(x,\xi)=f(x)+\eta(x,\xi),\] where \(\xi\) represents oracle randomness and \(\eta(x,\xi)\) is integrable. The noise is unbiased when, for every \(x\in X\), \[\mathbb E[\eta(x,\xi)\mid x]=0,\] equivalently \(\mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)\mid x]=f(x)\). This condition alone does not imply independence across calls, constant variance, bounded variance, or identical noise distributions at different query points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic evaluation noise is unbiased when the expected reported value, conditional on the query point, equals the true objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Stochastic Noise

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Stochastic optimization p. 161
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation preservation under arbitrary dependence among integrable unbiased replications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1(x),\ldots,Y_n(x)\) are conditionally integrable and \(\mathbb E[Y_r(x)\mid x]=f(x)\) for every \(r\), then \(\bar Y_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^nY_r(x)\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[\bar Y_n(x)\mid x]=f(x)\). Independence is unnecessary for this conclusion, although variance reduction requires covariance control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An average of unbiased evaluations remains unbiased even when calls are dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbiasedness of Replicated Sample Means

children.title: Biased Evaluation Noise
children.top_down_role: Persistent systematic distortion in derivative-free evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Replication Does Not Remove Evaluation Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy floor for independent replication of a biased response at a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x\) and suppose \(Y_r(x)=f(x)+b(x)+\eta_r(x)\), where \(\mathbb E[\eta_r(x)\mid x]=0\), \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_r(x)\mid x)=\sigma^2(x)<\infty\), and the centered errors are conditionally independent. For \(\overline Y_m=m^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^mY_r\),
\[
\mathbb E[\overline Y_m-f(x)\mid x]=b(x),\qquad
\mathbb E[(\overline Y_m-f(x))^2\mid x]=b(x)^2+\frac{\sigma^2(x)}m.
\]
Thus replication reduces centered variance but leaves the squared-bias floor unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent averaging reduces variance but cannot eliminate systematic evaluation bias.
assumptions_latex: Centered errors are conditionally independent with common finite variance.
The bias \(b(x)\) is unchanged across replications.
knowledge_statements.title: Replication Does Not Remove Evaluation Bias

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of evaluation bias on conditional means and pairwise objective comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(Y(x)=f(x)+b(x)+\eta(x)\) with \(\mathbb E[\eta(x)\mid x]=0\), then the conditional mean response is \(\mu(x)=f(x)+b(x)\). Hence
\[
\mu(x)-\mu(y)=f(x)-f(y)+b(x)-b(y).
\]
A constant bias cancels from every pairwise mean comparison, whereas an input-dependent bias can change the ordering and minimizers. If \(|b(z)|\leq\beta\) on the region of interest, the distortion of any pairwise mean difference is at most \(2\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bias adds a deterministic distortion to the mean objective; constant bias cancels in comparisons, but input-dependent bias can change rankings and minimizers.

notation.meaning: Conditional mean of the reported evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bias as Objective Distortion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Input-Dependent Bias Can Reverse Objective Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit comparison failure caused solely by differential evaluation bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=0\), \(f(y)=1\), and suppose evaluations have no centered noise, with \(b(x)=2\) and \(b(y)=0\). Then \(f(x)<f(y)\), but the mean reports satisfy \(\mu(x)=2>1=\mu(y)\). Thus minimizing the mean response selects \(y\), although \(x\) minimizes the true two-point objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently varying bias can reverse the true ordering of two objective values even without centered random noise.
knowledge_statements.title: Input-Dependent Bias Can Reverse Objective Ordering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removal of a known deterministic conditional-mean distortion from noisy evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y(x)=f(x)+b(x)+\eta(x)\), \(\mathbb E[\eta(x)\mid x]=0\), and \(b(x)\) is known, define \(\widetilde Y(x)=Y(x)-b(x)\). Then \(\mathbb E[\widetilde Y(x)\mid x]=f(x)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde Y(x)\mid x)=\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid x)\). Replacing \(b\) by a fixed approximation \(\widehat b\) leaves residual bias \(b(x)-\widehat b(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting known bias restores conditional unbiasedness without changing centered variance; an approximate correction leaves residual bias equal to its error.
assumptions_latex: The indicated conditional first and second moments exist.
The correction function is fixed when the corrected evaluation is formed.

notation.meaning: Bias correction applied at the query point.

knowledge_statements.title: Known-Bias Correction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: True-objective guarantee for approximately minimizing a uniformly biased conditional mean response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu(x)=f(x)+b(x)\) on \(D\), with \(|b(x)|\le\beta\). If \(\mu(\widehat x)\le\inf_{x\in D}\mu(x)+\varepsilon\), then \[f(\widehat x)-\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\le2\beta+\varepsilon.\] In particular, an exact minimizer of \(\mu\) has true-objective regret at most \(2\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimizing a mean response with uniformly bounded bias incurs at most twice the bias bound, plus the mean-response optimization error, in true objective value.

notation.meaning: Suboptimality of the returned point for the conditional mean response.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Bias Optimization Regret Bound
Biased Evaluation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-mean definition for noisy black-box evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the evaluation returned at input \(x\in\mathcal X\) be \(Y(x,\xi)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x,\xi)\), where \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is the target objective. Define the conditional bias by \(b(x)=\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x,\xi)\mid x]\), whenever the expectation exists. The evaluation noise is biased on \(D\subseteq\mathcal X\) if \(b(x)\neq0\) for at least one \(x\in D\); it is uniformly bias-bounded by \(\beta\ge0\) on \(D\) if \(\sup_{x\in D}|b(x)|\le\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation noise is biased when its conditional mean differs from zero; a uniform bias bound controls that mean error across the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b(x)=\mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)\mid x]-f(x)\), with biased noise characterized by \(b\not\equiv0\).

notation.meaning: random black-box evaluation at input x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no evidence record or standard-field rationale supports the conditional-bias convention and uniform bound.

children.title: Correlated Evaluation Noise
children.top_down_role: Dependence across repeated, neighboring, or jointly generated evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variance of an Average Under Correlated Evaluation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of equicorrelation on the precision of repeated noisy evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_m\) have common variance \(\sigma^2\) and common pairwise correlation \(\rho\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1m\sum_{r=1}^m\varepsilon_r\right)=\frac{\sigma^2}{m}\bigl(1+(m-1)\rho\bigr),
\]
where positive semidefiniteness requires \(-1/(m-1)\leq\rho\leq1\). For fixed \(\rho>0\), the variance tends to \(\rho\sigma^2\), so the independent-sampling \(1/m\) precision gain fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equicorrelated noise changes the variance of an average, and persistent positive correlation creates a nonzero variance floor.
assumptions_latex: The errors have finite common variance.
Every distinct pair has the same correlation \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.title: Variance of an Average Under Correlated Evaluation Noise

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Covariance Does Not Imply Independent Evaluation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary between uncorrelated and independent evaluation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[-1,1]\), set \(\varepsilon_1=U\), and \(\varepsilon_2=U^2-\tfrac13\). Then both errors have mean zero and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)=0\). Nevertheless, \(\varepsilon_2\) is a deterministic function of \(\varepsilon_1\), so the errors are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation errors may be dependent even when their covariance is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Covariance Does Not Imply Independent Evaluation Noise

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variance of a General Correlated Evaluation Average
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covariance-matrix expression for averaging an arbitrary dependent evaluation batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a centered noise vector \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R^m\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and weights \(w\) satisfying \(\mathbf1^\top w=1\), \[\operatorname{Var}(w^\top\varepsilon)=w^\top\Sigma w.\] For the ordinary average this is \(m^{-2}\mathbf1^\top\Sigma\mathbf1\). Thus mean-square consistency of the average requires this normalized covariance sum to vanish; bounded marginal variances alone do not suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The precision of a weighted average under correlated noise is governed by a quadratic form in the full covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Variance of a General Correlated Evaluation Average

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covariance-aware aggregation of repeated evaluations having a common conditional mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[Y]=\mu\mathbf1\) and have covariance \(\Sigma\succ0\). Among linear unbiased estimators \(w^TY\) with \(\mathbf1^Tw=1\), the unique minimum-variance weights are \[w_* = \frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1}{\mathbf1^T\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1},\] and the minimum variance is \((\mathbf1^T\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For correlated repeated evaluations with known nonsingular covariance, generalized least-squares weights give the minimum-variance linear unbiased aggregate.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Variance Linear Unbiased Aggregation
Correlated Evaluation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise conditional covariance of black-box evaluation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For evaluations \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) and \(Y_j=f(x_j)+\varepsilon_j\), assume finite conditional second moments. Their evaluation noises are conditionally correlated when \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j\mid x_i,x_j)\neq0\). For a batch \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), the conditional noise covariance matrix is \(\Sigma_{ij}=\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j\mid x_1,\ldots,x_m)\). Independent evaluation noise implies off-diagonal entries vanish, whereas nonzero off-diagonal entries encode correlation induced by shared randomness, temporal dependence, or another coupling mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation noise is correlated when errors from distinct evaluations have nonzero conditional covariance; a covariance matrix describes the dependence within a batch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covariance-based definition fits the leaf and is internally consistent, but it has no cited source or standard-field rationale.

children.title: Bias–Correlation Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Combined effects of systematic distortion and dependent observations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differential-Bias Floor Under Replicated Paired Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of repeated paired comparisons when differential bias and within-pair covariance coexist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_r=(Y_{1r}-Y_{2r})-(f(x_1)-f(x_2))=(b_1-b_2)+(\eta_{1r}-\eta_{2r})\). Suppose pairs are conditionally independent across \(r\), and each centered pair has variances \(\sigma_1^2,\sigma_2^2\) and covariance \(c_{12}\). For \(\overline E_m=m^{-1}\sum_rE_r\),
\[
\mathbb E[\overline E_m^2\mid x_1,x_2]=(b_1-b_2)^2+\frac{\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2-2c_{12}}m.
\]
Thus favorable correlation reduces the sampling term but cannot remove nonzero differential bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated paired comparisons average away centered correlated noise at rate one over the replication count but retain a differential-bias floor.
assumptions_latex: Pairs are conditionally independent across replications.
Each centered pair has finite common second moments.

notation.meaning: Average error of m paired comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Differential-Bias Floor Under Replicated Paired Comparisons

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covariance Bounds for Biased Paired Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible covariance range and its effect on the centered component of comparison error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For centered errors with standard deviations \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\), Cauchy–Schwarz gives \(-\sigma_1\sigma_2\le c_{12}\le\sigma_1\sigma_2\). Therefore \[(\sigma_1-\sigma_2)^2\le\operatorname{Var}(\eta_1-\eta_2)\le(\sigma_1+\sigma_2)^2.\] The total paired-comparison MSE adds the unchanged term \((b_1-b_2)^2\). Positive covariance decreases centered variance, while negative covariance increases it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covariance moves paired-comparison variance between sharp bounds but cannot alter the squared differential-bias component.
assumptions_latex: The centered errors have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.title: Covariance Bounds for Biased Paired Comparisons

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Sided Error Bound for a Biased Correlated Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-based bound on an erroneous sign in a paired noisy comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=Y_1-Y_2\), \(\delta=f(x_1)-f(x_2)\), \(d=b_1-b_2\), and \(v=\operatorname{Var}(D)=\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2-2c_{12}\). If \(\delta>0\) and \(\delta+d>0\), Cantelli's inequality gives \[\mathbb P(D\le0)\le\frac{v}{v+(\delta+d)^2}.\] If \(\delta<0\) and \(\delta+d<0\), then \(\mathbb P(D\ge0)\le v/[v+(\delta+d)^2]\). No analogous true-sign guarantee follows from this bound when differential bias reverses the sign of the mean comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differential bias shifts the comparison margin and covariance determines its variance; when the shifted mean retains the true sign, these moments bound the wrong-sign probability.
assumptions_latex: The paired comparison has finite second moments.
The true difference and shifted mean difference are nonzero and have the same sign.

notation.meaning: Variance of the paired noisy difference.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Error Bound for a Biased Correlated Comparison
Bias–Correlation Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean–covariance decomposition of comparison error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two evaluations \(Y_i=f(x_i)+b_i+\eta_i\), let \(\mathbb E[\eta_i\mid x_1,x_2]=0\), \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_i\mid x_1,x_2)=\sigma_i^2\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_1,\eta_2\mid x_1,x_2)=c_{12}\). Then the noisy difference \(D=Y_1-Y_2\) has conditional bias \(b_1-b_2\) relative to \(f(x_1)-f(x_2)\) and conditional variance \(\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2-2c_{12}\). Consequently, its conditional mean-squared comparison error is \((b_1-b_2)^2+\sigma_1^2+\sigma_2^2-2c_{12}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Comparison error separates into squared differential bias and a variance term modified by covariance; positive correlation reduces variance of paired differences.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mean–covariance decomposition is correct under the stated conditional moments and fits this interaction leaf, but the representation lacks source support.

children.title: Input-Dependent Noise Scale
children.top_down_role: Evaluation variance that changes across the search domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise precision law for independent replicated evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1(x),\ldots,Y_n(x)\) are conditionally independent with common conditional mean \(m(x)\) and variance \(\sigma(x)^2<\infty\), then \(\mathbb E[\bar Y_n(x)\mid x]=m(x)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_n(x)\mid x)=\sigma(x)^2/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent replications, sample-mean precision depends directly on the local noise variance.
assumptions_latex: The replications are conditionally independent at fixed \(x\).

notation.meaning: mean of n replicated evaluations at x

knowledge_statements.title: Replication Precision Under Input-Dependent Variance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Finite Variance Need Not Be Uniformly Bounded
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform scale control under pointwise heteroscedasticity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(0,1]\), \(Z\sim N(0,1)\), and \(Y(x)=f(x)+x^{-1}Z\). Then \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid x)=x^{-2}<\infty\) for every \(x\in D\), but \(\sup_{x\in D}\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid x)=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite variance at every query point does not imply a uniform variance bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Finite Variance Need Not Be Uniformly Bounded

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconstant conditional variance, with boundedness and regularity separated as additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y(x,\xi)\) has finite conditional variance for every \(x\in D\), and define \(\sigma(x)=\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,\xi)\mid x)}\). The oracle is heteroscedastic on \(D\) when \(x\mapsto\sigma(x)^2\) is not constant. A bound \(\sup_{x\in R}\sigma(x)<\infty\) on \(R\subseteq D\), or continuity or Lipschitz continuity of \(\sigma\), is an additional assumption not implied by heteroscedasticity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heteroscedasticity means that conditional variance changes with the query point; boundedness and regularity must be imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\) is heteroscedastic on \(D\iff x\mapsto\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,\xi)\mid x)\) is nonconstant.

notation.meaning: conditional standard deviation at input x

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Heteroscedasticity
Input-Dependent Noise Scale
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heteroscedastic scale model for stochastic evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stochastic evaluation model has input-dependent noise scale on \(D\subseteq\mathcal X\) if it can be written as \(Y(x,\xi)=f(x)+b(x)+\sigma(x)Z(x,\xi)\), where \(\mathbb E[Z(x,\xi)\mid x]=0\), \(\mathbb E[Z(x,\xi)^2\mid x]=1\), and \(\sigma:D\to[0,\infty)\) is not constant. Equivalently, \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,\xi)\mid x)=\sigma(x)^2\). A local scale bound on a region \(R\subseteq D\) is \(\sup_{x\in R}\sigma(x)\le\bar\sigma_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heteroscedastic evaluations have noise variance that changes with the input; local scale bounds quantify variability over the region sampled by a DFO method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,\xi)\mid x)=\sigma(x)^2\), with heteroscedasticity when \(\sigma\) is nonconstant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standardized heteroscedastic model is coherent and appropriate for the leaf, but no source establishes the selected definition or its local-bound formulation.

children.title: Heavy-Tailed Evaluation Noise
children.top_down_role: Evaluation errors with substantial extreme-event risk.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Fractional Moment Does Not Imply Finite Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp moment boundary for heavy-tailed evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(W>t)=t^{-\alpha}\) for \(t\ge1\), where \(1<p<\alpha<2\), and set \(\varepsilon=W-\mathbb EW\). Then \(\mathbb E\varepsilon=0\), \(\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^p<\infty\), and \(\mathbb E\varepsilon^2=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A centered Pareto error can have a finite fractional moment while having infinite variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Fractional Moment Does Not Imply Finite Variance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fractional Moments and Polynomial Tails Are Not Equivalent Conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary among common heavy-tail formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb P(|\varepsilon|>t)\le Ct^{-\alpha}\) for all \(t\ge t_0\), then \(\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^q<\infty\) for every \(0<q<\alpha\). Conversely, \(\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^p<\infty\) implies only the Markov bound \(\mathbb P(|\varepsilon|>t)\le \mathbb E|\varepsilon|^p t^{-p}\), and need not imply a bound with any prescribed exponent \(\alpha>p\) or regular variation. Thus fractional-moment, polynomial-tail, and regular-variation regimes are distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial-tail control yields lower-order moments, while a finite fractional moment does not determine a stronger tail exponent or regular variation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(|\varepsilon|>t)\le Ct^{-\alpha}\Rightarrow \mathbb E|\varepsilon|^q<\infty\) for \(q<\alpha\), but the converse formulations are not equivalent.

notation.meaning: moment order below the tail exponent

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Moments and Polynomial Tails Are Not Equivalent Conventions
Heavy-Tailed Evaluation Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite fractional-moment model without a variance assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x,\xi)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x,\xi)\). The centered evaluation noise belongs to a heavy-tail moment regime of order \(p\in(1,2)\) on \(D\subseteq\mathcal X\) if \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x,\xi)\mid x]=0\) and \(\sup_{x\in D}\mathbb E[|\varepsilon(x,\xi)|^p\mid x]\le M_p<\infty\), while no finite second moment is assumed. Thus estimators or decision rules requiring uniformly bounded variance are not justified by this regime alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heavy-tailed evaluation noise may have a bounded fractional moment but no assumed finite variance, so variance-based decisions require additional protection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in D}\mathbb E[|\varepsilon(x,\xi)|^p\mid x]\le M_p\), without requiring \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x,\xi)^2\mid x]<\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A finite p-th-moment regime with p in (1,2) is a legitimate heavy-tail model, but it is only one convention; an exact source is required to justify this terminal formulation.

children.title: Combined Robustness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Robust evaluation management under variable scale plus extreme observations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Component Conditions Do Not Give Uniform Combined Robustness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform joint control when scale and fractional moments are bounded only pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\mathbb N\), \(\sigma(x)=1\), and \(Y(x)=f(x)+Z_x\), where \(\mathbb E Z_x=0\) and \(\mathbb E|Z_x|^p=x\) for fixed \(p\in(1,2)\). Every input has a finite \(p\)-th noise moment, but \(\sup_{x\in D}\mathbb E|Y(x)-f(x)|^p=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise finite scale and fractional moments do not imply a uniform combined moment bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Component Conditions Do Not Give Uniform Combined Robustness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint uniform scale and standardized-moment condition, distinguished from its consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in(1,2]\). A centered oracle \(Y(x,\xi)=f(x)+\sigma(x)Z(x,\xi)\) satisfies a uniform heteroscedastic \(p\)-moment regime on \(D\) if \(\mathbb E[Z(x,\xi)\mid x]=0\), \(\sup_{x\in D}\mathbb E[|Z(x,\xi)|^p\mid x]\le M_p<\infty\), and \(\sup_{x\in D}\sigma(x)\le\bar\sigma<\infty\). These assumptions imply \(\mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)\mid x]=f(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[|Y(x,\xi)-f(x)|^p\mid x]\le M_p\sigma(x)^p\le M_p\bar\sigma^p\). The resulting moment inequality alone does not recover centering, the scale bound, or the standardized representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform scale and standardized fractional-moment bounds imply a uniform raw-noise moment bound, but the latter is not equivalent to the full joint regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)\mid x]=f(x)\) and \(\sup_{x\in D}\mathbb E|Y(x,\xi)-f(x)|^p\le M_p\bar\sigma^p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Heteroscedastic Fractional-Moment Regime
Combined Robustness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint heteroscedastic and heavy-tail moment condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A centered evaluation model \(Y(x,\xi)=f(x)+\sigma(x)Z(x,\xi)\) satisfies the combined heteroscedastic heavy-tail condition of order \(p\in(1,2]\) on \(D\) when \(\mathbb E[Z(x,\xi)\mid x]=0\), \(\sup_{x\in D}\mathbb E[|Z(x,\xi)|^p\mid x]\le M_p\), and \(0\le\sigma(x)\le\bar\sigma\). Equivalently, \(\mathbb E[|Y(x,\xi)-f(x)|^p\mid x]\le M_p\sigma(x)^p\). The condition permits input-varying scale and, when \(p<2\), does not impose finite variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The combined regime permits input-varying noise scale while controlling only a uniform fractional moment of standardized noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[|Y(x,\xi)-f(x)|^p\mid x]\le M_p\sigma(x)^p\) for every \(x\in D\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moment inequality follows from the model and standardized-moment bound, but it is not equivalent to all stated conditions because it does not recover centering, the scale bound, or the standardized-noise formulation. Source alignment is also absent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbiased Paired-Difference Estimation with Common Random Numbers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal unbiasedness and replication variance of a common-random-number comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_r=Y(x,\xi_r)-Y(x',\xi_r)\), where \(\xi_r\) are independent across replications and \(\mathbb E[Y(z,\xi)]=F(z)\) for \(z\in\{x,x'\}\). Then
\[
\mathbb E[\overline D_m]=F(x)-F(x'),\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\overline D_m)=\frac1m\operatorname{Var}(D_1),
\]
where \(\overline D_m=m^{-1}\sum_rD_r\). Sharing inputs changes covariance and variance but not the marginal mean difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With valid marginals and independent paired replications, common random numbers preserve unbiasedness and reduce paired-difference variance by the replication count.
assumptions_latex: Each simulator output has a finite second moment.
Shared draws are independent across replication indices.
Both marginal simulator means equal their target values.

notation.meaning: Average of m common-random-number paired differences.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Paired-Difference Estimation with Common Random Numbers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise regularity condition preventing variance blow-up in a derivative-free difference quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(|Y(x+h,\xi)-Y(x,\xi)|\leq L(\xi)\|h\|_2\) almost surely with \(\mathbb E[L(\xi)^2]<\infty\). Under a shared draw,
\[
Z_h=\frac{Y(x+h,\xi)-Y(x,\xi)}{\|h\|_2}
\quad\text{satisfies}\quad
\operatorname{Var}(Z_h)\leq\mathbb E[L(\xi)^2].
\]
With independent draws in the numerator, its variance is \([\operatorname{Var}Y(x+h,\xi)+\operatorname{Var}Y(x,\xi)]/\|h\|_2^2\); if the numerator is bounded below away from zero, this variance diverges as \(h\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pathwise common-random-number coupling can keep a stochastic difference quotient's variance bounded, whereas independent evaluations can produce inverse-square blow-up.
assumptions_latex: The simulator is pathwise Lipschitz between \(x\) and \(x+h\) with square-integrable random modulus.
The independent-stream comparison uses independent simulator inputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(Z_h)\leq\mathbb E[L^2]\) under common random numbers; independent-stream variance diverges under the stated lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Random-Number Stabilization of Difference Quotients

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common Random Numbers Can Increase Comparison Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit adverse shared-input coupling with negative covariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\) have mean zero and variance \(\sigma^2>0\), and define \(Y(x,\xi)=\xi\), \(Y(x',\xi)=-\xi\). With a common draw, \(D=2\xi\), so \(\operatorname{Var}(D)=4\sigma^2\). With independent draws \(\xi,\xi'\), \(D_{\mathrm{ind}}=\xi+\xi'\) has variance \(2\sigma^2\). Thus common random numbers need not reduce comparison variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared random inputs can be harmful when they induce negative covariance between competing outputs.
knowledge_statements.title: Common Random Numbers Can Increase Comparison Variance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variance-Reduction Criterion for Common Random Numbers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact comparison with independent-stream variance for two simulator outputs having fixed marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_x=Y(x,\xi)\) and \(Y_{x'}=Y(x',\xi)\) be a common-random-number pair with the same marginal variances as independently generated outputs. Then \[\operatorname{Var}(Y_x-Y_{x'})-\operatorname{Var}(Y_x-Y_{x'}^{\mathrm{ind}})=-2\operatorname{Cov}(Y_x,Y_{x'}).\] Thus common random numbers reduce, preserve, or increase comparison variance exactly when the induced covariance is positive, zero, or negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to independent streams with the same marginals, common random numbers help exactly when they induce positive covariance between paired outputs.
assumptions_latex: The paired and independent constructions have identical marginal output laws.
The outputs have finite second moments.

notation.meaning: Difference formed with a shared random input.
Difference formed with independent random inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduction Criterion for Common Random Numbers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Shared-Input Criterion for Beneficial Common Random Numbers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for nonnegative covariance and comparison-variance reduction under a scalar common input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\) be a scalar random variable, and let \(g(\xi)=Y(x,\xi)\) and \(h(\xi)=Y(x',\xi)\) have finite second moments. If \(g\) and \(h\) are both nondecreasing or both nonincreasing, then \(\operatorname{Cov}(g(\xi),h(\xi))\ge0\). Consequently, common random numbers do not increase the variance of \(Y(x,\xi)-Y(x',\xi)\) relative to independent streams with the same marginals; strictly positive covariance gives strict reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When both simulator outputs move monotonically in the same direction with a scalar shared input, common random numbers induce nonnegative covariance and cannot worsen comparison variance.
assumptions_latex: The two output functions are monotone in the same direction.
Both outputs have finite second moments.
The independent-stream comparator has the same marginal laws.

notation.meaning: Simulator outputs at the competing decisions as functions of the shared scalar input.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Shared-Input Criterion for Beneficial Common Random Numbers
Common-Random-Number Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired evaluations driven by the same random input.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a simulator returns \(Y(x,\xi)\) for decision \(x\) and random input \(\xi\). Under common random numbers, a comparison of \(x\) and \(x'\) uses paired observations \(Y(x,\xi_r)\) and \(Y(x',\xi_r)\) with the same draw \(\xi_r\) for each replication \(r\). The paired difference \(D_r=Y(x,\xi_r)-Y(x',\xi_r)\) has variance \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,\xi_r))+\operatorname{Var}(Y(x',\xi_r))-2\operatorname{Cov}(Y(x,\xi_r),Y(x',\xi_r))\), whenever the second moments exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common random numbers evaluate competing points with matched random draws, inducing covariance that can reduce or increase the variance of their difference.

notation.meaning: shared random input in replication r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The paired-input definition and variance identity correctly describe common random numbers, but the record supplies no inspectable source or standard-field rationale.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-law consistency result for fixed-sample empirical objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(X\) is compact, \(F\) is jointly measurable, \(F(\cdot,\xi)\) is continuous on \(X\) almost surely, and \(\sup_{x\in X}|F(x,\xi)|\leq M(\xi)\) with \(\mathbb E[M]<\infty\). For i.i.d. samples, \(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat f_N(x)-f(x)|\to0\) almost surely. Consequently, empirical optimal values converge to \(\min_Xf\), and every accumulation point of exact SAA minimizers lies in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_Xf\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness, continuity, measurability, and an integrable envelope yield uniform almost-sure convergence and consistency of SAA solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_X\widehat f_N\to\min_Xf\ \text{a.s., and every cluster point of exact SAA minimizers minimizes }f.
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency of SAA Minimizers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from uniform empirical-objective accuracy and empirical optimization error to a true objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\) and \(\widehat f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^NF(x,\xi_i)\) on nonempty \(X\). If \(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat f_N(x)-f(x)|\leq\varepsilon_N\) and \(\widehat f_N(\widehat x_N)\leq\inf_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)+\tau_N\), then \[f(\widehat x_N)-\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\leq2\varepsilon_N+\tau_N.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform sample-average error plus empirical optimization error bounds the true optimality gap.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform SAA Optimality Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe interface between a fixed empirical objective and a derivative-free solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) once, retain the same sample throughout the run, and define \(\widehat f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^NF(x,\xi_r)\). Apply a derivative-free method to the deterministic realized function \(\widehat f_N\), using only empirical values and feasibility information. Return the solver's incumbent or stationarity-certified point; assert a global empirical gap only when the chosen solver independently supplies such a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix one simulation sample, expose its empirical average as a deterministic value oracle, and make only the guarantees supplied by the selected DFO solver.
assumptions_latex: F(x,\xi_r)\text{ is finite at every queried }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The run optimizes one fixed realization }\widehat f_N;\quad \widehat f_N(\widehat x_N)-\inf_X\widehat f_N\le\tau\text{ is claimed only when certified by the solver.}

notation.meaning: solver-certified empirical global gap, when available

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Sample Derivative-Free SAA Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonasymptotic uniform sample complexity for a finite derivative-free candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite with \(|X|=M\), and suppose \(F(x,\xi)-f(x)\) is \(\sigma^2\)-sub-Gaussian for every \(x\in X\). For i.i.d. samples, \[\mathbb P\!\left(\sup_{x\in X}|\widehat f_N(x)-f(x)|>\varepsilon\right)\le2M\exp\!\left(-\frac{N\varepsilon^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).\] Hence uniform error at most \(\varepsilon\) holds with probability at least \(1-\delta\) whenever \(N\ge(2\sigma^2/\varepsilon^2)\log(2M/\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many candidates, uniform SAA accuracy has logarithmic dependence on candidate count and inverse-square dependence on accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Decision-Class SAA Deviation Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise SAA Convergence Does Not Imply Uniform Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-average family showing failure without uniform-law assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb N\), let \(\mathbb P(\xi=j)=p_j>0\) for every \(j\), and set \(F(j,\xi)=\mathbf1_{\{\xi=j\}}/p_j\). Then \(f(j)=1\) for every \(j\), and for each fixed \(j\), \(\widehat f_N(j)\to1\) almost surely. Every finite sample nevertheless omits some \(j\), for which \(\widehat f_N(j)=0\); therefore \(\sup_j|\widehat f_N(j)-f(j)|\ge1\) for every \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infinite decision class can have pointwise SAA consistency at every point while uniform empirical accuracy fails at every sample size.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise SAA Convergence Does Not Imply Uniform Convergence
Sample-Average Approximation in DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free optimization of an empirical mean objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given simulation outputs \(F(x,\xi)\), feasible set \(X\), sample size \(N\), and draws \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\), form the sample-average objective \(\widehat f_N(x)=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N F(x,\xi_i)\). Apply a derivative-free optimization method using only values of \(\widehat f_N\) and feasibility information, producing trial points in \(X\). Stop according to the chosen DFO method's evaluation-budget or stationarity rule and return an approximate empirical minimizer \(\widehat x_N\) satisfying \(\widehat f_N(\widehat x_N)\le\inf_{x\in X}\widehat f_N(x)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample-average approximation fixes a simulation sample, averages outputs into a deterministic empirical objective, and approximately minimizes it with a derivative-free method.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
source_refs.locator: 7 Stochastic optimization p. 161

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
source_witnesses.locator: 7 Stochastic optimization p. 161

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited general stochastic-optimization chapter does not specifically support this DFO algorithm. Moreover, stopping an arbitrary DFO method by budget or stationarity does not ensure the stated global epsilon-optimality inequality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed-horizon precision bound usable as one component of adaptive sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose evaluations at \(x\) are independent with mean \(f(x)\) and \(Y(x)-f(x)\) is \(v(x)\)-sub-Gaussian in the convention \(\mathbb E e^{\lambda(Y-f)}\le e^{\lambda^2v(x)/2}\). Then \(r_n(x)=\sqrt{2v(x)\log(2/\delta)/n}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(|\bar Y_n(x)-f(x)|>r_n(x))\le\delta\), and \(r_n(x)\le\tau\) whenever \(n\ge2v(x)\log(2/\delta)/\tau^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a known sub-Gaussian proxy, fixed precision needs order variance times log confidence divided by squared tolerance samples.
assumptions_latex: Evaluations at \(x\) are independent and identically distributed.
\(\mathbb E e^{\lambda(Y(x)-f(x))}\le e^{\lambda^2v(x)/2}\) for all \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Fixed-Precision Replication Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential precision sampling with predictable error allocation across inspected decision slots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At DFO iteration \(k\), enumerate the finitely many decision slots \(s\) whose values will be inspected, choose \(\tau_k>0\), and assign predictable numbers \(\delta_{k,s,n}>0\) with \(\sum_{k,s,n}\delta_{k,s,n}\le\alpha\). Conditional on the history before look \((k,s,n)\), construct an interval centered at \(\bar Y_{k,s,n}\) with radius \(r_{k,s,n}\) and conditional failure probability at most \(\delta_{k,s,n}\). Stop sampling slot \(s\) at \(N_{k,s}=\inf\{n:r_{k,s,n}\le\tau_k\}\), subject to the declared evaluation budget, and use completed estimates in the underlying trust-region, mesh, or comparison decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spend error probability over every inspected replication count and stop when the valid radius reaches the accuracy required by the current DFO decision.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration has finitely many enumerated decision slots
Each interval has the stated conditional failure bound
\(\tau_k>0\) and an evaluation budget are declared
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{k,s}=\inf\{n:r_{k,s,n}\le\tau_k\}\), truncated by the declared budget, and all inspected intervals cover simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: enumerated DFO decision slot and its queried point
predictable failure allocation for one look

knowledge_statements.title: Alpha-Spending Adaptive Replication

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional union-bound certificate valid at adaptive replication stops.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_{k,s,n}\) be the coverage failure at look \((k,s,n)\). If \(\mathbb P(E_{k,s,n}\mid\mathcal F_{k,s,n}^{-})\le\delta_{k,s,n}\) almost surely, the allocations are predictable, and \(\sum_{k,s,n}\delta_{k,s,n}\le\alpha\), then with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) every inspected interval covers. Consequently coverage holds at any stopping indices \(N_{k,s}\) taking values among those looks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predictable error spending converts conditionally valid fixed-look bounds into simultaneous bounds valid at adaptive precision stops.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduled-Look Coverage Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Repeated Fixed-Time Gaussian Intervals Eventually Undercover
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optional-stopping failure for repeatedly inspected fixed-sample intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_r\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim N(0,1)\), \(\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^nY_r\), and \(c>0\). Although \([\bar Y_n-c/\sqrt n,\bar Y_n+c/\sqrt n]\) has the same fixed-time coverage at every fixed \(n\), the law of the iterated logarithm gives \(\mathbb P(|\bar Y_n|>c/\sqrt n\text{ infinitely often})=1\). Thus stopping at the first exclusion of zero yields a false exclusion almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated inspection of an ordinary fixed-sample Gaussian interval destroys its nominal coverage.
assumptions_latex: The interval is inspected for every \(n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\exists n:\ 0\notin[\bar Y_n-c/\sqrt n,\bar Y_n+c/\sqrt n])=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Fixed-Time Gaussian Intervals Eventually Undercover
Adaptive Sampling in DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential replication until statistical precision meets a DFO tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At DFO iteration \(k\), for every point \(x\) whose value enters the current decision, draw independent replications sequentially and maintain the sample mean \(\bar Y_{k,n}(x)\) and a nonnegative error radius \(r_{k,n}(x)\). Continue sampling until \(r_{k,n}(x)\le\tau_k\), where \(\tau_k\) is the accuracy required by the current trust-region radius, mesh size, or comparison rule. Use the resulting means in the DFO step; stop when the underlying DFO termination rule or total evaluation budget is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive sampling increases replications only until estimated evaluation error is small enough for the current derivative-free decision.
assumptions_latex: \(r_{k,n}(x)\) is a valid prescribed error radius
\(\tau_k>0\) is supplied by the DFO decision rule
Replications satisfy the dependence assumptions used to construct \(r_{k,n}(x)\)

notation.meaning: mean after n replications at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but the validity, construction, and attainability of the error radius are method-dependent and unsupported by a source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Antithetic sampling interface for a noisy DFO value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U\stackrel d=1-U\), \(\mathbb E[Y(x,U)]=f(x)\), and second moments are finite, then \[A(x)=\tfrac12\{Y(x,U)+Y(x,1-U)\}\] is unbiased and \[\operatorname{Var}(A(x))=\tfrac12\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,U))+\tfrac12\operatorname{Cov}(Y(x,U),Y(x,1-U)).\] It has smaller variance than the average of two independent draws exactly when the antithetic covariance is negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Antithetic averaging improves on two independent draws exactly when the paired outputs have negative covariance.
knowledge_statements.title: Antithetic-Pair Variance Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance reduction for pairwise DFO comparisons through coupled evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent paired replications \((Y(x,\xi_r),Y(y,\xi_r))\), define \(\widehat d_m=m^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^m[Y(x,\xi_r)-Y(y,\xi_r)]\). Then \[\mathbb E\widehat d_m=f(x)-f(y),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\widehat d_m)=\frac{\sigma_x^2+\sigma_y^2-2\sigma_{xy}}{m}.\] Positive covariance reduces variance relative to independent sampling, while negative covariance increases it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common random numbers help a pairwise comparison when they induce positive covariance and can hurt when they induce negative covariance.

notation.meaning: paired estimator of an objective difference

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Random-Numbers Difference Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased value estimation by allocation across known strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let strata have probabilities \(p_h>0\), and let \(n_h\geq1\) independent conditional samples be drawn in stratum \(h\). Then \[\widetilde f(x)=\sum_{h=1}^Hp_h\bar Y_h(x)\] is unbiased and has variance \(\sum_{h=1}^Hp_h^2\sigma_h^2(x)/n_h\).
