With fixed total sample size and continuously relaxed allocations, the variance-minimizing allocation satisfies \(n_h\propto p_h\sigma_h(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stratified sampling gives an unbiased weighted estimate, with Neyman allocation minimizing variance in the continuous allocation relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \text{conditional samples are independent with finite variances }\sigma_h^2(x)
knowledge_statements.title: Stratified Evaluation Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias and infinite-variance failures of likelihood-ratio evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a measurable set \(A\) satisfies \(q(A)=0\) but \(\int_A F(x,z)p(z)\,dz\ne0\), samples from \(q\) cannot recover that contribution and the usual likelihood-ratio estimator is biased or undefined. Even with valid support, if \(\int F(x,z)^2p(z)^2/q(z)\,dz=\infty\), the unbiased estimator has infinite variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missing proposal support invalidates unbiasedness, while heavy likelihood ratios can leave an unbiased estimator with infinite variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampling Support and Variance Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Likelihood-ratio value estimator for a noisy derivative-free objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)=\int F(x,z)p(z)\,dz\), draw \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_N\) independently from density \(q\), and assume \(p(z)F(x,z)=0\) whenever \(q(z)=0\). Then \[\widehat f_{N,q}(x)=\frac1N\sum_{r=1}^N F(x,Z_r)\frac{p(Z_r)}{q(Z_r)}\] is unbiased when the summands are integrable, and \[\operatorname{Var}(\widehat f_{N,q}(x))=\frac1N\left(\int\frac{F(x,z)^2p(z)^2}{q(z)}\,dz-f(x)^2\right)\] when the integral is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance sampling supplies likelihood-ratio-weighted values; proposal support ensures unbiasedness and the weighted second moment determines variance.

notation.meaning: likelihood ratio on the support of q

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampling Evaluation Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance–cost allocation for a finite-level unbiased telescoping estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_0,\ldots,Y_L\) be coupled approximations, with \(\Delta_0=Y_0\) and \(\Delta_\ell=Y_\ell-Y_{\ell-1}\) for \(\ell\geq1\). Using independent sample sets across levels, define \[\widehat f_L=\sum_{\ell=0}^L\frac1{N_\ell}\sum_{r=1}^{N_\ell}\Delta_\ell^{(r)}.\] Then \(\mathbb E\widehat f_L=\mathbb EY_L\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\widehat f_L)=\sum_{\ell=0}^L V_\ell/N_\ell\), where \(V_\ell=\operatorname{Var}(\Delta_\ell)\). If \(V_\ell,C_\ell>0\), the continuous allocation minimizing \(\sum_\ell C_\ell N_\ell\) subject to \(\sum_\ell V_\ell/N_\ell\leq\varepsilon^2\) satisfies \(N_\ell\propto\sqrt{V_\ell/C_\ell}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilevel estimator telescopes coupled approximations and, in the continuous allocation relaxation, favors levels having high correction variance and low sampling cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\widehat f_L=\mathbb EY_L,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(\widehat f_L)=\sum_{\ell=0}^L V_\ell/N_\ell,\qquad N_\ell\propto\sqrt{V_\ell/C_\ell}.
knowledge_statements.title: Multilevel Telescoping Evaluation Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-expectation variance reduction for an unbiased noisy objective evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x)\in L^2\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[Y(x)]=f(x)\), and let \(S\) be an observable statistic for which \(R(x)=\mathbb E[Y(x)\mid S]\) is computable. Then \[\mathbb E[R(x)]=f(x),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(R(x))=\operatorname{Var}(Y(x))-\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid S)]\leq\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)).\] Equality holds exactly when \(Y(x)=R(x)\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning an unbiased evaluation on usable information preserves its mean and removes the expected residual conditional variance.
assumptions_latex: \(S\text{ is observable and }\mathbb E[Y(x)\mid S]\text{ is computable}\)
knowledge_statements.title: Rao–Blackwell Evaluation Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact excess-variance identity for an unbiased control-variate evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde Y_\alpha=Y-\alpha(C-\mu_C)\), where \(\mathbb E[C]=\mu_C\), \(Y,C\in L^2\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(C)>0\). With \(\alpha^*=\operatorname{Cov}(Y,C)/\operatorname{Var}(C)\), \[\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde Y_\alpha)=\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde Y_{\alpha^*})+\operatorname{Var}(C)(\alpha-\alpha^*)^2,\] and \[\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde Y_{\alpha^*})=\operatorname{Var}(Y)-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(Y,C)^2}{\operatorname{Var}(C)}.\] Thus coefficient error preserves unbiasedness but incurs an exactly quadratic variance penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A misspecified control-variate coefficient remains unbiased but adds variance equal to the control variance times the squared coefficient error.
knowledge_statements.title: Control-Variate Coefficient Misspecification Penalty

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical control-variate interface, including the scalar interface as a special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x)\in L^2\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[Y(x)\mid x]=f(x)\), and let \(C(x)\in L^2(\mathbb R^q)\) have known conditional mean \(\mu_C(x)\). For \(a\in\mathbb R^q\), define \(\widetilde Y_a(x)=Y(x)-a^{\mathsf T}(C(x)-\mu_C(x))\). Then \(\mathbb E[\widetilde Y_a(x)\mid x]=f(x)\) and \[\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde Y_a\mid x)=\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid x)-2a^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{Cov}(C,Y\mid x)+a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_C(x)a.\] If \(\Sigma_C(x)\) is positive definite, the unique variance-minimizing coefficient is \(a^*(x)=\Sigma_C(x)^{-1}\operatorname{Cov}(C,Y\mid x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centering controls at their known means preserves unbiasedness; the optimal coefficient solves the control covariance system.

notation.meaning: conditional covariance matrix of the controls

knowledge_statements.title: Multivariate Control-Variate Evaluation Interface
Variance-Reduction Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased corrected estimator exposed to a DFO decision rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x)\) be an unbiased evaluation of \(f(x)\), and let \(C(x)\) be an auxiliary random variable with known mean \(\mu_C(x)\). A variance-reduction interface may supply \(\widetilde Y_\alpha(x)=Y(x)-\alpha(x)(C(x)-\mu_C(x))\) to the DFO decision layer. Then \(\mathbb E[\widetilde Y_\alpha(x)\mid x]=f(x)\). If \(\operatorname{Var}(C(x)\mid x)>0\), the variance-minimizing coefficient is \(\alpha^*(x)=\operatorname{Cov}(Y(x),C(x)\mid x)/\operatorname{Var}(C(x)\mid x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variance-reduction layer can pass unbiased control-variate evaluations to DFO, using the covariance-to-variance ratio for minimum variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\widetilde Y_\alpha(x)\mid x]=f(x)\), and \(\alpha^*(x)\) minimizes its conditional variance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The control-variate calculation is mathematically standard, but it documents only one variance-reduction interface despite the plural leaf and has no source support.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Using Ranking and Selection to Clean Up after Simulation Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Using Ranking and Selection to Clean Up after Simulation Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic excess-value certificate for empirical-best selection among visited candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le m}\bar Y_i\), and suppose \(|\bar Y_i-f(x_i)|\le r_i\) simultaneously for all candidates. If \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i f(x_i)\), then \(f(x_{\widehat i})-f(x_{i^*})\le r_{\widehat i}+r_{i^*}\le2\max_i r_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous validation bounds certify that empirical-best selection is within twice the largest radius of the best visited candidate.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite and nonempty.
\(|\bar Y_i-f(x_i)|\le r_i\) holds simultaneously for every candidate.
\(\widehat i\) minimizes \(\bar Y_i\) under a fixed tie rule.

notation.meaning: index of a true best visited candidate

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Validation-Error Selection Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Holdout Selection Among Visited Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-shot validation and empirical-best selection on a finite visited set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite nonempty visited set \(V=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\), draw \(n_i\ge1\) validation observations at each \(x_i\), conditionally independent of the data used to construct \(V\). Form \(\bar Y_i=n_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{n_i}Y_{i,r}\), select \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i\bar Y_i\) using a fixed tie rule, and return \(x_{\widehat i}\). Any simultaneous validation radii are constructed solely from the holdout samples under a declared joint error allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reevaluate every visited candidate on independent holdout data and return the candidate with the smallest validated mean.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(V\), validation data are independent of candidate-generation data
A fixed tie rule is declared
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\widehat i}\) is returned with \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i\bar Y_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Holdout Selection Among Visited Points

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reuse of Search Data Creates Optimistic Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-candidate winner's-curse example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim N(0,1)\) be one noisy observation at each of \(m\ge2\) candidates whose true values are all zero. If the same observations score the recommendation \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_iY_i\), then \(\mathbb E[Y_{\widehat i}]=\mathbb E[\min_iY_i]<0=f(x_{\widehat i})\). Thus each observation is unbiased individually, but the reused winning estimate is optimistically biased.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting the smallest among reused unbiased observations makes the reported winning value systematically too low.
assumptions_latex: All candidates have true objective value zero
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse of Search Data Creates Optimistic Selection Bias
Selection Among Visited Trial Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-candidate selection by independent validation samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given distinct visited points \(V=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\), obtain a validation sample of size \(n_i\ge1\) at each point, independent of data used to generate \(V\). Compute \(\bar Y_i=n_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{n_i}Y_{ir}\), select \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le m}\bar Y_i\) using a fixed tie-breaking rule, and output \(x_{\widehat i}\). The rule selects the smallest estimated mean objective among visited candidates; statistical guarantees require additional distributional and sampling assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reevaluate visited candidates on independent validation samples and return the point with the smallest validated sample mean.
assumptions_latex: Validation observations are independent of candidate-generation data
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{\widehat i}\) is returned, where \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le m}\bar Y_i\).

notation.meaning: validation sample mean at candidate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-candidate validation rule is a coherent algorithm for this leaf, but no source supports the independence requirement or this particular selection interface.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous Allocation for Equalized Mean Precision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance-proportional allocation minimizing the worst variance of independent candidate means.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For known \(\sigma_i^2>0\), let positive real allocations satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^m n_i=N\). Then \(\min_{n_i>0}\max_i\sigma_i^2/n_i\) is attained at \(n_i=N\sigma_i^2/\sum_j\sigma_j^2\), with value \(\sum_j\sigma_j^2/N\). This equalizes sample-mean variances but need not maximize probability of correct selection, which also depends on mean gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variance-proportional allocation minimizes worst sample-mean variance but is not generally optimal for correct selection.
assumptions_latex: Allocations are positive real numbers with \(\sum_i n_i=N\).
Candidate observations are independent with variance \(\sigma_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Allocation for Equalized Mean Precision

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-stage variance-aware allocation for independent normal candidate estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose observations at candidate \(i\) are independent \(N(\mu_i,\sigma_i^2)\) with known \(\sigma_i^2>0\). Given \(\Delta>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), set \(z=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/(2m))\), take \(n_i=\lceil4z^2\sigma_i^2/\Delta^2\rceil\) independent validation observations, and return an index minimizing the sample means.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With known unequal normal variances, allocate in proportion to variance so each candidate mean has a common half-gap accuracy target.
knowledge_statements.title: Known-Variance Indifference-Zone Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct-selection certificate for the one-stage normal procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the known-variance allocation, suppose a unique best candidate \(i^*\) satisfies \(\mu_i-\mu_{i^*}>\Delta\) for every \(i\ne i^*\). Then \(\mathbb P(|\bar Y_i-\mu_i|\le\Delta/2\text{ for all }i)\ge1-\alpha\), and on this event \(\bar Y_{i^*}<\bar Y_i\) for all \(i\ne i^*\). Hence \(\mathbb P(\widehat i=i^*)\ge1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the best normal mean is separated by more than the declared gap, the Bonferroni allocation selects it with probability at least one minus alpha.
assumptions_latex: The known-variance validation algorithm is used
knowledge_statements.title: Known-Variance Indifference-Zone Correct-Selection Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rinott Two-Stage Selection under Unknown Unequal Variances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical two-stage indifference-zone selection for independent normal populations with unknown unequal variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let population \(i\) produce i.i.d. \(N(\mu_i,\sigma_i^2)\) observations, independently across \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Choose \(n_0\ge2\), \(\Delta>0\), \(0<\alpha<1\), and the Rinott constant \(h=h(m,n_0,1-\alpha)\), calibrated so the rule has worst-case probability of correct selection at least \(1-\alpha\) over indifference-zone configurations. From \(n_0\) pilot observations compute \(S_i^2\), set \(N_i=\max\{n_0,\lceil h^2S_i^2/\Delta^2\rceil\}\), collect \(N_i-n_0\) further observations, and select an index minimizing \(\bar Y_i(N_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rinott's procedure uses pilot variances and a calibrated critical constant to determine unequal second-stage sample sizes before selecting the smallest final mean.

notation.meaning: pilot sample variance for population i
total two-stage sample size for population i

knowledge_statements.title: Rinott Two-Stage Selection under Unknown Unequal Variances

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case correct-selection guarantee for the calibrated two-stage procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the Rinott two-stage rule is used and a unique best population \(i^*\) satisfies \(\mu_i-\mu_{i^*}\ge\Delta\) for every \(i\ne i^*\), then calibration with \(h(m,n_0,1-\alpha)\) gives \(\mathbb P(\widehat i=i^*)\ge1-\alpha\), uniformly over unknown positive variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under normality and the declared indifference gap, the calibrated two-stage rule selects the best population with probability at least one minus alpha despite unknown unequal variances.
assumptions_latex: i^*\text{ is the unique minimizer of the means}
knowledge_statements.title: Rinott Indifference-Zone Correct-Selection Guarantee
Selection Under Unequal Variances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance-aware finite-candidate selection using unequal replication counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidates \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), obtain independent observations with sample means \(\bar Y_i\), sample variances \(S_i^2\), and counts \(n_i\ge2\). Given a total additional replication budget \(B\), allocate replications using nonnegative weights increasing with estimated uncertainty, for example \(w_i=S_i/\sum_{j=1}^m S_j\) when the denominator is positive, and assign approximately \(Bw_i\) additional observations to candidate \(i\). Recompute the means and return an index in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_i\bar Y_i\) under a fixed tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When candidate variances differ, allocate more validation replications to noisier candidates before selecting the smallest updated sample mean.
assumptions_latex: Candidate samples are independent with finite variances
\(B\in\mathbb N\) is the additional replication budget
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le m}\bar Y_i^{\mathrm{updated}}\) is selected after variance-aware allocation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed allocation is a generic heuristic rather than an established unequal-variance selection procedure; it requires a source specifying its intended status and assumptions before the mathematical version can be trusted.

children.title: Candidate Screening
children.top_down_role: Early reduction of candidate sets under noisy evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic safety guarantee for lower-versus-best-upper screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite and nonempty, suppose \(L_i\le\mu_i\le U_i\) for every \(i\in I\), and let \(\delta\ge0\). Define \(I'=\{i\in I:L_i\le\min_{j\in I}U_j+\delta\}\). Then \(I'\neq\varnothing\), every minimizer of \(\mu_i\) belongs to \(I'\), and \(i\notin I'\) implies \(\mu_i>\min_j\mu_j+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under simultaneous valid ordered intervals, confidence-bound screening retains every true best candidate and removes only candidates worse by more than the tolerance.

notation.meaning: ordered interval for candidate i's mean

knowledge_statements.title: Safe Confidence-Bound Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Staged candidate screening with simultaneous error allocation and explicit stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Assume candidate \(i\) has mean \(\mu_i\) and known sub-Gaussian proxy \(v_i\). Choose \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), \(\delta\ge0\), and total evaluation budget \(B\). At stage \(n\), take one observation from each survivor, set \(\eta_{i,n}=6\alpha/(m\pi^2n^2)\), \(r_{i,n}=\sqrt{2v_i\log(2/\eta_{i,n})/n}\), \(L_{i,n}=\bar Y_{i,n}-r_{i,n}\), and \(U_{i,n}=\bar Y_{i,n}+r_{i,n}\). Retain \(I_n=\{i\in I_{n-1}:L_{i,n}\le\min_{j\in I_{n-1}}U_{j,n}+\delta\}\). Stop before a stage that would exceed \(B\), or when one candidate remains, and pass the nonempty survivor set to terminal selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample every survivor, spend error probability across candidates and stages, eliminate statistically inferior candidates, and stop at one survivor or the evaluation budget.
assumptions_latex: Replications are independent for each candidate
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_n=\{i\in I_{n-1}:L_{i,n}\le\min_{j\in I_{n-1}}U_{j,n}+\delta\}\), with total scheduled interval-failure probability at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Successive Elimination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample stage bound for removing a candidate beyond the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the simultaneous-coverage event, let \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i\mu_i\) and \(\Delta_i=\mu_i-\mu_{i^*}>\delta\). Candidate \(i\) is eliminated once \(r_{i,n}+r_{i^*,n}<\Delta_i-\delta\). For the stated radii, a sufficient stage count is \(O((v_i+v_{i^*})(\Delta_i-\delta)^{-2}\log(m(v_i+v_{i^*})/[\alpha(\Delta_i-\delta)^2]))\), up to universal constants and iterated-logarithmic terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate farther than the tolerance from the best is removed once its and the best candidate's confidence radii are small compared with the excess gap.
assumptions_latex: The Sub-Gaussian Successive Elimination algorithm is used

notation.meaning: mean gap above a best candidate

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-Dependent Elimination Stage
Candidate Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential elimination using simultaneous confidence bounds for finitely many noisy candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given candidates \(I_0=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), observations \(Y_{i,r}\) with mean \(\mu_i\), and stagewise confidence intervals \([L_{i,n},U_{i,n}]\), initialize \(I_0\). At stage \(n\), obtain the prescribed additional observations for every \(i\in I_{n-1}\), update all intervals, and set
\[
I_n=\left\{i\in I_{n-1}:L_{i,n}\leq \min_{j\in I_{n-1}}U_{j,n}+\delta\right\},
\]
where \(\delta\geq0\) is the indifference tolerance. Stop screening at its sampling budget or when \(|I_n|=1\), and pass the surviving set \(I_n\) to terminal selection. Empty-set output is prohibited by retaining an index attaining the smallest upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly discard candidates whose lower confidence bounds exceed the best surviving upper bound, allowing tolerance δ, and pass the nonempty survivor set to terminal selection.
assumptions_latex: Each interval \([L_{i,n},U_{i,n}]\) is computable from observations available at stage \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_n\neq\varnothing\), and every retained candidate satisfies \(L_{i,n}\leq\min_{j\in I_{n-1}}U_{j,n}+\delta\).

notation.meaning: stage-n confidence interval for candidate i's mean

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Candidate Screening, but no citation supports this particular confidence-bound elimination rule. Nonempty output also requires valid ordered intervals, such as L_{i,n}<=U_{i,n}, which is not assumed.

children.title: Terminal Selection
children.top_down_role: Final recommendation among retained derivative-free candidates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample certificate for a terminal choice, including the singleton case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(I\neq\varnothing\) and \(\Pr(\forall i\in I:\mu_i\in[L_i,U_i])\geq1-\alpha\). If \(|I|=1\), select its sole member. If \(|I|>1\) and \(\widehat i\) satisfies \[U_{\widehat i}\leq\min_{j\in I\setminus\{\widehat i\}}L_j+\delta,\] then \[\Pr\!\left(\mu_{\widehat i}\leq\min_{j\in I}\mu_j+\delta\right)\geq1-\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous intervals certify a delta-good terminal choice; a singleton survivor requires no pairwise test.

notation.meaning: simultaneously valid interval for candidate i's mean

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Interval Terminal Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness criterion for the final choice from a finite survivor set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For means \(\mu_i\), \(i\in I\), a terminal rule \(\widehat i\) is \((\delta,1-\alpha)\)-correct for minimization when \[\Pr\!\left(\mu_{\widehat i}\leq\min_{j\in I}\mu_j+\delta\right)\geq1-\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal rule is correct when it selects a candidate within delta of the best mean with the prescribed probability.

notation.meaning: true mean performance of candidate i

knowledge_statements.title: Indifference-Zone Correct Terminal Selection
Terminal Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Final selection from candidates surviving sequential screening under noisy evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\neq\varnothing\) be the screened candidate set. For each \(i\in I\), collect observations until a terminal allocation rule produces sample counts \(N_i\geq1\), and compute \(\bar Y_i=N_i^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^{N_i}Y_{i,r}\). Stop when the prescribed total budget is exhausted or the terminal precision condition holds. Return
\[
\widehat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{i\in I}\bar Y_i,
\]
using a fixed deterministic tie-breaking rule. If valid simultaneous terminal intervals \([L_i,U_i]\) are available, the precision condition may be \(U_{\widehat i}\leq\min_{j\in I\setminus\{\widehat i\}}L_j+\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate final samples among surviving candidates and return the one with the smallest terminal sample mean, using a fixed rule for ties.
assumptions_latex: The screened set \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
Every survivor receives at least one terminal observation.
The sampling budget or precision stopping rule is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat i\in I\) and \(\bar Y_{\widehat i}=\min_{i\in I}\bar Y_i\).

notation.meaning: terminal sample count for candidate i
terminal sample mean for candidate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Terminal Selection, but the allocation and stopping variants lack support. The displayed precision condition is undefined when the survivor set is a singleton unless that case is specified separately.

children.title: Screening-Induced Exclusion Risk
children.top_down_role: Loss of strong candidates through premature or inaccurate screening.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exclusion-Risk Bound from Simultaneous Screening Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk certificate for a declared practically optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a screening rule retains every member of \(I_\delta^*\) whenever an event \(E\) holds. If \(\mathbb P(E)\ge1-\alpha\), then \(\mathbb P(I_\tau\cap I_\delta^*=\varnothing)\le\alpha\). In particular, a confidence-bound rule that retains all \(\delta\)-optimal candidates under simultaneous ordered coverage has exclusion risk no larger than its total coverage-failure probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all practically optimal candidates survive whenever the screening bounds are valid, exclusion risk is at most the simultaneous coverage error.
assumptions_latex: On event \(E\), every member of \(I_\delta^*\) is retained
knowledge_statements.title: Exclusion-Risk Bound from Simultaneous Screening Coverage

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Look Screening Can Exclude the True Best Candidate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact positive exclusion probability under premature screening.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\) and \(Y_2\sim N(\Delta,\sigma^2)\) be independent, where \(\Delta>0\), and retain only the candidate with the smaller single observation. Candidate 1 is uniquely best but is excluded when \(Y_1>Y_2\), an event with probability \(\Phi(-\Delta/(\sqrt2\sigma))>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single noisy comparison can discard the uniquely best candidate with positive probability.
assumptions_latex: Only the smaller observation is retained
knowledge_statements.title: One-Look Screening Can Exclude the True Best Candidate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability that screening removes every candidate within the declared practical-optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_0\) be finite and nonempty, let \(I_\tau\subseteq I_0\) be the random terminal survivor set, and define \(I_\delta^*=\{i\in I_0:\mu_i\le\min_{j\in I_0}\mu_j+\delta\}\) for \(\delta\ge0\). The screening-induced exclusion risk is \(R_{\mathrm{excl}}(\delta)=\mathbb P(I_\tau\cap I_\delta^*=\varnothing)\). For \(\delta=0\) it is the probability that all exact minimizers are screened out; with a unique minimizer it is the probability that that candidate is screened out.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exclusion risk is the probability that screening removes every candidate whose mean is within the declared tolerance of the best.
assumptions_latex: Every candidate has a finite mean \(\mu_i\)

notation.meaning: set of candidates within delta of the smallest mean

knowledge_statements.title: Screening-Induced Exclusion Risk

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exclusion Risk Is Monotone in Practical Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-monotonicity of the all-protected-candidates-excluded event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0\le\delta_1\le\delta_2\), \(I_{\delta_1}^*\subseteq I_{\delta_2}^*\). Therefore \(\{I_\tau\cap I_{\delta_2}^*=\varnothing\}\subseteq\{I_\tau\cap I_{\delta_1}^*=\varnothing\}\), and \(R_{\mathrm{excl}}(\delta_2)\le R_{\mathrm{excl}}(\delta_1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the practical-optimality tolerance enlarges the protected set and cannot increase the probability of excluding all protected candidates.
assumptions_latex: The same terminal survivor set is used for both tolerances

notation.meaning: probability that no delta-optimal candidate survives

knowledge_statements.title: Exclusion Risk Is Monotone in Practical Tolerance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines stochastic approximation using only sampled function values as directly accessible oracle information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\in\Theta\) and a random sample \(\xi_k\), a stochastic zeroth-order method has access only to \(F(x_k,\xi_k)\) and seeks to approximate stochastic (sub)gradients using available stochastic function values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic zeroth-order method directly observes only sampled function values and uses those values to approximate stochastic gradients or subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Stochastic (sub)gradients are approximated using available stochastic function values.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary preventing arbitrary shrinkage of the Kiefer–Wolfowitz perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With central-difference squared bias of order \(c^4\) and fixed-replication independent value-noise variance of order \(\sigma^2/c^2\), shrinking \(c\) reduces truncation bias but increases stochastic variance. If \(\sigma^2>0\), the mean-square error of a fixed-replication difference estimate therefore cannot tend to zero as \(c\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking the perturbation reduces truncation bias but amplifies fixed-replication observation noise.
assumptions_latex: \text{the replication count per perturbed point remains fixed}
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference Radius Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error structure of the coordinatewise central-difference estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) has bounded third coordinate derivatives near \(x_k\), the noise-free central-difference vector satisfies \(g_k^{(0)}=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k^2)\). If each coordinate uses two conditionally centered, conditionally independent observation errors with variance at most \(\sigma^2\), then \[\mathbb E[g_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k^2),\qquad \mathbb E[\|g_k-\mathbb E(g_k\mid x_k)\|^2\mid x_k]\leq\frac{d\sigma^2}{2c_k^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinatewise central differences have quadratic bias, while independent observation noise is amplified as the inverse squared radius across d coordinates.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ has locally bounded third coordinate derivatives}
knowledge_statements.title: Kiefer–Wolfowitz Bias and Noise Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward coordinate-difference member of the Kiefer–Wolfowitz family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), query \(Y_k^0=Y(x_k)\) and \(Y_{k,i}^+=Y(x_k+c_ke_i)\), define \((g_k)_i=(Y_{k,i}^+-Y_k^0)/c_k\), and update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-a_kg_k)\). A shared baseline uses \(d+1\) evaluations per iteration; separate baselines use \(2d\). For twice continuously differentiable \(f\) with locally bounded second derivatives, the deterministic forward-difference bias is \(O(c_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The one-sided variant uses forward coordinate differences, reducing calls with a shared baseline but increasing truncation bias to first order.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is twice continuously differentiable near the queried points}
\Pi_X\text{ is available when constraints are imposed}
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Kiefer–Wolfowitz Recursion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Monro convergence route for two-sided coordinatewise finite-difference stochastic approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and convex, and suppose the projected ODE \(\dot x=\Pi_{T_X(x)}[-\nabla f(x)]\) has a unique globally asymptotically stable equilibrium \(x^*\). For the projected two-sided Kiefer–Wolfowitz recursion, assume \(f\) has Lipschitz gradient and bounded third derivatives near \(X\), the paired observation errors are conditionally centered with uniformly bounded conditional second moments, \(c_k\downarrow0\), \(\sum_ka_k=\infty\), \(\sum_ka_kc_k^2<\infty\), and \(\sum_ka_k^2/c_k^2<\infty\). Then \(x_k\to x^*\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection, stable limiting dynamics, vanishing finite-difference bias, and square-summable amplified noise yield almost-sure convergence.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is the unique globally asymptotically stable equilibrium of the projected gradient ODE}
\text{Paired observation errors are conditionally centered with uniformly bounded conditional second moments}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kiefer–Wolfowitz Mean-Square Rate under Balanced Gains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-specific rate for projected two-sided coordinate finite-difference stochastic approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with Lipschitz gradient and uniformly bounded third derivatives near a compact convex set \(X\), with minimizer \(x^*\in X\). For projected two-sided coordinate Kiefer–Wolfowitz iterates with conditionally centered paired observation errors having uniformly bounded conditional second moments, take \(a_k=a/(k+1)\) and \(c_k=c/(k+1)^{1/6}\). Under the usual current-noise conditional-independence condition and \(a\mu>1/3\), \[\mathbb E\|x_k-x^*\|^2=O(k^{-2/3}).\] Since an iteration evaluates both signs of every coordinate, its query cost is \(2d\), giving \(O(d\varepsilon^{-3/2})\) queries for mean-square error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balancing central-difference bias against amplified observation noise yields two-thirds mean-square decay and a dimension-linear query factor.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex with Lipschitz gradient}
\text{paired current observation errors are conditionally centered with uniformly bounded second moments}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Paired-Noise Variance in Coordinatewise Kiefer–Wolfowitz Differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of within-coordinate coupling on a central finite difference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coordinate \(i\), let the two observation errors in the central difference have conditional variances \(v_{i,+},v_{i,-}\) and conditional covariance \(c_i\). Then the observation-noise contribution \(\zeta_i=(\varepsilon_{i,+}-\varepsilon_{i,-})/(2c_k)\) satisfies \[\operatorname{Var}(\zeta_i\mid\mathcal F_k)=\frac{v_{i,+}+v_{i,-}-2c_i}{4c_k^2}.\] Positive paired covariance reduces variance relative to conditionally independent errors with the same marginal variances, whereas negative covariance increases it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling the two evaluations in a coordinate difference helps exactly through positive within-pair noise covariance.
assumptions_latex: The paired errors have finite conditional second moments.
The two errors are conditionally centered.

notation.meaning: conditional covariance of the coordinate-i observation errors
noise contribution to coordinate i of the difference estimator

knowledge_statements.title: Paired-Noise Variance in Coordinatewise Kiefer–Wolfowitz Differences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical symmetric coordinate-difference member with an explicit evaluation and coupling contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), \(a_k>0\), and \(c_k>0\), obtain for each \(i=1,\ldots,d\) a coupled pair \((Y_{k,i}^+,Y_{k,i}^-)\) at \(x_k+c_ke_i\) and \(x_k-c_ke_i\). Set \[(g_k)_i=\frac{Y_{k,i}^+-Y_{k,i}^-}{2c_k},\qquad x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-a_kg_k),\] with \(\Pi_X\) omitted in the unconstrained case. The iteration uses exactly \(2d\) value observations. Any within-pair coupling is admissible for the mechanical recursion; unbiased-noise analyses additionally require the paired difference noise to be conditionally centered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kiefer–Wolfowitz forms every gradient coordinate from a symmetric pair of values and takes a stochastic-approximation step, using 2d observations per iteration.
assumptions_latex: The \(2d\) queried points are admissible, or projection is applied to the update
The observation-pair coupling convention is fixed and recorded

notation.meaning: projection onto the feasible set when used

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Coordinatewise Kiefer–Wolfowitz Recursion
Kiefer–Wolfowitz Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise finite-difference stochastic approximation with noisy zeroth-order observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) using observations \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x)\), choose \(x_0\), gains \(a_k>0\), and perturbation radii \(c_k>0\). For each coordinate vector \(e_i\), obtain observations at \(x_k+c_ke_i\) and \(x_k-c_ke_i\), form
\[
(g_k)_i=\frac{Y(x_k+c_ke_i)-Y(x_k-c_ke_i)}{2c_k},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d,
\]
and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_kg_k\), or its projection onto a prescribed feasible set. Stop under a stated iteration, budget, or stationarity rule and return the last iterate or a prescribed average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate every gradient coordinate by two noisy symmetric function evaluations, then take a diminishing stochastic-approximation step.
assumptions_latex: Only noisy function observations are available.
Paired observations are generated according to a fixed noise-coupling convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration produces a coordinatewise central-difference estimator \(g_k\) using \(2d\) function observations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and coordinatewise finite-difference update fit the Kiefer–Wolfowitz family, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the stated variant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional boundary for finite SPSA estimator variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \((g_k)_i\) contains \((\Delta_k)_i^{-1}\), almost-surely nonzero perturbations do not ensure a finite second moment. In particular, if an additive observation-noise difference \(E_k\) is independent of \((\Delta_k)_i\), \(0<\mathbb E[E_k^2]<\infty\), and \(\mathbb E[(\Delta_k)_i^{-2}]=\infty\), then the corresponding noise term \(E_k/(2c_k(\Delta_k)_i)\) has infinite second moment. Rademacher perturbations avoid this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturbations with excessive mass near zero can give SPSA infinite estimator variance even though every coordinate is nonzero almost surely.

notation.meaning: additive difference of the two observation errors

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Perturbation Moment Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bernoulli SPSA Mean and Variance Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimator structure for independent Rademacher perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the coordinates of \(\Delta_k\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of conditionally centered observation errors. If \(f\) has bounded third derivatives near \(x_k\), then the two-sided SPSA estimator satisfies \[\mathbb E[g_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k^2).\] If the two evaluation errors are conditionally independent and each has variance at most \(\sigma^2\), the direct observation-noise contribution to each coordinate has conditional variance at most \(\sigma^2/(2c_k^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rademacher SPSA has quadratic smoothing bias and inverse-square observation-noise amplification while using two evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \Delta_k\text{ is independent of the evaluation errors conditionally on the past}
f\text{ has locally bounded third derivatives}
\text{evaluation errors are conditionally centered, independent, and have variance at most }\sigma^2
knowledge_statements.title: Bernoulli SPSA Mean and Variance Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided simultaneous-perturbation stochastic approximation using a shared baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw \(\Delta_k\) with nonzero coordinates, query \(Y_k^+=Y(x_k+c_k\Delta_k)\) and \(Y_k^0=Y(x_k)\), set \((g_k)_i=(Y_k^+-Y_k^0)/(c_k(\Delta_k)_i)\), and update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-a_kg_k)\). With independent symmetric Rademacher coordinates, conditional independence from current observation errors, and locally bounded second derivatives, \(\mathbb E[g_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+O(c_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided SPSA estimates the full gradient from a baseline and one simultaneous perturbation, with first-order bias under basic smoothness bounds.
assumptions_latex: \Delta_k\text{ has independent symmetric Rademacher coordinates and is conditionally independent of current observation errors}
f\text{ has locally bounded second derivatives near the queried points}
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided SPSA

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robbins–Monro convergence theorem for projected two-sided Bernoulli SPSA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and convex, and assume the projected gradient ODE has a unique globally asymptotically stable equilibrium \(x^*\). Let \(\Delta_k\) have independent Rademacher coordinates, conditionally independent of centered evaluation errors. If \(f\) has Lipschitz gradient and bounded third derivatives near \(X\), conditional error variances are uniformly bounded, \(c_k\downarrow0\), \(\sum_ka_k=\infty\), \(\sum_ka_kc_k^2<\infty\), and \(\sum_ka_k^2/c_k^2<\infty\), then the projected two-sided SPSA iterates converge almost surely to \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable projected dynamics plus summable smoothing bias and amplified noise give almost-sure convergence of Bernoulli SPSA.
assumptions_latex: \text{Evaluation errors are conditionally centered with uniformly bounded conditional variances}
knowledge_statements.title: Projected SPSA Almost-Sure Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bernoulli SPSA Mean-Square Rate under Balanced Gains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-specific rate for projected two-sided Bernoulli SPSA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with Lipschitz gradient and bounded third derivatives near a compact convex set \(X\). Use projected two-sided SPSA with independent Rademacher perturbations, conditionally centered evaluation errors of uniformly bounded conditional variance, \(a_k=a/(k+1)\), and \(c_k=c/(k+1)^{1/6}\). If current perturbations and errors satisfy the standard conditional-independence conditions and \(a\mu>1/3\), then \[\mathbb E\|x_k-x^*\|^2=O(k^{-2/3}).\] Two values are queried per iteration, so \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon)=O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})\), with dimension entering the hidden estimator constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced SPSA gains yield two-thirds mean-square decay with two queries per iteration, although dimension remains in the constants.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is }\mu\text{-strongly convex with Lipschitz gradient and bounded third derivatives

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic perturbation variance of the simultaneous estimator for an exact linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=a^{\mathsf T}x\) and let \(\Delta\) have independent Rademacher coordinates. The exact two-sided SPSA estimator satisfies \[(g)_i=\frac{f(x+c\Delta)-f(x-c\Delta)}{2c\Delta_i}=a_i+\sum_{j\ne i}a_j\Delta_j\Delta_i.\] Hence \(\mathbb E[g_i]=a_i\) and \[\operatorname{Var}(g_i)=\sum_{j\ne i}a_j^2=\|a\|^2-a_i^2.\] Thus two-query SPSA retains perturbation cross-talk variance even without observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear objective, Bernoulli SPSA is unbiased but each coordinate contains random cross-talk from the other gradient coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation coordinates are independent Rademacher variables.

notation.meaning: constant gradient of the linear objective

knowledge_statements.title: Rademacher SPSA Cross-Talk Variance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical reproducible SPSA member with fixed perturbation and evaluation conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), \(a_k>0\), and \(c_k>0\), draw \(\Delta_k\in\{-1,1\}^d\) with conditionally independent Rademacher coordinates, independent of the current evaluation noise given the past. Query \(Y_k^+=Y(x_k+c_k\Delta_k)\) and \(Y_k^-=Y(x_k-c_k\Delta_k)\), define \[(g_k)_i=\frac{Y_k^+-Y_k^-}{2c_k(\Delta_k)_i},\quad i=1,\ldots,d,\] and update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-a_kg_k)\). Exactly two value observations are used per iteration, independently of \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bernoulli SPSA perturbs every coordinate simultaneously and estimates the full gradient from two values.
assumptions_latex: Conditionally on the past, the coordinates of \(\Delta_k\) are independent Rademacher variables
\(\Delta_k\) is conditionally independent of the current evaluation noise

Simultaneous-Perturbation Stochastic Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-evaluation stochastic approximation using a random simultaneous perturbation of all coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), choose \(x_0\), gains \(a_k>0\), radii \(c_k>0\), and random vectors \(\Delta_k\) having almost surely nonzero coordinates. Query noisy values \(Y_k^+=Y(x_k+c_k\Delta_k)\) and \(Y_k^-=Y(x_k-c_k\Delta_k)\), define
\[
(g_k)_i=\frac{Y_k^+-Y_k^-}{2c_k(\Delta_k)_i},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d,
\]
and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-a_kg_k\), with projection when required. Stop under a prescribed budget or stationarity rule and return the final iterate or a specified average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perturb all coordinates simultaneously, use two noisy evaluations to estimate the full gradient, and take a stochastic-approximation step.
assumptions_latex: Two noisy zeroth-order observations are available per iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The estimator \(g_k\in\mathbb R^d\) is formed from two function observations independently of dimension \(d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits SPSA, but no canonical source is cited. Almost-surely nonzero perturbation coordinates alone do not state the usual distributional and inverse-moment conditions needed to characterize the standard estimator beyond its mechanical definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferred family-level description because second-order SPSA measurement, Hessian-estimation, averaging, and stabilization conventions vary materially.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A second-order SPSA scheme may combine a simultaneous-perturbation gradient estimate \(g_k\) with a random symmetric Hessian estimate \(\widehat H_k\), a recursive average \(\bar H_k=(1-w_k)\bar H_{k-1}+w_k\widehat H_k\), and an invertible stabilization \(S_k(\bar H_k)\), followed by \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_X\!\left(x_k-a_kS_k(\bar H_k)^{-1}g_k\right).\] A fixed algorithm must additionally specify the perturbation distributions, queried measurements and reuse convention, Hessian estimator, averaging weights, and stabilization map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order SPSA recursively estimates and stabilizes curvature before applying a preconditioned stochastic-approximation step, but a publishable variant must fix all measurement and stabilization conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(a_k>0\) and all perturbation radii are positive.
Perturbation coordinates satisfy the nonzero and inverse-moment requirements of the selected estimators.
\(S_k(\bar H_k)\) is measurably defined and invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=\Pi_X\!\left(x_k-a_kS_k(\bar H_k)^{-1}g_k\right)\text{ after recursive Hessian estimation and stabilization}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variant-independent accuracy condition for sampled pattern-search comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A_k=\{\max_{y\in\mathcal T_k}|\widehat f_k(y)-f(y)|\leq\varepsilon_k\}. If \sum_k\mathbb P(A_k^c\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})<\infty almost surely, then almost surely A_k holds eventually. On A_k, \widehat f_k(y)\leq\widehat f_k(x_k)-\rho_k implies f(y)\leq f(x_k)-\rho_k+2\varepsilon_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable conditional comparison-error probabilities make all sufficiently late sampled comparisons accurate almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \widehat f_k(y) is defined for y\in\mathcal T_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Summably Reliable Sampled Comparisons

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent Gaussian-noise obstruction for shrinking pattern-search differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every comparison uses a fixed number N of observations with independent Gaussian noise of variance \sigma^2>0 and the nonzero true difference d_k between the compared values tends to zero, then the probability that the two sample means reverse the true ordering tends to 1/2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed replication cannot reliably classify vanishing objective differences under persistent Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Replication Misclassification Boundary
Sampled Pattern Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pattern search whose acceptance decisions use replicated noisy function samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\), mesh size \(\Delta_0>0\), and finite positive-spanning direction sets \(D_k\), form trial points \(x_k+\Delta_k d\) for \(d\in D_k\). Estimate every compared objective value by a sample mean \(\widehat f_k(x)\) using the stage-\(k\) sampling rule. If some trial satisfies \(\widehat f_k(x_k+\Delta_kd)\leq\widehat f_k(x_k)-\rho(\Delta_k)\), accept one such trial and optionally enlarge \(\Delta_k\); otherwise retain \(x_k\) and reduce \(\Delta_k\). Stop at the evaluation budget or prescribed minimum mesh size and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare replicated sample means on a positive-spanning pattern, moving after sufficient estimated decrease and shrinking the mesh after failure.
assumptions_latex: The sampling rule returns finite sample means at compared points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration either accepts a sampled sufficient-decrease trial or retains the incumbent and contracts the search scale.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Sampled Pattern Search, but its sampling, sufficient-decrease, acceptance, and scale-update rules describe an unsourced family rather than a supported specific variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic MADS
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mesh adaptive direct search with noisy estimates and asymptotically dense polling directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an incumbent \(x_0\), mesh parameter \(\Delta_0^m>0\), and poll parameter \(\Delta_0^p\geq\Delta_0^m\). At iteration \(k\), optionally search finitely many mesh points, then poll feasible points \(x_k+\Delta_k^m d\) using directions \(d\in D_k\). Compare sampled estimates by a prescribed noise-aware acceptance test. On success, choose an accepted point and update the parameters without contraction; on failure, retain \(x_k\) and contract \(\Delta_k^m\) and \(\Delta_k^p\). Require normalized poll directions to become dense asymptotically. Stop at the budget or mesh tolerance and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run mesh adaptive direct search with sampled acceptance tests, contracting after failure while polling directions become asymptotically dense.
assumptions_latex: All evaluated trial points lie on the current mesh and satisfy the constraints.
Each poll set is finite and positively spans the relevant tangent directions.
The normalized polling directions satisfy the MADS density requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method preserves the MADS mesh-poll structure while replacing exact comparisons by a specified stochastic acceptance test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Stochastic MADS, but the stochastic acceptance test and mesh/poll updates are not specified sufficiently or tied to a source.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventual classification correctness alone is insufficient to state a complete stochastic-MADS stationarity theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Accuracy Does Not Imply Conditional Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between marginal reliability and history-conditional model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Z be Bernoulli with \mathbb P(Z=1)=\alpha, reveal Z after the first model, and set E_k=\{Z=1\} thereafter. Then \mathbb P(E_k)=\alpha, but on \{Z=0\}, \mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated failures can satisfy every marginal accuracy bound while violating the required conditional bound.
assumptions_latex: The filtration reveals Z before iterations k\geq2.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Accuracy Does Not Imply Conditional Accuracy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure under weaker probability and error requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the fully-linear event with constants (\kappa_f,\kappa_g) has conditional probability at least \alpha, then the event with \kappa_f'\geq\kappa_f and \kappa_g'\geq\kappa_g has conditional probability at least every \alpha'\leq\alpha.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lowering the probability level or enlarging error allowances preserves probabilistic full linearity.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Probabilistic Full-Linearity Parameters

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Long-Run Frequency of Fully Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic consequence of history-conditional model accuracy, without inter-iteration independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let E_k\in\mathcal F_k and suppose \mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\alpha almost surely for every k, where 0<\alpha\leq1. Then \[\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^N\mathbf1_{E_k}\geq\alpha\qquad\text{almost surely}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform conditional accuracy probability ensures that accurate models occur with asymptotic lower frequency at least alpha, even under dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\alpha\) almost surely for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Long-Run Frequency of Fully Linear Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition conditioned on all information preceding the current model-construction randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G_k\) contain all information available before drawing any randomness used to construct \(M_k\). For \(B_k=B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), define \[E_k=\left\{\sup_{y\in B_k}|f(y)-M_k(y)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\quad \sup_{y\in B_k}\|\nabla f(y)-\nabla M_k(y)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k\right\}.\] A random model sequence is \((\alpha,\kappa_f,\kappa_g)\)-probabilistically fully linear if \(E_k\) is measurable after model construction and \(\mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal G_k)\ge\alpha\) almost surely for every \(k\), with constants independent of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model sequence is probabilistically fully linear when uniform trust-region value and gradient bounds hold with a fixed probability conditional on everything known before current sampling.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and each realized \(M_k\) are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B_k\)
\(\mathcal G_k\) precedes every random draw used to construct \(M_k\)
knowledge_statements.title: Preconstruction-Conditional Probabilistic Full Linearity
Probabilistically Fully Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional high-probability version of fully linear model accuracy on a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be continuously differentiable, let \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\) be the current trust region, and let the random model \(M_k\) be measurable after its sampling is completed. For constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\), define the event
\[
E_k=\left\{\sup_{y\in B(x_k,\Delta_k)}|f(y)-M_k(y)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\quad
\sup_{y\in B(x_k,\Delta_k)}\|\nabla f(y)-\nabla M_k(y)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\right\}.
\]
The model sequence is probabilistically fully linear with probability level \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) if \(\mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\alpha\) almost surely for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random model is fully linear with conditional probability at least α when its value and gradient errors have trust-region-order bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on neighborhoods of all trust regions.
\(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) represents the information available before constructing \(M_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\alpha\) almost surely for every iteration \(k\).

Adaptive-Sampling Trust-Region DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region DFO that increases replication until estimation error matches the current radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\), \(\Delta_0>0\), and a sampling rule. At iteration \(k\), increase sample sizes until the objective estimates used to construct \(m_k\) and compute the ratio have prescribed errors of order at most \(\Delta_k^2\), with stated confidence. Compute a step \(s_k\) satisfying \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) and sufficient model decrease, and form
\[
\widehat\rho_k=\frac{\widehat f_k(x_k)-\widehat f_k(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)}.
\]
Accept according to fixed ratio and model-quality thresholds; otherwise reject. Update \(\Delta_k\) by the trust-region rules, and stop at the budget or stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase replication until estimation errors match trust-region scale, then accept and resize using a sampled actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.
assumptions_latex: The sampling rule can request additional independent or conditionally controlled observations.
The model step provides a prescribed fraction of attainable model decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\); after rejection, \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), with sampling precision coupled to \(\Delta_k^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Adaptive-Sampling Trust-Region DFO, but the Delta_k^2 sampling-accuracy requirement, confidence mechanism, and acceptance thresholds require a specific source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability bookkeeping for simultaneous random-model and random-estimate accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\alpha and \mathbb P(B_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\beta, then \mathbb P(A_k\cap B_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\max\{0,\alpha+\beta-1\}. Conditional independence strengthens this to \alpha\beta.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint accuracy follows from a conditional union bound, or a product bound under conditional independence.
assumptions_latex: A_k and B_k are measurable accuracy events.
The conditional lower bounds hold almost surely.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a random reduction ratio when differential bias matches predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let b_k^0-b_k^s be the bias in the estimated reduction and let the predicted reduction q_k satisfy q_k=\Theta(\Delta_k^2). If (b_k^0-b_k^s)/q_k does not tend to zero, then the estimated and ideal reduction ratios need not approach one another; systematic acceptance or rejection errors may persist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differential bias comparable to predicted reduction can permanently corrupt trust-region decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale condition ensuring that random objective estimates cannot arbitrarily perturb a trust-region ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let q_k=M_k(x_k)-M_k(x_k+s_k)\geq c\Delta_k^2 with c>0. If |F_k^0-f(x_k)|\leq\varepsilon\Delta_k^2 and |F_k^s-f(x_k+s_k)|\leq\varepsilon\Delta_k^2, then \[\left|\frac{F_k^0-F_k^s}{q_k}-\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{q_k}\right|\leq\frac{2\varepsilon}{c}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When predicted reduction is at least order radius squared, equally scaled objective-estimate errors perturb the acceptance ratio by a controlled amount.
assumptions_latex: Both objective estimates have absolute error at most \(\varepsilon\Delta_k^2\).

Random-Model Trust Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region iteration driven by models and estimates that are random conditional on past information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\) and \(\Delta_0>0\), construct at iteration \(k\) a random model \(M_k\) from zeroth-order samples. Compute \(s_k\) with \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\) and prescribed model decrease, obtain random estimates \(F_k^0\) and \(F_k^s\) of \(f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k+s_k)\), and set
\[
\rho_k=\frac{F_k^0-F_k^s}{M_k(x_k)-M_k(x_k+s_k)}.
\]
Accept the step when \(\rho_k\) and a model-criticality test meet fixed thresholds; otherwise reject it. Enlarge, retain, or contract \(\Delta_k\) by fixed trust-region factors. Stop under the prescribed budget or stationarity rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a random local model, compare sampled and predicted reductions, and update the iterate and radius through trust-region tests.
assumptions_latex: The computed step gives positive predicted reduction.
Model and estimate accuracy events have stated conditional probabilities.
Trust-region update factors and acceptance thresholds are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration produces \(x_{k+1}\in\{x_k,x_k+s_k\}\) and a radius \(\Delta_{k+1}>0\) determined by the stochastic trust-region tests.

notation.meaning: random objective estimates at the incumbent and trial point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient certificate obtained when no coordinate-stencil point improves the noisy incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(f\) has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(|Y(z)-f(z)|\leq\delta\) at the stencil points and center. If \(Y(x\pm he_i)\geq Y(x)\) for every \(i\), then \[|\partial_i f(x)|\leq\frac{Lh}{2}+\frac{2\delta}{h}\] and hence \[\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\leq\sqrt n\left(\frac{Lh}{2}+\frac{2\delta}{h}\right).\] For \(L,\delta>0\), this bound is minimized at \(h=2\sqrt{\delta/L}\), with value \(2\sqrt{nL\delta}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete coordinate-stencil failure certifies approximate stationarity, but bounded noise imposes a nonzero best resolution.
assumptions_latex: \nabla f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz on the stencil neighborhood}.
knowledge_statements.title: Stencil-Failure Approximate-Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit-filtering specialization of finite-difference error under bounded evaluation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(Y(z)=f(z)+e(z)\) with \(|e(z)|\leq\delta\). For \[(g_h)_i=\frac{Y(x+he_i)-Y(x-he_i)}{2h},\] one has \[\|g_h-\nabla f(x)\|_\infty\leq\frac{Lh}{2}+\frac{\delta}{h}.\] For \(L,\delta>0\), the bound is minimized at \(h=\sqrt{2\delta/L}\), where it equals \(\sqrt{2L\delta}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reducing the stencil scale lowers smooth truncation error but amplifies bounded evaluation noise.
assumptions_latex: \nabla f\text{ is }L\text{-Lipschitz on every stencil segment}.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise–Truncation Balance for Stencil Gradients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity of accumulation points of shrinking-scale complete coordinate-stencil failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^1\) have locally Lipschitz gradient on a neighborhood of a bounded sequence \(\{x_j\}\). Suppose exact values are used, \(h_j\downarrow0\), and \(f(x_j\pm h_je_i)\geq f(x_j)\) for every coordinate \(i\) and every \(j\). Then \(\|\nabla f(x_j)\|_2\to0\), and every accumulation point of \(\{x_j\}\) is first-order stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact evaluations, complete coordinate-stencil failures at vanishing scales force stationary accumulation points.
assumptions_latex: f\in C^1\text{ and }\nabla f\text{ is locally Lipschitz around the bounded sequence}.
Each x_j is a complete coordinate-stencil failure point at scale h_j.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Free Stencil-Failure Convergence
Noise-Aware Implicit Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit filtering with finite-difference scales bounded below by estimated noise resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\), stencil scales \(h_0>h_1>\cdots>0\), and a noise estimate \(\widehat\sigma\). At scale \(h_j\), evaluate a coordinate stencil, form centered differences \((g_j)_i=[Y(x+h_je_i)-Y(x-h_je_i)]/(2h_j)\), and use \(g_j\) in a projected line-search or quasi-Newton step. Continue optimization at scale \(h_j\) until its local stopping test holds, then reduce the scale. Terminate and return the incumbent when the evaluation budget is exhausted or when the predicted finite-difference signal is not reliably larger than the noise floor, for example when \(h_j\leq c\sqrt{\widehat\sigma/L}\) under an available curvature bound \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize with coordinate finite differences at decreasing scales, but stop scale refinement when differencing error becomes dominated by estimated noise.
assumptions_latex: The scale sequence is strictly decreasing.
Any used curvature bound \(L\) and noise estimate \(\widehat\sigma\) are nonnegative and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm does not refine the finite-difference scale below its prescribed noise-resolution threshold.

notation.meaning: stencil gradient estimate at scale j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits noise-aware implicit filtering, but the example threshold h_j<=c sqrt(sigma_hat/L), the meaning of the noise measure, and the scale-transition rules require a specific source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implicit filtering for a smooth underlying function observed through noisy evaluations, particularly when evaluation noise decreases near a solution or can be reduced under algorithmic control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Implicit filtering replaces the unavailable or unreliable gradient by a finite-difference estimate \(\nabla_{\epsilon}f(x)\), possibly using a non-small difference scale. For each fixed \(\epsilon\), it applies an Armijo line search along \(-\nabla_{\epsilon}f(x)\). If bounded backtracking cannot find an acceptable step, the method decreases \(\epsilon\) and repeats. The approach is best suited to regimes in which the evaluation-noise level decreases near a solution or can be reduced by the user.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Implicit filtering uses a finite-difference gradient, possibly with a difference scale that is not especially small. At each fixed scale it performs an Armijo search and reduces the scale if bounded backtracking cannot find an acceptable step. It is particularly suitable when evaluation noise decreases near a solution or can be reduced by the user.
assumptions_latex: \nabla_{\epsilon}f(x)\text{ is a finite-difference estimate formed from the noisy evaluations}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Apply Armijo search along }-\nabla_{\epsilon}f(x)\text{ and reduce }\epsilon\text{ after bounded backtracking failure.}
