For minimization, the expected improvement below \(y^\star\) is proportional, as a function of \(x\), to \(\bigl(\gamma+(1-\gamma)g(x)/\ell(x)\bigr)^{-1}\). Thus candidate points are ranked by a conditional-density ratio rather than by a direct regression estimate of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A density-based surrogate models inputs conditional on good or bad responses and ranks candidates through the ratio of those conditional densities.
knowledge_statements.title: Density-Based Surrogates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The density-ratio representation matches the density-based-surrogate leaf, but the expected-improvement proportionality is a nontrivial claim and has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Ensemble Surrogates
children.top_down_role: Combined surrogate predictors used for global derivative-free search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-validated constrained least-squares weighting of deterministic component surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{ij}\) be an out-of-sample prediction by component \(j\) for response \(y_i\). Convex stacking solves \[\widehat w\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{w_j\geq0,\,\sum_jw_j=1}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(y_i-\sum_{j=1}^Jw_jz_{ij}\right)^2\] and predicts \(s_E(x)=\sum_j\widehat w_js_j(x)\). Thus \(s_E(x)\) lies in the convex hull of the component predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex stacking learns simplex-constrained weights from held-out predictions and remains within the component prediction range.
assumptions_latex: Out-of-sample or cross-validated component predictions are available.
Weights lie on the probability simplex.

notation.meaning: held-out prediction by component \(j\) for observation \(i\)

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Stacking of Surrogate Predictions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Component Disagreement Is Not Calibrated Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting ensemble spread as predictive uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The disagreement term \[D(x)=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j(x)(m_j(x)-m_E(x))^2\] is zero when all component means agree, but their common prediction may still differ from the objective because all components can share misspecification or data bias. Hence disagreement alone is not an error certificate, and mixture variance is calibrated only under additional probabilistic assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero ensemble disagreement does not certify correctness because every component can share the same bias.
assumptions_latex: Component means and normalized nonnegative weights are given.
knowledge_statements.title: Component Disagreement Is Not Calibrated Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential additive ensemble fitted to residuals or loss gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(F_0\), define \(r_{im}=-\partial_a\ell(y_i,a)|_{a=F_{m-1}(x_i)}\), fit a weak surrogate \(h_m\) to \((x_i,r_{im})\), choose \(\gamma_m\), and update \(F_m(x)=F_{m-1}(x)+\nu\gamma_mh_m(x)\), where \(0<\nu\le1\). For squared loss, \(r_{im}=y_i-F_{m-1}(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boosting builds an additive surrogate by fitting weak learners successively to residuals or negative loss gradients.
assumptions_latex: The loss is differentiable in its prediction argument.
Each weak learner is fitted to the current pseudo-responses.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Boosted Surrogate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bagging construction for deterministic regression surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw bootstrap data sets \(D^{(1)},\ldots,D^{(B)}\), fit a common base-surrogate rule to obtain \(s_1,\ldots,s_B\), and predict \(s_{\mathrm{bag}}(x)=B^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^B s_b(x)\). The empirical spread \(B^{-1}\sum_b(s_b(x)-s_{\mathrm{bag}}(x))^2\) measures component disagreement but is not, without further assumptions, a calibrated prediction-error variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bagging averages surrogates fitted to bootstrap samples; their spread is only an empirical disagreement diagnostic.
assumptions_latex: Bootstrap resamples are drawn from the observed data.
The same base fitting rule is used for every resample.
knowledge_statements.title: Bootstrap Aggregation of Surrogates

assumptions_latex: Surrogates provide predictive means \(m_j(x)\) and variances \(v_j(x)\) for \(j=1,\ldots,J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixture mean is the weighted mean of component predictions, while its variance includes both within-model uncertainty and between-model disagreement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite probabilistic mixture of surrogate predictions with normalized weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let component \(j\) define a predictive distribution with mean \(m_j(x)\) and variance \(v_j(x)\). The ensemble predictive distribution is \(P_E(\,\cdot\mid x)=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j(x)P_j(\,\cdot\mid x)\). Its mean and variance are \(m_E(x)=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j(x)m_j(x)\) and \(v_E(x)=\sum_{j=1}^Jw_j(x)\bigl(v_j(x)+(m_j(x)-m_E(x))^2\bigr)\). Hence uncertainty contains a within-surrogate term and a between-surrogate disagreement term. Deterministic averaging is recovered when every \(v_j(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ensemble surrogate mixes component predictions; its uncertainty combines each model's predictive variance with disagreement among component means.
knowledge_statements.title: Ensemble Surrogates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of EI-driven exploration when the posterior assigns no uncertainty and predicts no improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\sigma_n(x)=0\) and \(\mu_n(x)\geq f_n^\star\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), then \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=0\) everywhere. EI then provides no preference among candidates and cannot force exploration without an external tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the posterior is everywhere certain and predicts no improvement, EI is identically zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Posterior EI Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Positivity Under Positive Gaussian Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support property of Gaussian noise-free expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\) is Gaussian with finite mean and \(\sigma_n(x)>0\), then \(\Pr(f(x)<f_n^\star\mid\mathcal D_n)>0\), and consequently \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondegenerate Gaussian posterior gives strictly positive EI at every point with positive posterior standard deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Positivity Under Positive Gaussian Uncertainty

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero EI at Noiseless Interpolation Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing expected improvement at previously observed points under an interpolating noiseless posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_i\) has been observed without noise and the posterior interpolates there, then \(\sigma_n(x_i)=0\) and \(\mu_n(x_i)=f(x_i)\geq f_n^\star\). Hence \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x_i)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under noiseless interpolation, every previously evaluated point has zero expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero EI at Noiseless Interpolation Points

assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized and observed without noise at \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
The posterior marginal satisfies \(f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x))\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Expected improvement has the closed form \((f_n^\star-\mu_n(x))\Phi(z)+\sigma_n(x)\varphi(z)\) when \(\sigma_n(x)>0\).

notation.meaning: standard normal distribution and density functions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical closed form of Gaussian expected improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-point expected improvement for noiseless minimization under a Gaussian posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_n^\star=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\) and define improvement by \(I_n(x)=(f_n^\star-f(x))_+\). The noise-free expected improvement is \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=\mathbb E[I_n(x)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). If \(\sigma_n(x)>0\) and \(z=(f_n^\star-\mu_n(x))/\sigma_n(x)\), then \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=(f_n^\star-\mu_n(x))\Phi(z)+\sigma_n(x)\varphi(z)\). If \(\sigma_n(x)=0\), then \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)=(f_n^\star-\mu_n(x))_+\). A next evaluation may be selected from \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise-free expected improvement averages the positive reduction below the best observed value and has a closed form under a Gaussian posterior.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Free Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monte Carlo Evaluation of Noisy Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior Monte Carlo evaluation of single-point noisy expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For conditionally i.i.d. joint-posterior draws \((F_X^{(s)},F_x^{(s)})\), define \[\widehat{\operatorname{NEI}}_{n,S}(x)=S^{-1}\sum_{s=1}^S\left(\min_iF_{X,i}^{(s)}-F_x^{(s)}\right)_+.\] This estimator is conditionally unbiased; if posterior improvement is integrable, it converges almost surely to \(\operatorname{NEI}_n(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint posterior samples give an unbiased, strongly consistent Monte Carlo estimator of noisy expected improvement.
assumptions_latex: The draws are conditionally i.i.d. given \(\mathcal D_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monte Carlo Evaluation of Noisy Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Plug-In Incumbents Do Not Equal Posterior-Integrated Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating NEI from plug-in improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Generally, \(\mathbb E[(\min_i f(x_i)-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\neq(\min_i\mathbb E[f(x_i)\mid\mathcal D_n]-\mathbb E[f(x)\mid\mathcal D_n])_+\). For one incumbent \(F_1\in\{-1,1\}\) equiprobably and deterministic candidate value zero, NEI is \(1/2\), while posterior-mean plug-in improvement is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing uncertain latent values by posterior means can erase positive noisy expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Posterior integration cannot generally be replaced by a plug-in incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Incumbents Do Not Equal Posterior-Integrated Improvement

assumptions_latex: Observations satisfy \(y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\), so the latent incumbent values are uncertain.
A joint posterior for \(f_X=(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_n))\) and \(f(x)\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Noisy expected improvement integrates ordinary latent improvement over posterior uncertainty in both the incumbent and the candidate value.

notation.meaning: latent objective values at observed inputs

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: posterior-integrated expected improvement with a latent incumbent
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-point expected improvement integrated over uncertain latent incumbent values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization with noisy data \(\mathcal D_n\), define the latent incumbent \(f_X^\star=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\). Noisy expected improvement at \(x\) is \(\operatorname{NEI}_n(x)=\mathbb E[(f_X^\star-f(x))_+\mid\mathcal D_n]\), where the expectation is taken under the joint posterior of \(f_X\) and \(f(x)\). Equivalently, \(\operatorname{NEI}_n(x)=\mathbb E_{f_X\mid\mathcal D_n}[\mathbb E[(\min_i f(x_i)-f(x))_+\mid f_X,\mathcal D_n]]\). This integration prevents a noisy observed minimum from being treated as the exact incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy expected improvement averages improvement over uncertainty about the latent values of previous observations as well as the proposed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Expected Improvement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The posterior-integrated latent-incumbent formulation matches the noisy expected-improvement leaf and is internally consistent, but no inspectable source is cited for this particular NEI definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit redundancy boundary demonstrating the need for a joint posterior batch functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the duplicate batch \(X_2=(x,x)\), both prospective values are the same random variable. Therefore \(2\operatorname{EI}_n(x,x)=\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\), whereas summing marginal scores gives \(2\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\). Whenever \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x)>0\), the marginal sum strictly overvalues this redundant batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two copies of the same candidate deliver only one candidate's improvement, although summing marginal EI counts it twice.
assumptions_latex: Both batch entries are the same input x.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-EI Summation Overvalues Duplicate Candidates

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sum Upper Bound for Batch Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence-free upper bound relating joint and marginal expected improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X_q=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)})\), \[(f_n^\star-\min_jf(x^{(j)}))_+=\max_j(f_n^\star-f(x^{(j)}))_+\leq\sum_{j=1}^q(f_n^\star-f(x^{(j)}))_+.\] Hence \(q\operatorname{EI}_n(X_q)\leq\sum_{j=1}^q\operatorname{EI}_n(x^{(j)})\), regardless of posterior dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint batch EI never exceeds the sum of its members' marginal EIs.
knowledge_statements.title: Sum Upper Bound for Batch Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic structural properties of joint noiseless batch expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite batches \(A\subseteq B\), let \(I_n(A)=(f_n^\star-\min_{x\in A}f(x))_+\). Then \(I_n(A)\leq I_n(B)\) pointwise and hence \(\mathbb E[I_n(A)\mid\mathcal D_n]\leq\mathbb E[I_n(B)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). For \(A=\{x\}\), batch expected improvement equals ordinary expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a candidate cannot reduce batch EI, and a one-point batch recovers ordinary EI.
assumptions_latex: The batch values have a joint posterior distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch-EI Monotonicity and Singleton Reduction

assumptions_latex: A batch \(X_q=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)})\in\mathcal X^q\) is evaluated in parallel.
The objective is minimized, observations are noiseless, and the joint posterior of batch values is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Batch expected improvement is the posterior expectation of the reduction achieved by the best member of the batch.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical joint batch expected-improvement functional
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint expected improvement for a parallel noiseless batch in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_n^\star=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\). For a proposed batch \(X_q=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)})\), define its realized improvement by \(I_n(X_q)=(f_n^\star-\min_{1\le j\le q}f(x^{(j)}))_+\). The batch expected improvement is \(q\operatorname{EI}_n(X_q)=\mathbb E[I_n(X_q)\mid\mathcal D_n]\), with expectation under the joint posterior distribution of \((f(x^{(1)}),\ldots,f(x^{(q)}))\). A batch is selected from \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{X_q\in\mathcal X^q}q\operatorname{EI}_n(X_q)\); posterior dependence among batch values is retained in this joint expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch expected improvement averages the reduction produced by the best point in a jointly modeled parallel batch, retaining dependence among candidate outcomes.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Expected Improvement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint batch functional matches the batch expected-improvement leaf and retains posterior dependence correctly, but it has no inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probability of Improvement Can Prefer Negligible Gains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Magnitude-blindness of threshold-crossing probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If candidate \(a\) improves by \(10^{-6}\) with probability \(0.9\), while \(b\) improves by \(100\) with probability \(0.1\), then \(\operatorname{PI}(a)=0.9>0.1=\operatorname{PI}(b)\), but \(\operatorname{EI}(a)=9\times10^{-7}<10=\operatorname{EI}(b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PI can prefer a likely negligible gain to a less-likely large gain because it ignores magnitude.
assumptions_latex: Improvement means a strictly positive reduction below a fixed threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PI and expected improvement can rank candidates oppositely.
knowledge_statements.title: Probability of Improvement Can Prefer Negligible Gains

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian PI ordering at a fixed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\sigma_n(x)>0\), \(\operatorname{PI}_n(x)=\Phi(z_n(x))\), where \(z_n(x)=(\tau_n-\mu_n(x))/\sigma_n(x)\). Since \(\Phi\) is strictly increasing, PI and \(z_n\) induce the same ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian PI ranks candidates by standardized threshold crossing.
assumptions_latex: Compared posterior marginals are Gaussian with positive standard deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Standardized-Improvement Ordering
Probability of Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian-posterior acquisition for noiseless minimization relative to an incumbent threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_n\) be the observations and suppose \(f(x)\mid D_n\sim\mathcal N(\mu_n(x),\sigma_n^2(x))\). For an improvement threshold \(\tau_n\), the probability-of-improvement acquisition is \[\operatorname{PI}_n(x)=\mathbb P(f(x)<\tau_n\mid D_n)=\Phi\!\left(\frac{\tau_n-\mu_n(x)}{\sigma_n(x)}\right)\] when \(\sigma_n(x)>0\). When \(\sigma_n(x)=0\), set \(\operatorname{PI}_n(x)=\mathbf 1\{\mu_n(x)<\tau_n\}\). The interface selects any \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{PI}_n(x)\); an optional positive margin may replace \(\tau_n\) by \(\tau_n-\xi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability of improvement selects a point maximizing the posterior probability that its objective value beats the incumbent threshold.
assumptions_latex: The conditional marginal posterior of \(f(x)\) is Gaussian.
\(\tau_n\in\mathbb R\) is fixed when the acquisition is optimized.

notation.meaning: Posterior mean and standard deviation after n observations.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the probability-of-improvement formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and Gaussian PI formula are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but the record supplies no citation or inspectable locator supporting the formula, zero-variance convention, margin convention, and selection rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LCB Values Are Not Unconditional Objective Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a probabilistic confidence acquisition from a deterministic lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without a stated event or deterministic error bound ensuring \(f(x)\geq\mu_n(x)-\sqrt{\beta_n}\sigma_n(x)\), the numerical value \(\operatorname{LCB}_n(x)\) is only an acquisition score and need not lower-bound \(f(x)\). Minimizing LCB alone therefore does not certify objective optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LCB is not a deterministic lower-bound certificate unless its confidence event is established.
assumptions_latex: No valid simultaneous confidence event or deterministic surrogate-error bound is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{LCB}_n(x)\leq f(x)\) cannot be inferred solely from posterior moments and \(\beta_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: LCB Values Are Not Unconditional Objective Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimism on a Valid Confidence Event
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of LCB as an optimistic acquisition score for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(|f(x)-\mu_n(x)|\leq\sqrt{\beta_n}\sigma_n(x)\) simultaneously for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) on an event \(E_n\), then \[\mu_n(x)-\sqrt{\beta_n}\sigma_n(x)\leq f(x)\leq\mu_n(x)+\sqrt{\beta_n}\sigma_n(x)\quad\forall x\in\mathcal X\] on \(E_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under simultaneous confidence coverage, LCB lies below the true objective and is optimistic for minimization.
assumptions_latex: The displayed confidence inequality holds simultaneously on \(E_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Optimism on a Valid Confidence Event
Lower-Confidence-Bound Interface for DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior lower confidence bound for derivative-free minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given posterior mean \(\mu_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), posterior standard deviation \(\sigma_n:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)\), and exploration parameter \(\beta_n>0\), define the lower confidence bound \[\operatorname{LCB}_n(x)=\mu_n(x)-\sqrt{\beta_n}\,\sigma_n(x).\] The associated derivative-free acquisition interface returns any \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{LCB}_n(x)\), using only surrogate predictions during acquisition optimization. The negative quantity \(-\operatorname{LCB}_n\) may equivalently be maximized. Increasing \(\beta_n\) gives greater preference to locations having high posterior uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LCB chooses a point minimizing posterior mean minus an uncertainty bonus, thereby balancing predicted objective value and exploration.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu_n(x)\) and \(\sigma_n(x)\) are finite for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports Bayesian lower confidence bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition has the correct role for the LCB interface and is internally consistent, but no cited source with a specific locator supports the normalization by sqrt(beta_n), the minimization convention, or the exploration interpretation.

children.title: Constraint-Aware Confidence Bounds
children.top_down_role: Confidence-bound acquisitions incorporating feasibility information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Marginal Coverage Does Not Imply Simultaneous Feasibility Confidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between separate pointwise intervals and a valid joint feasibility guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Statements \(\Pr(g_j(x)\leq U_{j,n}(x))\geq1-\delta\) made separately for each \((j,x)\) do not, without a simultaneous-coverage argument, imply coverage for all constraints and candidate points at level \(1-\delta\). Marginal bounds therefore do not automatically certify an adaptively selected point at that level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate marginal confidence bounds cannot automatically be read as a simultaneous feasibility guarantee.
assumptions_latex: No simultaneous band or multiplicity correction is supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Coverage Does Not Imply Simultaneous Feasibility Confidence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-aware confidence-bound interface without prescribing a noncanonical empty-set restoration policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_j(x)\leq0\) and upper confidence functions \(U_{j,n}(x)\), define \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}=\{x\in\mathcal X:U_{j,n}(x)\leq0\ \forall j\}\). A constraint-aware objective acquisition may be optimized over \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}\) when this set is nonempty. If it is empty, this interface alone does not determine a next point; a separately declared feasibility-restoration or fallback rule is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint upper bounds define a confidence-feasible set; an empty set requires an explicitly chosen fallback policy.
assumptions_latex: Each \(U_{j,n}(x)\) is defined on the relevant domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}=\bigcap_j\{x:U_{j,n}(x)\leq0\}\), and no empty-set action follows from this definition alone.
review_flags: Does not adopt the deferred seed's unsupported restoration and stopping rules.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Feasible Set Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safety of Simultaneous Constraint Upper Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility implication of simultaneously valid upper confidence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_{j,n}(x)\) satisfy \(g_j(x)\leq U_{j,n}(x)\) for every relevant \(j,x\) on an event \(E_n\). Then, on \(E_n\), every \(x\in\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}\) is truly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneously valid constraint upper bounds make the confidence-feasible set a subset of the true feasible set.
assumptions_latex: On \(E_n\), \(g_j(x)\leq U_{j,n}(x)\) simultaneously for all relevant \(j,x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Safety of Simultaneous Constraint Upper Bounds
Constraint-Aware Confidence Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Confidence-bound acquisition with separately modeled unknown inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization subject to \(g_j(x)\leq0\), define the conservative feasible set \[\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}=\{x\in\mathcal X:\mu_{g_j,n}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_{g_j,n}}\sigma_{g_j,n}(x)\leq0\text{ for every }j\}.\] If \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}\neq\varnothing\), choose a minimizer over this set of \(\mu_{f,n}(x)-\sqrt{\beta_{f,n}}\sigma_{f,n}(x)\). If it is empty, choose a point minimizing \(\max_j\{\mu_{g_j,n}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_{g_j,n}}\sigma_{g_j,n}(x)\}\). Stop when the evaluation budget or a prescribed confidence-bound tolerance is reached, and return the best observed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative constraint bounds restrict objective LCB optimization; when no point is confidently feasible, the method minimizes worst predicted constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: The objective and each unknown constraint have posterior means and finite standard deviations on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next evaluation either minimizes the objective confidence bound over \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}\) or minimizes worst constraint upper confidence bound when that set is empty.

notation.meaning: Posterior mean and standard deviation of constraint j.
Posterior mean and standard deviation of the objective.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not identify a canonical constraint-aware confidence-bound convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is plausible for this leaf, but the conservative feasible-set rule, empty-set fallback, confidence-bound stopping tolerance, and returned recommendation constitute a particular algorithm rather than a uniquely determined constraint-aware confidence-bound interface. No source establishes these choices.

children.title: Contextual Confidence Bounds
children.top_down_role: Confidence-bound acquisitions conditioned on observed or assigned context.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applicability boundary for confidence claims at contexts outside their established support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A confidence statement established only for contexts in \(\mathcal C_0\subseteq\mathcal C\) supplies no guarantee at an observed \(c_n\notin\mathcal C_0\). Conditional posterior moments and a confidence parameter alone do not establish calibrated coverage under arbitrary context shift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contextual confidence guarantees do not automatically extrapolate beyond the contexts covered by their assumptions.
assumptions_latex: The available confidence result is restricted to \(\mathcal C_0\).
The observed context may lie outside \(\mathcal C_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_n\notin\mathcal C_0\Rightarrow\) the restricted confidence result is inapplicable at \(c_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported-Context Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal separation of an observed context from controllable decision coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If context \(C_n=c_n\) is observed before the decision, a contextual acquisition policy has the form \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X(c_n)}a_n(x;c_n)\). Joint optimization over \((x,c)\) generally represents a different problem because it permits selection of an exogenous coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contextual acquisition conditions on the observed context and optimizes only the controllable decision.
assumptions_latex: The decision maker cannot choose the context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X(c_n)}a_n(x;c_n)\) is the admissible interface, not \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,c}a_n(x;c)\).

notation.meaning: Acquisition score conditional on context c.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning–Optimization Separation
Contextual Confidence Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional confidence-bound decision rule for an observed, noncontrolled context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c_n\in\mathcal C\) be the context observed before decision \(n+1\), and let the conditional objective posterior at \((x,c_n)\) have mean \(\mu_n(x,c_n)\) and standard deviation \(\sigma_n(x,c_n)\). The contextual lower-confidence-bound acquisition is \[\operatorname{CLCB}_n(x;c_n)=\mu_n(x,c_n)-\sqrt{\beta_n}\sigma_n(x,c_n).\] Its decision interface chooses \(x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X(c_n)}\operatorname{CLCB}_n(x;c_n)\). Only \(x\) is optimized: the observed context is conditioned upon and is not treated as a controllable design coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After observing a context, contextual LCB minimizes a conditional lower confidence bound over decisions admissible for that context.
assumptions_latex: \(\beta_n>0\), and the conditional posterior moments are finite.

notation.meaning: Observed context for the next decision.
Decisions admissible under the observed context.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports contextual confidence-bound optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contextual LCB definition fits the leaf and correctly distinguishes observed context from controllable decisions, but no cited source with a specific locator supports this precise conditional decision rule and notation.

children.title: Joint Constraint–Context Regimes
children.top_down_role: Acquisition settings combining feasibility uncertainty with contextual variation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contextwise Feasibility Need Not Be Uniformly Available
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Impossibility boundary caused by an empty true feasible decision fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F(c)=\{x\in\mathcal X(c):g_j(x,c)\leq0\ \forall j\}\). A policy required to return a feasible decision for every context can exist only if \(\mathcal F(c)\neq\varnothing\) throughout the required context support. If \(\mathcal F(c_0)=\varnothing\), no acquisition rule can produce a feasible decision at \(c_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No policy can ensure feasibility at a context whose true feasible decision fiber is empty.

notation.meaning: True feasible decision fiber at context c.

knowledge_statements.title: Contextwise Feasibility Need Not Be Uniformly Available

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of contextual decision fibers with constraint confidence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After observing \(c_n\), define \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}(c_n)=\{x\in\mathcal X(c_n):U_{j,n}(x,c_n)\leq0\ \forall j\}\). When this set is nonempty, a joint constraint-context acquisition optimizes its conditional objective score over \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}(c_n)\). If it is empty, a separately specified restoration, abstention, or fallback policy is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The joint regime intersects the observed context's admissible decisions with conditional confidence constraints.
assumptions_latex: The context is observed before the decision.
Conditional constraint upper bounds are defined on \(\mathcal X(c_n)\).

notation.meaning: Confidence-feasible decision fiber at context c.

review_flags: Does not adopt the deferred seed's particular restoration loop.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Conditional Confidence-Feasible Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Contextwise Safety Under Joint Confidence Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety implication for conditional constraint bounds at the observed context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On an event where \(g_j(x,c)\leq U_{j,n}(x,c)\) simultaneously for all relevant \((j,x,c)\), any selection \(x_n\in\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{cb}}(c_n)\) produces a truly feasible pair \((x_n,c_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneously valid conditional upper bounds turn contextwise confidence feasibility into true feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The stated upper bounds hold simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_j(x_n,c_n)\leq0\) for every j on the simultaneous-coverage event.
knowledge_statements.title: Contextwise Safety Under Joint Confidence Coverage
Joint Constraint–Context Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-conditioned confidence-bound selection under unknown inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After observing \(c_n\), form \[\mathcal F_n(c_n)=\{x\in\mathcal X(c_n):\mu_{g_j,n}(x,c_n)+\sqrt{\beta_{g_j,n}}\sigma_{g_j,n}(x,c_n)\leq0\text{ for every }j\}.\] When \(\mathcal F_n(c_n)\neq\varnothing\), select a minimizer on this set of \(\mu_{f,n}(x,c_n)-\sqrt{\beta_{f,n}}\sigma_{f,n}(x,c_n)\). Otherwise minimize the largest constraint upper confidence bound over \(\mathcal X(c_n)\). Evaluate the objective and constraints at the selected decision and observed context, update every posterior, and repeat for the next exogenously supplied context.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each observed context, the rule enforces conservative conditional constraints and then minimizes the conditional objective confidence bound.
assumptions_latex: Each context is observed before its decision is selected.
Objective and constraint posteriors provide finite conditional means and standard deviations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected decision is confidence-feasible for the observed context whenever \(\mathcal F_n(c_n)\neq\varnothing\); otherwise it targets restoration of conditional feasibility.
review_flags: The supplied sources do not establish a canonical joint constraint–context confidence-bound regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits a joint constraint-context regime, but the conservative conditional feasible set, worst-UCB restoration fallback, observation protocol, and posterior-update loop are one particular construction. A source is required to establish this version and its hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic equivalence underlying entropy search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever defined, \[H(X^*\mid D_n)-\mathbb E[H(X^*\mid D_n,Y_x)\mid D_n]=I(X^*;Y_x\mid D_n)\] and, by symmetry, \[I(X^*;Y_x\mid D_n)=H(Y_x\mid D_n)-\mathbb E[H(Y_x\mid D_n,X^*)\mid D_n].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected optimizer-entropy reduction equals conditional mutual information and has a symmetric predictive-entropy form.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional entropies and mutual information are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy Reduction as Mutual Information

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which optimizer entropy is not directly defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If posterior sample paths need not attain a global minimum, or no measurable rule selects among minimizers, a posterior optimizer variable \(X^*\) need not exist. On continuous domains differential entropy depends on coordinates, although mutual information is invariant under measurable bijective reparameterizations when defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer entropy requires a well-defined optimizer random variable; mutual information is the coordinate-invariant quantity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Entropy-search formulas require an explicit optimizer variable or specified finite approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropy-Search Well-Posedness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entropy-search variant targeting the unknown global minimum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^*=\inf_{z\in\mathcal X}f(z)\) be a posterior random minimum value. A minimum-value entropy-search acquisition is \[\alpha_n^{\mathrm{MVES}}(x)=I(F^*;Y_x\mid D_n)=H(F^*\mid D_n)-\mathbb E[H(F^*\mid D_n,Y_x)\mid D_n],\] whenever these quantities are defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-value entropy search chooses observations informative about the unknown optimal value rather than the optimizer location.
assumptions_latex: \(F^*\) is measurable and finite almost surely.
The displayed information quantities are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Value Entropy Search
Entropy-Search Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-value acquisition targeting uncertainty about the global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^*\) denote a posterior random global minimizer of \(f\) on \(\mathcal X\), with current distribution \(p_n\). For a prospective noisy observation \(Y_x\) at \(x\), the entropy-search acquisition is \[\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}(x)=H(p_n)-\mathbb E_{Y_x\mid D_n}\!\left[H(p_{n+1}^{x,Y_x})\right],\] whenever these entropies are finite. Here \(p_{n+1}^{x,Y_x}\) is the minimizer distribution after conditioning on the hypothetical observation. The next evaluation maximizes \(\alpha_n^{\mathrm{ES}}\). Variants replacing entropy reduction by another divergence or targeting the minimum value belong to the same information-search family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy search evaluates where the expected observation most reduces posterior uncertainty about the global optimizer.
assumptions_latex: A posterior distribution over a measurable global minimizer \(X^*\) is defined.
The predictive law of \(Y_x\mid D_n\) is available.
The displayed entropies and expectation are finite.

notation.meaning: Current posterior distribution of the minimizer.
Entropy functional for the chosen minimizer representation.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports entropy-search acquisitions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Expected entropy reduction about a posterior global minimizer is an appropriate defining representation for entropy search, but no source supports the formula or the broader claim that divergence replacements and minimum-value targets belong to the same family. The entropy type and minimizer representation also require source-specific qualification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-dimensional evaluation for a finite Gaussian decision set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For terminal alternatives \(z_1,\ldots,z_M\), a scalar Gaussian observation permits \(\mu_{n+1}^{x,Y_x}(z_i)=a_i+b_iZ\), \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\). Hence \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=\min_i a_i-\mathbb E[\min_i(a_i+b_iZ)].\] The expectation is obtained from the lower envelope of the affine functions and normal integration over its active intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-alternative Gaussian KG reduces to a one-dimensional normal expectation of an affine lower envelope.
assumptions_latex: The terminal decision set is finite.
The posterior and prospective observation are jointly Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: KG evaluation reduces to integrating a piecewise-affine lower envelope against a standard normal law.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Alternative Gaussian Knowledge Gradient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for zero KG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sampling \(x\) leaves every terminal posterior mean unchanged almost surely, then \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=0\). KG can also vanish when posterior means change but their optimized infimum remains almost surely equal to its current value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sample has zero KG when it cannot improve the optimized posterior-mean decision value.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Value Information Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-of-information property for minimization KG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb E[\mu_{n+1}^{x,Y_x}(z)\mid D_n]=\mu_n(z)\) pointwise and the quantities are finite, then \[\mathbb E[\inf_z\mu_{n+1}^{x,Y_x}(z)\mid D_n]\le\inf_z\mu_n(z),\] so \(\operatorname{KG}_n(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reoptimizing after an observation makes the expected value of information nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: Posterior means satisfy the conditional martingale identity.
The infima and expectations are measurable and finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegativity of the Knowledge Gradient
Knowledge-Gradient Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step expected value-of-information acquisition for posterior-mean decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, let \(m_n^*=\inf_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_n(z)\). If sampling \(x\) produces predictive observation \(Y_x\) and updated posterior mean \(\mu_{n+1}^{x,Y_x}\), define the knowledge gradient by \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=m_n^*-\mathbb E_{Y_x\mid D_n}\!\left[\inf_{z\in\mathcal X}\mu_{n+1}^{x,Y_x}(z)\right].\] The next point maximizes \(\operatorname{KG}_n\), optionally after subtracting an evaluation cost. Thus the acquisition measures the expected one-step improvement in the value of the decision recommended by the posterior mean, rather than improvement of the sampled response itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Knowledge gradient samples where one observation is expected to improve the best posterior-mean decision value most.
assumptions_latex: The posterior mean has a finite infimum on \(\mathcal X\).
The predictive observation and updated posterior mean are well defined.
The expectation of the updated infimum is finite.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the knowledge-gradient formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-step posterior-mean value-of-information formula is appropriate for the knowledge-gradient family and uses the correct minimization sign convention, but no cited source or locator supports the formula, cost-adjusted variant, or selection rule.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of probability matching and exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the posterior assigns probability zero to functions whose selected minimizer lies in a measurable region \(A\), posterior sampling selects \(A\) with probability zero. With multiple minimizers, the selected distribution depends on the declared measurable tie-breaking kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior sampling cannot explore optimizer regions excluded by posterior support, and ties require an explicit selection rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Probability matching is relative to posterior support and the chosen optimizer-selection kernel.

notation.meaning: Measurable region of the search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Support and Tie-Breaking Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional characterization of Thompson-style sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If posterior draws have an almost surely unique measurable minimizer \(X^*(f)\), then for every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\), \[\Pr(x_{n+1}\in A\mid D_n)=\Pi_n\{f:X^*(f)\in A\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior sampling selects regions with their posterior probability of containing the optimizer.
assumptions_latex: The posterior draw has a unique minimizer almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Probability Matching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite- or countable-action Bayesian regret bound for posterior sampling under a uniform information-ratio bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*\) be the random optimal action, let \(A_t\) be selected by posterior sampling, and define \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[\ell(A_t)-\ell(A^*)\mid D_{t-1}]\) and \(I_t=I(A^*;(A_t,Y_t)\mid D_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\le\Gamma I_t\) almost surely for every \(t\), then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)=\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E[\Delta_t]\le\sqrt{\Gamma T H(A^*)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform information-ratio bound converts entropy of the unknown optimal action into a square-root Bayesian-regret bound for posterior sampling.
assumptions_latex: A^*\text{ takes values in a finite or countable action set and }H(A^*)<\infty.
The posterior-sampling and observation kernels are well defined.

notation.meaning: conditional mutual information gained about the optimal action at round t
prior entropy of the optimal action

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Ratio Bayesian-Regret Bound
Posterior-Sampling Acquisitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thompson-style acquisition generated by optimizing a posterior function draw.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observations \(D_n\) and a posterior law \(\Pi_n\) on objective functions over \(\mathcal X\), draw \(\widetilde f_n\sim\Pi_n\). Select \[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}\widetilde f_n(x),\] evaluate the black-box objective at \(x_{n+1}\), append the observation to \(D_n\), and update \(\Pi_n\). Repeat until the evaluation budget or stopping rule is met, then return a prescribed recommendation such as the best observed point or a posterior-mean minimizer. Random tie-breaking among sampled-function minimizers preserves the posterior-sampling interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior sampling draws a plausible objective function and evaluates a minimizer of that draw, naturally randomizing exploration and exploitation.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi_n\) is a probability law on functions defined over \(\mathcal X\).
A measurable minimizer-selection rule exists for almost every draw.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditionally on \(D_n\), the next decision is obtained by minimizing an objective function drawn from \(\Pi_n\).

notation.meaning: Posterior law of the objective function.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports posterior-sampling acquisitions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind for the stated Thompson-style posterior-sampling procedure, but the record has no source for the sampled-function minimization rule, measurable selection condition, tie-breaking interpretation, or alternative terminal recommendations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected multistart interface retaining every locally, globally, or explicitly generated feasible candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_n\subset\mathcal X\) be the finite set containing every feasible candidate returned by the prescribed local starts, boundary searches, and optional global-search stage. If \(C_n\neq\varnothing\), return \(\widehat x_n\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C_n}\alpha_n(z)\). The returned point is best only over \(C_n\); it is globally optimal on \(\mathcal X\) only when candidate generation or a separate certificate establishes that fact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous acquisition search compares all retained feasible candidates, but finite multistart search alone does not guarantee a global maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_n(\widehat x_n)=\max_{z\in C_n}\alpha_n(z)\), with no implied equality to \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(x)\).

notation.meaning: All feasible candidates retained by every acquisition-search stage.

review_flags: Replaces the inconsistent candidate set in the deferred seed without asserting a global guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Candidate Continuous Acquisition Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certificate for approximate global acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\widehat x\in\mathcal X\), if \(U\geq\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(x)\) and \(U-\alpha_n(\widehat x)\leq\varepsilon\), then \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(x)-\alpha_n(\widehat x)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid global upper bound within epsilon of the incumbent acquisition value certifies epsilon-global optimality.

notation.meaning: Certified upper bound on the globally maximal acquisition value.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Acquisition-Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Acquisition Optimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth one-dimensional boundary separating local acquisition optimization from global acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal X=[-2,2]\), let \(\alpha(x)=x^3-2.9x\). The interior point \(x=-\sqrt{2.9/3}\) is a strict local maximizer, but \(\alpha(2)=2.2\) is larger. Thus convergence of a local run to a stationary local maximizer does not certify global acquisition optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth acquisition can have a strict local maximizer whose value is below a boundary value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=-\sqrt{2.9/3}\) is locally maximizing but is not globally maximizing on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Certify Global Acquisition Optimality

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a Continuous Acquisition Maximizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment for continuous acquisition optimization, without an algorithmic global-optimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and compact and \(\alpha_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous, then \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(x)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous acquisition on a nonempty compact domain attains its maximum.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence of a Continuous Acquisition Maximizer
Continuous Acquisition Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multistart optimization of a continuous acquisition over a continuous design domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact continuous domain \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^d\), acquisition \(\alpha_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), and starting points \(s_1,\ldots,s_R\in\mathcal X\), run a bound- or constraint-respecting continuous optimizer from every \(s_r\) to obtain candidates \(z_r\). Include any explicitly evaluated boundary or global-search candidates, and return \[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in\{z_1,\ldots,z_R\}}\alpha_n(z).\] Stop each local run at its prescribed stationarity tolerance or resource limit. This interface guarantees a global acquisition maximizer only when the candidate-generation procedure itself provides global optimization guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous acquisition optimization uses multiple constrained starts and returns the candidate with the largest acquisition value, without automatically guaranteeing global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and compact.
Each local run returns a feasible candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point maximizes \(\alpha_n\) over the generated candidate set, but need not maximize it over all of \(\mathcal X\).

notation.meaning: Starting point for local run r.
Feasible candidate returned by local run r.

review_flags: The supplied locators do not specifically support continuous Bayesian acquisition optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits continuous acquisition optimization, but no source supports this particular multistart interface. In addition, the statement says boundary or global-search candidates are included, while the displayed argmax ranges only over {z_1,...,z_R}; a sourced revision must define one candidate set containing every retained candidate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mixed-domain acquisition optimization when every discrete assignment can be enumerated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(q\in\mathcal Q\) with \(\mathcal X_q\neq\varnothing\), compute \(z_q\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in\mathcal X_q}\alpha_n(q,z)\), and return \((\widehat q,z_{\widehat q})\) with \(\widehat q\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{q}\alpha_n(q,z_q)\). Exact conditional solves give a global maximizer; approximate conditional solves give only the corresponding approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate valid discrete assignments, solve each continuous fiber, and compare the resulting acquisition values.
assumptions_latex: Each retained conditional maximum is attained and computed exactly for the exact guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widehat q,z_{\widehat q})\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(q,z)\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(q,z)\text{ under exact conditional solves}.
review_flags: Explicitly separates exact and approximate conditional solves.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Conditional Enumeration Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of conditional approximation bounds into a global mixed-domain certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose feasible \(z_q\in\mathcal X_q\) and numbers \(\varepsilon_q\geq0\) satisfy \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal X_q}\alpha_n(q,z)-\alpha_n(q,z_q)\leq\varepsilon_q\) for every nonempty fiber. If \(\widehat q\in\operatorname*{argmax}_q\alpha_n(q,z_q)\), then \[\sup_{(q,z)\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(q,z)-\alpha_n(\widehat q,z_{\widehat q})\leq\max_q\varepsilon_q.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known additive errors for all conditional solves combine into a global error bounded by the largest conditional error.
assumptions_latex: Every nonempty fiber has a feasible returned point and a valid additive gap bound.

notation.meaning: Certified additive error for conditional fiber q.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Conditional-Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work accounting for finite discrete enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If solving fiber \(q\) costs at most \(C_q\) acquisition evaluations, exact enumeration solves \(|\{q:\mathcal X_q\neq\varnothing\}|\) conditional problems and uses at most \(\sum_{q:\mathcal X_q\neq\varnothing}C_q\) such evaluations, plus linear-time comparison of the returned values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumeration work is the sum of the costs of all nonempty conditional solves.
assumptions_latex: Every nonempty discrete fiber is enumerated.
\(C_q\) bounds the work of conditional solve q.

notation.meaning: Acquisition-evaluation cost of solving conditional fiber q.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Enumeration Work

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional-Domain Decomposition of Mixed Acquisition Maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decomposition over finitely many discrete assignments and their continuous fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\bigcup_{q\in\mathcal Q}(\{q\}\times\mathcal X_q)\), where \(\mathcal Q\) is finite. Omitting empty fibers, \[\sup_{(q,z)\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(q,z)=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q}\sup_{z\in\mathcal X_q}\alpha_n(q,z).\] If every retained supremum is attained, a best conditional pair is a global maximizer on \(\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-domain acquisition maximization decomposes into continuous conditional problems followed by comparison across discrete assignments.
assumptions_latex: At least one \(\mathcal X_q\) is nonempty.

notation.meaning: Continuous feasible fiber conditional on discrete assignment q.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Domain Decomposition of Mixed Acquisition Maximization
Mixed-Domain Acquisition Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acquisition maximization over coupled continuous, integer, and categorical coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\bigcup_{q\in\mathcal Q}(\{q\}\times\mathcal X_q)\), where \(\mathcal Q\) is a finite set of discrete assignments and each \(\mathcal X_q\subset\mathbb R^{d_q}\) is the associated feasible continuous domain. For every \(q\), compute a feasible approximate maximizer \(z_q\) of \(z\mapsto\alpha_n(q,z)\) on \(\mathcal X_q\). Return \[(q_{n+1},z_{n+1})\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{q\in\mathcal Q}\alpha_n(q,z_q).\] If enumeration is impractical, a mixed-integer search may replace it, but must preserve categorical validity and coupled constraints. Stop at the acquisition-search budget and report the best feasible candidate found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-domain optimization compares valid discrete assignments and their optimized continuous coordinates, or uses a constraint-preserving mixed-integer search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of single-start local acquisition maximization distinct from the deferred seed example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal X=[0,2]\), let \(\alpha(x)=-x^2(x-2)^2+x^2(3-x)/4\). The point \(x=0\) is a strict local maximizer with \(\alpha'(0)=0\) and \(\alpha''(0)<0\), so gradient ascent initialized there remains there. Yet \(x=2\) is the unique global maximizer: writing \(h(x)=x^2(3-x)/4\), one has \(0\leq h(x)\leq1\) and \(\alpha(x)\leq h(x)\), with equality \(\alpha(2)=1>\alpha(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth acquisition can trap a single-start local solver at a strict local maximum whose acquisition value is below the global maximum.

Thus an exact-argmax interface requires compactness or another attainment condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous acquisition may have no maximizer on an open domain, making an exact-argmax interface ill posed.

Acquisition Optimization Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of single-start local acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal X=[0,1]\), consider the continuous acquisition \(\alpha(x)=4x^2-3x\). Its global maximizer is \(x=1\), with \(\alpha(1)=1\), while \(x=0\) is a strict constrained local maximizer because \(\alpha(x)<0=\alpha(0)\) for every sufficiently small \(x>0\). Moreover, projected gradient ascent initialized at \(x_0=0\) remains there: for any positive step size \(\eta\), \(\operatorname{proj}_{[0,1]}(x_0+\eta\alpha'(x_0))=0\). Hence a locally solved acquisition can return a strictly suboptimal next evaluation even when the acquisition is smooth and exactly evaluable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth acquisition can have a suboptimal constrained local maximum where projected ascent stops, so single-start optimization can select the wrong evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Global–Local Surrogate Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinated global exploration and local surrogate refinement using shared evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a global surrogate \(M_n^G\), a local surrogate \(M_n^L\), an incumbent \(x_n^*\), and a neighborhood \(B_n\) around the incumbent. Generate a global candidate by optimizing a global-search acquisition over \(\mathcal X\), and a local candidate by optimizing a model-based merit function over \(B_n\cap\mathcal X\). Select one candidate using a prescribed scheduler, evaluate the true objective there, and update both surrogates with the new observation. Expand or contract \(B_n\) according to agreement between local predicted and observed improvement. Stop at the evaluation budget and return the best evaluated feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared evaluation loop alternates global exploration with neighborhood refinement while updating both surrogates and adapting the local search region.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\neq\varnothing\), and every selected candidate is feasible.
Both surrogates can be updated from shared objective evaluations.
The scheduler invokes both global and local modes according to a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every expensive evaluation updates the global and local models, while neighborhood adaptation controls the scale of local refinement.
review_flags: The supplied locators do not establish this specific global–local surrogate coordination loop.

children.title: Surrogate Validation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to assess surrogate adequacy during global search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data-separation semantics for holdout, leave-one-out, k-fold, and sequential validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given indexed data \(D\), holdout validation fits on \(D\setminus V\) and scores on \(V\); leave-one-out excludes one response at a time; k-fold validation partitions \(D=V_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup V_K\), fits on \(D\setminus V_j\), and scores on \(V_j\); sequential validation scores a prediction recorded before the new response is assimilated. Aggregation weights and repeated partitioning must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Holdout, leave-one-out, k-fold, and sequential validation differ by which responses are excluded when predictions are formed.
assumptions_latex: Each validation fold is disjoint from its corresponding fitting set.
Sequential predictions are frozen before the response becomes available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i\notin D_{\rm fit}^{(i)}\) when the validation prediction for observation \(i\) is produced.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and interval diagnostics under noisy observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y_i=f(x_i)+\epsilon_i\), \(\operatorname{Var}(f(x_i)\mid D_{-i})=v_i\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(\epsilon_i)=\tau_i^2\), calibration diagnostics use total predictive variance \(v_i+\tau_i^2\). Under a correctly specified Gaussian predictive distribution, \[r_i=\frac{y_i-\mu_i}{\sqrt{v_i+\tau_i^2}}\sim N(0,1),\qquad \Pr\{y_i\in I_i(1-\alpha)\}=1-\alpha.\] Empirical agreement is diagnostic evidence, not proof of model correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy validation includes observation noise in predictive uncertainty, and nominal calibration is diagnostic rather than conclusive.
assumptions_latex: The predictive distribution and noise variance are correctly specified for the calibration implication.
The validation response was excluded when producing its prediction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_i\sim N(0,1)\) and the nominal interval has coverage \(1-\alpha\) under the stated model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Apparent validation success outside the represented decision region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), let all fitting and validation sites lie in \([0,1/2]\), and let \(s(x)=0\). Define \(f(x)=0\) on \([0,1/2]\) and \(f(x)=-1\) on \([3/4,1]\), with a continuous transition between them. Every validation error is zero, yet the surrogate is wrong throughout the minimizer region \([3/4,1]\).

assumptions_latex: Each validation prediction excludes its corresponding response from fitting.

Surrogate Validation Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical validation of a deterministic surrogate on withheld or newly evaluated sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k:X\to\mathbb R\) approximate \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(V_k\subset X\) be a nonempty validation set disjoint from the surrogate-fitting sites. For prescribed tolerances \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}},\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge 0\), define \[E_k=\max_{x\in V_k}\frac{|f(x)-s_k(x)|}{\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}|f(x)|},\] with a zero denominator interpreted as requiring exact agreement. The surrogate passes validation precisely when \(E_k\le 1\). If predicted rankings matter, one may additionally require \((s_k(x)-s_k(y))(f(x)-f(y))\ge 0\) for designated pairs \((x,y)\in V_k^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate is valid when normalized prediction errors stay within tolerance and, when required, its predicted ordering agrees with observed objective values.
review_flags: Exact validation criteria vary across surrogate-management frameworks.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the terminal container and is internally understandable, but the normalized-error threshold and optional ranking test are framework-specific choices with no cited source. A source is required to establish these as recognized surrogate-validation criteria rather than a newly proposed rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Refresh Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal refresh rule combining validation, age, and search-region coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(E_k\) be the current validation statistic, \(a_k\) the number of iterations since the last surrogate fit, and \(d_k=\min_{z\in D_k}\|x_k^{\mathrm{cand}}-z\|\), where \(D_k\) contains evaluated sites. Given thresholds \(1\), \(a_{\max}\in\mathbb N\), and \(d_{\max}>0\), trigger a refresh exactly when \[E_k>1\quad\lor\quad a_k\ge a_{\max}\quad\lor\quad d_k>d_{\max}.\] A refresh augments the fitting data with all newly completed evaluations and refits or updates the surrogate before its next search decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh the surrogate after validation failure, excessive age, or a proposal too far from evaluated data; include all newly completed observations.
assumptions_latex: The quantities \(E_k\), \(a_k\), and \(d_k\) are computable at the decision time.

children.title: Stale-Surrogate Failure
children.top_down_role: Search degradation caused by retaining an outdated surrogate.

assumptions_latex: No exploration or data-incorporation rule overrides surrogate minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=0\not\to x^\star=1\), so convergence to the true minimizer fails.

Content kind corrected from failure_boundary to counterexample.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing failure caused by indefinitely optimizing an unrefreshed surrogate without exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), let the unchanged surrogate be \(s(x)=x\), and let the true objective be \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\). Suppose every iteration minimizes \(s\) over \(X\), returns \(x_k=0\), and neither incorporates the observed value \(f(0)=1\) nor forces evaluation away from \(0\). Then \(x_k=0\) for all \(k\), while the unique global minimizer of \(f\) is \(x^\star=1\) with \(f(x^\star)=0\). Thus, without refresh or an exploration mechanism, repeated surrogate minimization need not approach a true minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unrefreshed surrogate can repeatedly select the wrong point forever, so surrogate minimization alone gives no global-convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Surrogate Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: RBF global search using exclusion balls around evaluated sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fit an RBF surrogate \(s_k\), prescribe \(\rho_k\ge0\), and solve \(x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}s_k(x)\) subject to \(d(x,D_k)\ge\rho_k\). Positive \(\rho_k\) enforces exploration; \(\rho_k=0\) permits pure surrogate minimization. The constrained subproblem must be feasible, and a global-search claim requires a specified radius schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CORS minimizes the RBF surrogate outside exclusion balls, with the radius controlling exploration.
assumptions_latex: The distance-constrained subproblem is feasible when invoked.
review_flags: Global consistency depends on the exact exclusion-radius schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: CORS Distance-Constrained RBF Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Need for explicit exploration in sequential RBF global optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The rule \(x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_Xs_k(x)\) alone need not produce a dense sample set or visit a neighborhood of a global minimizer. Interpolation and exact solution of each surrogate subproblem therefore do not imply global convergence; a distance, target, randomized, or other globally exploring mechanism is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly minimizing only the current RBF interpolant has no general global-consistency guarantee.
assumptions_latex: No mechanism forces sampling of unexplored regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \arg\min s_k\text{ sampling alone does not imply global consistency}.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure Surrogate-Minimization Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target-value sampling through minimum additional native-space bumpiness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k\) be a minimum-seminorm RBF interpolant of \((x_i,f_i)_{i=1}^k\), and choose \(T_k<f_k^{\min}\). For each admissible \(x\notin D_k\), let \(s_{k,x}\) interpolate the existing data and satisfy \(s_{k,x}(x)=T_k\). Select \[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X\setminus D_k}\|s_{k,x}\|_{\mathcal H_\phi},\] subject to the kernel's polynomial side conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gutmann target-value step samples where imposing an aspirational value requires the least native-space bumpiness.
assumptions_latex: The kernel and polynomial space make every invoked augmented interpolation problem well posed.
Candidate optimization is over admissible unsampled points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) minimizes the augmented-interpolant seminorm for target \(T_k\).

notation.meaning: native space or seminorm associated with the RBF kernel

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Exclusion Radius Cannot Persist Indefinitely
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing boundary for CORS-style distance constraints on compact domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and suppose a sequential rule requires \[d(x_{k+1},D_k)\geq\rho\] for one fixed \(\rho>0\) at every iteration. Then all evaluated sites are pairwise at least \(\rho\) apart. Every \(\rho\)-separated subset of a compact set is finite, so after finitely many evaluations the distance-constrained subproblem becomes infeasible. An infinite CORS run must therefore reduce the exclusion radius along a subsequence or otherwise relax the distance constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive exclusion radius permits only finitely many samples on a compact domain, so an infinite CORS schedule must eventually shrink or relax it.
assumptions_latex: The same exclusion radius \(\rho>0\) is enforced at every iteration.
Previously evaluated sites are retained in \(D_k\).

notation.meaning: distance from x to the evaluated set

Radial-Basis Global Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential global search using an interpolating radial-basis surrogate and an exploration term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given compact \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\), evaluated sites \(D_k=\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}\), and values \(f(x_i)\), fit \[s_k(x)=\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i\phi(\|x-x_i\|)+p(x)\] subject to \(s_k(x_i)=f(x_i)\) and the side conditions required by the chosen kernel and polynomial space. Select \(x_{k+1}\) by minimizing \(s_k(x)-\eta_k d(x,D_k)\) over \(X\), where \(d(x,D_k)=\min_i\|x-x_i\|\) and \(\eta_k\ge0\) follows a schedule containing infinitely many positive exploration weights. Evaluate \(f(x_{k+1})\), augment \(D_k\), and stop at the evaluation budget, returning the best evaluated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit an RBF interpolant, balance low predicted values against distance from sampled sites, evaluate the selected point, and return the best observation.
assumptions_latex: The RBF interpolation system is solvable for every fitted data set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is \(x_{i^\star}\), where \(i^\star\in\arg\min_{1\le i\le k} f(x_i)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal EGO extensions for batches and unknown feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X_q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), define \(q\operatorname{EI}(X_q)=\mathbb E[(f^{\min}-\min_{1\le j\le q}Y(x_j))_+]\). If feasibility is modeled independently of objective improvement with probability \(p_F(x)\), constrained expected improvement is \(\operatorname{CEI}(x)=\operatorname{EI}(x)p_F(x)\). These reduce to ordinary EI when \(q=1\) and \(p_F(x)=1\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch EI values joint improvement from several points; constrained EI weights improvement by modeled feasibility.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior of the batch predictions is defined.
The CEI product uses conditional independence of improvement and feasibility.
review_flags: The CEI product is not generally valid without the stated independence assumption.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch and Constrained Expected-Improvement Variants

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the noiseless-EI interpretation under observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(y_i=f(x_i)+\epsilon_i\) with nondegenerate noise, then \(\min_i y_i\) need not be the best latent objective value and posterior variance need not vanish at sampled sites. Substituting \(\min_i y_i\) into classical noiseless EI can therefore react to a noise outlier rather than latent improvement; a noisy incumbent and noise-aware acquisition must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With observation noise, the best observed response can be an outlier, so classical noiseless EI is not a valid latent-improvement rule.
assumptions_latex: At least one observation has nonzero noise variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy-Incumbent Boundary for Classical EI

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core exploitation-exploration structure of Gaussian expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y(x)\sim N(\mu(x),\sigma(x)^2)\), \(\operatorname{EI}(x)=\mathbb E[(f^{\min}-Y(x))_+]=(f^{\min}-\mu(x))\Phi(z)+\sigma(x)\varphi(z)\), where \(z=(f^{\min}-\mu(x))/\sigma(x)\). If \(\sigma(x)=0\), the continuous extension is \((f^{\min}-\mu(x))_+\); at a noiseless interpolated sampled site it is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected improvement combines predicted improvement with uncertainty and vanishes at noiseless interpolated sample sites.
assumptions_latex: The scalar posterior prediction is Gaussian.
The incumbent is the best noiseless observed value.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Improvement Decomposition and Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior one-step improvement bound, not a deterministic global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\sup_{x\in X}\operatorname{EI}_k(x)\le\varepsilon\), then for every \(x\in X\), \[\mathbb E[(f_k^{\min}-Y_k(x))_+\mid D_k]\le\varepsilon.\] This does not imply \(f_k^{\min}-\min_X f\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small maximum EI bounds posterior one-step expected improvement but does not certify deterministic global optimality.
assumptions_latex: EI is computed from the stated posterior and incumbent.
The supremum is evaluated or validly bounded.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-EI One-Step Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exploitation-exploration monotonicity of scalar Gaussian expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\sigma>0\), let \(\operatorname{EI}(\mu,\sigma)=(f^{\min}-\mu)\Phi(z)+\sigma\varphi(z)\), where \(z=(f^{\min}-\mu)/\sigma\). Then \[\frac{\partial\operatorname{EI}}{\partial\mu}=-\Phi(z)\le0,\qquad \frac{\partial\operatorname{EI}}{\partial\sigma}=\varphi(z)>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian expected improvement decreases with posterior mean and increases strictly with posterior uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Improvement Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Domain Termination of Exact Noiseless EGO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global identification by expected improvement on a finite design space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite, let observations be noiseless, and let the fixed Gaussian-process kernel be strictly positive definite on \(X\). Suppose classical expected improvement is maximized exactly at every iteration. Conditional variance is zero at evaluated sites and positive at every unevaluated site; hence EI is zero at evaluated sites and strictly positive at unevaluated sites. Each iteration therefore evaluates a new point, and after at most \(|X|-|D_0|\) additional evaluations the incumbent is a global minimizer of \(f\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite domain with a fixed strictly positive-definite kernel, exact noiseless expected improvement samples a new point each iteration and identifies a global optimum after at most all remaining designs are evaluated.
assumptions_latex: The GP kernel is fixed and strictly positive definite on \(X\).
Expected improvement is maximized exactly at each iteration.
The initial evaluated set \(D_0\) is nonempty and contains distinct sites.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{additional}}\leq |X|-|D_0|\quad\text{and the resulting incumbent lies in }\arg\min_{x\in X}f(x).

Efficient Global Optimization Family

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and let \(D_k\) contain noiseless observations of \(f\). Condition a Gaussian-process model on \(D_k\), obtaining posterior mean \(\mu_k(x)\) and standard deviation \(\sigma_k(x)\), and set \(f_k^{\min}=\min_{(x_i,f_i)\in D_k}f_i\). For minimization define \[\operatorname{EI}_k(x)=(f_k^{\min}-\mu_k(x))\Phi(z_k(x))+\sigma_k(x)\varphi(z_k(x)),\qquad z_k(x)=\frac{f_k^{\min}-\mu_k(x)}{\sigma_k(x)},\] with \(\operatorname{EI}_k(x)=0\) when \(\sigma_k(x)=0\). Choose a maximizer of expected improvement, evaluate it, update the posterior, and return the best observation when the budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: EGO repeatedly evaluates the point with greatest posterior expected improvement over the best observed objective value.
assumptions_latex: A maximizer of \(\operatorname{EI}_k\) is selected at each iteration.
