children.title: Lipschitz Global Search
children.top_down_role: Global derivative-free search organized by Lipschitz information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invalid Lower Envelope Under Lipschitz Underestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of lower bounds when the supplied constant is too small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[0,1]\), let \(f(x)=-Lx\) and sample only \(x_1=0\). If \(0\le\widehat L<L\), the declared envelope is \(\widehat\ell(x)=-\widehat Lx\), but \(\widehat\ell(1)=-\widehat L>-L=f(1)\). It is therefore not a lower bound, and an incumbent-envelope gap based on it is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant below the true Lipschitz modulus can place the supposed lower envelope above the objective.

notation.meaning: envelope formed using the underestimated constant

knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Lower Envelope Under Lipschitz Underestimation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct extremal characterization of the sample-induced lower envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For mutually \(L\)-consistent samples \((x_i,f_i)\), define \(\ell(x)=\max_i\{f_i-Ld(x,x_i)\}\). Then \(\ell\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(\ell(x_i)=f_i\). Every \(L\)-Lipschitz function \(g\) interpolating the samples satisfies \(g(x)\ge\ell(x)\) for all \(x\). Thus \(\ell\) is the pointwise least \(L\)-Lipschitz interpolating extension and the sharpest sample-only lower bound for an unknown admissible objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cone envelope is the least Lipschitz interpolant consistent with the samples and hence the sharpest universal lower bound.
review_flags: Corrected the Builder's reversed extremal inequality: the lower envelope is the least consistent extension, not the greatest minorant.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Consistent Lipschitz Extension
Lipschitz Global Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global minimization using valid Lipschitz lower bounds on spatial regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be compact and suppose \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le Ld(x,y)\) for known \(L\ge0\). From evaluated sites \(D_k\), define the global lower envelope \[\ell_k(x)=\max_{x_i\in D_k}\{f(x_i)-L d(x,x_i)\}.\] Choose \(x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X}\ell_k(x)\), evaluate \(f(x_{k+1})\), and augment \(D_k\). With incumbent \(u_k=\min_{x_i\in D_k}f(x_i)\) and lower bound \(b_k=\min_{x\in X}\ell_k(x)\), stop when \(u_k-b_k\le\varepsilon\); return an incumbent minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known Lipschitz continuity yields a global lower envelope; searching its minimum continues until the incumbent–lower-bound gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a nonempty compact metric space.
The lower-envelope minimization is solved globally.
review_flags: Supplied source locators do not identify Lipschitz global optimization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower envelope and termination certificate are mathematically coherent and fit an algorithm container, but no source specifically supports this Lipschitz global-search formulation.

children.title: Partition-Based Global Search
children.top_down_role: Global search organized through adaptive domain partitions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when refinement permanently ignores the minimizer's region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \([0,1]\), let \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\). A partition scheme that evaluates representatives only in \([0,1/2]\) has incumbents at least \(1/4\), although \(\min f=0\). Thus nested partitions alone do not imply global consistency: selection must eventually sample arbitrarily near every possible minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition method may miss the optimum forever if it never samples or refines the minimizer's region.
assumptions_latex: The refinement rule may permanently ignore a nonempty region.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonshrinking-Cell Failure Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic convergence of partition search without Lipschitz-specific bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact and \(f\) continuous. If the evaluated representatives \(\{x_k\}\) have the property that every neighborhood of every global minimizer contains some \(x_k\), then \(u_k=\min_{i\le k}f(x_i)\) decreases to \(\min_Xf\). In particular, the conclusion holds when refinement and representative selection guarantee this minimizer-neighborhood density.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous objective is solved asymptotically when partition refinement evaluates points arbitrarily near every global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Evaluated representatives enter every neighborhood of every global minimizer.

notation.meaning: best evaluated value through iteration k

review_flags: Geometric diameter conditions are sufficient only when they also guarantee representative density near minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive-Refinement Global Consistency

assumptions_latex: Every \(\mathcal P_k\) is a finite partition of compact \(X\).
Selected cells admit finite refinements covering the parent cell.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for cell C

review_flags: Generic partition framework; a source is needed to select a named implementation.
Undefined eta_k corrected to the defined lower bound beta_k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimistic refinement of a nested partition using valid cell lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact and let \(\mathcal P_k\) be a finite partition of \(X\) into cells. For every active cell \(C\), maintain a sampled representative \(x_C\in C\), an upper value \(f(x_C)\), and a certified lower bound \(B(C)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(C_k\in\arg\min_{C\in\mathcal P_k}B(C)\), replace it by finitely many child cells whose union is \(C_k\), and evaluate any previously unevaluated child representatives. Stop when \(u_k-\beta_k\le\varepsilon\), where \(u_k\) is the best evaluated value and \(\beta_k=\min_{C\in\mathcal P_k}B(C)\); return an incumbent minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly split the cell with the best valid lower bound and stop when its bound nearly matches the best sampled value.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Based Global Search

children.title: Coupled Lipschitz–Partition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Frameworks where Lipschitz information guides partition-based exploration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate coupling a partition cell with a valid Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz, \(x_C\in C\), and \(r_C=\sup_{x\in C}d(x,x_C)\), then \(f(x)\ge f(x_C)-Ld(x,x_C)\ge f(x_C)-Lr_C=:B_L(C)\) for every \(x\in C\). Hence \(B_L(C)\le\inf_C f\), and \(\min_{C\in\mathcal P}B_L(C)\) is a global lower bound for any covering partition \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cell representative and radius convert a valid Lipschitz constant into cellwise and global lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: The active cells cover the search domain.

notation.meaning: Lipschitz lower bound for cell C

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Cell Lower-Bound Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for Lipschitz partition-cell bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=[0,1]\), take \(x_C=0\) and \(f(x)=-Lx\). If \(0\le\widehat L<L\), then \(f(0)-\widehat Lr_C=-\widehat L>-L=\inf_Cf\). Thus a cell bound formed with an underestimated constant can invalidate pruning and incumbent-minus-bound stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Underestimating the Lipschitz constant can cause false pruning or false optimality certification.
assumptions_latex: A cell bound is formed with \(\widehat L<L\).
knowledge_statements.title: Underestimated-Lipschitz Coupling Failure
Coupled Lipschitz–Partition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition search whose cell certificates are constructed from Lipschitz continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be compact, let \(f\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz, and let each active cell \(C\) have representative \(x_C\in C\) and radius \(r_C=\sup_{x\in C}d(x,x_C)\). Assign the certified bound \[B_L(C)=f(x_C)-Lr_C.\] Select a cell minimizing \(B_L(C)\), refine it into children, evaluate their representatives, and repeat. If the incumbent is \(u_k\), stop when \(u_k-\min_{C\in\mathcal P_k}B_L(C)\le\varepsilon\). A globally convergent refinement regime additionally requires that every repeatedly selected nested cell sequence have radii tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lipschitz continuity converts each partition cell’s center value and radius into a lower bound used for optimistic refinement and certification.
assumptions_latex: Each active cell has a finite-radius evaluated representative.
Repeatedly selected nested cells have radii converging to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_L(C)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\), and the stated stopping rule yields an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal incumbent.

notation.meaning: radius of cell C about its representative

review_flags: Supplied locators do not cover coupled Lipschitz–partition search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latent-value expected improvement when sampled objective values remain uncertain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_n\) be noisy data and let \((F_1,\ldots,F_n,F_x)\) be the joint posterior latent values at sampled sites and candidate \(x\). For minimization, \[\operatorname{NEI}_n(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[\left(\min_{1\le i\le n}F_i-F_x\right)_+\mid D_n\right].\] Equivalently, ordinary expected improvement conditional on sampled latent values is averaged over their posterior law. If the sampled latent values are known, this becomes ordinary expected improvement relative to their minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy expected improvement integrates improvement over uncertainty in the latent incumbent and candidate value.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate supplies their joint posterior distribution.
Improvement is measured relative to sampled latent values rather than raw noisy observations.

notation.meaning: latent value at sampled site i

Noisy Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Bayesian optimization with conditionally noisy observations and latent-objective acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observations satisfy \(y_i=f(x_i)+\epsilon_i\), with conditionally independent \(\epsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_i^2)\). Given data \(D_k=\{(x_i,y_i,\sigma_i^2)\}_{i=1}^k\), condition a probabilistic surrogate for the latent function \(f\). Choose \(x_{k+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in X}\alpha_k(x;D_k)\), where \(\alpha_k\) is computed from the noisy posterior and targets a stated utility, such as expected reduction of the posterior minimum. Observe \(y_{k+1}\), update the posterior, and repeat until the evaluation budget is exhausted. Return a point minimizing the final posterior mean, or the point maximizing a separately declared recommendation utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy Bayesian optimization updates a latent-function posterior from uncertain observations and chooses evaluations through a noise-aware acquisition function.
assumptions_latex: Observation variances \(\sigma_i^2\) are known or inferred within the surrogate model.
Observation noises are conditionally independent given the latent function.
The recommendation rule is fixed before termination.
review_flags: Acquisition and recommendation conventions vary; supplied locators do not cover noisy Bayesian optimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Replication Reduces Measurement Uncertainty but Not Latent Prior Uncertainty Instantly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Gaussian variance update for repeated noisy evaluations at one location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on all data away from \(x\), with \(f(x)\sim\mathcal N(m,v)\). If \(y_j=f(x)+\varepsilon_j\), where the \(r\) errors are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\), then \(\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid y_{1:r})=(v^{-1}+r\sigma^{-2})^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent replication adds precision linearly and therefore has diminishing posterior-variance benefit.
assumptions_latex: Replicate errors are conditionally independent with common variance.
review_flags: deferred_misplaced: The precision law is primarily owned by the replication-regime topic, not by noisy Bayesian optimization.

children.title: Synchronous Batch Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization using coordinated groups of simultaneously proposed evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint expected improvement for a simultaneously evaluated batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization with declared latent or noiseless incumbent \(f_\star\), the \(q\)-point expected improvement of \(X_q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\) is \[q\operatorname{-EI}(X_q)=\mathbb E\!\left[\left(f_\star-\min_{1\le j\le q}F(x_j)\right)_+\mid D\right].\] It uses the joint posterior distribution and reduces to ordinary expected improvement for \(q=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch expected improvement measures improvement by the best member of a jointly modeled batch.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate supplies the joint posterior law of batch values.
The incumbent convention matches the observation-noise regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Expected Improvement
Synchronous Batch Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch Bayesian optimization with barrier synchronization between successive posterior updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given posterior data \(D_k\), batch size \(q\), and joint acquisition \(\alpha_k^{(q)}:X^q\to\mathbb R\), select \[(x_{k,1},\ldots,x_{k,q})\in\arg\max_{(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in X^q}\alpha_k^{(q)}(x_1,\ldots,x_q).\] Dispatch all \(q\) evaluations simultaneously and wait until every result \(y_{k,j}\) is returned. Then set \(D_{k+1}=D_k\cup\{(x_{k,j},y_{k,j}):1\le j\le q\}\), update the posterior once, and launch the next batch. Stop when the evaluation or batch budget is exhausted and return the declared posterior or observed incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a joint batch, wait for every evaluation to finish, then update the posterior once and launch the next batch.
assumptions_latex: Exactly \(q\) evaluations are dispatched per full batch.
No posterior update occurs before all results in the current batch return.
A maximizer of the joint acquisition is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each posterior update incorporates an entire completed batch of \(q\) observations.
review_flags: Supplied asynchronous-optimization locator is not specific to Bayesian batch scheduling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The barrier-synchronized batch procedure and algorithm kind match the terminal container, but no Bayesian-optimization source supports the joint acquisition and scheduling formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic idle-time accounting for a synchronous evaluation batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For simultaneously started evaluations with durations \(T_1,\ldots,T_q\), the barrier releases at \(T_{\max}=\max_jT_j\), and aggregate idle time is \(W=\sum_j(T_{\max}-T_j)=qT_{\max}-\sum_jT_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous batch releases at its slowest evaluation and incurs slowest-minus-individual idle time.
assumptions_latex: Each evaluation occupies one worker until completion.
review_flags: deferred_misplaced: This is generic synchronous barrier accounting, already owned outside the Bayesian-optimization leaf.

children.title: Asynchronous Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization issuing new proposals as evaluation capacity becomes available.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion-order selection when evaluation duration carries unmodeled outcome information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be evaluation duration and \(Y\) its outcome. If duration depends on the outcome, then generally \[p(Y\mid x,D,T\le t)\ne p(Y\mid x,D).\] An asynchronous BO update that ignores this completion selection can therefore be misspecified. Ignoring completion time is justified under \(T\perp Y\mid x,D\), or when the runtime/censoring mechanism is modeled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Completion order can bias asynchronous inference when runtimes depend on outcomes.
assumptions_latex: Completion status is observed while other outcomes remain pending.
The surrogate does not otherwise model runtime or censoring.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\not\!\perp Y\mid x,D\Longrightarrow p(Y\mid x,D,T\le t)\text{ may differ from }p(Y\mid x,D).
review_flags: Claim is limited to the conditional-selection boundary; runtime-aware BO models require separate specification.
knowledge_statements.title: Informative-Runtime Boundary
Asynchronous Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worker-based Bayesian optimization without a barrier between posterior updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain completed data \(D_t\), pending locations \(P_t\), and \(q\) workers. Whenever any worker becomes free, incorporate every newly returned observation into \(D_t\), remove its location from \(P_t\), update the posterior, and choose \[x_{\mathrm{new}}\in\arg\max_{x\in X\setminus P_t}\alpha_t(x\mid D_t,P_t).\] Dispatch \(x_{\mathrm{new}}\) immediately and add it to \(P_t\), without waiting for other pending evaluations. Continue until the dispatch budget is exhausted, subsequently collect required outstanding results, and return the declared incumbent based on completed data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever a worker finishes, update with completed results and immediately dispatch a new acquisition maximizer while accounting for pending evaluations.
assumptions_latex: At most \(q\) evaluations are pending concurrently.
The acquisition function explicitly conditions on or adjusts for \(P_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A free worker is assigned without waiting for all other pending evaluations to finish.

notation.meaning: completed observations at scheduling time t

children.title: Pending-Evaluation Management
children.top_down_role: Treatment of incomplete evaluations during acquisition decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo marginalization over unfinished evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given completed data \(D\), pending locations \(P\), and acquisition \(a(x;D,Y_P)\), draw conditionally independent joint fantasies \(Y_P^{(m)}\sim p(Y_P\mid D)\) and set \[\widehat a_M(x)=M^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^M a(x;D,Y_P^{(m)}).\] If the acquisition is integrable, this estimator is conditionally unbiased and converges almost surely, for fixed \(x\), to \(\mathbb E[a(x;D,Y_P)\mid D]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint posterior fantasies Monte Carlo-approximate exact marginalization over pending outcomes.
assumptions_latex: Fantasis are conditionally independent draws from the joint pending predictive law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[\widehat a_M(x)\mid D]=\mathbb E[a(x;D,Y_P)\mid D],\quad \widehat a_M(x)\to\mathbb E[a(x;D,Y_P)\mid D]\text{ a.s.}
review_flags: Almost-sure convergence is pointwise in the candidate unless stronger uniform assumptions are added.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Fantasization for Pending Outcomes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior-mean hallucination and constant-liar pending rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A plug-in rule chooses deterministic pending outcomes \(\widetilde Y_P\) and evaluates \(a(x;D,\widetilde Y_P)\). Posterior-mean hallucination uses \(\widetilde Y_P=\mathbb E[Y_P\mid D]\); constant liar assigns a declared constant \(L\). Generally, \[a(x;D,\mathbb E[Y_P\mid D])\ne\mathbb E[a(x;D,Y_P)\mid D],\] so these rules are approximations rather than exact marginalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior-mean and constant-liar rules replace pending outcomes by deterministic guesses and are generally inexact.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition can be evaluated after hypothetical data augmentation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a(x;D,\widetilde Y_P)\text{ is generally not the posterior-marginal acquisition.}
knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Pending-Value Approximations
Pending-Evaluation Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior-acquisition consistency conditions for locations whose outcomes have not returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At scheduling time \(t\), partition dispatched evaluations into completed data \(D_t\) and pending locations \(P_t\). A pending-aware decision rule must satisfy three conditions: pending outcomes are not inserted into \(D_t\) as observations; the acquisition \(\alpha_t(x\mid D_t,P_t)\) accounts for uncertainty at every point in \(P_t\), for example by integrating over their joint posterior predictive outcomes; and duplicate dispatch is prohibited unless replication is explicitly allowed. Under exact integration, \[\alpha_t(x\mid D_t,P_t)=\mathbb E\!\left[\alpha_t(x\mid D_t,Y_{P_t})\mid D_t\right],\] where \(Y_{P_t}\) denotes the random pending outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track pending sites separately, integrate over their unknown outcomes when scoring new points, and prevent accidental duplicate dispatches.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate defines a joint posterior predictive law for pending outcomes.
Completed and pending evaluations are consistently identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditional expectation defines an exact pending-aware acquisition value.
review_flags: Pending-value strategies differ, and supplied locators do not support the Bayesian conditional-expectation formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Separating completed and pending evaluations fits the container, but exact posterior integration is one pending-evaluation strategy rather than a universal management condition. The conditional-expectation formula and duplicate-dispatch policy require a Bayesian-optimization source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Posterior Feasibility Is Not a Feasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes acquisition weighting from verified feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<p_n^{\mathrm{feas}}(x)<1\), selection using posterior feasibility does not imply actual satisfaction of all constraints. Certification requires an evaluation, a valid deterministic bound, or a calibrated probabilistic guarantee under stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: High modeled feasibility probability is not proof of feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Posterior feasibility guides sampling but does not generally certify constraint satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Feasibility Is Not a Feasibility Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected improvement gated by posterior feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_n^*\) be the best observed feasible value and \(C(x)=\{c_j(x)\le0\ \forall j\}\). Then \[\operatorname{CEI}_n(x)=\mathbb E[(f_n^*-f(x))_+\mathbf1_{C(x)}\mid D_n].\] If the candidate objective and constraint vector are conditionally independent, \(\operatorname{CEI}_n(x)=\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\Pr(C(x)\mid D_n)\); otherwise the factorization need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained EI is expected feasible improvement and factors only under posterior independence.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint feasibility for multiple black-box constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasibility weight is \(p_n^{\mathrm{feas}}(x)=\Pr(c_1(x)\le0,\ldots,c_m(x)\le0\mid D_n)\). It equals the product of marginal feasibility probabilities only under conditional independence of the constraints at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple-constraint feasibility is a joint probability; multiplying marginals requires conditional independence.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior constraint distribution is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Marginal constraint probabilities do not generally determine joint feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Posterior Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety-preserving constrained Bayesian optimization using simultaneous upper confidence bounds and a known safe seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(c_j(x)\le0\), suppose \(U_{j,n}(x)\) satisfy the simultaneous event \(\mathcal E=\{c_j(x)\le U_{j,n}(x)\ \forall x,j,n\}\). Starting from a nonempty certified set \(S_0\), define \(S_n=\{x:U_{j,n}(x)\le0\ \forall j\}\) and select every evaluation \(x_{n+1}\) from \(S_n\) using a declared safe objective or expansion acquisition. On \(\mathcal E\), every evaluated point satisfies every constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safe constrained Bayesian optimization restricts evaluations to a confidence-certified safe set initialized from known-safe designs.
assumptions_latex: S_0\neq\varnothing\text{ and every point in }S_0\text{ is certified feasible}.
Every queried point belongs to the current certified set.

notation.meaning: simultaneous upper confidence bound for constraint value c_j(x)
simultaneous validity event for all constraint bounds

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Certified Safe Evaluation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Safe Exploration Requires Certified Initialization and Reachability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization and reachability boundary for safety-preserving Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose no point is independently certified feasible and, for every candidate \(x\), the model class contains observationally indistinguishable constraint alternatives under which respectively \(c(x)\le0\) and \(c(x)>0\). Then no algorithm can both guarantee feasibility of its first evaluation and evaluate a new point. Even from a safe seed, a policy restricted to certified points cannot reach a disconnected safe component unless its assumptions certify a safe path or directly certify a point in that component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guaranteed safety requires certified initialization, and exploration may remain confined to the safely reachable component.
assumptions_latex: Safety must hold before the queried constraint value is observed.
The stated feasible and infeasible alternatives belong to the model class and are indistinguishable from available data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nontrivial guaranteed-safe exploration requires certified initialization and a valid certification or reachability mechanism.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Exploration Requires Certified Initialization and Reachability
Constrained Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-weighted acquisition for expensive black-box inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given objective observations and constraint observations, fit probabilistic surrogates for \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and \(c_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), \(j=1,\ldots,m\). At iteration \(n\), initialize the incumbent as the best observed feasible point, when one exists, and select
\[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_n(x)\Pr_n\!\left(c_j(x)\leq0\ \text{for all }j=1,\ldots,m\right),\]
where \(a_n\) is an objective-improvement acquisition. If no feasible observation exists, use a specified feasibility acquisition instead. Evaluate \(f\) and the constraints at \(x_{n+1}\), update all surrogates, and stop at the evaluation budget; output the best observed feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly maximize an objective acquisition weighted by joint posterior feasibility, update the objective and constraint surrogates, and return the best evaluated feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is a nonempty search domain.
Objective and constraint evaluations are available at queried points.
The acquisition maximization rule and evaluation budget are specified.

notation.meaning: posterior probability conditional on current data

children.title: Mixed-Variable Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization across domains containing multiple variable types.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact type-preserving acquisition optimization over finite discrete assignments and conditional continuous domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be a finite set of admissible integer-categorical assignments, let \(C(d)\) be the continuous feasible set conditional on \(d\), and let \(a_n(c,d)\) be an acquisition function. If every conditional maximum is attained, then
\[\max_{\substack{d\in D\\c\in C(d)}}a_n(c,d)=\max_{d\in D}\max_{c\in C(d)}a_n(c,d).\]
Thus enumerating \(d\), globally solving each conditional continuous subproblem, and selecting the best result is an exact type-preserving acquisition optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed acquisition can be optimized exactly by enumerating finite discrete assignments and globally solving their conditional continuous subproblems.
assumptions_latex: Each conditional acquisition maximum is attained and solved globally.

notation.meaning: continuous domain conditional on assignment d

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Assignment Acquisition Decomposition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of optimize-then-round proposals on mixed conditional domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let d\in\{0,1\}, C(0)=[0,1/4], and C(1)=[3/4,1]. The relaxed point (c,d)=(1/2,0.6) rounds componentwise to (1/2,1), but 1/2\notin C(1).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent rounding can violate constraints whose continuous domain depends on the selected discrete assignment.

notation.meaning: continuous feasible set conditional on d

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Can Destroy Conditional Feasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-consistency boundary for mixed-variable search with dense conditional continuous sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be finite, each nonempty \(C(d)\) be compact, and \(f(\cdot,d)\) be continuous on \(C(d)\). If the evaluated sequence is dense in every \(C(d)\times\{d\}\), then \[\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\longrightarrow\min_{d\in D,\,c\in C(d)}f(c,d).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense sampling within every finite discrete assignment makes incumbent values converge to the mixed-domain global minimum.
assumptions_latex: Evaluated points are dense in every conditional domain.

notation.meaning: finite set of admissible discrete assignments
continuous feasible set conditional on assignment d

review_flags: Coverage theorem only; it does not establish dense sampling for an unspecified Bayesian acquisition policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Type-Preserving Dense-Sampling Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Type-preserving mixed acquisition optimization with certified conditional approximation errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be finite and let \(C(d)\) be the continuous feasible set for assignment \(d\). Suppose \(\widehat c_d\in C(d)\) satisfies
\[a_n(\widehat c_d,d)\geq\sup_{c\in C(d)}a_n(c,d)-\varepsilon_d\]
for every \(d\in D\), and choose \(\widehat d\in\arg\max_{d\in D}a_n(\widehat c_d,d)\). Then
\[a_n(\widehat c_{\widehat d},\widehat d)\geq\sup_{d\in D,\,c\in C(d)}a_n(c,d)-\max_{d\in D}\varepsilon_d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solving every conditional continuous acquisition problem and selecting the best type-valid result gives a global mixed-domain approximation bound.
assumptions_latex: Each conditional solution has the displayed certified error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a_n(\widehat c_{\widehat d},\widehat d)\geq\sup_{d\in D,\,c\in C(d)}a_n(c,d)-\max_d\varepsilon_d.

notation.meaning: conditional acquisition-optimization error for assignment d

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Conditional Acquisition Decomposition
Mixed-Variable Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian optimization on product domains containing multiple variable types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\mathcal X=\mathcal X_{m cont}\times\mathcal X_{m int}\times\mathcal X_{m cat},\]
where \(\mathcal X_{m cont}\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), \(\mathcal X_{m int}\subseteq\mathbb Z^q\), and \(\mathcal X_{m cat}=\prod_{r=1}^s\mathcal C_r\) with finite category sets \(\mathcal C_r\). Mixed-variable Bayesian optimization is sequential optimization of an expensive black-box function \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) using a probabilistic surrogate and an acquisition function defined on this product domain. Every proposed point must retain integer and categorical validity; continuous relaxation followed by an unspecified projection does not itself define the method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-variable Bayesian optimization uses a probabilistic surrogate and acquisition rule while preserving continuous, integer, and categorical domains at every query.
assumptions_latex: Each categorical set \(\mathcal C_r\) is finite and nonempty.
The black-box objective can be evaluated at every admissible query.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports its particular three-block scope or its categorical-validity and projection qualifications.

children.title: Categorical Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization specialized to unordered discrete choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact global-optimality certificate and identifiability boundary for an unrestricted finite categorical domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be finite and \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be deterministic and otherwise unrestricted. If every \(x\in\mathcal X\) has been evaluated, any least-observed point \(\widehat x\) is globally optimal. If an element \(u\in\mathcal X\) remains unevaluated, the observations alone cannot certify global optimality, because another objective can agree at all evaluated points and take a strictly smaller value at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhausting a finite categorical domain certifies the optimum; without structural assumptions, one unevaluated configuration prevents such a certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=\mathcal X\Rightarrow\min_{x\in S}f(x)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x),\quad S\neq\mathcal X\Rightarrow\text{observations alone do not certify equality}.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Exhaustion Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relabeling-invariant covariance for unordered categorical coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x,x'\in\prod_{r=1}^s\mathcal C_r\), \(\theta_r\geq0\), and \(\sigma^2\geq0\), define
\[k(x,x')=\sigma^2\exp\!\left(-\sum_{r=1}^s\theta_r\mathbf1\{x_r\neq x'_r\}\right).\]
Then \(k\) is positive semidefinite and invariant under any consistent permutation of the labels within each \(\mathcal C_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponentiating weighted Hamming distance gives a valid covariance independent of arbitrary categorical label names.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal C_r\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is positive semidefinite and invariant under coordinatewise category relabeling.
knowledge_statements.title: Exponentiated Hamming Covariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for applying a one-dimensional distance kernel to unordered labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let e:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R be injective and k_e(c,c')=\varphi(|e(c)-e(c')|), where \varphi is injective on the attained distances. Invariance under every permutation of \mathcal C requires all distinct encoded labels to be equidistant. This is impossible in \mathbb R when |\mathcal C|\geq3.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-dimensional numeric encoding of at least three unordered labels makes a distance-sensitive kernel depend on arbitrary label ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\mathcal C|\geq3\Rightarrow k_e\text{ is not invariant under all label permutations}.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordinal-Encoding Relabeling Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain posterior, acquisition, update, and recommendation interface for categorical-only Bayesian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize data \(D_0\) on \(\mathcal X=\prod_r\mathcal C_r\). At iteration \(n\), fit or update a declared categorical probabilistic surrogate, construct acquisition \(a_n\), and choose \(x_{n+1}\in\mathcal X\) satisfying \(a_n(x_{n+1})\ge\max_{x\in\mathcal X}a_n(x)-\varepsilon_n\). Observe \(Y_{n+1}\), update \(D_{n+1}=D_n\cup\{(x_{n+1},Y_{n+1})\}\), and repeat to the budget. For deterministic exact evaluations, recommend a least-valued evaluated configuration; with noise, use the separately declared posterior decision rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The categorical BO loop updates a category-aware posterior, approximately maximizes its acquisition over the finite label domain, records the observation, and returns a recommendation appropriate to the observation model.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate and observation model are specified.
The recommendation rule matches whether evaluations are exact or noisy.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Categorical Bayesian Optimization Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Bayesian optimization on a finite product of unordered label sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\prod_{r=1}^s\mathcal C_r\), where every \(\mathcal C_r\) is finite and nonempty and no ordering of its labels is assumed. Categorical Bayesian optimization maintains a probabilistic surrogate on \(\mathcal X\), constructs an acquisition \(a_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), queries an exact or declared approximate maximizer, and updates the surrogate after observing the response. Category encodings and surrogate predictions must be invariant under consistent relabeling unless domain knowledge explicitly supplies nonexchangeable category structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Categorical Bayesian optimization performs surrogate-based sequential search over finite unordered label combinations without treating arbitrary label numbers as an ordinal scale.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal C_r\) is finite and nonempty.
The response is evaluable on \(\mathcal X\).
Any nonexchangeable similarity between labels is explicitly part of the model rather than induced by arbitrary numbering.

notation.meaning: finite label set for categorical coordinate r

knowledge_statements.title: Categorical Bayesian Optimization Regime
Categorical Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian optimization when every decision coordinate takes finitely many labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\prod_{r=1}^s\mathcal C_r\), where every \(\mathcal C_r\) is a finite nonempty set without an assumed numerical ordering. Categorical Bayesian optimization is sequential optimization of an expensive function \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) in which posterior predictions and an acquisition \(a_n:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) are defined using category-aware representations, kernels, or probabilistic models. A query satisfies
\[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_n(x),\]
and the surrogate is updated after observing \(f(x_{n+1})\). Encoding labels by integers must not impose an unintended ordinal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Categorical Bayesian optimization selects label combinations using a category-aware surrogate and acquisition without assuming that arbitrary numeric label encodings are ordered.
assumptions_latex: Every category set is finite and nonempty.
The objective is evaluable on the categorical product domain.

notation.meaning: finite label set for coordinate r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local scope fit, but the category-aware modeling requirement and warning about ordinal encodings have no cited source.

children.title: Cross-Type Surrogate Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Surrogate representations linking continuous, integer, and categorical inputs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semantic-validity condition for kernels on encoded conditional domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q:\widetilde{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X\) be a surjective map identifying encodings of the same admissible configuration. A symmetric kernel \(\widetilde k\) on \(\widetilde{\mathcal X}\) factors as \(\widetilde k=k\circ(q\times q)\) for a well-defined kernel \(k\) on \(\mathcal X\) exactly when \(\widetilde k\) is constant on every fiber of \(q\) in each argument. If this invariance fails, covariance values and posterior predictions may depend on meaningless inactive-coordinate placeholders.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kernel for conditional variables must be invariant to alternative encodings of the same semantic configuration.
assumptions_latex: Points in the same fiber of \(q\) represent the same configuration.
\(\widetilde k\) is a symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widetilde k=k\circ(q\times q)\iff\widetilde k\text{ is constant on fibers of }q\text{ in both arguments}.\)

notation.meaning: map from encoded points to semantic configurations

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Coordinate Quotient Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite kernel composition on a heterogeneous product domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal X=\prod_{r=1}^R\mathcal X_r and let k_r be positive-semidefinite on \mathcal X_r. Then k_\Pi(x,x')=\prod_{r=1}^Rk_r(x^{(r)},x'^{(r)}) and k_+(x,x')=\sum_{r=1}^Rw_rk_r(x^{(r)},x'^{(r)}) with w_r\geq0 are positive-semidefinite kernels on \mathcal X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Products and nonnegative sums of type-specific kernels give valid covariances on heterogeneous product domains.
assumptions_latex: Each k_r is positive semidefinite on \mathcal X_r.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k_\Pi\text{ and }k_+\text{ are positive semidefinite on }\mathcal X.
knowledge_statements.title: Closure of Type-Specific Kernels
Cross-Type Surrogate Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A type-preserving kernel interface for heterogeneous product domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(R)})\) in a heterogeneous product domain \(\mathcal X=\prod_{r=1}^R\mathcal X_r\), assign each coordinate block a positive-semidefinite kernel \(k_r\) appropriate to its type. A cross-type surrogate interface may use
\[k(x,x')=\prod_{r=1}^R k_r(x^{(r)},x'^{(r)})\quad\text{or}\quad k(x,x')=\sum_{r=1}^R w_rk_r(x^{(r)},x'^{(r)}),\]
with \(w_r\geq0\). Both constructions are positive semidefinite and therefore define a valid Gaussian-process covariance while leaving domain validation and acquisition optimization type-aware.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Type-specific positive-semidefinite kernels can be combined by products or nonnegative sums to form a valid surrogate covariance on a heterogeneous domain.
assumptions_latex: Each \(k_r\) is positive semidefinite on \(\mathcal X_r\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel sum and product claims are mathematically standard and the representation kind fits, but the record supplies no source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Multifidelity Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization using evaluations with differing cost or accuracy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Autoregressive co-kriging representation for ordered correlated fidelities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fidelities \(\ell=1,\ldots,L\), let
\[f_1(x)=\delta_1(x),\qquad f_\ell(x)=\rho_\ell f_{\ell-1}(x)+\delta_\ell(x),\quad \ell\geq2,\]
where \(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_L\) are mutually independent zero-mean Gaussian processes with positive-semidefinite covariance kernels \(k_1,\ldots,k_L\). Then \((f_1,�ldots,f_L)\) is a valid joint Gaussian process, and
\[\operatorname{Cov}(f_\ell(x),f_\ell(x'))=\rho_\ell^2\operatorname{Cov}(f_{\ell-1}(x),f_{\ell-1}(x'))+k_\ell(x,x').\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Autoregressive co-kriging models each fidelity as a scaled lower fidelity plus an independent discrepancy process.
assumptions_latex: The discrepancy processes are mutually independent.

notation.meaning: independent discrepancy process at fidelity level l

knowledge_statements.title: Autoregressive Multifidelity Surrogate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which an auxiliary fidelity cannot update a Gaussian target prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let T be a target-fidelity latent value and L an auxiliary-fidelity observation. If (T,L)\mid D_n is jointly Gaussian, \operatorname{Var}(L\mid D_n)>0, and \operatorname{Cov}(T,L\mid D_n)=0, then \mathcal L(T\mid D_n,L)=\mathcal L(T\mid D_n).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditionally uncorrelated auxiliary fidelity cannot update a Gaussian target prediction.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Correlation Fidelity Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Auxiliary Fidelity Cannot Certify the Target Optimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target-identifiability failure without a valid cross-fidelity relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\) and \(f_L(0)=f_L(1)=0\). The target functions \(f_H^{(a)}(0)=0,f_H^{(a)}(1)=1\) and \(f_H^{(b)}(0)=1,f_H^{(b)}(1)=0\) generate identical auxiliary-fidelity data but have different target minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical low-fidelity data can correspond to opposite high-fidelity optima, so auxiliary data alone cannot identify the target solution.
assumptions_latex: No valid relation between auxiliary and target fidelities is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\min_X f_H^{(a)}\ne\arg\min_X f_H^{(b)}\) despite identical low-fidelity data.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Fidelity Cannot Certify the Target Optimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance of a Cheaper Information-Equivalent Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination of a more expensive fidelity under a nonnegative utility-per-cost acquisition when both fidelities supply the same target-relevant posterior experiment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditionally on \(D_n\), suppose candidate observations \(Y_a\) and \(Y_b\) induce the same joint law with the target latent quantity \(T\): \(\mathcal L(T,Y_a\mid D_n)=\mathcal L(T,Y_b\mid D_n)\). Let \(U\) be a nonnegative target-relevant utility determined only by this conditional joint law, and suppose \(0<c_b<c_a\). Then \[U(Y_a)=U(Y_b),\qquad \frac{U(Y_a)}{c_a}\leq\frac{U(Y_b)}{c_b},\] with strict inequality when the common utility is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative utility-per-cost rule weakly prefers the cheaper of two fidelities that provide identical target-relevant information.
assumptions_latex: The two candidate observations have identical conditional joint laws with the target quantity.
The acquisition utility is a nonnegative functional only of that law.

notation.meaning: evaluation costs of the two fidelities

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance of a Cheaper Information-Equivalent Fidelity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact target uncertainty reduction supplied by one correlated auxiliary-fidelity observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Conditionally on data \(D\), let target-fidelity quantity \(T\) and prospective auxiliary-fidelity observation \(L\) be jointly Gaussian with \(\operatorname{Var}(L\mid D)>0\). Then
\[\operatorname{Var}(T\mid D,L)=\operatorname{Var}(T\mid D)-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(T,L\mid D)^2}{\operatorname{Var}(L\mid D)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian auxiliary-fidelity observation reduces target variance by squared conditional cross-fidelity covariance divided by auxiliary variance.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Fidelity Gaussian Variance Reduction
Multifidelity Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware sequential selection of both design point and information fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x,z)\) denote an evaluation at design \(x\in\mathcal X\) and fidelity \(z\in\mathcal Z\), with target fidelity \(z_\star\) and positive cost \(c(z)\). Initialize with observations at one or more fidelities and fit a joint surrogate over \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z\). At iteration \(n\), choose
\[(x_{n+1},z_{n+1})\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(x,z)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Z}\frac{a_n(x,z;z_\star)}{c(z)},\]
where \(a_n\) measures expected information or utility for optimizing \(f(\cdot,z_\star)\). Evaluate, update the joint posterior and accumulated cost, and stop when the cost budget is exhausted; output the recommended target-fidelity design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multifidelity method jointly chooses a design and fidelity by target-relevant utility per cost, updates a joint surrogate, and respects a cost budget.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate models statistical dependence across fidelities.
A target fidelity \(z_\star\) and total cost budget are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in\mathcal X\) is the final recommendation for minimizing \(f(\cdot,z_\star)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Utility divided by cost describes a particular multifidelity acquisition template rather than every multifidelity Bayesian optimization algorithm. A specific authoritative source is needed to confirm this variant and its recommendation rule.

children.title: Multitask Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization sharing information across related optimization tasks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-task covariance and equivalent shared-latent-process representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(k_x\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel on \(\mathcal X\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be positive semidefinite. Then
\[k((x,t),(x',t'))=k_x(x,x')B_{tt'}\]
is a positive-semidefinite covariance on \(\mathcal X\times\{1,\ldots,m\}\). If \(B=AA^\top\), the same covariance is obtained from
\[f_t(x)=\sum_{q=1}^r A_{tq}u_q(x),\]
where the independent latent processes \(u_q\) share covariance \(k_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intrinsic coregionalization couples tasks through a positive-semidefinite task matrix and is equivalently a linear mixture of shared latent processes.
assumptions_latex: The latent processes are independent and share covariance \(k_x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_x(x,x')B_{tt'}\) is positive semidefinite and admits the displayed latent-factor representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsic Coregionalization Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduction of a Gaussian multitask surrogate to independent task surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let k((x,t),(x',t'))=k_x(x,x')B_{tt'}. If B is diagonal and observation noise is independent across tasks, conditioning on data from t\neq t_\star leaves the posterior of f(\cdot,t_\star) unchanged. Any acquisition depending only on that target posterior therefore equals its single-task counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With diagonal task covariance, auxiliary-task data do not affect the target posterior or a target-posterior acquisition.
assumptions_latex: Observation noise is independent across tasks.
The acquisition is a functional only of the target-task posterior.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Diagonal Task Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact target uncertainty reduction from one correlated auxiliary-task observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditionally on \(D\), let target quantity \(T\) and auxiliary observation \(A\) be jointly Gaussian with \(\operatorname{Var}(A\mid D)>0\). Then \[\operatorname{Var}(T\mid D,A)=\operatorname{Var}(T\mid D)-\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(T,A\mid D)^2}{\operatorname{Var}(A\mid D)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gaussian auxiliary-task observation reduces target variance by squared conditional covariance divided by auxiliary variance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}(T\mid D)-\operatorname{Var}(T\mid D,A)=\operatorname{Cov}(T,A\mid D)^2/\operatorname{Var}(A\mid D)\ge0\), with strict inequality exactly when the covariance is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Task Gaussian Variance Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative Transfer Under False Task Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target-prediction degradation caused solely by misspecified coupling to an independent auxiliary task.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T,A\sim N(0,1)\) be independent. The misspecified coupled predictor \(\widehat T=rA\), with \(r\ne0\), satisfies \(\mathbb E[(T-\widehat T)^2]=1+r^2>1\), whereas the independent-task predictor \(\widehat T=0\) has mean-square error \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imposing false coupling to an independent auxiliary task can strictly worsen target prediction.
review_flags: This is a prediction-risk counterexample, not an optimization-regret theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Negative Transfer Under False Task Coupling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General finite-task covariance obtained by summing latent-process groups with distinct input kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_q\) be positive-semidefinite kernels on \(\mathcal X\), let \(B_q\succeq0\) be task covariance matrices for \(q=1,\ldots,Q\), and define \[k((x,t),(x',t'))=\sum_{q=1}^Q k_q(x,x')(B_q)_{tt'}.\] Then \(k\) is positive semidefinite on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal T\). If \(B_q=A_qA_q^{\mathsf T}\), an equivalent representation is \[f_t(x)=\sum_{q=1}^Q\sum_{r=1}^{R_q}(A_q)_{tr}u_{qr}(x),\] where the \(u_{qr}\) are mutually independent zero-mean Gaussian processes with covariance \(k_q\). Intrinsic coregionalization is the special case \(Q=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear model of coregionalization sums task-covariance factors paired with distinct input kernels and generalizes intrinsic coregionalization.
assumptions_latex: The latent processes in the equivalent representation are mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k=\sum_{q=1}^Q k_q\otimes B_q\text{ is positive semidefinite, and }Q=1\text{ recovers intrinsic coregionalization}.

notation.meaning: task covariance matrix for latent group q
input covariance kernel for latent group q

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Model of Coregionalization
Multitask Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian optimization using correlated observations from multiple indexed tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite task set and let \(f:\mathcal X\times\mathcal T\to\mathbb R\), with target task \(t_\star\in\mathcal T\). Multitask Bayesian optimization fits a joint probabilistic surrogate whose covariance may couple distinct tasks, then sequentially chooses \((x,t)\) using an acquisition measuring the utility of observing \(f(x,t)\) for optimizing \(f(\cdot,t_\star)\). The method reduces to independent single-task optimization when the surrogate covariance between every distinct pair of tasks is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multitask Bayesian optimization exploits modeled correlations among task-indexed objectives to choose observations that help optimize a designated target task.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is finite and contains the target task \(t_\star\).
Observations are indexed by both design and task.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_{n+1},t_{n+1})\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal T\) is selected for target-task utility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the leaf, but neither the target-task acquisition formulation nor the asserted reduction under zero intertask covariance is cited.

children.title: Cross-Fidelity Task Transfer
children.top_down_role: Joint transfer structures spanning multiple fidelities plus multiple tasks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative transfer caused by imposing dependence between truly independent target and auxiliary outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\sim N(0,1)\) and \(L\sim N(0,1)\) be independent under the data-generating law. If a misspecified surrogate predicts \(T\) from a noiseless observation of \(L\) by \(\widehat T=rL\), where \(r\neq0\), then
\[\mathbb E[(T-\widehat T)^2]=1+r^2>1=\mathbb E[(T-0)^2].\]
Thus incorrect cross-fidelity or cross-task coupling can strictly worsen target prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Imposing nonzero transfer on independent target and auxiliary outputs strictly increases mean-square target prediction error.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(L\) are independent standard normal variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Misspecified-Transfer Risk

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Fidelity-Task Covariance and Transfer Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable covariance and Gaussian posterior transfer across both fidelity and task indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For u=(x,z,t) and v=(x',z',t'), let k(u,v)=k_x(x,x')k_z(z,z')k_t(t,t'), where all three factors are positive-semidefinite. Then k is positive semidefinite. After conditioning on D_n, a Gaussian observation y at u with noise variance \sigma^2 changes the posterior mean at v by \frac{k_n(v,u)}{k_n(u,u)+\sigma^2}(y-\mu_n(u)); hence k_n(v,u)=0 blocks the direct update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product covariance jointly couples designs, fidelities, and tasks; conditional posterior covariance controls transfer from a new observation.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Fidelity-Task Covariance and Transfer Update
Cross-Fidelity Task Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable covariance representation for transferring information across fidelities and tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Index observations by design \(x\in\mathcal X\), fidelity \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and task \(t\in\mathcal T\). A separable cross-fidelity task surrogate may use the prior covariance
\[k((x,z,t),(x',z',t'))=k_x(x,x')k_z(z,z')k_t(t,t').\]
If \(k_x\), \(k_z\), and \(k_t\) are positive semidefinite, then \(k\) is a valid covariance. Given current data \(D_n\), an observation at \(u=(x,z,t)\) can transfer information to \(v=(x',z',t')\) through the conditional posterior covariance \(k_n(v,u)\). For a Gaussian observation with noise variance \(\sigma^2\), the posterior-mean update at \(v\) is proportional to
\[\frac{k_n(v,u)}{k_n(u,u)+\sigma^2}\bigl(y-\mu_n(u)\bigr).\]
Thus nonzero conditional covariance permits transfer, while zero conditional covariance blocks the direct update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product kernel is a valid joint covariance across designs, fidelities, and tasks; after conditioning on existing data, transfer from a new observation is controlled by its conditional posterior covariance with the prediction target.
assumptions_latex: The joint surrogate uses the displayed separable prior covariance.
The Gaussian observation variance satisfies \(\sigma^2\geq0\) and \(k_n(u,u)+\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is positive semidefinite, and a direct posterior-mean update from \(u\) to \(v\) is blocked when \(k_n(v,u)=0\).

notation.meaning: conditional posterior covariance given current data

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Bayesian trust-region policy confined to a fixed proper subset need not discover a global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=[0,2]\), \(f(x)=(x-2)^2\), and suppose every query \(x_k\) lies in a region \(R_k\subseteq[0,\tfrac12]\). Then
\[\inf_k f(x_k)\geq\frac94>0=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x).\]
Thus local acquisition optimization and radius adaptation alone do not imply global discovery; such a conclusion requires an exploration or restart condition providing adequate domain coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region BO policy permanently confined to one neighborhood can miss the global optimum, so global-discovery guarantees need an explicit coverage or restart assumption.

notation.meaning: Bayesian trust region at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Locality and Restart Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit, well-defined Bayesian trust-region acceptance statistic; it is not universal to all trust-region BO methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, define p_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(y_k) and r_k=f(x_k)-f(y_k), where m_k is fixed before evaluating y_k. Use \rho_k=r_k/p_k only when p_k>0. If p_k\leq0, apply a separately declared rule such as rejection and contraction or restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posterior-mean decrease can define predicted reduction, but a nonpositive prediction cannot serve as an acceptance-ratio denominator.
assumptions_latex: m_k is fixed before f(y_k) is observed.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Mean Reduction Ratio

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive global-discovery boundary for a trust-region Bayesian policy with bounded exhaustive coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal X be finite and f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R deterministic. If the policy retains the best evaluated point and its restart safeguard evaluates every x\in\mathcal X within B evaluations, then x_B^{\rm inc}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite domain, a bounded exhaustive-restart safeguard guarantees global discovery within its coverage bound.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent is the best evaluated point.
Every point is evaluated by evaluation B.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Restart Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit hybrid interface combining local posterior acquisition with posterior-mean reduction ratios, radius safeguards, posterior updates, and restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(R_k=\mathcal X\cap B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), fix the posterior mean \(m_k\), and choose an exact or declared approximate maximizer \(y_k\) of acquisition \(a_k\) over \(R_k\). After evaluating \(f(y_k)\), set \(p_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(y_k)\). If \(p_k>0\), form \(\rho_k=[f(x_k)-f(y_k)]/p_k\), accept \(y_k\) when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_1\), enlarge the radius when \(\rho_k\ge\eta_2\), and otherwise retain or contract it according to declared thresholds. If \(p_k\le0\), do not form the ratio and apply a declared contraction or restart rule. Update the posterior with every completed evaluation. Invoke the declared restart or coverage safeguard when its trigger holds, and retain the best evaluated point as incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface optimizes an acquisition locally, uses a pre-evaluation posterior-mean reduction only when positive, updates acceptance and radius by declared thresholds, updates the posterior after every evaluation, and invokes an explicit restart safeguard.
assumptions_latex: The acquisition approximation, radius-update, null-prediction, and restart rules are specified before observing \(f(y_k)\).
The posterior mean \(m_k\) is fixed before evaluating \(y_k\).

notation.meaning: actual-to-predicted reduction ratio when p_k is positive

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization Interface
Trust-Region Bayesian Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Bayesian acquisition coupled to standard trust-region acceptance and radius updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given incumbent \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and posterior acquisition \(a_k\), define \(R_k=\mathcal X\cap\{x:\lVert x-x_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\}\) and choose \(y_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in R_k}a_k(x)\). After evaluating \(f(y_k)\), compute the ratio \(\rho_k\) of actual reduction to the surrogate-predicted reduction when the denominator is positive. Accept \(y_k\) as the next incumbent when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); enlarge \(\Delta_k\) when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\), shrink it when \(\rho_k<\eta_1\), and otherwise retain it. Update the posterior and stop at the evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the Bayesian acquisition locally, accept candidates by actual-versus-predicted improvement, and adapt the trust-region radius before updating the posterior.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate supplies a positive predicted reduction for ratio-based updates.
Minimum and maximum radius safeguards are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\in\{x_k,y_k\}\) and the next query region has an updated radius \(\Delta_{k+1}>0\).

notation.meaning: current trust region intersected with the domain

source_refs.locator: 10.1 The trust-region framework basics p. 173

source_witnesses.locator: 10.1 The trust-region framework basics p. 173

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited trust-region chapter supports the classical acceptance and radius framework but not this Bayesian acquisition interface. The record also does not identify which surrogate quantity supplies predicted reduction. A specific hybrid or Bayesian trust-region source is required.

children.title: Additive-Structure Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: High-dimensional Bayesian optimization exploiting additive objective structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable acquisition optimization on disjoint product groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathcal X=\prod_m\mathcal X_{G_m}\), the groups are disjoint, and \(a(x)=\sum_ma_m(x_{G_m})\), then component maximizers combine into a global maximizer and \(\max_xa(x)=\sum_m\max_ua_m(u)\). Overlapping groups or coupled constraints generally invalidate independent optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable acquisition on disjoint product groups can be optimized componentwise.
assumptions_latex: The domain is the Cartesian product of group domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent component maximizers form a global acquisition maximizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Componentwise Acquisition Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summed kernels from independent component priors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(F_m\) are independent Gaussian processes with means \(\mu_m\) and kernels \(k_m\), then \(F(x)=\sum_mF_m(x_{G_m})\) is Gaussian with mean \(\sum_m\mu_m(x_{G_m})\) and covariance \(\sum_mk_m(x_{G_m},x'_{G_m})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent component Gaussian processes sum to a Gaussian process with summed mean and kernel.
assumptions_latex: The component processes are mutually independent.
The finite sums are well defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Gaussian-Process Closure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Component Functions Are Not Individually Identifiable
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-shift freedom in additive decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f=\sum_mf_m\) and constants \(b_m\) satisfy \(\sum_mb_m=0\), then \(\widetilde f_m=f_m+b_m\) gives the same full objective. Component levels therefore require centering or another normalization for individual identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive component offsets can shift while preserving their sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition has constant-shift gauge freedom without normalization.
knowledge_statements.title: Component Functions Are Not Individually Identifiable

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential Bayesian optimization under specified additive coordinate groups and an additive Gaussian-process prior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_M\), component kernels \(k_m\), data \(D_n\), and \(k(x,x')=\sum_{m=1}^M k_m(x_{G_m},x'_{G_m})\), compute the posterior induced by \(k\), construct a declared acquisition \(a_n\), select an exact or \(\varepsilon_n\)-approximate maximizer \(x_{n+1}\in\mathcal X\), observe the response, set \(D_{n+1}=D_n\cup\{(x_{n+1},Y_{n+1})\}\), and repeat to the declared budget. Componentwise acquisition optimization is valid only when the acquisition and feasible domain satisfy the separability conditions stated in Exact Componentwise Acquisition Optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive Bayesian optimization updates a summed-kernel posterior, optimizes a declared acquisition, observes the chosen design, and repeats; independent component optimization requires actual acquisition and domain separability.
assumptions_latex: Each \(k_m\) is positive semidefinite on its group domain.
The observation model and posterior update are specified.
The acquisition maximization rule and numerical tolerance are specified.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Gaussian-Process Bayesian Optimization Loop

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-gain decomposition for a summed additive Gaussian-process kernel, including overlapping coordinate groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k=\sum_{m=1}^M k_m\), let \(K_A=\sum_m K_{m,A}\) be the Gram matrix on an \(n\)-point design \(A\), and let \(\tau^2>0\). Then \[\frac12\log\det(I+\tau^{-2}K_A)\leq\sum_{m=1}^M\frac12\log\det(I+\tau^{-2}K_{m,A}).\] Consequently, for \(\gamma_n(k)=\max_{|A|=n}\frac12\log\det(I+\tau^{-2}K_A)\), \[\gamma_n(k)\leq\sum_{m=1}^M\gamma_n(k_m).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum information gain of a summed additive kernel is at most the sum of the component information gains.
assumptions_latex: Observations have independent Gaussian noise with common variance \(\tau^2>0\).
Information gain is evaluated on finite designs of common cardinality.

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of component kernel m on design A
maximum n-point Gaussian information gain for kernel k

review_flags: This kernel-complexity bound is not by itself a Bayesian-optimization regret theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive-Kernel Information-Gain Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior dependence induced among independently modeled additive components by observations of their sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent component priors satisfy \(F_m\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k_m)\), and observe \(y_i=\sum_{j=1}^M F_j((x_i)_{G_j})+\varepsilon_i\), where \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\tau^2I)\). Write \(K=\sum_jK_j\), and let \(k_{m,u}\) contain the covariances between \(F_m(u)\) and the observations. Then \[\operatorname{Cov}(F_m(u),F_\ell(v)\mid y)=\mathbf1_{m=\ell}k_m(u,v)-k_{m,u}^{\mathsf T}(K+\tau^2I)^{-1}k_{\ell,v}.\] Hence independently modeled components are generally posterior-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observations of the component sum generally make independently modeled additive Gaussian-process components dependent in the posterior.
assumptions_latex: The component Gaussian processes are mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m\ne\ell\Longrightarrow\operatorname{Cov}(F_m(u),F_\ell(v)\mid y)=-k_{m,u}^{\mathsf T}(K+\tau^2I)^{-1}k_{\ell,v},\text{ which need not vanish}.

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of component kernel m on the observations

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Coupling of Additive Components

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Decomposition of the Posterior Mean
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise representation of the summed-kernel Gaussian-process posterior mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let independent zero-mean component priors have kernels \(k_m\), let \(K=\sum_m K_m\), and observe \(y_i=\sum_m F_m((x_i)_{G_m})+\varepsilon_i\) with \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\tau^2I)\). Then
\[\mathbb E[F(x)\mid y]=\sum_{m=1}^M k_m(x_{G_m},X_{G_m})^{\mathsf T}(K+\tau^2I)^{-1}y=\sum_{m=1}^M\mathbb E[F_m(x_{G_m})\mid y].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The posterior mean under a summed additive kernel is the sum of component posterior means, although the components are generally posterior-dependent.
assumptions_latex: The component Gaussian-process priors are mutually independent and have zero mean.
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\tau^2>0\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of component kernel m
posterior mean of additive component m

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Decomposition of the Posterior Mean

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled Constraints Defeat Componentwise Acquisition Maximization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of independent additive-acquisition optimization when the feasible domain is not a product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{(x_1,x_2)\in[0,1]^2:x_1+x_2\leq1\}\) and \(a(x)=a_1(x_1)+a_2(x_2)=x_1+x_2\). The independent component maximizers are \(x_1=x_2=1\), but \((1,1)\notin\mathcal X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a separable acquisition cannot be optimized by independently combining component maximizers when constraints couple the groups.
assumptions_latex: The feasible domain contains the coupling constraint \(x_1+x_2\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Constraints Defeat Componentwise Acquisition Maximization
Additive-Structure Bayesian Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-dimensional objective represented by low-dimensional additive components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_1,\ldots,G_M\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be coordinate groups and write \(x_{G_m}\) for the corresponding subvector. An additive surrogate assumes
\[f(x)=\sum_{m=1}^M f_m(x_{G_m}),\qquad k(x,x')=\sum_{m=1}^M k_m(x_{G_m},x'_{G_m}),\]
where each \(k_m\) is positive semidefinite. The resulting \(k\) is positive semidefinite, and posterior inference represents only functions compatible with the selected additive groups, up to the support of the component priors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive Bayesian optimizer models a high-dimensional objective as a sum of functions over selected coordinate groups and uses the corresponding summed kernel.
assumptions_latex: Each component kernel \(k_m\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is a positive-semidefinite additive covariance on the full domain.

notation.meaning: coordinate group of additive component m

children.title: Active-Subspace Bayesian Optimization
children.top_down_role: Bayesian optimization conducted through a learned low-dimensional subspace.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness boundary for an active subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}\), the leading rank-\(r\) invariant subspace of \(C\) is unique, although its orthonormal basis is not. If \(\lambda_r=\lambda_{r+1}\), \(C\) does not identify a unique rank-\(r\) truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eigengap identifies the active subspace; a tie at the truncation index makes it nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_r>\lambda_{r+1}\) yields a unique leading invariant subspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Subspace Identifiability Requires an Eigengap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical gradient-informed active-subspace construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For reference distribution \(ho\), define \[C=\mathbb E_ho[
abla f(X)
abla f(X)^	op]=W\Lambda W^	op.\] The rank-\(r\) active subspace is the leading invariant subspace \(\operatorname{span}(W_r)\), and \(\mathbb E_ho\|W_\perp^	op
abla f(X)\|^2=\sum_{i=r+1}^d\lambda_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical active subspace is the leading eigenspace of a gradient second-moment matrix under a declared input measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Covariance Active Subspace

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Ridge Functions Have Inactive Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implication of exact low-dimensional ridge dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f(x)=g(W_r^	op x)\), then \(
abla f(x)=W_r
abla g(W_r^	op x)\) and \(W_\perp^	op
abla f(x)=0\). Hence \(\operatorname{range}(C)\subseteq\operatorname{span}(W_r)\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(C)\le r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every gradient of an exact ridge function lies in its active subspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Ridge Functions Have Inactive Gradients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-only Bayesian optimization with an active subspace estimated from differentiable surrogate posterior derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At update time \(n\), fit a differentiable probabilistic surrogate to value observations and form \(\widehat C_n=\int \mathbb E_n[\nabla F(x)\nabla F(x)^{\mathsf T}]\,\rho(dx)\), or a declared quadrature or Monte Carlo approximation. Let \(\widehat W_{r,n}\) contain orthonormal leading eigenvectors. Optimize a reduced acquisition over \(\widehat W_{r,n}^{\mathsf T}\mathcal X\), choose an attainable reduced point \(y_{n+1}\), lift it to a specified \(x_{n+1}\in\mathcal X\) satisfying \(\widehat W_{r,n}^{\mathsf T}x_{n+1}=y_{n+1}\), evaluate it, update the posterior, and periodically recompute the subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value-only active-subspace Bayesian optimization loop estimates gradient covariance from a differentiable surrogate, optimizes in learned coordinates, and explicitly lifts candidates to the original domain.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate admits square-integrable spatial derivatives under \rho.
The reduced acquisition, attainable-domain, and feasible lifting rules are specified.
The leading rank-r eigenspace is selected by a measurable rule.

notation.meaning: posterior estimate of the gradient second-moment matrix
reference measure used to average surrogate gradients

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Gradient Active-Subspace Bayesian Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenspace accuracy resulting from spectral error in an estimated gradient second-moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) and \(\widehat C\) be symmetric, let \(W_r\) span the leading rank-\(r\) invariant subspace of \(C\), and suppose \(\gamma=\lambda_r(C)-\lambda_{r+1}(C)>0\). If \(\|\widehat C-C\|_2<\gamma/2\), then the leading rank-\(r\) subspace \(\widehat W_r\) of \(\widehat C\) is separated and satisfies \[\|\sin\Theta(\widehat W_r,W_r)\|_2\le\frac{2\|\widehat C-C\|_2}{\gamma}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eigengap converts spectral error in estimated gradient covariance into a quantitative active-subspace error bound.

notation.meaning: sines of the principal angles between estimated and true subspaces
eigenvalue gap at the truncation index

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Subspace Perturbation Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square approximation guarantee connecting inactive active-subspace eigenvalues to a reduced ridge response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=W_r^{\mathsf T}X\) and \(g(Y)=\mathbb E[f(X)\mid Y]\). Suppose that, for almost every \(y\), the conditional law of \(X\) given \(Y=y\) satisfies a Poincaré inequality with a common constant \(C_P\) along inactive directions.
