knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp identifiability failure for smoothing confined to an incorrect proper subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose any nonzero \(a\in\operatorname{range}(U)^\perp\) and let \(f_a(x)=a^\top x\). For every \(z\in\mathbb{R}^r\) and \(\mu>0\),
\[
f_a(x+\mu Uz)=f_a(x),
\]
so every function difference generated by subspace perturbations is zero. Nevertheless,
\[
\nabla f_a(x)=a\ne0.
\]
Hence observations restricted to \(\operatorname{range}(U)\) cannot distinguish \(f_a\) from a constant function, and estimators whose outputs lie in that subspace cannot recover the full gradient. Full-gradient identifiability therefore requires the perturbation covariance to have full rank or an assumption excluding orthogonal variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If smoothing misses a direction where the objective varies, all permitted differences can vanish despite a nonzero gradient, making full-gradient recovery impossible.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Mismatch Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identifiability counterexample precisely matches the geometry-mismatch boundary leaf, and failure_boundary is the correct content kind. Nevertheless, the record has no source reference or inspectable locator supporting the stated impossibility boundary.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of correlation between paired oracle errors in a Gaussian difference estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((\xi_+,\xi_0)\) is independent of \(u\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)\), centered, has \(\operatorname{Var}(\xi_+)=\operatorname{Var}(\xi_0)=\sigma^2\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\xi_+,\xi_0)=\rho\sigma^2\). For \(N_\mu=(\xi_+-\xi_0)u/\mu\), \[\mathbb E\|N_\mu\|^2=\frac{2(1-\rho)\sigma^2d}{\mu^2}.\] Independent noise gives \(\rho=0\), perfectly shared additive noise cancels, and negative correlation increases amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small-radius variance depends on the coupling of paired oracle errors; common noise can cancel while adverse coupling worsens amplification.
assumptions_latex: The paired errors are centered, have common variance \(\sigma^2\), correlation \(\rho\), and are independent of the Gaussian direction.

notation.meaning: correlation coefficient between paired oracle errors

knowledge_statements.title: Noise Coupling Controls Differenced-Estimator Variance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Smoothing Bias and Independent-Noise Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Competing smoothing-gradient bias and oracle-noise terms for a two-evaluation Gaussian estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and let \(G_\mu=[F(x+\mu u)-F(x)]u/\mu\), where \(u\sim\mathcal N(0,I_d)\), \(F(y)=f(y)+\xi_y\), and the two centered oracle errors are independent of each other and of \(u\), with variances at most \(\sigma^2\). Then \[\|\nabla f_\mu(x)-\nabla f(x)\|\leq L\mu\sqrt d,\qquad \mathbb E\|N_\mu\|^2\leq\frac{2\sigma^2d}{\mu^2},\] where \(N_\mu=(\xi_+-\xi_0)u/\mu\). Thus decreasing \(\mu\) reduces smoothing bias but amplifies differenced oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Gaussian smoothing radius creates opposing linear bias and inverse-square noise-variance effects.
assumptions_latex: The two centered oracle errors are mutually independent, independent of \(u\), and have variances at most \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\mu(x)-\nabla f(x)\|\leq L\mu\sqrt d\) and \(\mathbb E\|N_\mu\|^2\leq2\sigma^2d/\mu^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Smoothing Bias and Independent-Noise Amplification

assumptions_latex: Oracle observations are \(F(x)=f(x)+\xi\), where independent noises have mean zero and variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The smoothing bias is at most \(L\mu\sqrt d\), while the differenced-noise contribution to the estimator's second moment is at most \(2\sigma^2d/\mu^2\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports these Gaussian smoothing bias and noisy-estimator variance bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian two-point estimation under smooth objectives and independent additive oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
G_\mu=\frac{F(x+\mu u)-F(x)}{\mu}u.
\]
For Gaussian smoothing, Lipschitz continuity of \(\nabla f\) implies
\[
\|\nabla f_\mu(x)-\nabla f(x)\|\le L\mu\mathbb{E}\|u\|\le L\mu\sqrt d.
\]
If the two oracle noises are independent, their contribution \(N_\mu\) to \(G_\mu\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb{E}\|N_\mu\|^2
=\frac{\mathbb{E}[(\xi_+-\xi_0)^2]\mathbb{E}\|u\|^2}{\mu^2}
\le\frac{2\sigma^2d}{\mu^2}.
\]
Thus decreasing \(\mu\) reduces smoothing bias but amplifies differenced oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smaller Gaussian smoothing radius reduces gradient bias linearly but amplifies additive-noise variance quadratically, creating a fundamental tuning boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing Bias–Variance Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bias-versus-noise tradeoff fits the boundary leaf and failure_boundary content kind. The second-moment factorization additionally requires the oracle noises to be independent of the sampled Gaussian direction, which is not explicit, and no source locator supports either quantitative bound.

children.title: Pure Random Search
children.top_down_role: Random-search regimes without learned proposal adaptation.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure Random Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent global sampling with incumbent retention and no adaptation of the sampling law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible set \(X\), an objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), a probability measure \(\mu\) on \(X\), and a budget \(N\), draw \(Y_0\sim\mu\) and set \(x_0=Y_0\). For \(k=1,\ldots,N\), independently draw \(Y_k\sim\mu\) and update \[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\{x_{k-1},Y_k\}} f(z).\] Return \(x_N\). The distribution \(\mu\) is fixed throughout; thus only the incumbent changes. If ties occur, any fixed measurable tie-breaking rule may be used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently sample feasible points from one fixed distribution, retain the best point observed, and return it when the evaluation budget is exhausted.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(f\) is evaluable at every sampled point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact iid evaluation budget for hitting a target sublevel with prescribed confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_\varepsilon=\mu(\{x:f(x)\le f_*+\varepsilon\})>0\). After \(M\) iid evaluations, the failure probability is \((1-p_\varepsilon)^M\). It is at most \(\delta\in(0,1)\) whenever \(M\ge\lceil\log(\delta)/\log(1-p_\varepsilon)\rceil\); the simpler sufficient bound is \(M\ge p_\varepsilon^{-1}\log(1/\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sample complexity is determined exactly by the sampling mass of the target sublevel set.
assumptions_latex: The evaluations are iid with law \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: sampling probability of the epsilon-optimal sublevel set

knowledge_statements.title: Sublevel Hitting Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitation imposed by the fixed sampling law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_\varepsilon=\mu(\{x:f(x)\le f_*+\varepsilon\})=0\) for some \(\varepsilon>0\), then no countable sequence of iid samples from \(\mu\) reaches that sublevel set with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed sampler cannot find an accuracy region to which it assigns zero probability.
assumptions_latex: Every proposal has the fixed law \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Limited Global Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-budget law for the immutable iid algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iid samples \(Y_0,\ldots,Y_N\sim\mu\), let \(Z_N=\min_{0\le i\le N}f(Y_i)\) and \(F(t)=\mu(\{x:f(x)\le t\})\). Then \(\mathbb P(Z_N>t)=(1-F(t))^{N+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best-value tail probability is the one-sample failure probability raised to the number of samples.
assumptions_latex: The \(N+1\) samples are independent with common law \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: best objective value among N+1 samples

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Value Distribution

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Convergence to the Essential Infimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact asymptotic guarantee for fixed-law iid pure random search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_\mu=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\sim\mu}f(x)\). If \(f(Y_0)\) is bounded below almost surely, then iid sampling with best-so-far retention satisfies \(f(x_N)\downarrow m_\mu\) almost surely. It converges to \(\inf_X f\) exactly when \(m_\mu=\inf_X f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure random search converges to the best objective level visible to its fixed sampling law, which may exceed the global infimum.
assumptions_latex: The samples are iid with law \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: essential infimum under the sampling law

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Sure Convergence to the Essential Infimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Random search for validation-based hyperparameter selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A hyperparameter-tuning specialization of pure random search; independence among hyperparameter coordinates is common but not required by the extracted description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a probability distribution $P$ over joint hyperparameter configurations. Typical coordinate choices include Bernoulli or categorical distributions for discrete parameters and log-uniform distributions for positive real parameters. For each trial $t=1,\ldots,T$, sample a configuration $\theta^{(t)}\sim P$, train and evaluate the corresponding model, and return a sampled configuration having minimum observed validation error. Continuous hyperparameters need not be discretized. When several coordinates have little effect on validation performance, random search can explore distinct values of influential coordinates more efficiently than a Cartesian grid and may be exponentially more efficient in the stated regime. Subsequent searches may refine $P$ using earlier results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Specify a distribution over hyperparameter configurations, sample and evaluate T configurations, and return one with the lowest observed validation error. Continuous parameters need not be binned. When many hyperparameters have little influence, random search may explore influential values substantially—and in the stated regime exponentially—more efficiently than grid search. Later runs may refine the sampling distribution.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is a probability distribution over the joint hyperparameter space}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized neighborhood search that accepts only strict objective improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(k=0\) and choose \(x^{(0)}\in\Omega\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(z^{(k)}\) from the prescribed distribution on \(N(x^{(k)})\), and set
\[
x^{(k+1)}=\begin{cases}
z^{(k)},& f(z^{(k)})<f(x^{(k)}),\\
x^{(k)},&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Stop if the stopping criterion is satisfied; otherwise increment \(k\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin at a feasible point. Repeatedly sample a candidate from the current point's prescribed neighborhood distribution, accept it only if it strictly reduces the objective, and otherwise retain the current point.
assumptions_latex: \forall x\in\Omega,\quad N(x)\subseteq\Omega\text{ has a prescribed sampling distribution}

children.title: Adaptive Random Search
children.top_down_role: Random-search regimes that modify proposal behavior from observed performance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-level definition independent of a particular parameter-update convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incumbent random search is history-adaptive when its proposal at iteration \(k\) has a probability kernel \(Q_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)\) whose choice may depend on previously observed proposals, objective values, or acceptance outcomes. A fixed-law iid sampler is obtained when \(Q_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)=\mu(\cdot)\) for every \(k\) and history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive random search changes its proposal law using observed search history; fixed-law iid sampling is its nonadaptive special case.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Q_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)\) is a probability kernel on the feasible search space.
knowledge_statements.title: History-Adaptive Random Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise property of adaptive searches retaining only improving trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_{k+1}=Y_k\) only when \(f(Y_k)<f(x_k)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise, then proposal adaptation does not affect \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-so-far acceptance makes incumbent values nonincreasing regardless of proposal adaptation.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent is replaced only by a strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Monotonicity Under Elitist Acceptance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Convergence from Persistent Conditional Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value convergence for elitist adaptive search on a compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and retain the best sampled value. If every nonempty relatively open set \(O\subseteq X\) has a constant \(p_O>0\) satisfying \(\mathbb P(Y_k\in O\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_O\) almost surely for all \(k\), then \(f(x_k)\to\min_X f\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly persistent conditional access to every open region yields almost-sure convergence of the best objective value.
assumptions_latex: The incumbent retains the best sampled value.
Every nonempty relatively open set has a positive history-uniform conditional sampling probability.

notation.meaning: uniform conditional coverage probability for O

knowledge_statements.title: Global Convergence from Persistent Conditional Coverage
Adaptive Random Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-based random search whose proposal distribution adapts to accepted and rejected trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in X\), an initial scale \(\sigma_0>0\), multipliers \(\gamma_+>1\) and \(0<\gamma_-<1\), and budget \(N\), draw independent directions \(U_k\) from a fixed base law. Form a feasible trial \(Y_k=\Pi_X(x_k+\sigma_kU_k)\). If \(f(Y_k)<f(x_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=Y_k\) and \(\sigma_{k+1}=\gamma_+\sigma_k\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(\sigma_{k+1}=\gamma_-\sigma_k\). Stop after \(N\) trials or when a prescribed scale or objective test holds, and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate random trials around the incumbent, enlarge the search scale after improvement, shrink it after failure, and return the final incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and admits a specified feasible projection \(\Pi_X\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is evaluable at all trial points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates satisfy \(x_k\in X\) and \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)\) for every completed iteration.

notation.meaning: specified mapping to a feasible trial

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated expand-on-success and contract-on-failure scheme is one plausible adaptive random-search variant, but the title does not uniquely determine this update, projection convention, or stopping rule. An authoritative algorithm locator is required.

children.title: Adaptation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search degradation caused by unstable or misleading proposal adaptation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive proposal support collapses before reaching an improving region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb R\), \(x_0=0\), \(Y_k\in[x_k-\sigma_k,x_k+\sigma_k]\) almost surely, and \(\sum_{k\ge0}\sigma_k<1\). Suppose rejected trials leave the incumbent unchanged and only strict improvements are accepted. For \(f(x)=0\) on \(( -\infty,1]\) and \(f(x)=-1\) on \([2,\infty)\), every incumbent remains \(x_k=0\), every proposal satisfies \(Y_k<1\), and the improving region \([2,\infty)\) is never sampled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Premature scale collapse can make a globally improving region unreachable despite infinitely many evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Only strict improvements replace the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Scale-Collapse Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-probability boundary for repeated access to an improving region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k=\{Y_k\in B\}\in\mathcal F_{k+1}\). If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)<\infty\) almost surely, then the conditional Borel--Cantelli lemma gives \(\mathbb P(A_k\ \mathrm{i.o.})=0\). Infinitely many iterations therefore do not ensure recurrent exploration of \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A region whose conditional access probabilities are summable is visited only finitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Persistent Exploration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-refinement failure when adaptive random search never tests smaller displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=(x-1)^2\), \(x_0=0\), and \(Y_k=x_k+2U_k\), where \(U_k\in\{-1,1\}\). If only strict improvements are accepted, then \(f(2)=f(0)=1\) and \(f(-2)=9\), so every proposal is rejected, \(x_k=0\) for all \(k\), and \(f'(0)=-2\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random search that never refines its proposal scale can remain forever at a smooth nonstationary point.
assumptions_latex: The proposal scale remains fixed at \(2\).
The direction law is supported on \(\{-1,1\}\).
Only strict objective improvements replace the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Scale Nonstationary Stagnation
Adaptation Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete mechanisms by which scale adaptation destroys global exploration or local refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider adaptive proposals \(Y_k=x_k+\sigma_kU_k\). Adaptation fails to ensure exploration if there exists a measurable region \(B\subset X\) containing better points such that \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}(Y_k\in B\mid\mathcal{F}_k)<\infty\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Conditional Borel--Cantelli then permits \(B\) to be visited only finitely often. A distinct local failure occurs when unsuccessful steps do not force \(\sigma_k\to0\): the method may never test arbitrarily small neighborhoods of a nonstationary incumbent. Thus convergence claims require both persistent access to improving regions and an appropriate scale-refinement mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptation can fail by making promising regions summably unlikely or by preventing the sampling scale from shrinking enough for local refinement.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{F}_k\) contains the search history before proposal \(Y_k\).
\(B\) is measurable under every conditional proposal law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Summable access probabilities or absent scale refinement invalidate the corresponding exploration or local-convergence guarantee.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind fits, but the record combines a conditional Borel–Cantelli exploration condition with a separate scale-refinement condition. Their exact implications and required hypotheses need an authoritative convergence source.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Direct Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Opportunistic direct search using randomly generated polling directions and sufficient decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(\alpha_0>0\), a forcing function \(\rho:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\), and random finite nonempty direction sets \(D_k\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), evaluate trial points \(x_k+\alpha_kd\) for \(d\in D_k\). If some direction satisfies \(f(x_k+\alpha_kd)\leq f(x_k)-\rho(\alpha_k)\), accept one such point and choose \(\alpha_{k+1}\geq\alpha_k\) according to the declared expansion rule. Otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and choose \(0<\alpha_{k+1}<\alpha_k\) according to the declared contraction rule. Stop under a prescribed budget or step-size test and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Poll randomly generated directions at the current step size, accept a point satisfying sufficient decrease, expand after success, and contract after an unsuccessful poll.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is evaluable at every trial point.
Each \(D_k\) is generated according to a declared probability law and is finite and nonempty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that randomization alone does not ensure recurrent descent coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) be the event that poll \(k\) contains a descent-generating direction and let \(p_k=\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\). If \(\sum_kp_k<\infty\) almost surely, then \(A_k\) occurs only finitely often almost surely. Persistent randomized directional coverage therefore cannot be inferred from infinitely many polls.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Waiting Time for a Descent-Generating Poll
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-time consequence of uniform conditional useful-direction coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k\) be the event that poll \(k\) contains a \(\kappa\)-descent direction, and suppose \(\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p>0\) almost surely until the first such event. For \(T=\inf\{k\ge0:A_k\}\), \[\mathbb P(T\ge m)\le(1-p)^m,\qquad \mathbb E[T+1]\le p^{-1}.\] Successive polls need not be independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform conditional directional coverage gives a geometric tail and reciprocal-probability expected waiting time for a useful poll.
assumptions_latex: Before the first success, \(\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p>0\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summably Rare Descent Directions Can Cause Nonstationary Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete smooth realization of the vanishing-coverage boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x\), \(x_0=0\), and suppose every failed poll sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and \(\alpha_{k+1}\le\gamma\alpha_k\) for a fixed \(0<\gamma<1\). Independently set \(D_k=\{-1\}\) with probability \(p_k=2^{-k-2}\) and \(D_k=\{1\}\) otherwise. With probability \(\prod_{k\ge0}(1-p_k)>0\), no descent direction is ever sampled; on that event every poll fails, \(x_k=0\), and \(\alpha_k\to0\), although \(f'(0)=1\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If useful directions are summably rare, randomized direct search can contract forever at a smooth nonstationary point with positive probability.
assumptions_latex: Failed polls retain the incumbent and contract the step by a uniform factor \(\gamma<1\).
The sufficient-decrease rule rejects the direction \(1\) for \(f(x)=x\).

At test \(k\), hold \((x_k,\alpha_k)\) fixed and perform \(r_k\) successive random polls. Assume each poll, conditional on the preceding history and outcomes, contains a unit direction \(d\) satisfying \(
abla f(x_k)^Td\le-\kappa\|

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional model-accuracy notion for randomized derivative-free trust regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_k\), \(\Delta_k\), and \(\mathcal F_k\), a random model \(m_k\) is probabilistically fully linear with probability \(p\) if, conditional on \(\mathcal F_k\), with probability at least \(p\), every \(s\) with \(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\) satisfies \[|f(x_k+s)-m_k(s)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k+s)-\nabla m_k(s)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random model is probabilistically fully linear when standard value and gradient error bounds hold throughout the current trust region with uniform conditional probability.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m_k\) are differentiable on the trust region.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)\) be revealed by the first model and let every model be accurate exactly on \(\{Z=1\}\). Then \(\mathbb P(E_k)=p\) for every \(k\), but on \(\{Z=0\}\), \(\mathbb P(E_k\mid\mathcal F_k)=0\) after revelation. For \(f(x)=x^2\), an inaccurate model at \(x_0=1\) may repeatedly predict decrease for \(s_k=\Delta_k\); actual increase causes rejection and radius contraction, leaving \(x_k=1\) and \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\) on that event.

On \(Z=0\), each model predicts positive reduction for \(s_k=\Delta_k>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines random-model and random-estimate reliability without assuming conditional independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) be the event that the random model is fully linear and \(F_k\) the event that all function estimates used at iteration \(k\) satisfy their declared accuracy bounds. If \(\mathbb P(M_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_m\) and \(\mathbb P(F_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_f\), then \[\mathbb P(M_k\cap F_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge\max\{0,p_m+p_f-1\}.\] If the events are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_k\), the lower bound is \(p_mp_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate conditional accuracy guarantees provide only a union-bound guarantee for joint accuracy unless conditional independence is established.
assumptions_latex: Both probability bounds are relative to the same pre-iteration history \(\mathcal F_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Recurrence of Jointly Accurate Trust-Region Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recurrence and waiting-time consequence for iterations whose random model and function estimates are jointly accurate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J_j\in\mathcal F_{j+1}\) be the event that iteration \(j\) has both a fully linear model and all declared accurate function estimates. If \(\mathbb P(J_j\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge q>0\) almost surely for every \(j\), then \(J_j\) occurs infinitely often almost surely. For any \(k\), define \(T_k=\inf\{t\ge0:J_{k+t}\}\). Then \[\mathbb P(T_k\ge m\mid\mathcal F_k)\le(1-q)^m,\qquad \mathbb E[T_k+1\mid\mathcal F_k]\le q^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform conditional joint accuracy makes accurate trust-region iterations recur and gives a geometric waiting-time bound.

Randomized Trust-Region Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region iteration using random models whose accuracy is required probabilistically.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), construct from sampled function values a random model \(m_k\) on \(\{s:\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta_k\}\), compute a step \(s_k\) giving a prescribed fraction of model decrease, and evaluate \(f(x_k+s_k)\). Define \[r_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}.\] Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) when \(r_k\geq\eta\), otherwise retain \(x_k\). Update \(\Delta_k\) by specified contraction or expansion factors based on \(r_k\) and model criticality. Stop under a budget, radius, or stationarity test and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a random local model, approximately minimize it inside a radius, compare actual with predicted decrease, and update both point and radius.
assumptions_latex: The model decrease denominator is positive whenever the ratio is evaluated.
Conditioned on the past, sufficiently accurate models occur with a prescribed positive probability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian zeroth-order estimator equals the smoothed gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian finite-difference representation of the gradient of a smoothed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be smooth, \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d\), \(\delta>0\), and \(F_\delta(\theta)=\mathbb E_{z\sim\mathcal N(0,I)}[F(\theta+\delta z)]\). Then \[\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{F(\theta+\delta z)-F(\theta)}{\delta}z\right]=\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{F(\theta+\delta z)}{\delta}z\right]=F_\delta'(\theta).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth function, the expected Gaussian finite-difference estimator, with or without subtracting F(theta), equals the gradient of the Gaussian-smoothed objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained exact-oracle rate for one random sphere direction per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and globally \(L\)-Lipschitz, let \(x_*\) be a minimizer with \(\|x_0-x_*\|\le R\), and let \(G_k\) be conditionally unbiased for \(\nabla f_\delta(x_k)\) with \(\mathbb E\|G_k\|^2\le n^2L^2\). For \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha G_k\), \(\alpha=R/(nL\sqrt N)\), and \(\bar x_N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}x_k\), \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_N)]-f_*\le \frac{RnL}{\sqrt N}+2L\delta.\] Hence \(N=O(n^2L^2R^2/\varepsilon^2)\) and \(\delta=O(\varepsilon/L)\) suffice for expected error \(O(\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Baseline convex random-direction descent has a stochastic-subgradient rate with a dimension penalty and controllable smoothing bias.
assumptions_latex: Function values are exact and the stated estimator moment bound holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Baseline Convex Zeroth-Order Dimension Penalty

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-specific approximation properties of uniform-ball smoothing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is convex and \(L\)-Lipschitz on every translated smoothing ball, then its uniform-ball smoothing \(f_\delta(x)=\mathbb E[f(x+\delta V)]\) is convex and satisfies \[f(x)\le f_\delta(x)\le f(x)+L\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform-ball smoothing preserves convexity and raises a convex Lipschitz objective by at most its Lipschitz constant times the smoothing radius.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is uniform on the unit ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Smoothing Bias

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-oracle strongly convex rate for unbiased random-direction gradients of a smoothed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_\delta\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex, \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f_\delta(x_k)\), and \(\mathbb E\|G_k\|^2\le M^2\). With \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\frac{2}{\mu(k+2)}G_k\) and \(\bar x_N=\frac{2}{N(N+1)}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}(k+1)x_k\), a standard strongly convex stochastic-gradient bound gives \[\mathbb E[f_\delta(\bar x_N)]-\min f_\delta\le\frac{2M^2}{\mu(N+1)}.\] If \(f(x)\le f_\delta(x)\le f(x)+L\delta\), then \(\mathbb E[f(\bar x_N)]-\min f\le2M^2/(\mu(N+1))+L\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity improves the smoothed objective-gap decay to order one over the iteration count, plus smoothing bias.
assumptions_latex: \(f_\delta\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex and attains its minimum.
The estimator is conditionally unbiased for \(\nabla f_\delta\) and has second moment at most \(M^2\).
All iterates lie in the region where the stated assumptions hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adversarial Value Noise Creates a Convex Accuracy Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex oracle-indistinguishability under uniformly bounded deterministic value errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(L>0\) and \(
u>0\), set \(a=
u/L\), and define \(f_+(x)=L|x-a|\) and \(f_-(x)=L|x+a|\). The common response \(y(x)=	frac12(f_+(x)+f_-(x))\) satisfies \(|y(x)-f_\pm(x)|\le
u\) for every \(x\). Thus both objectives yield identical oracle transcripts, while every returned \(\widehat x\) satisfies \[\max\{f_+(\widehat x)-\min f_+,\ f_-(\widehat x)-\min f_-\}\ge
u.\] For randomized algorithms, the corresponding maximum of the two expected losses is also at least \(
u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two convex Lipschitz objectives with separated minimizers can produce identical bounded-error responses, forcing worst-case objective error at least the noise magnitude.
assumptions_latex: The value oracle may choose deterministic errors satisfying \(|e(x)|\le\nu\).
The algorithm obtains only oracle values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Objective-Gap Certificate from a Calibrated Gradient Estimate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-specific conversion of a calibrated zeroth-order gradient estimate into an objective-gap bound when a minimizer-distance bound is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be differentiable and convex, let \(x_*\) be a minimizer, and suppose \(\|x-x_*\|\le R\). If a value-oracle construction returns \(\widehat g(x)\) and an event \(E\) on which \(\|\widehat g(x)-\nabla f(x)\|\le e\), then on \(E\), \[f(x)-f_*\le\langle\nabla f(x),x-x_*\rangle\le R\bigl(\|\widehat g(x)\|+e\bigr).\] If \(\mathbb P(E\mid\mathcal H)\ge1-\delta\) for a point fixed before validation, then this is a \((1-\delta)\)-valid objective-gap upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, a calibrated gradient estimate and a known distance to a minimizer give a probabilistic upper bound on suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: The tested point is fixed before validation data are drawn unless simultaneous calibration is supplied.

notation.meaning: known upper bound on distance from the tested point to a minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained convex descent using a sphere-direction estimator of uniform-ball smoothing and explicit iterate averaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex, let \(V\) be uniform on the Euclidean unit ball, and define \(f_\delta(x)=\mathbb E[f(x+\delta V)]\). Given \(x_0\), steps \(\alpha_k>0\), and independent \(U_k\) uniform on the unit sphere, set \[G_k=\frac{n}{\delta}\bigl(f(x_k+\delta U_k)-f(x_k)\bigr)U_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kG_k.\] Return the declared weighted average \(\bar x_N=(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_kx_k\). Whenever the ball-smoothing differentiation identity applies, \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f_\delta(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use exact random-direction differences to descend on a uniform-ball smoothing of a convex objective and return the explicitly step-weighted iterate average.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and finite on a neighborhood containing every queried smoothing ball.
The uniform-ball convolution is differentiable and the standard sphere-boundary identity applies.

notation.meaning: uniform-ball smoothing of the convex objective

Convex Zeroth-Order Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected descent for convex objectives using a two-point random-direction gradient estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex. Given \(x_0\in X\), radii \(\delta_k>0\), steps \(\alpha_k>0\), and independent directions \(U_k\) uniform on the unit sphere, query \(f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k+\delta_kU_k)\), form \[G_k=\frac{n}{\delta_k}\bigl(f(x_k+\delta_kU_k)-f(x_k)\bigr)U_k,\] and update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kG_k)\). Stop after the prescribed oracle budget and return either the final iterate or a stated weighted average of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate a smoothed gradient from two function values in a random direction, take a projected step, and return an iterate or average.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex on a neighborhood containing every queried point.
All function queries are exact, or the noise model is specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditioned on \(x_k\), \(G_k\) is an unbiased gradient estimator for the corresponding spherical smoothing of \(f\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias boundary when transferring a smoothed-gradient guarantee to the original objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bound on \(\|
abla f_\delta(x)\|\) alone does not bound \(\|
abla f(x)\|\). The transfer requires an explicit bias estimate; for example, if \(f\) has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, then uniform-ball smoothing satisfies \(\|
abla f_\delta(x)-
abla f(x)\|\le L\delta\). Without such regularity and control of \(\delta\), stationarity may hold only for the smoothed objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be bounded below with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(U_k\) be independent and uniform on the unit sphere, and set \(G_k=\frac n\delta(f(x_k+\delta U_k)-f(x_k))U_k\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha G_k\). If \(0<\alpha\le(4Ln)^{-1}\), then for \(R\) uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\), \[\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2\le\frac{4(f(x_0)-f_*)}{\alpha N}+(2+L\alpha n^2)L^2\delta^2.\] Consequently, \(\alpha=(4Ln)^{-1}\), \(N=O(nL(f(x_0)-f_*)/\varepsilon^2)\), and \(\delta=O(\varepsilon/(L\sqrt n))\) suffice for \(\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2=O(\varepsilon^2)\), using two value queries per iteration.

Directions are independent and uniform on the unit sphere.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Radius Smoothing Can Cancel a Nonzero Original Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional separation between smoothed and original stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\delta>0\) and define \(f(x)=x-\frac{\delta}{\sin 1}\sin(x/\delta)\). For uniform-interval smoothing at radius \(\delta\), \[f_\delta'(0)=\frac{f(\delta)-f(-\delta)}{2\delta}=0,\qquad f'(0)=1-\frac1{\sin1}\ne0.\] Thus exact stationarity of a fixed-radius smoothed objective need not imply stationarity of the original smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sinusoidal component can cancel a linear trend under fixed-radius smoothing although the original derivative is nonzero.

If \(x\) is selected using the same validation samples, fresh samples or simultaneous calibration is required.

Nonconvex Zeroth-Order Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained descent toward smoothed first-order stationarity using randomized finite differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), smoothing radii \(\delta_k>0\), steps \(\alpha_k>0\), and independent unit-sphere directions \(U_k\), evaluate \(f(x_k)\) and \(f(x_k+\delta_kU_k)\), set \[G_k=\frac{n}{\delta_k}\bigl(f(x_k+\delta_kU_k)-f(x_k)\bigr)U_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kG_k.\] Stop after \(N\) iterations and output an index \(R\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\) sampled according to the declared step-size weights, together with \(x_R\); performance is measured by \(\mathbb{E}\lVert\nabla f_{\delta_R}(x_R)\rVert^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use random two-point gradient estimates for unconstrained steps and assess a sampled iterate by the expected squared gradient of a smoothed objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is bounded below and smooth enough for its spherical smoothing to be differentiable.
Function-value noise, if present, has a separately specified bias and variance model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output convention targets smoothed stationarity through \(\mathbb{E}\lVert\nabla f_{\delta_R}(x_R)\rVert^2\).

notation.meaning: spherically smoothed objective at radius delta

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the nonconvex leaf, but the smoothing definition and probability law for the weighted output index are not specified. These choices affect the stationarity claim and require an authoritative algorithm locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic estimator identity proposed under the nonconvex terminal leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For uniform-ball smoothing and a uniform sphere direction, the standard one-sided random-direction difference is unbiased for the smoothed gradient whenever the convolution identity is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The random sphere-difference estimator targets a uniform-ball-smoothed gradient.
assumptions_latex: The smoothing identity is valid and both value queries are available.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothed-Gradient Estimator Identity

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns unconstrained nonconvex smoothed-gradient descent, random-output stationarity bounds, and the boundary between smoothed and original stationarity. The generic estimator identity belongs at the parent; convex objective-gap analysis and constrained geometry belong to siblings. Dimension-explicit, noisy, variance-reduced, and source-fixed algorithm variants remain frontier items.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian finite-difference descent for stochastic nonconvex objectives with a randomized output index.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_1\), an iteration limit \(N\), stepsizes \(\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge1}\), a smoothing parameter \(\mu\), and a probability mass function \(P_R\) supported on \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\), draw \(R\sim P_R\). For \(k=1,\ldots,R\), generate \(u_k\) using the specified Gaussian random-vector generator, compute \[G_\mu(x_k,\xi_k,u_k)=\frac{F(x_k+\mu u_k,\xi_k)-F(x_k,\xi_k)}{\mu}u_k,\] and update \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\gamma_kG_\mu(x_k,\xi_k,u_k).\] Output \(x_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a stopping index, repeatedly form a Gaussian two-point stochastic function-value estimator using the same sample in both evaluations, take the prescribed descent steps, and output the iterate x_R.
assumptions_latex: u_k\text{ is generated by the specified Gaussian random-vector generator}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Target first-order certificate for smooth optimization over a closed convex set; it is not directly computable from value queries without estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha>0\), define \(\mathcal G_\alpha(x)=\alpha^{-1}(x-\Pi_X(x-\alpha\nabla f(x)))\). Then \(\mathcal G_\alpha(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+N_X(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected-gradient mapping vanishes exactly at a constrained first-order stationary point.

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to X at x

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Mapping Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-aware query requirement for constrained zeroth-order descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constrained zeroth-order estimator at \(x\in X\) is feasibility preserving when every queried point lies in \(X\) almost surely. A declared feasible-direction law, interior shrinkage rule, or valid extension oracle may enforce this, but the chosen mechanism must also identify the smoothed or directional quantity estimated in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained estimator must keep its queries feasible and state what gradient-like quantity remains unbiased after boundary handling.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set and oracle domain are specified.
The boundary mechanism is fixed before unbiasedness is claimed.

notation.meaning: j-th oracle query at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unmodified symmetric perturbations on a restricted oracle domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the oracle is defined only on \(X\) and \(x\in\partial X\), an estimator requiring both \(f(x+\delta u)\) and \(f(x-\delta u)\) is undefined whenever either perturbation leaves \(X\). Discarding infeasible directions changes their conditional distribution and, absent an explicit correction, does not preserve the usual isotropic smoothing identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a boundary, symmetric queries may be infeasible, and uncorrected rejection generally invalidates the standard unbiasedness identity.
assumptions_latex: The perturbation law crosses the boundary with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P(x+\delta U\notin X\ \text{or}\ x-\delta U\notin X)>0\implies\text{the unmodified estimator is not well-defined}.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Query Bias and Infeasibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from a zeroth-order gradient estimate to the true constrained stationarity mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\), \(\alpha>0\), and an estimate \(g\), define \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_\alpha(x;g)=\alpha^{-1}(x-\Pi_X(x-\alpha g))\). Projection nonexpansiveness gives \[\|\widehat{\mathcal G}_\alpha(x;g)-\mathcal G_\alpha(x)\|\le\|g-\nabla f(x)\|.\] Hence \(\|\widehat{\mathcal G}_\alpha(x;g)\|\le\tau\) and \(\|g-\nabla f(x)\|\le e\) imply \(\|\mathcal G_\alpha(x)\|\le\tau+e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimated projected-gradient residual certifies true constrained stationarity up to the gradient-estimation error.

notation.meaning: projected-gradient mapping formed with an estimated gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Estimated Projected-Gradient Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving variant using an eroded feasible set and symmetric queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta>0\), define \(X_\delta=\{x\in X:x+\delta B\subseteq X\}\), where \(B\) is the closed Euclidean unit ball, and assume \(X_\delta\ne\varnothing\). Given \(x_0\in X_\delta\), draw \(U_k\) uniformly on the unit sphere, form \[G_k=\frac{n}{2\delta}\bigl(f(x_k+\delta U_k)-f(x_k-\delta U_k)\bigr)U_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=\Pi_{X_\delta}(x_k-\alpha_kG_k).\] Every query and iterate lies in \(X\); where the convolution identity applies, \(G_k\) is unbiased for the gradient of uniform-ball smoothing at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict centers to an eroded feasible set so symmetric queries remain feasible, then project every estimated-gradient step back onto that set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(X_\delta\) is nonempty and its Euclidean projection is available.
The smoothing differentiation identity is valid when unbiasedness is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in X_\delta\quad\text{and}\quad x_k\pm\delta U_k\in X\quad\text{for every }k.

notation.meaning: erosion of X by a radius-delta Euclidean ball

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Erosion Projected Zeroth-Order Descent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-aware constrained variant using a declared objective extension instead of eroding the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and suppose an oracle evaluates an extension \(\widetilde f\) on \(X+\delta B\) with \(\widetilde f=f\) on \(X\). For independent \(U_k\) uniform on the unit sphere, form \[G_k=\frac{n}{2\delta}\bigl(\widetilde f(x_k+\delta U_k)-\widetilde f(x_k-\delta U_k)\bigr)U_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kG_k).\] Then every iterate is feasible, and whenever the convolution differentiation identity applies, \(G_k\) is unbiased for the gradient of the uniform-ball smoothing of \(\widetilde f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a declared off-domain extension for symmetric queries and project each estimated-gradient step onto the original feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The extension oracle is defined on \(X+\delta B\) and agrees with \(f\) on \(X\).
The smoothing differentiation identity is valid when unbiasedness is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in X\ \text{for every }k,\qquad \mathbb E[G_k\mid x_k]=\nabla\widetilde f_\delta(x_k).

notation.meaning: declared extension of the constrained objective
radius-delta neighborhood of the feasible set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inward Coordinate-Difference Projected Descent on a Box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-constrained feasibility-preserving variant requiring neither an extension oracle nor erosion of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), where \(\ell_i<u_i\). At \(x_k\in X\), choose \(s_{k,i}\in\{-1,1\}\) and \(h_{k,i}>0\) such that \(h_{k,i}\le u_i-x_{k,i}\) if \(s_{k,i}=1\), or \(h_{k,i}\le x_{k,i}-\ell_i\) if \(s_{k,i}=-1\). Define \[(G_k)_i=s_{k,i}\frac{f(x_k+s_{k,i}h_{k,i}e_i)-f(x_k)}{h_{k,i}},\qquad x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kG_k).\] Every query and iterate is feasible. If \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the queried segments, then \[\|G_k-\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\frac L2\left(\sum_{i=1}^nh_{k,i}^2\right)^{1/2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a feasible inward coordinate difference in every coordinate and project the estimated-gradient step onto the box.
assumptions_latex: The gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz on queried coordinate segments when the error bound is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in X\text{ and every query lies in }X,\qquad \|G_k-\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\frac L2\|h_k\|_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Inward Coordinate-Difference Projected Descent on a Box
Constrained Zeroth-Order Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected zeroth-order descent with feasibility enforced after every estimated-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Given \(x_0\in X\), \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\delta_k>0\), and independent unit-sphere directions \(U_k\), obtain a zeroth-order estimator \(G_k\) from feasible function queries, for example by a declared one-sided, two-sided, or feasibility-preserving smoothing scheme. Update \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kG_k).\] Stop under a prescribed oracle budget or projected-stationarity test and return the selected iterate. When ordinary perturbations leave \(X\), the oracle scheme must explicitly use an extension, shrinking radius, or feasible-direction construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate a gradient from function values, project each descent step onto the convex feasible set, and explicitly handle perturbations that would leave the domain.
assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is evaluable at every point requested by the declared oracle scheme.
The projection \(\Pi_X\) is well-defined and computationally available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every iterate generated by the update satisfies \(x_k\in X\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

children.top_down_role: Derivative-free methods exploiting residual maps, sparsity, partial separability, convexity, composite outer structure, or nested black boxes.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Interpolation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise interpolation models for derivative-free nonlinear least-squares residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residual map \(r=(r_1,\ldots,r_m):\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and sample set \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^p\}\), choose a finite-dimensional polynomial space \(\mathcal{P}\). For each component, construct \(m_i\in\mathcal{P}\) satisfying \[m_i(y^j)=r_i(y^j),\qquad j=0,\ldots,p.\] With \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_m)\), the induced least-squares objective model is \[M(x)=\frac12\lVert m(x)\rVert_2^2.\] If the interpolation system is square, existence and uniqueness require the evaluation map on \(Y\) to be nonsingular; underdetermined systems require an explicit model-selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interpolate every residual component on a sample set, then square and sum those models to obtain a structured model of the least-squares objective.
assumptions_latex: The sample geometry and model-selection rule make each interpolation problem well posed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(y^j)=\tfrac12\lVert r(y^j)\rVert_2^2\) for every interpolation point \(y^j\in Y\).

source_refs.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform accuracy of componentwise affine interpolation for smooth nonlinear residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(r_i\) have Lipschitz-continuous gradient near \(B(x,\Delta)\). If \(n+1\) interpolation points in the ball are uniformly poised for affine interpolation, then constants independent of \(\Delta\) satisfy \[|r_i(x+s)-m_i(x+s)|\le\kappa_i^f\Delta^2,\qquad \|\nabla r_i(x+s)-\nabla m_i\|\le\kappa_i^g\Delta\] for every \(\|s\|\le\Delta\). If the residuals and Jacobians are locally bounded, \(M=\tfrac12\|m\|^2\) is fully linear for \(F=\tfrac12\|r\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly poised affine interpolation set gives first-order-accurate residual models and a fully linear least-squares objective model.
assumptions_latex: Each residual component has a locally Lipschitz gradient.
The interpolation set is uniformly poised in the trust-region ball.
Residuals and Jacobians are locally bounded when objective-model accuracy is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|F-M|=O(\Delta^2)\) and \(\|\nabla F-\nabla M\|=O(\Delta)\) uniformly on the ball.
knowledge_statements.title: Poised Affine Residual Interpolation Accuracy
Residual-Regression Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overdetermined componentwise regression models for noisy or redundant residual samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For residual observations \(z_i^j=r_i(y^j)+\varepsilon_i^j\), positive weights \(w_j\), and polynomial basis vector \(\phi(x)\in\mathbb{R}^q\), define each residual model by \[c_i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{c\in\mathbb{R}^q}\sum_{j=0}^{p}w_j\bigl(\phi(y^j)^{\mathsf T}c-z_i^j\bigr)^2,\qquad m_i(x)=\phi(x)^{\mathsf T}c_i.\] The structured objective model is \(M(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^m m_i(x)^2\). If the weighted design matrix has full column rank, every coefficient vector \(c_i\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit each residual component by weighted least squares over sampled points, then combine the fitted residuals into a least-squares objective model.
assumptions_latex: \(p+1\geq q\), \(w_j>0\), and every observation \(z_i^j\) is available.
The weighted design matrix has full column rank when uniqueness is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient vectors minimize the stated weighted residual errors, and \(M(x)=\tfrac12\lVert m(x)\rVert_2^2\).

notation.meaning: regression coefficients for residual component i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of coefficient uniqueness and predictive interpretation in residual regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) lacks full column rank, the coefficient minimizer is nonunique unless an additional selection rule or regularizer is declared. If \(A^{\mathsf T}WA\) is nearly singular, observation perturbations can be strongly amplified. Even with full rank, a small sample regression residual does not by itself certify accuracy away from the sample set when the residual component is outside the chosen model class or the sample geometry is inadequate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank loss destroys uniqueness, poor conditioning amplifies noise, and sample fit alone does not guarantee predictive accuracy under misspecification.
assumptions_latex: Residual components are fitted in a declared finite-dimensional basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reliable residual regression requires rank and conditioning control plus an approximation or sampling assumption for out-of-sample accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank, Conditioning, and Model-Misspecification Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Recovery and Noise Propagation in Residual Regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic recovery and covariance of the weighted componentwise fit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_{j,:}=\phi(y^j)^{\mathsf T}\), \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_j)\succ0\), and suppose \(A\) has full column rank. Then \[\widehat c_i=(A^{\mathsf T}WA)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}Wz_i.\] If \(z_i=Ac_i^*\), then \(\widehat c_i=c_i^*\). If \(z_i=Ac_i^*+\varepsilon_i\), \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_i)=\Sigma_i\), then \[\mathbb E\widehat c_i=c_i^*,\quad \operatorname{Cov}(\widehat c_i)=(A^{\mathsf T}WA)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}W\Sigma_iWA(A^{\mathsf T}WA)^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-rank residual regression exactly recovers in-model residuals and propagates observation noise through the weighted pseudoinverse.
assumptions_latex: Noise has zero mean and finite covariance for the stochastic assertions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The fit is exact for in-model data and has the stated covariance under additive noise.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Recovery and Noise Propagation in Residual Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured quadratic induced by an affine residual model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(m_k(s)=r_k+J_ks\), define \[M_k(s)=\frac12\|r_k+J_ks\|^2=\frac12\|r_k\|^2+s^{\mathsf T}J_k^{\mathsf T}r_k+\frac12s^{\mathsf T}J_k^{\mathsf T}J_ks.\] Then \(\nabla M_k(0)=J_k^{\mathsf T}r_k\) and \(\nabla^2M_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine residual model induces a positive-semidefinite Gauss–Newton quadratic without residual derivatives.
assumptions_latex: The residual vector is available at the center.
An affine model of each residual component is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Gauss–Newton Model

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Accuracy Transfers to a Fully Linear Objective Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy transfer for a residual-squared trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|^2\). On \(\|s\|\le\Delta\), suppose \(\|r(x+s)-m(s)\|\le\kappa_f\Delta^2\) and \(\|J_r(x+s)-J_m(s)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta\). If \(r,m,J_r,J_m\) are uniformly bounded there, then constants \(K_f,K_g\), independent of \(\Delta\), satisfy \[|F(x+s)-\tfrac12\|m(s)\|^2|\le K_f\Delta^2,\qquad \|\nabla F(x+s)-J_m(s)^{\mathsf T}m(s)\|\le K_g\Delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accurate residual and residual-Jacobian models induce a fully linear least-squares objective model.
assumptions_latex: The stated residual and Jacobian approximation bounds hold throughout the trust region.
Residuals, models, and their Jacobians are uniformly bounded there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tfrac12\|m\|^2\) is fully linear for \(F\) on the same trust region.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Accuracy Transfers to a Fully Linear Objective Model
Least-Squares Trust-Region DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free trust-region method preserving the residual-sum-of-squares structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12\lVert r(x)\rVert_2^2\), maintain \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and a residual model \(m_k(s)\) built from sampled residual vectors. Define \(M_k(s)=\tfrac12\lVert m_k(s)\rVert_2^2\), approximately solve \[\min_{\lVert s\rVert\leq\Delta_k}M_k(s),\] and evaluate \(r(x_k+s_k)\). Compare actual and predicted reductions using \(\rho_k=[F(x_k)-F(x_k+s_k)]/[M_k(0)-M_k(s_k)]\). Accept according to a fixed threshold, update \(\Delta_k\), repair the sample geometry when required, and stop under a budget, radius, or stationarity test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model the residual vector, minimize its squared norm inside a trust region, and use the reduction ratio to accept steps and update the radius.
assumptions_latex: Residual vectors \(r(x)\) can be evaluated without derivatives.
The residual model and sample geometry satisfy the declared local-accuracy conditions.
The predicted reduction is positive whenever \(\rho_k\) is evaluated.

notation.meaning: local model of the residual vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between a reusable derivative pattern and accidental zeros at one point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative entry vanishing at one point does not establish structural sparsity. Structural Jacobian sparsity requires \(\partial_jF_i(x)=0\) throughout the declared domain for every excluded pair \((i,j)\); structural Hessian sparsity analogously requires persistent zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accidental zeros at sampled points do not establish a structural derivative pattern.
assumptions_latex: The pattern is intended to hold throughout a declared domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Versus Pointwise Sparsity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation of a known structural Jacobian pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a structural Jacobian pattern \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the column-intersection graph has vertices \(1,\ldots,n\) and an edge \(\{j,k\}\) when some row \(i\) satisfies \((i,j)\in S\) and \((i,k)\in S\). An independent vertex set therefore consists of columns that never share a structurally permitted nonzero row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The column-intersection graph records which derivative columns can interfere in the same row.
assumptions_latex: The structural pattern \(S\) is declared on a common domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Column-Intersection Graph
Sparse Derivative Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Known or inferable sparsity in gradients, Jacobians, or Hessians exploited by derivative-free models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(F_1,\ldots,F_m):\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be differentiable on an open set \(U\). It has Jacobian sparsity pattern \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{1,\ldots,n\}\) on \(U\) when \[\frac{\partial F_i(x)}{\partial x_j}=0\quad\text{for every }x\in U\text{ and every }(i,j)\notin S.\] The structure is sparse when \(|S|\ll mn\). For a scalar twice-differentiable objective, Hessian sparsity is defined analogously by a set \(T\subseteq\{1,,n\}^2\) outside which \(\nabla^2 f(x)\) vanishes throughout \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative structure is sparse when only a small specified set of Jacobian or Hessian entries can be nonzero throughout the domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Entries outside \(S\), or outside \(T\) in the scalar second-order case, vanish identically on \(U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but no source is supplied, the Hessian index set contains malformed LaTeX (\{1,,n\}^2), and the condition |S| much less than mn is informal rather than a defined threshold. An authoritative sparse-derivative-structure source is needed before choosing a corrected formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed simultaneous recovery using exact Jacobian-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coloring of the column-intersection graph can group columns in exact products \(J(x)d_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed record uses exact Jacobian-vector products to recover grouped derivative columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The proposed operation is a derivative-product oracle, not a derivative-free evaluation interface.}
review_flags: Exact Jacobian-vector products belong to sparse derivative recovery or automatic-differentiation theory; finite-difference grouping would require a separate error model and is not exact for nonlinear maps.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for exploiting a known additive decomposition in DFO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Knowledge that \(f=\sum_i f_i\circ P_i\) does not itself expose the values \(f_i(P_i x)\). With only aggregate evaluations of \(f\), the individual element functions are generally nonidentifiable without element-value access or additional identifying assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elementwise DFO requires element values or equivalent identifying information; an aggregate objective oracle does not generally reveal them.
assumptions_latex: No element-identifying side information is available.
