knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative structure induced by differentiable element functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^q f_i(P_i x)\) and every \(f_i\) is twice differentiable, then \[
abla f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^qP_i^	op
abla f_i(P_i x),\qquad 
abla^2f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^qP_i^	op
abla^2f_i(P_i x)P_i.\] Hence \((
abla^2f(x))_{jk}=0\) whenever no element set contains both \(j\) and \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Element derivatives assemble by zero-padding and summation, and variables can interact in the Hessian only through an element containing both.
knowledge_statements.title: Derivative Assembly and Induced Sparsity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial representation of a fixed partially separable decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^qf_i(x_{I_i})\), let \(H=(V,E)\) have \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and hyperedges \(E=\{I_1,\ldots,I_q\}\). Its incidence matrix \(B\in\{0,1\}^{q\times n}\), defined by \(B_{ij}=1\iff j\in I_i\), records every element-variable incidence and determines element overlap through \(I_i\cap I_\ell\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed partially separable decomposition is represented by a hypergraph whose hyperedges are its element-variable sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Element–Variable Hypergraph Representation
Partial Separability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional additive partial separability by overlapping variable subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is partially separable if there exist index sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_q\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and element functions \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^{|I_i|}\to\mathbb{R}\) such that \[f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{q}f_i(x_{I_i})\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Its degree of partial separability is \(s=\max_i|I_i|\). The structure is low-complexity when \(s\ll n\), although the sets may overlap and their union must contain every coordinate on which \(f\) depends.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partially separable objective is a sum of element functions, each depending on only a small, possibly overlapping subset of the variables.

notation.meaning: Subvector of x indexed by I_i.
Largest number of variables in an element function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, but no cited source supports the specialized definition or the stated degree convention.

children.title: Active-Subspace Structure
children.top_down_role: Dominant low-dimensional directional structure in black-box variation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample construction of the gradient second-moment eigenspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given independent \(x_j\sim\rho\) and gradient or gradient-surrogate vectors \(g_j\), form \[\widehat C=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N g_jg_j^{\mathsf T}\] and take its leading \(r\) eigenvectors. If \(\|\widehat C-C\|_2\le\varepsilon_C<\gamma/2\), where \(\gamma=\lambda_r(C)-\lambda_{r+1}(C)>0\), then a Davis–Kahan perturbation bound gives \[\|\sin\Theta(\widehat W_1,W_1)\|_2\le\frac{2\varepsilon_C}{\gamma}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the gradient covariance by sampling; subspace error is controlled by covariance error relative to the eigengap.
assumptions_latex: The sampled outer products are well defined.
The total covariance error, including gradient-surrogate bias, is bounded by \(\varepsilon_C\).
The selected eigenspace has gap \(\gamma>0\) and \(\varepsilon_C<\gamma/2\).

notation.meaning: Spectral gap at the selected active dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Empirical Active-Subspace Estimation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness and instability at a repeated eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda_r(C)=\lambda_{r+1}(C)\), a leading \(r\)-dimensional eigenspace need not be uniquely determined inside the repeated-eigenvalue invariant subspace. Arbitrarily small perturbations can then rotate a selected \(r\)-dimensional subspace by an order-one angle, so no finite gap-independent Lipschitz perturbation bound is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without an eigengap, the selected active subspace can be nonunique and unstable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected dimension-\(r\) active subspace is not stably identifiable.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Gap Identifiability Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-square approximation by conditioning on active coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=W\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)W^{\mathsf T}\), let \(W_1\) contain its first \(r\) eigenvectors, and set \(g(y)=\mathbb E[f(X)\mid W_1^{\mathsf T}X=y]\). If the conditional measures on inactive fibers satisfy a Poincare inequality with a common constant \(C_P\), then \[\mathbb E[(f(X)-g(W_1^{\mathsf T}X))^2]\le C_P\sum_{i=r+1}^n\lambda_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trailing active-subspace eigenvalues bound the mean-square error of the conditional-expectation ridge approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has a square-integrable gradient under the input measure.
A uniform conditional Poincare inequality holds on the inactive fibers.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Subspace Ridge Approximation Bound
Active-Subspace Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient-covariance definition under a specified input distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable almost everywhere and let \(ho\) be a probability measure on \(\Omega\). If \(
abla f\in L^2(ho)\), define \[C=\int_{\Omega}
abla f(x)
abla f(x)^{\mathsf T}\,dho(x)=W\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)W^{\mathsf T},\] where \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n\geq0\). For a chosen dimension \(r<n\), the active subspace is \(\operatorname{span}(W_1)\), where \(W_1\) contains the first \(r\) eigenvectors; the remaining mean-square directional sensitivity equals \(\sum_{i=r+1}^n\lambda_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active subspace is the leading eigenspace of the gradient second-moment matrix under a chosen input distribution.

notation.meaning: Matrix of the r leading eigenvectors of C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gradient-covariance definition fits the active-subspace leaf, but the eigenspace and inactive-sensitivity claims lack a specific supporting citation.

children.title: Low-Effective-Dimension Structure
children.top_down_role: Problems whose influential dimension is substantially below ambient dimension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unconstrained optimization reduction for a known effective subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)=g(U^{\mathsf T}x)\) with \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\), then \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R^r}g(y).\] Moreover, \[\arg\min f=\{x:U^{\mathsf T}x\in\arg\min g\}.\] Thus each reduced minimizer \(y_*\) lifts to \(Uy_*+\ker(U^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact ridge objective can be optimized entirely in its effective coordinates, with ambient minimizers lying on inactive affine fibers.
assumptions_latex: \(f=g\circ U^{\mathsf T}\), \(U\) has orthonormal columns, and optimization is unconstrained.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Optimization Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Random Embeddings Capture an Exact Effective Subspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure unconstrained reduction for an exact ridge objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=g(U^{\mathsf T}x)\) have effective dimension \(r\), and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}\), \(q\ge r\), have a distribution absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. Then \(\operatorname{rank}(U^{\mathsf T}A)=r\) almost surely. Consequently, \[\inf_{z\in\mathbb R^q}f(Az)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\quad\text{almost surely}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generic random embedding of dimension at least the effective dimension preserves the unconstrained optimum almost surely.
assumptions_latex: The objective is an exact ridge function.
\(q\ge r\) and the embedding distribution is absolutely continuous.
Both ambient and embedded problems are unconstrained.
knowledge_statements.title: Random Embeddings Capture an Exact Effective Subspace
Low-Effective-Dimension Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ridge-function notion of effective dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) has effective dimension at most \(r\) if there exist a matrix \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) with \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\) and a function \(g:\mathbb{R}^r\to\mathbb{R}\) such that \[f(x)=g(U^{\mathsf T}x)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Its exact effective dimension is the least such \(r\). Consequently, \(f(x+v)=f(x)\) for every \(v\in\ker(U^{\mathsf T})\), so optimization depends only on the reduced coordinates \(U^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective has effective dimension r when it is exactly a function of r orthogonal linear combinations of its n variables.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis matrix for the effective subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact ridge-function definition is coherent and appropriately classified, but no source establishes that this is the intended effective-dimension convention.

children.title: Subspace-Misspecification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes caused by inaccurate dimension or subspace identification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reachability Criterion for a Selected Search Subspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion separating harmless enlargement from dimension or orientation loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=g(U^{\mathsf T}x)\), assume \(\arg\min g\ne\varnothing\), and restrict optimization to \(x_0+\operatorname{range}(V)\). The reachable effective coordinates are \[\mathcal Y_V=U^{\mathsf T}x_0+\operatorname{range}(U^{\mathsf T}V).\] The restricted problem preserves the attained global minimum if and only if \(\mathcal Y_V\cap\arg\min g\ne\varnothing\). In particular, \(\operatorname{rank}(U^{\mathsf T}V)=r\) guarantees preservation for every such \(g\), whereas rank deficiency permits a reduced objective whose minimizer is unreachable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selected search subspace is sufficient exactly when its reachable effective coordinates contain a reduced minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The objective has exact ridge form \(f=g\circ U^{\mathsf T}\).
Search is restricted to the stated affine subspace.

notation.meaning: Effective coordinates reachable from the selected affine search space.

knowledge_statements.title: Reachability Criterion for a Selected Search Subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective distortion caused by subspace orientation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=g(U^{\mathsf T}x)\), let \(P_V=VV^{\mathsf T}\), and suppose \(g\) is \(L_g\)-Lipschitz on the compared reduced points. For \(\|x\|\le R\), \[|f(x)-f(P_Vx)|\le L_g\|U^{\mathsf T}(I-P_V)x\|\le L_gR\|(I-P_V)U\|_2.\] The final factor is the largest sine of the principal angles between the true and selected subspaces. No analogous uniform global bound follows without bounded search radius or suitable regularity of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Angular error controls objective distortion only together with bounded search and reduced-objective regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is \(L_g\)-Lipschitz on the compared reduced points.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the selected subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Principal-Angle Approximation Boundary
Subspace-Misspecification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-gradient boundary for optimization in an approximate subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=UU^{\mathsf T}\) be an orthogonal projector and restrict searches to \(x_0+\operatorname{range}(U)\). If \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(\|(I-P)\nabla f(x)\|\leq\eta\) on a convex region, then for every admissible segment, \[|f(x)-f(x_0+P(x-x_0))|\leq\eta\|(I-P)(x-x_0)\|.\] This control disappears when no uniform residual bound exists. In particular, for \(f(y,z)=y^2+(z-1)^2\), choosing \(U=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(x_0=(0,0)\) yields the reduced stationary point \((0,0)\), which is not stationary for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-space stationarity need not imply full stationarity; approximation error is controlled only when the omitted gradient component is uniformly small.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on a convex region containing the relevant segments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|f(x)-f(x_0+P(x-x_0))|\leq\eta\|(I-P)(x-x_0)\|\), while reduced stationarity alone is insufficient.

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on omitted gradient components.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-gradient bound and counterexample fit a failure-boundary container, but the quantitative claim has no cited source.

children.title: Manifold Sampling Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods organized around active smooth pieces of nonsmooth composite objectives; unrelated to Riemannian manifold optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideal stationarity test approximated by manifold-sampling models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For G(x)=\partial_C f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{F'(x)^\mathsf T\nabla h_j(F(x)):j\in J(F(x))\}, Clarke stationarity is equivalent to 0\in G(x), or equivalently \operatorname{dist}(0,G(x))=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero minimum norm of the exact active-gradient hull is equivalent to Clarke stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The Regular Active-Manifold Gradient Hull assumptions hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Active-Hull Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order representation under an explicitly assumed regular finite-selection formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f=h\circ F with F continuously differentiable. Suppose h has finitely many local C^1 selections h_j and the representation is Clarke regular with \partial_C h(F(x))=\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla h_j(F(x)):j\in J(F(x))\}. Then \partial_C f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{F'(x)^\mathsf T\nabla h_j(F(x)):j\in J(F(x))\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an exact regular active-selection formula, composite generalized gradients form the convex hull of active composite gradients.
assumptions_latex: F is continuously differentiable near x.
The stated finite-selection Clarke formula holds at F(x).
The composite chain rule is exact at x.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular Active-Manifold Gradient Hull

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Missed Active Manifold Can Produce False Nonstationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an incomplete discovered-manifold hull at a truly stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f(x)=|x|=\max\{x,-x\}. At x=0, the exact active-gradient hull is [-1,1], so 0\in\partial_C f(0). If manifold discovery retains only the selection h_1(x)=x, its sampled hull is \{1\}, whose distance from zero is one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the minimizer of absolute value, discovering only one active branch incorrectly reports a nonzero stationarity measure.
assumptions_latex: The sampled hull is formed only from discovered active selections.
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Active Manifold Can Produce False Nonstationarity
Manifold Sampling Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region manifold sampling for nonsmooth composite objectives, not Riemannian optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=h(F(x))\), where \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) is smooth but available only through values and \(h\) is locally represented by finitely many smooth selections \(h_j\). At iterate \(x_k\), construct derivative-free models of the components of \(F\), sample nearby points, and identify selections active at their images. Form modeled gradients \(g_{k,j}\) of the sampled composites and compute a trust-region step by minimizing a model built from \(\operatorname{conv}\{g_{k,j}\}\) over \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\). Accept the step by actual-to-predicted reduction, update \(\Delta_k\), and stop when the minimum-norm convex combination is sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Manifold sampling models the smooth inner map, samples nearby active smooth pieces, and uses their convex-hull gradients in a trust-region step.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) has finitely many locally smooth selection functions.
The derivative-free component models are poised on the trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an iterate whose sampled generalized-gradient model has minimum norm below the prescribed tolerance.

notation.meaning: Modeled gradient for sampled selection j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and nonsmooth-composite interpretation fit the leaf, but the active-selection model, trust-region subproblem, and stopping measure depend on an uncited manifold-sampling variant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order certificate for a finite maximum of continuously differentiable selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f(x)=\max_{1\leq j\leq m}\phi_j(x), with every \phi_j continuously differentiable near x, and let J(x)=\{j:\phi_j(x)=f(x)\}. Then \[\partial_C f(x)=\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla\phi_j(x):j\in J(x)\},\] so \[0\in\partial_C f(x)\iff\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\operatorname{conv}\{\nabla\phi_j(x):j\in J(x)\}\right)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-max objective is Clarke stationary exactly when zero belongs to the convex hull of its active gradients.
assumptions_latex: The maximum has finitely many selections.

notation.meaning: active indices in the finite maximum

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Max Linearization Stationarity Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Epigraph Form of the Piecewise-Linearized Trust-Region Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical computational representation of a finite maximum of affine local models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let m_k(s)=\max_{1\leq j\leq m}\{c_{k,j}+g_{k,j}^{\mathsf T}s\}. Then \[\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}m_k(s)=\min_{s,t}\left\{t:c_{k,j}+g_{k,j}^{\mathsf T}s\leq t\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\ \|s\|\leq\Delta_k\right\}.\] This is a linear program for a polyhedral trust region and a second-order cone program for a Euclidean ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a maximum of affine linearizations becomes an epigraph LP or conic trust-region problem.
assumptions_latex: The model is a finite maximum of affine functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}m_k(s)\text{ has the stated convex epigraph formulation}.

notation.meaning: epigraph variable for the maximum model value

knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Form of the Piecewise-Linearized Trust-Region Subproblem
Piecewise-Linearization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free trust-region linearization for convex piecewise-linear outer functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=h(F(x))\), where \(h(z)=\max_{1\leq j\leq m}(a_j^{\mathsf T}z+b_j)\). At iterate \(x_k\), build value-based affine models \(M_{k,i}(s)=F_i(x_k)+g_{k,i}^{\mathsf T}s\) for every component of \(F\). Compute \[s_k\in\arg\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}\max_j\{a_j^{\mathsf T}M_k(s)+b_j\}.\] Evaluate \(f(x_k+s_k)\), accept the step when actual reduction is a prescribed fraction of predicted reduction, and enlarge or contract \(\Delta_k\) accordingly. Stop when the predicted decrease is below tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method replaces the inner map by derivative-free affine models and minimizes the resulting piecewise-linear composite inside a trust region.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is a finite maximum of affine functions.
Every component of \(F\) can be evaluated.
The interpolation set produces affine models on the current trust region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each trial step minimizes the piecewise-linear composite model over \(\|s\|\leq\Delta_k\).

notation.meaning: Vector of affine derivative-free models of F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The piecewise-linear trust-region construction fits the leaf, but its model, acceptance rule, radius update, and stopping criterion lack a specific algorithm citation.

children.title: Convex Outer Compositions
children.top_down_role: Composite derivative-free problems with convex outer structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Outer Does Not Ensure Convex Composite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between outer convexity and full-objective convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For h(z)=z and F(x)=-x^2, h is convex but (h\circ F)(x)=-x^2 is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex identity outer function composed with minus x squared gives a nonconvex objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Outer Does Not Ensure Convex Composite

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector-valued convex-inner composition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be convex, let each F_i:X\to\mathbb R be convex, and let h be convex and coordinatewise nondecreasing on a convex set containing F(X). Then x\mapsto h(F_1(x),\ldots,F_p(x)) is convex on X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinatewise nondecreasing convex outer function preserves convexity of convex inner components.
assumptions_latex: h is convex and coordinatewise nondecreasing on the relevant range.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Coordinatewise Convex Composition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical sufficient condition transferring outer convexity to the composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If h is proper convex, F(x)=Ax+b, and X is convex with F(X)\subseteq\operatorname{dom}h, then h\circ F is convex on X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex outer function composed with an affine inner map is convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Inner Convexity Preservation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex subdifferential representation for an affine inner map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For f(x)=h(Ax+b), with h proper closed convex, if Ax+b\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}h), then \partial f(x)=A^\mathsf T\partial h(Ax+b). Thus stationarity is equivalent to the existence of v\in\partial h(Ax+b) with A^\mathsf Tv=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, affine-composite subgradients are adjoint images of outer subgradients.
assumptions_latex: h is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Composite Subdifferential Chain Rule

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Derivative Chain Rule for Convex Outer Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional first-order formula without assuming convexity of the full composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F be differentiable at x, and let the proper convex function h be finite and locally Lipschitz near F(x). Then \[(h\circ F)'(x;d)=h'(F(x);F'(x)d)=\max_{v\in\partial h(F(x))}\langle v,F'(x)d\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The composite directional derivative is the support function of the outer subdifferential evaluated along the linearized inner direction.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, convex, finite, and locally Lipschitz near \(F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Derivative Chain Rule for Convex Outer Functions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fenchel Supremum Representation of a Convex-Outer Composite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical dual-affine representation supplied by a proper closed convex outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If h:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\} is proper, closed, and convex, then for every x with F(x)\in\operatorname{dom}h, \[(h\circ F)(x)=\sup_{v\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\{\langle v,F(x)\rangle-h^*(v)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex outer function is the supremum of affine supports, making its composite a supremum of scalarized inner mappings.

notation.meaning: Fenchel conjugate of the outer function

knowledge_statements.title: Fenchel Supremum Representation of a Convex-Outer Composite

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional-Stationarity Certificate for a Convex Outer Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact no-descent-direction test for a differentiable nonlinear inner map without asserting convexity of the composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be differentiable at \(x\), and let \(h\) be proper, convex, finite, and locally Lipschitz near \(F(x)\). Then the following are equivalent: \[(h\circ F)'(x;d)\geq0\quad\text{for every }d,\] \[0\in F'(x)^\mathsf T\partial h(F(x)),\] and \[\exists v\in\partial h(F(x)):\ F'(x)^\mathsf Tv=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz convex outer function, absence of a first-order descent direction is equivalent to an outer subgradient annihilated by the adjoint inner derivative.
assumptions_latex: \(h\text{ is finite and locally Lipschitz near }F(x)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (h\circ F)'(x;d)\geq0\ \forall d\iff\exists v\in\partial h(F(x)):\ F'(x)^\mathsf Tv=0.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of the outer function

knowledge_statements.title: Directional-Stationarity Certificate for a Convex Outer Function

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Convexity Transfer through an Injective Affine Inner Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative curvature transfer for a strongly convex outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a convex set containing \(AX+b\), where \(X\) is convex. If \(\underline\sigma(A):=\inf_{d\ne0}\|Ad\|/\|d\|>0\), then \(f(x)=h(Ax+b)\) is \(\mu\underline\sigma(A)^2\)-strongly convex on \(X\). If \(A\) has a nontrivial nullspace containing a feasible chord direction, strong convexity of \(h\) alone cannot make \(h(Ax+b)\) strongly convex along that direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong outer curvature transfers through an affine inner map to the extent that the map is injective on feasible directions.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on the relevant range.

notation.meaning: minimum gain of the affine map's linear part

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Transfer through an Injective Affine Inner Map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical regime definition separating outer convexity from convexity of the composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-outer composite objective is \(f=h\circ F\) on \(X\), where \(F:X\to\mathbb R^p\), \(h:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(F(X)\subseteq\operatorname{dom}h\). The regime asserts convexity of \(h\), not of \(f\). Convexity of \(f\) follows only under an additional valid composition rule, such as affine \(F\), or convex component functions together with coordinatewise monotonicity of \(h\) on the relevant range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-outer problem composes a proper closed convex outer function with an inner map; the resulting objective need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)=h(F(x)),\qquad h\text{ convex};\quad f\text{ need not be convex without an additional composition rule}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Outer Composite Regime
Convex Outer Compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite objectives with a convex, possibly nonsmooth outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-outer composite objective has the form \[f(x)=h(F(x)),\] where \(F:X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) is an inner mapping and \(h:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a set containing \(F(X)\). Convexity of \(h\) supplies supporting affine minorants \(h(z')\geq h(z)+v^{\mathsf T}(z'-z)\) for \(v\in\partial h(z)\). It does not, without additional composition rules, imply that \(h\circ F\) is convex in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-outer composite applies a proper closed convex function to an inner map; the full objective need not itself be convex.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=h\circ F\), and every \(v\in\partial h(z)\) defines a supporting affine minorant of \(h\).

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of h at z.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes convexity of the outer function from convexity of the composite, but the record has no supporting source.

children.title: Nonconvex Outer Compositions
children.top_down_role: Composite derivative-free problems with nonconvex outer structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer Nonconvexity May Disappear on the Attained Range
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range boundary for composition-relevant nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h(z)=-z^2 and F(x)=0. Then h is globally nonconvex, while (h\circ F)(x)=0 is constant and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global outer nonconvexity can be irrelevant when the inner range is a single point.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer Nonconvexity May Disappear on the Attained Range

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Obstruction to importing convex-outer model arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For h(z)=-z^2, the tangent \ell_{z_0}(z)=-z_0^2-2z_0(z-z_0) satisfies h(z)-\ell_{z_0}(z)=-(z-z_0)^2\leq0. It is an upper support rather than a global affine minorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex outer function need not provide convex supporting minorants.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Supporting Minorants

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order representation in the smooth subregime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If F and h are continuously differentiable near x and F(x), then \nabla(h\circ F)(x)=F'(x)^\mathsf T\nabla h(F(x)); convexity of h is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordinary chain rule remains exact for a smooth nonconvex outer function.
assumptions_latex: F is continuously differentiable near x.
h is continuously differentiable near F(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Nonconvex Outer Chain Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized first-order representation for a locally Lipschitz outer function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If F is strictly differentiable at x and h is locally Lipschitz near F(x), then \partial_C(h\circ F)(x)\subseteq F'(x)^\mathsf T\partial_C h(F(x)). Equality requires additional regularity and qualification conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally Lipschitz nonconvex outer function, Clarke calculus generally gives an inclusion rather than automatic equality.
assumptions_latex: F is strictly differentiable at x.
h is locally Lipschitz near F(x).
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Composite Chain-Rule Inclusion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Clarke-stationarity test in a regular nonconvex-outer subregime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose F is continuously differentiable near x, F'(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p is surjective, and h is locally Lipschitz and Clarke regular at F(x). Then \[\partial_C(h\circ F)(x)=F'(x)^\mathsf T\partial_C h(F(x)),\] and hence \[0\in\partial_C(h\circ F)(x)\iff\exists v\in\partial_C h(F(x)):\ F'(x)^\mathsf Tv=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Clarke regularity and a surjective inner derivative, composite stationarity is exactly an adjoint outer-subgradient condition.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is locally Lipschitz and Clarke regular at \(F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Submersion Chain-Rule Stationarity Equivalence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient-domain definition that classifies the outer mapping without asserting nonconvexity of the composite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(F:X\to D\subseteq\mathbb R^p\), and let \(D\) be a specified convex modeling domain. A nonconvex-outer composite has the form \(f=h\circ F\), where \(h:D\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and is not convex on \(D\); equivalently, there exist \(z_0,z_1\in D\) and \(t\in(0,1)\) such that \(h((1-t)z_0+tz_1)>(1-t)h(z_0)+th(z_1)\). This classifies \(h\), and does not imply that \(h\circ F\) is nonconvex on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex-outer composite uses an outer function that violates convexity on a declared convex modeling domain containing the inner range; the resulting composite may nevertheless be convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h\text{ is nonconvex on }D,\qquad h\text{ nonconvex does not imply }h\circ F\text{ nonconvex}.

notation.meaning: declared convex modeling domain for the outer function

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex-Outer Composite Regime
Nonconvex Outer Compositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite objectives whose outer mapping lacks convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonconvex-outer composite objective has the form \(f(x)=h(F(x))\), where \(F:X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) and the proper outer function \(h:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is nonconvex on a set intersecting \(F(X)\). If \(h\) is locally Lipschitz and \(F\) is continuously differentiable, generalized first-order analysis may use the Clarke inclusion \[\partial_C(h\circ F)(x)\subseteq F'(x)^{\mathsf T}\partial_C h(F(x)),\] with equality requiring additional regularity. Convex supporting-minorant arguments are therefore unavailable in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex-outer composite has a nonconvex outer mapping; generalized chain rules may be inclusions, and convex minorant arguments generally fail.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable near the point considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C(h\circ F)(x)\subseteq F'(x)^{\mathsf T}\partial_C h(F(x))\), subject to the stated local hypotheses.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Clarke inclusion requires authoritative support, and saying that h is nonconvex on a set merely intersecting F(X) does not ensure nonconvexity on the composition-relevant range.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed range-sensitive refinement of outer nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For R=F(X), call h composition-relevantly nonconvex on R if there exist z_0,z_1,z_t\in R with z_t=(1-t)z_0+tz_1, t\in(0,1), and h(z_t)>(1-t)h(z_0)+th(z_1).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal calls outer nonconvexity relevant when an attained chord violates convexity entirely on the attained range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h|_R\text{ contains a violated convexity chord whose interpolation point also lies in }R.

notation.meaning: attained range of the inner mapping

knowledge_statements.title: Composition-Relevant Outer Nonconvexity

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns nonconvex-outer smooth and Clarke calculus, qualified stationarity, loss of convex supports, and the attained-range caveat. Its definition remains unresolved, so expansion is required. Convex-outer duality and composition algorithms were excluded.

children.title: Outer-Composition Regime Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural transitions affecting treatment of the outer composition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary principle showing that only outer-function values on the attained inner range determine the composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R=F(X). If h_1(z)=h_2(z) for every z\in R, then \[h_1(F(x))=h_2(F(x))\qquad\forall x\in X.\] Consequently, behavior of either outer function outside R cannot change the composite objective on X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer functions agreeing on the attained inner range define the same composite, regardless of their behavior elsewhere.

notation.meaning: attained range of the inner map

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Equivalence Principle for Outer Compositions
Outer-Composition Regime Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of transferring convexity or stationarity through composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Outer convexity alone neither makes the composite convex nor validates an unrestricted stationarity chain rule. For example, \(h(z)=z\) is convex, but with \(F(x)=-x^2\), the composite \((h\circ F)(x)=-x^2\) is nonconvex. Conversely, a nonconvex outer function need not produce a nonconvex restricted composite: \(h(z)=-z^2\) and \(F(x)=0\) give the convex constant function \(h(F(x))=0\). Thus the regime is determined jointly by the outer function, the inner mapping, its range, and the regularity conditions needed for the applicable generalized chain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity of the outer function is neither sufficient nor necessary for convexity of a particular composite; the inner map and its range matter.
assumptions_latex: The compositions are finite on their stated domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outer-function convexity alone does not determine convexity or stationarity properties of \(h\circ F\).

notation.meaning: Composition of outer function h with inner mapping F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convexity counterexamples correctly illustrate the regime boundary, but the broader stationarity-chain-rule claim is uncited and not established by those examples.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Convex DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected coordinate finite-difference method with exact deterministic values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and value-accessible. Given \(x_0\in X\), stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), and radii \(\delta_k>0\), evaluate feasible coordinate perturbations and form \((g_k)_i=(f(x_k+\delta_ke_i)-f(x_k))/\delta_k\) whenever both points lie in \(X\), using an admissible one-sided alternative at the boundary. Update \[x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kg_k).\] Stop when the evaluation budget is exhausted or a finite-difference stationarity measure is below tolerance, and return the best evaluated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic convex DFO method estimates coordinate derivatives from exact function values and takes projected descent steps.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and evaluated without random noise.
Required coordinate perturbations or boundary alternatives are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kg_k)\), with output chosen from evaluated iterates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits deterministic convex DFO, but the boundary finite-difference rule and stationarity measure are not defined precisely enough without a cited method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Infeasibility of Symmetric Coordinate Differences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed objection to a coordinate-difference variant on a constrained domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For X=[0,\infty)\subset\mathbb R and x=0, the symmetric difference \[\frac{f(x+\delta)-f(x-\delta)}{2\delta}\] is unavailable from an oracle defined only on X because x-\delta\notin X for every \delta>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Central differences are unavailable at this boundary unless the oracle extends outside the feasible set or a feasible alternative is specified.
assumptions_latex: The value oracle is defined only on \(X=[0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x-\delta\notin X,\quad\text{so the symmetric difference is unavailable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Infeasibility of Symmetric Coordinate Differences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed smooth finite-difference fact not specific to convexity-exploiting DFO.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R have an L-Lipschitz gradient and define (g_\delta(x))_i=(f(x+\delta e_i)-f(x))/\delta. Then \[|(g_\delta(x))_i-\nabla_i f(x)|\leq\frac{L\delta}{2},\qquad\|g_\delta(x)-\nabla f(x)\|_2\leq\frac{\sqrt nL\delta}{2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward coordinate differences approximate a Lipschitz gradient with error linear in the sampling radius.
assumptions_latex: Every \(x+\delta e_i\) lies in the oracle domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Coordinate-Difference Error Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information assumptions required by stochastic convex zeroth-order guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mathbb E[F(x,\xi)]\ne f(x)\), the expected difference estimator targets the smoothing of the oracle mean rather than \(f\). If \(\mathbb E\|G_k\|^2=\infty\), the finite-second-moment projected bound does not apply. Without any condition linking response distributions to \(f\), distinct convex objectives can produce identical observations, so their distinct minimizers are not uniformly identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uncontrolled oracle bias or noise invalidates the standard guarantee and may make the minimizer unidentifiable.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm observes only oracle responses at its queried points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A uniform guarantee requires an explicit oracle-mean relation and suitable moment control.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Bias and Moment Boundaries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gaussian Smoothing and Stochastic Two-Point Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian smoothing identity for a pointwise-unbiased stochastic value oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\sim N(0,I_n)\) and \(f_\delta(x)=\mathbb E_u[f(x+\delta u)]\). Whenever the expectations and differentiation are well defined, \[\nabla f_\delta(x)=\frac1\delta\mathbb E_u[(f(x+\delta u)-f(x))u].\] If \(\mathbb E_\xi F(x,\xi)=f(x)\), then \[G_\delta(x;u,\xi)=\frac{F(x+\delta u,\xi)-F(x,\xi)}{\delta}u\] satisfies \(\mathbb E[G_\delta(x;u,\xi)]=\nabla f_\delta(x)\). Convexity of \(f\) implies convexity of \(f_\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic Gaussian two-point estimator is unbiased for the gradient of the smoothed objective, not generally for the original objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f_\delta\) is finite and differentiable at the query point.
The required expectations are integrable and differentiation may be interchanged with expectation.
The stochastic oracle is pointwise unbiased.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Smoothing and Stochastic Two-Point Gradients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected convex objective-gap bound separating stochastic optimization and smoothing errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be closed and convex with diameter at most \(D\), let \(x_*\in\arg\min_X f\), and suppose \(\sup_{x\in X}|f_\delta(x)-f(x)|\le b_\delta\). For \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\alpha_kG_k)\), assume \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid x_k]=\nabla f_\delta(x_k)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|G_k\|^2\mid x_k]\le G^2\). Then, for \(\bar x_T=(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_kx_k)/(\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k)\), \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_T)]-f(x_*)\le\frac{D^2+G^2\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k^2}{2\sum_{k<T}\alpha_k}+2b_\delta.\] In particular, constant steps \(\alpha_k=D/(G\sqrt T)\) give \(DG/\sqrt T+2b_\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected averaging converges at the stochastic convex rate up to the smoothing bias.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and has diameter at most \(D\).
The estimator is conditionally unbiased for \(f_\delta\) and has bounded conditional second moment.
The smoothing error is uniformly bounded on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Stochastic Zeroth-Order Error Bound
Stochastic Convex DFO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point Gaussian smoothing with a stochastic value oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic convex DFO estimates a smoothed gradient from two noisy values in a random direction, projects each update, and averages iterates.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[F(x,\xi)]\) is finite and convex on a neighborhood of \(X\).
The paired oracle values have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns the weighted projected-iterate average \(\bar x_T\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-point common-sample Gaussian estimator and projected averaging scheme fit stochastic convex DFO, but their exact oracle assumptions and algorithmic form require a specific source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-convexity objective-gap certificate accounting for finite-difference error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For differentiable \(\mu\)-strongly convex \(f\), suppose a zeroth-order surrogate satisfies \(\|g(x)-\nabla f(x)\|\le\eta\). Then \[f(x)-f_*\le\frac{\|\nabla f(x)\|^2}{2\mu}\le\frac{(\|g(x)\|+\eta)^2}{2\mu}.\] Thus \(\|g(x)\|+\eta\le\sqrt{2\mu\varepsilon}\) certifies \(f(x)-f_*\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small surrogate gradient certifies objective accuracy only after its approximation error is included.
assumptions_latex: A valid bound \(\eta\) on the surrogate-gradient error is available.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate-Gradient Accuracy Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Forward-Difference Radius Produces an Error Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quadratic boundary for coordinate forward differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac\mu2\|x\|^2\), the coordinate forward-difference surrogate of radius \(\delta>0\) is \(g_\delta(x)=\mu x+(\mu\delta/2)\mathbf1\). Its zero is \(x_\delta=-(\delta/2)\mathbf1\), while \(x_*=0\), and \[f(x_\delta)-f(x_*)=\frac{n\mu\delta^2}{8}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed one-sided difference radius shifts the stationary point and prevents arbitrary accuracy even with exact values.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Forward-Difference Radius Produces an Error Floor

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact-Gradient Linear Convergence to an Error Floor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex convergence with uniformly bounded zeroth-order gradient error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient. If \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)+e_k\), \(\|e_k\|\le\eta\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-g_k/L\), then \[f(x_{k+1})-f_*\le\left(1-\frac\mu L\right)(f(x_k)-f_*)+\frac{\eta^2}{2L},\] and hence \[f(x_k)-f_*\le\left(1-\frac\mu L\right)^k(f(x_0)-f_*)+\frac{\eta^2}{2\mu}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity gives geometric convergence until the zeroth-order gradient error creates a nonzero floor.
assumptions_latex: The gradient-surrogate error is uniformly bounded by \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Gradient Linear Convergence to an Error Floor
Strongly Convex Zeroth-Order Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-value coordinate finite differences for smooth strongly convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and suppose exact values are available. Use forward coordinate differences of radius \(\delta\) and gradient steps of size \(1/L\). Since each coordinate error is at most \(L\delta/2\), choosing \(\delta\leq\sqrt{8\mu\varepsilon}/(L\sqrt n)\) makes the limiting function-error contribution at most \(\varepsilon\). Up to universal constants, \[N=O\!\left(n\frac{L}{\mu}\log\frac{f(x_0)-f(x_*)}{\varepsilon}\right)\] value evaluations suffice to obtain an iterate with function error of order \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact coordinate finite differences attain logarithmic accuracy dependence for smooth strongly convex objectives, with a linear dimension factor in value evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable, \(\mu\)-strongly convex, and has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N=O\!\left(n(L/\mu)\log((f(x_0)-f(x_*))/\varepsilon)\right)\) evaluations achieve function error of order \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf and the scaling is plausible, but the bias floor, radius constant, and evaluation bound require an authoritative theorem or derivation source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for an approximate lower-level response when the lower value is known or bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)=\inf_{z\in Y}f(x,z)\). A feasible \(y\in Y\) is \(\delta\)-optimal exactly when \(f(x,y)-v(x)\le\delta\). If \(\ell(x)\le v(x)\), then \(f(x,y)-\ell(x)\le\delta\) is a sufficient certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-level objective gap certifies response accuracy; a valid lower bound yields a conservative certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(x)\le v(x)\) when the lower-bound form is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Response Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by nonunique, unstable, or absent lower-level solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Continuity of \(F\) and \(f\) alone does not ensure continuity of a selection \(y(x)\in S(x)\) or of the optimistic and pessimistic upper values. If minimizers switch or \(S(x)\) becomes empty, a single-valued nested oracle can jump or be undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonunique or disappearing lower solution can make the induced upper oracle discontinuous or undefined even when the original objectives are continuous.
assumptions_latex: No uniqueness, existence, or stability assumption is imposed on \(S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Response-Selection Discontinuity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical response-selection conventions for nonunique lower solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(S(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}f(x,y)\), define \[\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}(x)=\inf_{y\in S(x)}F(x,y),\qquad \Phi_{\mathrm{pes}}(x)=\sup_{y\in S(x)}F(x,y).\] They coincide if \(S(x)\) is a singleton or \(F(x,\cdot)\) is constant on \(S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimistic selection uses the best lower minimizer for the leader, whereas pessimistic selection uses the worst.
assumptions_latex: The displayed extended-real values are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_{\mathrm{opt}}(x)\le\Phi_{\mathrm{pes}}(x)\), with equality under the stated conditions.

notation.meaning: Optimistic and pessimistic upper value functions.

Bilevel Black-Box Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-free interface for nested optimization with an implicitly selected lower-level response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(F:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be accessible only through function evaluations. Define \(S(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y}f(x,y)\). The optimistic bilevel black-box problem is \[\min_{x\in X,\,y\in S(x)}F(x,y).\] An admissible interface supplies queried values of \(F(x,y)\) and \(f(x,y)\), feasibility decisions for \(X\) and \(Y\), and a declared rule for handling an empty or non-singleton set \(S(x)\); it supplies no derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bilevel black-box interface minimizes an upper objective subject to lower-level optimality, using only evaluations, feasibility checks, and an explicit response-selection convention.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted query returns finite objective values or a declared evaluation failure.
The optimistic convention is used when \(S(x)\) is non-singleton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{minimize}_{x\in X,\,y\in S(x)}F(x,y)\) is specified using zeroth-order access only.

notation.meaning: set of lower-level minimizers at upper decision x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct nested solution approach for the continuous bilevel approximation BP2
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation-specific nested approach for the natural-gas cash-out bilevel approximation, including its simplification and stated failure boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After initialization, iterate between selecting an upper-level vector $x\in\mathbb{X}$, for example with a nongradient nonlinear optimization method, and evaluating the upper-level objective by minimizing the lower-level problem parameterized by $x$. For the stated TSO formulation, fixing $x^I$ makes constraints (6.2d)--(6.2h) linear when the lower-level problem is considered. The approach may nevertheless select an upper-level vector that leaves the TSO feasible region empty, and nonconvexity of the upper-level objective together with disconnectedness of the feasible region may lead only to a local optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After initialization, alternate between choosing an upper-level vector, for example with a nongradient nonlinear optimization method, and evaluating its upper-level objective by minimizing the lower-level problem with that vector fixed. In the stated TSO formulation, fixing the designated upper-level components makes the listed logical constraints linear. The selected vector may leave the TSO problem infeasible, and nonconvexity and disconnectedness can lead to only a local optimum.
assumptions_latex: \text{The problem is the continuous bilevel approximation BP2.}
\text{The lower-level problem is parameterized by the selected }x.
\text{The linearity observation is specific to constraints (6.2d)--(6.2h) with }x^I\text{ fixed.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The direct nested procedure supplies objective evaluations but has no stated guarantee of feasibility or global optimality.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case certificate for uncertain black-box constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_j(x,u)\le0\) for all \(u\in U\), define \(G_j(x)=\sup_{u\in U}g_j(x,u)\). Then \(x\) is robustly feasible exactly when \(G_j(x)\le0\) for all \(j\). Certified upper bounds \(\widehat G_j(x)\ge G_j(x)\) with \(\widehat G_j(x)\le0\) are sufficient certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case constraint values characterize robust feasibility, and certified upper bounds can verify it.
assumptions_latex: Each supremum is well defined in the extended real line.
\(\widehat G_j(x)\ge G_j(x)\) when an upper bound is used.

notation.meaning: Worst-case value of uncertain constraint j.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Feasibility Margin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between sampled performance and robustness over the full uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U_k\subset U\), \(\max_{u\in U_k}f(x,u)\le\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). Thus performance or feasibility on \(U_k\) alone does not certify robustness on \(U\) unless the sample exhausts a finite set or a valid bound covers the unsampled supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passing sampled scenarios is not a full robust guarantee without exhaustive coverage or a bound on unsampled scenarios.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Sampling Certification Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent robust formulation for a finite prescribed uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(U=\{u_1,\ldots,u_m\}\), then \[\inf_{x\in X}\max_i f(x,u_i)=\inf_{x\in X,t}\{t:f(x,u_i)\le t,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many prescribed scenarios, robust optimization has an equivalent epigraph formulation with one bound per scenario.

notation.meaning: Upper bound on every prescribed scenario value.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Scenario Robust Epigraph
Robust Black-Box Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static robust optimization over a prescribed uncertainty set with zeroth-order objective access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a decision set, let \(U\) be a nonempty uncertainty set, and let \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb{R}\) be evaluable but derivative information unavailable. Define the robust value \(\phi(x):=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). Robust black-box optimization is the problem \[\inf_{x\in X}\phi(x)=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u).\] A point \(x_\varepsilon\in X\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-robust solution when \(\phi(x_\varepsilon)\leq\inf_{x\in X}\phi(x)+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust black-box optimization chooses a decision minimizing its worst objective value over a fixed uncertainty set, using function evaluations without derivatives.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x,u)\) can be queried for feasible pairs \((x,u)\).
The robust value \(\phi(x)\) is well defined in the extended real line.

children.title: Minimax Black-Box Optimization
children.top_down_role: Derivative-free optimization of worst-case inner responses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for replacing the supremum by sampled responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every finite \(Y_k\subseteq Y\), \(\max_{y\in Y_k}L(x,y)\le\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y)\). Consequently, sampled responses alone cannot certify the worst payoff unless a valid bound controls \(\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y)-\max_{y\in Y_k}L(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite response sample can underestimate the adversary; a certified inner gap is needed for a worst-case guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Unverified Inner Maximization Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function and epigraph forms for finitely many adversarial responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_m\}\), then \[\phi(x)=\max_{1\le i\le m}L(x,y_i)\] and \[\inf_{x\in X}\phi(x)=\inf_{x\in X,t}\{t:L(x,y_i)\le t,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Even when every \(L(\cdot,y_i)\) is smooth, \(\phi\) can be nonsmooth at response ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite adversary gives a pointwise maximum and an equivalent epigraph problem; ties can create nonsmoothness.

notation.meaning: Epigraph bound on all adversarial payoffs.

Minimax Black-Box Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-player worst-response formulation with derivative-free access to the payoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be nonempty strategy sets, and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be available through evaluations only. Minimax black-box optimization computes or approximates \[v_{\min\max}:=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y).\] A pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\in X\times Y\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-saddle pair when \[L(\bar x,y)-\varepsilon\leq L(\bar x,\bar y)\leq L(x,\bar y)+\varepsilon\] for every \(x\in X\) and \(y\in Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimax black-box optimization minimizes the largest payoff selected by an opposing response; an approximate saddle pair satisfies both unilateral optimality inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible payoff query returns \(L(x,y)\) or a declared failure.
No derivative oracle for \(L\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The target value is \(v_{\min\max}=\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{y\in Y}L(x,y)\).

children.title: Uncertainty-Set Versus Adversarial Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural distinctions between uncertainty-set robustness and adversarial inner optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier and information distinction between fixed uncertainty and adaptive adversarial policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A static robust model quantifies over a prescribed set \(U\). A sequential adversary may instead choose a nonanticipative policy \(\pi\in\Pi\). Replacing policies by open-loop uncertainty trajectories preserves the formulation only when the attainable response sets and information restrictions coincide for every outer decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static uncertainty and adaptive adversarial policies coincide only when they generate the same feasible responses under the same information rules.
assumptions_latex: The regimes use the same outer decisions and payoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Equal attainable responses and identical timing/information rules are required for equivalence.}
knowledge_statements.title: Open-Loop Versus Adaptive Response Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating worst-case suprema from probabilistic risk criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an essentially bounded random payoff \(Z=f(x,U)\), \(\mathbb E[Z]\le\operatorname{ess\,sup}Z\), generally strictly. Expectations, quantiles, and finite-level conditional value at risk therefore do not generally equal \(\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\); substituting them changes the criterion unless equality holds on the relevant payoff family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected-value and finite-risk optimization are not generally equivalent to worst-case robustness.
assumptions_latex: The selected probabilistic risk functional is well defined.
The expectation comparison assumes \(Z\) is integrable and essentially bounded above.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho(f(x,U))=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\text{ is required to preserve the worst-case criterion}.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Aggregation Non-Equivalence
Uncertainty-Set Versus Adversarial Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence boundary between static robust uncertainty and strategic minimax response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty sets \(X\) and \(U\) and a payoff \(f:X\times U\to\mathbb{R}\), a static robust problem and a minimax game share the expression \[\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\] when the adversary may select any \(u\in U\) after observing \(x\), with the same feasibility and information rules. The interpretations cease to be equivalent if the adversary has a decision-dependent strategy set \(U(x)\), is restricted by nonanticipativity or information constraints, or randomizes under a criterion not represented by the displayed supremum.

assumptions_latex: The uncertainty set \(U\) is independent of \(x\).
Both regimes use the same payoff \(f\) and response timing.
The inner criterion is the pointwise supremum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:\mathbb R^r\to T_xM\) be a linear isomorphism. A finite set \(D\subset T_xM\) positively spans \(T_xM\) if and only if \(Q^{-1}D\) positively spans \(\mathbb R^r\).

Manifold Direct-Search Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retraction-based direct search on a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Riemannian manifold \(M\), an objective \(f:M\to\mathbb{R}\) available only by evaluation, an initial point \(x_0\in M\), and step size \(\alpha_0>0\), iteration \(k\) selects a finite positive-spanning set \(D_k\subset T_{x_k}M\). It evaluates trial points \(R_{x_k}(\alpha_k d)\) for \(d\in D_k\), where \(R\) is a retraction. If some trial point sufficiently decreases \(f\), accept one as \(x_{k+1}\) and retain or enlarge \(\alpha_k\); otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and reduce \(\alpha_k\). Stop when the prescribed evaluation budget or step tolerance is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Manifold direct search evaluates retracted tangent-space polling directions, accepts sufficient decrease, and reduces the step after an unsuccessful poll.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the last accepted point \(x_k\in M\) at termination.

A differentiable model \(m:T_xM\to\mathbb R\) is \((\kappa_f,\kappa_g)\)-fully linear on \(B_x(0,\Delta)\) when, for every \(\|s\|_x\le\Delta\), \[|\widehat f_x(s)-m(s)|\le\kappa_f\Delta^2,\qquad \|\operatorname{grad}\widehat f_x(s)-\operatorname{grad}m(s)\|_x\le\kappa_g\Delta.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Function-Evaluation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case evaluation count for a deterministic zeroth-order algorithm and a fixed accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of objectives, let \(A\) be a deterministic algorithm whose only objective oracle returns exact values \(f(x)\), and let \(C_\varepsilon(f,x)\) denote a prescribed \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy certificate. For \(f\in\mathcal F\), let \(T_A(f,\varepsilon)\) be the number of oracle calls made before \(A\) first outputs \(x\) satisfying \(C_\varepsilon(f,x)\). The deterministic function-evaluation complexity is \[N_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal F):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}T_A(f,\varepsilon).\] Repeated evaluations are counted separately, and unsuccessful or rejected trial evaluations are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic function-evaluation complexity is the worst-case number of exact value-oracle calls required to produce a point satisfying a specified accuracy certificate.
assumptions_latex: The certificate \(C_\varepsilon\) and function class \(\mathcal F\) are fixed.

notation.meaning: evaluations used on objective f before certification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected and High-Probability Randomized Query Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Class-uniform query accounting for a zeroth-order algorithm with internal randomness and a fixed oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) denote the internal randomness of a zeroth-order algorithm \(A\), and let \(T_A(f,\varepsilon,U)\in\mathbb N\cup\{+\infty\}\) be its query count until a fixed certificate \(C_\varepsilon\) is attained. Define \[N_A^{\mathrm{exp}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal F)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_U[T_A(f,\varepsilon,U)]\] and, for \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \[N_A^{\mathrm{hp}}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal F)=\inf\{N\in\mathbb N:\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P_U(T_A(f,\varepsilon,U)>N)\leq\delta\}.\] Either quantity may equal \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized query complexity is reported either as a worst-case expected stopping count or as a uniform high-probability query quantile, with the failure probability stated explicitly.
assumptions_latex: The oracle model and unit query cost are fixed.
\(\mathcal F\), \(C_\varepsilon\), and, for the high-probability form, \(\delta\), are fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected and High-Probability Randomized Query Complexity
Randomized Query Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected or high-probability zeroth-order query count for algorithms with internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a randomized zeroth-order algorithm, \(\mathcal F\) a function class, and \(C_\varepsilon(f,x)\) an accuracy certificate. If \(T_A(f,\varepsilon,\omega)\) counts oracle queries until certification under random seed \(\omega\), its expected query complexity is \[N_A^{\mathrm{exp}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal F):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_\omega[T_A(f,\varepsilon,\omega)].\] For failure probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\), its high-probability complexity is the least integer \(N\) such that every \(f\in\mathcal F\) satisfies \(\mathbb P_\omega(T_A(f,\varepsilon,\omega)\leq N)\geq1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized query complexity measures worst-case expected queries, or queries sufficient with prescribed confidence, over the algorithm's internal randomness.
assumptions_latex: The oracle model and the cost of one query are fixed.
\(C_\varepsilon\), \(\mathcal F\), and any failure level \(\delta\) are specified.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected and High-Probability Stochastic Sample Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total observation count for a specified class of stochastic zeroth-order oracle laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\in\mathcal P\) specify an objective and the conditional laws of stochastic oracle observations, and let \(T_A(P,\varepsilon)\in\mathbb N\cup\{+\infty\}\) count individual observations used before algorithm \(A\) attains certificate \(C_\varepsilon\). Define \[S_A^{\mathrm{exp}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal P)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[T_A(P,\varepsilon)]\] and \[S_A^{\mathrm{hp}}(\varepsilon,\delta;\mathcal P)=\inf\{N\in\mathbb N:\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb P_P(T_A(P,\varepsilon)>N)\leq\delta\}.\] A batch containing \(b\) observations increases \(T_A\) by \(b\). Unbiasedness, independence, variance, and tail assumptions are properties of \(\mathcal P\), not consequences of the definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic sample complexity counts individual noisy observations, including every member of a batch, and may be stated in expectation or with uniform high probability over a declared oracle-law class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) specifies the objective-oracle laws and all dependence or noise restrictions.
The certificate \(C_\varepsilon\) and unit cost per observation are fixed.
review_flags: Corrects the deferred seed by not treating unbiasedness or independence as universal parts of sample-complexity accounting.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected and High-Probability Stochastic Sample Complexity
Stochastic Sample Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of noisy oracle samples required for a probabilistic or expected optimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a stochastic zeroth-order oracle return \(Y(x,\xi)\) with \(\mathbb E[Y(x,\xi)]=f(x)\), and let \(A\) use independent samples unless dependence is explicitly modeled. For a function-distribution class \(\mathcal P\), accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\), and failure probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\), the sample complexity is the least integer \(N\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal P\), the output \(x_N\) after at most \(N\) oracle samples satisfies \[\mathbb P_P\bigl(C_\varepsilon(f,x_N)\bigr)\geq1-\delta.\] Batch size counts multiplicatively: a batch of \(b\) observations costs \(b\) samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic sample complexity counts noisy observations needed to meet a specified optimization certificate with a stated probability, including every observation in each batch.
assumptions_latex: The distribution class \(\mathcal P\) specifies required noise conditions.
Accuracy \(\varepsilon\), failure level \(\delta\), and certificate \(C_\varepsilon\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After at most \(N\) samples, \(\mathbb P_P(C_\varepsilon(f,x_N))\geq1-\delta\) uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P\).

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation complexity for producing an approximately first-order stationary point of a smooth unconstrained objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of continuously differentiable functions \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and let \(A\) access each \(f\) only through function values. Define \(T_A^{(1)}(f,\varepsilon)\) as the number of evaluations before \(A\) returns \(x\) satisfying \(\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\). The first-order stationarity evaluation complexity is \[N_A^{(1)}(\varepsilon;\mathcal F):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}T_A^{(1)}(f,\varepsilon).\] The gradient is used only to state or verify the certificate, not as algorithmic oracle information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order stationarity complexity counts worst-case function evaluations until a derivative-free method returns a point whose gradient norm is at most epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) receives function values but no derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation complexity for approximate second-order stationarity of a twice-differentiable unconstrained objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of twice continuously differentiable functions \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), and let \(A\) use only function evaluations. For tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H>0\), define \(T_A^{(2)}(f,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)\) as the evaluations used before returning \(x\) such that \[\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon_g,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\geq-\varepsilon_H.\] The second-order stationarity complexity is \[N_A^{(2)}(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H;\mathcal F):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}T_A^{(2)}(f,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H).\] Derivatives occur only in the certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each environment parameter \(\theta\), let \[R_T(\theta,\pi)=\mathbb E_\theta^\pi\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(\ell_t(X_t,\theta)-\ell_t(x^*(\theta),\theta)\bigr)\right].\] Whenever this function is measurable and integrable, \[\operatorname{BR}_T(\Pi,\pi)=\int R_T(\theta,\pi)\,\Pi(d\theta).\] Consequently, a uniform bound \(R_T(\theta,\pi)\leq b_T\) implies \(\operatorname{BR}_T(\Pi,\pi)\leq b_T\), whereas a bound for one prior need not imply a uniform bound over \(\theta\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shared Decision Spaces Do Not Give Reverse Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation between informative and uninformative feedback on the same decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be uniform on \(\{0,1\}\), let the action set be \(\{0,1\}\), and let \(\ell(a,\theta)=\mathbf 1\{a\ne\theta\}\), with \(\Theta\) fixed through horizon \(T\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Dimension Variance of a Spherical Direction Estimator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp dimension dependence for a two-call isotropic estimator on an affine objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be uniform on the unit sphere in \(\mathbb R^d\), and for \(f(x)=a^\mathsf Tx+b\) define \[G_h(x)=d\,\frac{f(x+hU)-f(x-hU)}{2h}\,U.\] Then \(\mathbb E[G_h(x)]=a\), \(\mathbb E\|G_h(x)\|^2=d\|a\|^2\), and \[\mathbb E\|G_h(x)-a\|^2=(d-1)\|a\|^2.\] Thus two evaluations remove dimension dependence from the call count but not from estimator variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-call isotropic estimator is unbiased on affine objectives, yet its exact variance grows linearly with ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Dimension Variance of a Spherical Direction Estimator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact ambient-dimension call count for a full coordinate finite-difference gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), the central coordinate estimator \[(g_h(x))_i=\frac{f(x+he_i)-f(x-he_i)}{2h},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d,\] requires \(2d\) function evaluations. If \(f(x)=a^\mathsf Tx+b\), then \(g_h(x)=a=\nabla f(x)\) for every \(h>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full central coordinate gradient costs two evaluations per dimension and is exact on affine objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Central-Difference Call Burden

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Two-Point Query Complexity with Explicit Dimension Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end expected-suboptimality bound isolating ambient dimension for an exact two-query spherical oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty, closed, and convex with diameter at most \(R\), and let \(f(x)=a^{\mathsf T}x+b\) be available exactly on \(\mathbb R^d\). For independent \(U_k\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathbb S^{d-1})\), form \[G_k=d\,\frac{f(x_k+hU_k)-f(x_k-hU_k)}{2h}U_k\] and update \(x_{k+1}=\Pi_X(x_k-\eta G_k)\). If \(a\neq0\), choose \(\eta=R/(\|a\|\sqrt{dN})\) and return \(\bar x_N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}x_k\). Then \[\mathbb E[f(\bar x_N)-f(x^*)]\leq R\|a\|\sqrt{d/N}.\] Hence \(N=O(dR^2\|a\|^2/\varepsilon^2)\) iterations and twice as many exact value queries suffice for expected gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with exactly two calls per iteration, an isotropic zeroth-order method has an end-to-end query bound linear in ambient dimension on affine objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[G_h(x)=\frac{f(x+hU)-f(x)}{h}U.\] Then \(\mathbb{E}[G_h(x)]=\nabla f_h(x)\) for Gaussian smoothing \(f_h(x)=\mathbb{E}[f(x+hU)]\), and the estimator satisfies the representative bound \[\mathbb{E}\|G_h(x)\|^2\leq2(d+4)\|\nabla f(x)\|^2+\frac{h^2L^2}{2}(d+6)^3.\] Thus both stochastic variability and smoothing error introduce dimension-dependent factors into zeroth-order query bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian finite differences incur dimension-dependent second moments, which propagate into the number of oracle calls required for accurate optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Dependence

children.title: Noise-Level Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity variation across oracle-noise magnitudes and noise regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated-query cost under finite variance using a robust mean estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) are independent with common mean \(f(x)\) and variance at most \(\sigma^2\), then a median-of-means estimator \(\widetilde f_m(x)\) can be chosen so that \[\mathbb P\!\left(|\widetilde f_m(x)-f(x)|>t\right)\le\delta\] whenever \[m=O\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2}{t^2}\log\frac1\delta\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite variance still permits quadratic noise-to-tolerance and logarithmic confidence complexity when repeated samples are combined robustly.
assumptions_latex: The observations are independent with a common mean f(x).

notation.meaning: median-of-means estimate of the queried value

review_flags: Universal constants depend on the block-count and median convention.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of the ordinary sample mean when only a variance bound is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) be independent with \(\mathbb EY_i=f(x)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Y_i)\le\sigma^2\). Then \[\mathbb P\!\left(|\overline Y_m-f(x)|>t\right)\le\frac{\sigma^2}{mt^2}.\] Thus \(m\ge\sigma^2/(\delta t^2)\) suffices for the ordinary-mean variance-only certificate. The exponential sample-mean tail in the sub-Gaussian seed does not follow from a variance bound alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With only a variance bound, Chebyshev's certificate for the ordinary average has inverse-delta confidence dependence, although robust estimators can do better.
review_flags: This is a boundary for the ordinary average, not a minimax lower bound for all finite-variance estimators.

assumptions_latex: Each query returns \(Y_i=f(x)+\xi_i\), where the independent noises are mean-zero and \(\sigma^2\)-sub-Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Averaging \(m\geq 2\sigma^2t^{-2}\log(2/\delta)\) repeated evaluations estimates \(f(x)\) within \(t\) with confidence \(1-\delta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies the repeated-query cost of suppressing additive sub-Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\overline{Y}_m=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mY_i\), sub-Gaussian concentration gives \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(|\overline{Y}_m-f(x)|>t\right)\leq2\exp\!\left(-\frac{mt^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).\] Hence it suffices to use \[m\geq\frac{2\sigma^2}{t^2}\log\frac{2}{\delta}\] repeated calls to achieve \(\mathbb{P}(|\overline{Y}_m-f(x)|\leq t)\geq1-\delta\).
