knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under sub-Gaussian noise, repeated-sample complexity scales quadratically with noise-to-accuracy ratio and logarithmically with inverse failure probability.

children.title: Confidence-Level Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity variation across required success probabilities and reliability levels.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic necessity of logarithmic inverse-confidence dependence for one repeated Gaussian estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)\). If \(\widehat\mu\) satisfies \(\mathbb P_\mu(|\widehat\mu-\mu|\le t)\ge1-\delta\) for both \(\mu=-2t\) and \(\mu=2t\), where \(t>0\) and \(0<\delta<1/4\), then \[m\ge \frac{\sigma^2}{8t^2}\log\frac1{4\delta}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even one Gaussian mean estimate requires order log one over the failure probability samples, in addition to the noise-to-tolerance squared factor.
assumptions_latex: The accuracy guarantee holds for both \mu=-2t and \mu=2t.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widehat f_j\) averages \(m\) samples at the \(j\)-th point, then \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(\max_{1\leq j\leq K}|\widehat f_j-f_j|>t\right)\leq2K\exp\!\left(-\frac{mt^2}{2\sigma^2}\right).\] Therefore \[m\geq\frac{2\sigma^2}{t^2}\log\frac{2K}{\delta}\] suffices for simultaneous accuracy with probability at least \(1-\delta\). The total observation count is \(Km\), so raising confidence changes this certificate only through a logarithmic factor.

children.title: Noise-Confidence Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between noise severity and confidence requirements in evaluation complexity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint failure-budget allocation for estimates with different noise scales and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(j=1,\ldots,K\), suppose the samples forming \(\widehat f_j\) have conditionally mean-zero \(\sigma_j^2\)-sub-Gaussian errors. For any \(\delta_j>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{j=1}^K\delta_j\le\delta\), choosing \[m_j=\left\lceil\frac{2\sigma_j^2}{t_j^2}\log\frac{2}{\delta_j}\right\rceil\] ensures \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{j=1}^K\{|\widehat f_j-f_j|\le t_j\}\right)\ge1-\delta.\] Hence \[M=\sum_{j=1}^K m_j\le K+2\sum_{j=1}^K\frac{\sigma_j^2}{t_j^2}\log\frac{2}{\delta_j}.\] Uniform allocation \(\delta_j=\delta/K\) recovers the common \(\log(2K/\delta)\) factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint confidence budget may be split across heterogeneous estimates; each cost scales with its noise-to-tolerance ratio squared and the logarithm of its allocated inverse failure probability.
assumptions_latex: Each estimate uses errors that are conditionally mean-zero and \sigma_j^2-sub-Gaussian relative to the query history.

children.title: Smoothness-Class Dependence
children.top_down_role: Complexity changes across objective regularity and smoothness classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Difference Bias–Noise Balance under Lipschitz Gradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of a one-sided directional estimate on smoothness, step size, and bounded evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(\|u\|=1\), and suppose \(y(z)=f(z)+e(z)\) with \(|e(z)|\le\eta\). For \(h>0\), define \(D_h=[y(x+hu)-y(x)]/h\). Then \[|D_h-\langle\nabla f(x),u\rangle|\le\frac{Lh}{2}+\frac{2\eta}{h}.\] If \(L,\eta>0\), this upper bound is minimized at \(h=2\sqrt{\eta/L}\), where it equals \(2\sqrt{L\eta}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective with bounded value error, decreasing finite-difference bias amplifies noise; the best bound scales as the square root of smoothness times noise.
assumptions_latex: \nabla f is L-Lipschitz near the segment from x to x+hu.
review_flags: The bound describes deterministic bounded evaluation error, not stochastic averaging complexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference Bias–Noise Balance under Lipschitz Gradients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform function-value bias for smoothing a nonsmooth Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be \(M\)-Lipschitz, let \(V\) be supported on the Euclidean unit ball, and define \(f_h(x)=\mathbb E[f(x+hV)]\). Then \[|f_h(x)-f(x)|\le Mh\,\mathbb E\|V\|\le Mh.\] Consequently, if the relevant infima are finite, every \(\varepsilon\)-optimal point of \(f_h\) is \((\varepsilon+2Mh)\)-optimal for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothing an M-Lipschitz objective at radius h changes values by at most Mh and transfers objective accuracy with at most an additional 2Mh loss.
assumptions_latex: The objective infima used in the accuracy statement are finite.
review_flags: This is an approximation property, not an oracle-complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz-Objective Smoothing Bias

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Higher regularity improves directional finite-difference truncation from first to second order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) is twice differentiable and its Hessian is \(\rho\)-Lipschitz on \(\{x+tu:|t|\le h\}\), where \(\|u\|=1\). Then \[C_h=\frac{f(x+hu)-f(x-hu)}{2h}\] satisfies \[|C_h-\langle\nabla f(x),u\rangle|\le\frac{\rho h^2}{6}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz Hessian makes the centered directional difference second-order accurate in its radius.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\nabla^2 f(z)-\nabla^2 f(w)\|\le\rho\|z-w\|\) on the relevant segment.
review_flags: Evaluation noise contributes an additional inverse-radius error term.
knowledge_statements.title: Centered-Difference Improvement under Lipschitz Hessians

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothness Alone Does Not Determine Zeroth-Order Query Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting smoothness-dependent bias formulas as complete oracle-complexity results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fixing only a smoothness class does not determine a minimax zeroth-order query rate. The query complexity can change when the domain, dimension, convexity, accuracy certificate, noise law, allowed queries, or success criterion changes while the same smoothness condition is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothness controls approximation bias, but a query-complexity comparison requires the remaining problem and oracle coordinates to be fixed.
assumptions_latex: Only the smoothness class is fixed; at least one other complexity coordinate is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{smoothness class alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{a unique zeroth-order query-complexity rate}.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness Alone Does Not Determine Zeroth-Order Query Complexity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Finite-Difference Stencil Error under Higher Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional truncation order obtained from stencil moment cancellation and matching regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varphi(t)=f(x+tu)\), \(\|u\|=1\), and suppose \(\varphi\in C^{p+1}([-Rh,Rh])\) with \(\sup_{|t|\le Rh}|\varphi^{(p+1)}(t)|\le M_{p+1}\). If \(c_j\in[-R,R]\) and \(\sum_j a_jc_j^\ell=\mathbf 1_{\{\ell=1\}}\) for \(0\le\ell\le p\), then \[D_h=\frac1h\sum_j a_jf(x+c_jhu)\] satisfies \[|D_h-\langle\nabla f(x),u\rangle|\le\frac{M_{p+1}h^p}{(p+1)!}\sum_j|a_j||c_j|^{p+1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stencil cancelling Taylor terms through degree p has order-p directional-derivative error under a bounded derivative of order p+1.
assumptions_latex: \(h>0\) and every stencil point is in the domain.
The directional restriction has a bounded derivative of order \(p+1\).
The stencil weights satisfy the stated moment equations.
review_flags: Evaluation noise adds an inverse-radius error term, so truncation order alone does not determine oracle complexity.
knowledge_statements.title: General Finite-Difference Stencil Error under Higher Smoothness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-value approximation order for smoothing a possibly nondifferentiable Hölder objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|^\alpha\), where \(\alpha\in(0,1]\). If \(\|V\|\le1\) almost surely and \(f_h(x)=\mathbb E[f(x+hV)]\), then \[|f_h(x)-f(x)|\le Lh^\alpha\mathbb E\|V\|^\alpha\le Lh^\alpha.\] If the relevant infima are finite, \[f(x)-\inf f\le f_h(x)-\inf f_h+2Lh^\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smoothing an alpha-Hölder objective creates function-value bias of order h to the alpha power and transfers objective accuracy with at most twice that bias.
assumptions_latex: The infima used in the accuracy-transfer statement are finite.
review_flags: This approximation result does not determine an end-to-end oracle rate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Centered-Difference Bias–Error Balance under Lipschitz Hessians
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal radius scaling when second-order truncation competes with bounded value error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\nabla^2f\) is \(\rho\)-Lipschitz on \(\{x+tu:|t|\le h\}\), \(\|u\|=1\), and observations satisfy \(y(z)=f(z)+e(z)\) with \(|e(z)|\le\eta\). knowledge_statements.title: Centered-Difference Bias–Error Balance under Lipschitz Hessians

children.title: Convexity-Class Dependence
children.top_down_role: Complexity changes across nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex regimes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong-Convexity Conversion from Objective Error to Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of an objective-gap complexity certificate into point accuracy under strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a convex set \(X\), \(\mu>0\), and \(x^*\) minimizes \(f\) on \(X\), then \[f(x)-f(x^*)\ge\frac\mu2\|x-x^*\|^2.\] Hence \[f(\widehat x)-f(x^*)\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow\|\widehat x-x^*\|\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon/\mu}.\] Convexity without positive curvature gives no uniform conversion of this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts objective-gap accuracy into distance-to-solution accuracy; ordinary convexity alone does not.
assumptions_latex: f is \mu-strongly convex on X with \mu>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Convexity Conversion from Objective Error to Distance
Convexity-Class Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity of minimax zeroth-order complexity under stronger convexity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a function class \(\mathcal F\), let \(N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F)\) be the smallest worst-case number of function-value queries required to return \(\widehat x\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-\inf_X f]\leq\varepsilon\). If \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sc}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cvx}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{gen}}\), representing strongly convex, convex, and unrestricted classes under the same domain and oracle model, then \[N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sc}})\leq N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cvx}})\leq N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{gen}}).\] Thus every complexity certificate must identify its convexity class; a bound proved on a smaller class does not automatically extend to a larger one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimax query complexity cannot increase when the admissible function class is restricted from general to convex or from convex to strongly convex objectives.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and the zeroth-order oracle model are identical for all three classes.
The accuracy criterion is \(\mathbb E[f(\widehat x)-\inf_X f]\leq\varepsilon\).

children.title: Joint Regularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes distinguished by combined smoothness and curvature structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative conversion between objective-gap and gradient-norm accuracy in the smooth strongly convex regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, with minimizer \(x^*\). Then \[2\mu\bigl(f(x)-f(x^*)\bigr)\le\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\le2L\bigl(f(x)-f(x^*)\bigr).\] Consequently, an objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\) implies gradient norm at most \(\sqrt{2L\varepsilon}\), while gradient norm at most \(\eta\) implies objective gap at most \(\eta^2/(2\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth strongly convex objectives, objective-gap and gradient-norm certificates convert into one another using the smoothness and curvature constants.
assumptions_latex: f is differentiable and L-smooth on \mathbb R^d.
x^* is the minimizer of f.
review_flags: The unconstrained-domain assumption is material to using the full gradient as the optimality measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Strongly Convex Certificate Equivalence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificate Equivalence Fails without Positive Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for converting gradient-norm accuracy into objective-gap accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There is no universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that every differentiable convex function with an attained minimum satisfies \(f(x)-f^*\le C\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\). For \(f(t)=t^4\), \[\frac{f(t)-f(0)}{|f'(t)|^2}=\frac{1}{16t^2}\to\infty\quad(t\to0,\ t\ne0).\] Thus the gradient-to-gap conversion supplied by strong convexity does not persist after positive curvature is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strong convexity, small gradient norm need not give a uniform quadratic objective-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Equivalence Fails without Positive Curvature
Joint Regularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A joint indexing of zeroth-order complexity by smoothness and convexity classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_{r,c}(L,\mu;X)\) denote objectives on \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) having smoothness class \(r\) and convexity class \(c\), with regularity constant \(L\) and, when applicable, strong-convexity modulus \(\mu\). A complete zeroth-order complexity assertion is represented as \[N_\varepsilon=N_\varepsilon(r,c,L,\mu,d,\mathsf O,X),\] where \(\mathsf O\) specifies the oracle and noise law. Comparisons between two regimes are valid only after fixing all coordinates except those explicitly varied; neither smoothness nor convexity alone determines the query complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zeroth-order rate belongs to a joint smoothness–convexity regime and must also specify dimension, domain, oracle, noise, and accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is the common feasible domain.

children.top_down_role: Complexity sensitivity to sparse variables, gradients, or active coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle equivalence with an s-dimensional problem when the active coordinate support is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(|S|=s\), be known, let \(X=X_S\times X_{S^c}\), and suppose \(f(x)=g(x_S)\). Under a value oracle, every query to \(g\) is simulated by fixing \(\bar x_{S^c}\in X_{S^c}\) and querying \(f(x_S,\bar x_{S^c})\); conversely, every query to \(f\) returns a value of \(g\). For an accuracy criterion depending only on objective behavior, the minimax query complexities of the two classes are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With known active support, coordinate-sparse zeroth-order optimization is exactly an s-dimensional oracle problem.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=g(x_S)\) for a known support \(S\) of size \(s\).
The oracle returns function values and the accuracy criterion is invariant to inactive coordinates.

notation.meaning: Objective class having the declared active support S.

knowledge_statements.title: Known-Support Dimension Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Sparsity Is Not Rotation Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-dependence boundary for coordinate sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\ge2\), let \(g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be nonconstant, and set \(f(x)=g(x_1)\). If \(Q\) is orthogonal and its first row \(q^{\mathsf T}\) has no zero component, then in coordinates \(y=Qx\) the objective is \(\widetilde f(y)=g(q^{\mathsf T}y)\), which generally depends on every component of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-coordinate-sparse objective can become coordinate-dense after a rotation.
assumptions_latex: Every component of the first row of \(Q\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is one-coordinate sparse, whereas }\widetilde f\text{ generally depends on all }d\text{ coordinates}.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Sparsity Is Not Rotation Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why known-support dimension reduction does not itself give an unknown-support rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal F_s=\bigcup_{|S|\le s}\mathcal F_S\) with the support unavailable to the algorithm, the known-support simulation is not implementable. An \(s\)-dimensional upper bound transfers only when the oracle and algorithm identify the support or employ measurements whose guarantees hold uniformly over all admissible supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown support requires support discovery or uniformly valid sparse measurements; sparsity alone does not transfer a known-support rate.
assumptions_latex: The active support is not supplied to the algorithm.
More than one support is admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_s)\text{ is not upper-bounded by the known-support reduction alone}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Support Overhead Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Sparse Linear Recovery by Value Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unknown-support recovery for an exact sparse linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a(x)=\langle a,x\rangle\) on the Euclidean unit ball, where \(a\ne0\) and \(\|a\|_0\le s\). Choose \(M\in\mathbb R^{2s\times d}\) with unit-norm rows and \(\operatorname{spark}(M)>2s\). Querying \(f_a\) at the rows of \(M\) returns \(y=Ma\), and \(a\) is the unique vector with at most \(s\) nonzeros satisfying \(Mz=y\). Recovering it and returning \(-a/\|a\|\) exactly minimizes \(f_a\) using \(2s\) value queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unknown s-sparse linear objective can be identified and minimized with 2s exact value queries using a full-spark measurement design.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{spark}(M)>2s\) and every row of \(M\) is a feasible query.
Computational recovery cost is not counted as oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_0\le2s\quad\text{for the stated sparse linear class}.

notation.meaning: Smallest number of linearly dependent columns of M.
Number of nonzero coordinates of a.

review_flags: This noiseless information bound does not imply stable or polynomial-time recovery under noise.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Sparse Linear Recovery by Value Queries

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Spark Does Not Give Uniform Noisy Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise boundary for full-spark sparse value measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(\operatorname{spark}(M)>2s\) guarantees noiseless uniqueness for each fixed design but gives no stability constant uniform over full-spark designs. For every \(\kappa>0\), there exists a full-spark design \(M\) and distinct unit \(s\)-sparse vectors \(a,b\) such that \(\|M(a-b)\|<\kappa\). Additive observation error comparable to this separation can therefore confound the two objectives; stable noisy recovery requires a quantitative restricted singular-value or analogous condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full spark ensures noiseless uniqueness but not stability uniform over measurement designs.
assumptions_latex: Only the qualitative full-spark condition is imposed across the design class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{spark}(M)>2s\ \not\Rightarrow\ \text{a positive sparse singular-value lower bound uniform over full-spark designs}.
review_flags: For each fixed finite full-spark matrix the sparse minimum singular value is positive; the failure is lack of a uniform quantitative bound over designs.
knowledge_statements.title: Full Spark Does Not Give Uniform Noisy Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic certificate converting measurement residual into stable sparse recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=Ma+e\), where \(a\) is \(s\)-sparse and \(\|e\|_2\le\delta\). Define \[\gamma_{2s}(M)=\inf\{\|Mv\|_2/\|v\|_2:v\ne0,\ \|v\|_0\le2s\}.\] If \(\gamma_{2s}(M)>0\) and an \(s\)-sparse \(\widehat a\) satisfies \(\|M\widehat a-y\|_2\le\delta\), then \[\|\widehat a-a\|_2\le\frac{2\delta}{\gamma_{2s}(M)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive restricted singular value turns a small measurement residual into a quantitative sparse-recovery error certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(a\) and \(\widehat a\) are each at most \(s\)-sparse.

notation.meaning: minimum gain on nonzero vectors having at most 2s nonzeros

review_flags: The certificate is conditional and does not assert an efficient decoder or an efficient exact computation of the restricted gain.
knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Singular-Value Stability Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable Sparse Recovery by Convex Residual Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-time noisy coefficient recovery under a robust null-space condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=Ma+e\), where \(a\) is \(s\)-sparse and \(\|e\|_2\le\delta\). Compute \[\widehat a\in\arg\min_z\|z\|_1\quad\text{s.t.}\quad\|Mz-y\|_2\le\delta.\] Suppose that for every vector \(v\) and every \(|S|\le s\), \[\|v_S\|_1\le\rho\|v_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Mv\|_2,\qquad 0\le\rho<1.\] Then \[\|\widehat a-a\|_1\le\frac{4\tau}{1-\rho}\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis-pursuit denoising stably recovers an exactly sparse coefficient when the measurement design satisfies a quantitative robust null-space property.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) satisfies the displayed robust null-space property with \(\rho<1\).
The convex program is solved to optimality.

notation.meaning: restriction of v to coordinates in S

review_flags: This coefficient-recovery theorem yields an optimization-gap guarantee only after an additional objective-sensitivity bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Stable Sparse Recovery by Convex Residual Minimization
Sparsity Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax monotonicity for coordinate-dependence classes with bounded active-support size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\leq s\leq d\), let \(\mathcal F_s\) be the class of objectives \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) for which there exist \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(|S|\leq s\), and a function \(g\) such that \(f(x)=g(x_S)\). Let \(N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_s)\) be the minimax number of function-value queries needed to meet a fixed accuracy criterion under a fixed oracle model. Since \(\mathcal F_s\subseteq\mathcal F_{s+1}\subseteq\mathcal F_d\), \[N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_s)\leq N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_{s+1})\leq N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_d).\] This nesting alone does not establish a particular upper bound depending on \(s\); such a bound requires an algorithm and oracle model that exploit the active-coordinate structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For objectives depending on at most s coordinates, enlarging the allowed support cannot reduce minimax query complexity. A specific rate in s additionally requires a method that exploits the active coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The domain, oracle model, function regularity, and accuracy criterion are fixed across the nested classes.

notation.meaning: Restriction of x to coordinates in S.
Minimax function-value query complexity for the coordinate-sparse class.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimax complexity is monotone under inclusion of coordinate-sparse problem classes

children.title: Intrinsic-Dimension Dependence
children.top_down_role: Complexity sensitivity to latent, active-subspace, or manifold dimension.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Ridge Complexity Scales with Intrinsic Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Near-tight deterministic exact-query count for linear optimization on a known intrinsic subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}\) satisfy \(U^\top U=I_k\), let \(X=\{Uz:\|z\|\le1\}\), and consider \(f_a(Uz)=\langle a,z\rangle\) with unknown \(a\in\mathbb R^k\), \(\|a\|=1\), under an exact value oracle. For every deterministic algorithm and every \(\varepsilon<1\), \[N_\varepsilon\ge k-1.\] Querying \(Ue_1,\ldots,Ue_k\) recovers \(a\) and permits the exact minimizer \(-Ua\), so \[k-1\le N_\varepsilon\le N_0\le k.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact deterministic optimization of an unknown linear function on a known k-dimensional subspace needs order k value queries, independently of ambient dimension.
assumptions_latex: The value oracle is exact and the algorithm is deterministic.
review_flags: This deterministic exact-oracle statement does not cover randomized, noisy, manifold, or unknown-subspace regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Ridge Complexity Scales with Intrinsic Dimension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface boundary for intrinsic-dimensional oracle reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f(x)=g(U^\top x)\) on a constrained set \(X\). The standard one-for-one oracle simulation applies only if every requested \(z\in U^\top X\) can be mapped, without counted black-box queries, to some \(x\in X\) satisfying \(U^\top x=z\). Without such a lifting interface, the ridge representation alone implies no query-preserving reduction; any feasibility or lifting queries must be included in the total oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low intrinsic dimension yields a query-preserving reduction only when intrinsic queries can be lifted feasibly without hidden oracle cost.
assumptions_latex: No query-free lifting interface is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=g\circ U^\top\ \text{alone does not imply a one-for-one intrinsic oracle simulation on }X.
knowledge_statements.title: Unavailable Lifting Breaks Query Preservation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic reduction through a known parameterization and lifting interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:Z\to X\) be known, and consider objective pairs satisfying \(f(\phi(z))=g(z)\) for every \(z\in Z\). If \(\phi(z)\) can be evaluated without a counted oracle query and admissible intrinsic outputs can be lifted through \(\phi\), then a value-oracle algorithm for \(g\) is simulated with exactly one query to \(f\) per query to \(g\). Under matching accuracy criteria on \(Z\) and \(\phi(Z)\), \[N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_\phi,\phi(Z))\le N_\varepsilon(\mathcal G,Z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A known query-free latent parameterization transfers an intrinsic-dimensional value-oracle algorithm without additional value queries.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:Z\to X\) is known and query-free to evaluate.

notation.meaning: Known latent parameterization or global manifold chart.

review_flags: Multiple local charts require additional chart-selection and transition accounting.
knowledge_statements.title: Query-Preserving Latent-Parameter Reduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noisy Linear Ridge Recovery in Intrinsic Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian-noise upper bound whose dimension dependence is intrinsic when the active basis is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a(Uz)=\langle a,z\rangle\) on \(\{Uz:\|z\|\le1\}\), where \(U^\top U=I_k\), \(\|a\|=1\), and each query returns \(f_a(x)+\xi\) with independent \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). Query each \(Ue_j\) independently \(r\) times and let \(\widehat a_j\) be the sample mean. Then \(\mathbb E\|\widehat a-a\|\le\sigma\sqrt{k/r}\). Return \(-U\widehat a/\|\widehat a\|\) when \(\widehat a\ne0\), with any fixed feasible fallback when \(\widehat a=0\). The expected objective gap is at most \(2\sigma\sqrt{k/r}\). Thus \(q=kr\) queries give expected gap at most \(\varepsilon\) when \(r\ge4\sigma^2k/\varepsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known intrinsic coordinates permit noisy linear recovery with a query bound depending on k rather than ambient dimension d.
assumptions_latex: Noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\).
Computational cost is excluded from query complexity.

notation.meaning: sample-mean estimate of the intrinsic coefficient

review_flags: This constructive upper bound is not asserted to be minimax optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Linear Ridge Recovery in Intrinsic Coordinates

Intrinsic-Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Query-preserving reduction of a known exact ridge class to its intrinsic domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}\) satisfy \(U^\top U=I_k\), let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and set \(Z=U^\top X\). For a class \(\mathcal G\) of functions on \(Z\), define \(\mathcal F_U=\{g\circ U^\top:g\in\mathcal G\}\). Assume \(U\) is known and that, for every \(z\in Z\), a point \(x(z)\in X\) satisfying \(U^\top x(z)=z\) can be obtained without function-value queries. Then each value query to \(g\) at \(z\) can be simulated by one value query to \(f=g\circ U^\top\) at \(x(z)\), and an output \(z\) can be lifted to \(x(z)\). Under matching accuracy criteria, \[N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F_U,X)\leq N_\varepsilon(\mathcal G,Z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the active subspace is known and projected points can be lifted to the feasible domain, an intrinsic k-dimensional oracle algorithm transfers to the ridge class without additional function-value queries.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) and a query-free lifting map \(x:Z\to X\) with \(U^\top x(z)=z\) are available.
The two problem classes use matching oracle and accuracy conventions.

notation.meaning: Ridge-objective class induced by U and the intrinsic class G.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a known ridge map with an available lifting gives a query-preserving oracle reduction

children.title: Ambient-to-Effective Dimension Gap
children.top_down_role: Regimes where effective structure reduces or fails to reduce ambient-dimensional cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hidden One-Dimensional Direction Requires Ambient Exploration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic exact-oracle separation between hidden and supplied one-dimensional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|\le1\}\) and \(\mathcal F=\{f_{u,s}(x)=s\langle u,x\rangle:\|u\|=1,\ s\in\{-1,1\}\}\). If \(u\) is hidden, every deterministic exact-value algorithm using \(m\le d-2\) queries has some \(f_{u,s}\in\mathcal F\) for which its output \(\widehat x\) satisfies \[f_{u,s}(\widehat x)-\min_Xf_{u,s}=1.\] Therefore error below one requires at least \(d-1\) queries. If \(u\) is supplied, one query at \(u\) identifies \(s\) and yields an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hidden one-dimensional linear objective can require ambient-order deterministic exploration, whereas supplying its active direction reduces exact optimization to one query.
assumptions_latex: d\ge2 and X is the Euclidean unit ball.
The active direction u is hidden in the lower-bound regime.
review_flags: This is a deterministic exact-oracle lower bound and does not establish the corresponding randomized or noisy complexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Hidden One-Dimensional Direction Requires Ambient Exploration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy loss caused by objective variation outside an effective subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=g(U^\top x)+r(x)\) on \(X\), where \(U^\top U=I_k\) and \(\operatorname{osc}_X r:=\sup_Xr-\inf_Xr\le\tau\). If \(\widehat x\in X\) satisfies \[g(U^\top\widehat x)\le\inf_{x\in X}g(U^\top x)+\varepsilon,\] then \[f(\widehat x)-\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\le\varepsilon+\tau.\] No smaller uniform transfer loss follows from the residual-oscillation assumption alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an approximate ridge objective, intrinsic optimization transfers with an additive residual-oscillation loss, which cannot generally be removed without stronger residual structure.
review_flags: This is an accuracy-transfer boundary, not by itself an ambient-dimensional query lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Ridge Residual Limits Effective-Dimension Reduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General known-versus-hidden minimax comparison without undefined subtraction of infinite complexities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix one objective class, domain, oracle law, risk or success criterion, target accuracy \(\varepsilon\), and computational permissions. Let \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hidden}}\) be the admissible algorithms when effective structure is hidden and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{known}}\supseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{hidden}}\) the algorithms receiving that structure as side information. If \(N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{hidden}}\) and \(N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{known}}\) are the corresponding minimax query complexities in \(\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}\), then \[N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{known}}\le N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{hidden}}.\] The ambient-to-effective information gap is this matched-experiment separation; an additive gap \(G_\varepsilon=N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{hidden}}-N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{known}}\) is defined only when both terms are finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supplying effective structure cannot increase minimax query complexity; a numerical gap is meaningful only under otherwise identical experimental conventions.
assumptions_latex: The objective class, domain, oracle, risk, accuracy, and permissions are identical in both regimes
The known-structure algorithm class contains the hidden-structure class
Subtraction is used only when both complexities are finite

notation.meaning: minimax complexity with effective structure supplied
minimax complexity with effective structure hidden

knowledge_statements.title: Matched-Experiment Effective-Structure Information Gap
Ambient-to-Effective Dimension Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additional minimax query cost caused by withholding the active subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the same ridge-objective class, domain, oracle model, and accuracy criterion in two information regimes: in the known-subspace regime the active matrix \(U\in\mathbb R^{d\times k}\) is supplied to the algorithm, while in the hidden-subspace regime it is not. Let their minimax query complexities be \(N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(k,d)\) and \(N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{hidden}}(k,d)\), respectively. Because an algorithm can ignore supplied information, \[N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(k,d)\leq N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{hidden}}(k,d).\] When both quantities are finite, define \[G_\varepsilon(k,d)=N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{hidden}}(k,d)-N_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{known}}(k,d)\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supplying the active subspace cannot increase minimax complexity. When both complexities are finite, their difference measures the extra query cost of discovering the hidden subspace.
assumptions_latex: The two regimes differ only in whether \(U\) is supplied to the algorithm.
Both complexities are finite when \(G_\varepsilon(k,d)\) is defined by subtraction.

notation.meaning: Minimax query complexity when the active subspace is supplied.
Minimax query complexity when the active subspace is hidden.
Finite difference between hidden- and known-subspace complexities.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additional side information cannot increase minimax query complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Oracle Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covering-radius lower bound for deterministic exact-value optimization of Lipschitz objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a deterministic algorithm that makes \(q\) exact function-value queries on \(X=[0,1]^d\) and then returns \(\widehat x\). Let \(T_A\) be the queried points together with \(\widehat x\) on the transcript consisting entirely of zero responses, and define \[r(T_A)=\sup_{x\in X}\inf_{t\in T_A}\lVert x-t\rVert_\infty.\] Over the class \(\operatorname{Lip}_L(X)\) of all real-valued functions that are \(L\)-Lipschitz in \(\ell_\infty\), the worst-case optimization error of \(A\) is at least \[\sup_{f\in\operatorname{Lip}_L(X)}\bigl(f(\widehat x_A)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\bigr)\geq Lr(T_A).\] Therefore an error guarantee of at most \(\varepsilon\) requires \(r(T_A)\leq\varepsilon/L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For deterministic exact-value optimization of arbitrary Lipschitz functions, the worst-case error is at least the Lipschitz constant times the covering radius of the zero-transcript queries and output.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm is deterministic and receives exact function values.

notation.meaning: Queries and output generated by A on the all-zero transcript.
Covering radius of T_A in X under the infinity norm.
Class of L-Lipschitz real-valued objectives on X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of small stochastic transcript divergence into optimization failure probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let objectives \(f_0,f_1\) have disjoint \(\varepsilon\)-solution sets, and let \(P_0,P_1\) be the transcript laws of an arbitrary \(q\)-query algorithm. Every output rule fails to be \(\varepsilon\)-optimal on at least one objective with probability at least \[\frac{1-\|P_0-P_1\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{2}\ge\frac{1-\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_0\|P_1)/2}}{2}.\] Hence a uniform success probability at least \(1-\alpha\), where \(\alpha<1/2\), requires \[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_0\|P_1)\ge2(1-2\alpha)^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two objectives with disjoint valid outputs cannot both be optimized reliably until their stochastic transcripts have constant statistical separation.
assumptions_latex: The two epsilon-solution sets are disjoint.
The same algorithm and query budget define transcript laws \(P_0,P_1\).
review_flags: The KL threshold follows from Pinsker's inequality and is not generally sharp.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Point Testing Lower-Bound Template

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information representation underlying stochastic zeroth-order lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), an adaptive algorithm chooses \(X_t\) from its preceding transcript and observes \(Y_t=f_i(X_t)+\xi_t\), where \(\xi_t\overset{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). If \(P_i^{(q)}\) is the law of the \(q\)-round transcript under \(f_i\), including the algorithm's internal randomness, then \[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_0^{(q)}\|P_1^{(q)})=\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{t=1}^q\mathbb E_0\bigl[(f_0(X_t)-f_1(X_t))^2\bigr].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With Gaussian value noise, adaptive transcript KL divergence is the expected sum of per-query squared mean separations divided by twice the noise variance.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_t\) is measurable with respect to the preceding transcript and internal randomness.
The algorithm uses the same conditional query rule under both objectives.

notation.meaning: Distribution of the adaptive q-query transcript under objective i.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Gaussian Transcript Divergence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-hypothesis stochastic lower-bound mechanism for dimension-dependent zeroth-order complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_M\) have pairwise disjoint \(\varepsilon\)-solution sets, let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,M\}\), and let \(P_j\) be the transcript law of a \(q\)-query algorithm under \(f_j\). If \(\bar P=M^{-1}\sum_jP_j\), every output rule has worst-case \(\varepsilon\)-failure probability at least \[1-\frac{M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_j\|\bar P)+\log2}{\log M}.\] Consequently, success probability at least \(1-\alpha\) on every instance requires average transcript information at least \((1-\alpha)\log M-\log2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A packing of objectives with disjoint solution sets forces transcript information proportional to the logarithm of the packing size.
assumptions_latex: All transcript laws arise from the same adaptive algorithm and query budget.
review_flags: This template requires a concrete hard family and transcript-divergence bound to yield an optimization rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Fano Packing Lower-Bound Template

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stochastic Zeroth-Order Minimax Risk and Query Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Risk convention for lower bounds under adaptive noisy value queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a function class \(\mathcal F\), stochastic value-oracle family \(\{P_f(\cdot\mid x):f\in\mathcal F\}\), and loss \(\ell_f(\widehat x)\ge0\), define the \(q\)-query minimax risk by \[R_q(\mathcal F)=\inf_{A:\,N(A)\le q}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[\ell_f(\widehat x_A)].\] The expected-risk query complexity is \[N_\varepsilon(\mathcal F)=\inf\{q:R_q(\mathcal F)\le\varepsilon\}.\] Under a success-probability convention, replace expected loss by \(\sup_fP_f(\ell_f(\widehat x_A)>\varepsilon)\) and declare the required confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic zeroth-order lower bounds measure the best worst-case risk of any adaptive algorithm using a fixed number of noisy value observations; the loss and confidence convention must be stated.
assumptions_latex: Algorithms may choose each query adaptively from the preceding transcript and internal randomness.
The oracle law, loss, function class, query accounting, and output convention are fixed.

notation.meaning: Number of oracle observations used by algorithm A.
Declared optimization loss on instance f.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Zeroth-Order Minimax Risk and Query Complexity
Stochastic Oracle Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point Gaussian zeroth-order lower bound for shifted strongly convex quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), let \(f_\theta(x)=\frac{\mu}{2}(x-\theta a)^2\), where \(\theta\in\{-1,1\}\), \(0<a\leq1\), and each query returns \(f_\theta(x)+\xi\) with independent \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). For every adaptive algorithm using \(q\) observations and returning \(\widehat x\), the two-point testing bound gives \[\sup_{\theta\in\{-1,1\}}\mathbb E_\theta[f_\theta(\widehat x)-f_\theta(\theta a)]\geq\frac{\mu a^2}{4}\left(1-\frac{\mu a\sqrt q}{\sigma}\right)_+.\] Thus constant-order accuracy \(\mu a^2\) requires order \(\sigma^2/(\mu^2a^2)\) noisy evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinguishing two nearby quadratic minimizers under Gaussian value noise requires quadratically many samples in the inverse signal-to-noise ratio.
assumptions_latex: Oracle noises are independent Gaussian variables with variance \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_\theta\mathbb E_\theta[f_\theta(\widehat x)-f_\theta(\theta a)]\geq\frac{\mu a^2}{4}(1-\mu a\sqrt q/\sigma)_+\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-point Gaussian lower bound is mathematically plausible and the complexity-bound kind fits, but its exact constant and adaptive-testing reduction require an authoritative theorem or section locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential ambient-dimension lower bound for deterministic exact-value optimization of unrestricted Lipschitz functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]^d\) with the \(\ell_\infty\) metric, and let \(0<\varepsilon<L/2\). Any deterministic exact-value algorithm that guarantees \[f(\widehat x)-\min_{x X}f(x)\leq\varepsilon\] for every real-valued \(L\)-Lipschitz function on \(X\) must use at least \[q\geq\left(\frac{L}{2\varepsilon}\right)^d-1\] function-value queries. Thus the worst-case query requirement for this unrestricted class grows exponentially with the ambient dimension \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic exact-value algorithm for all Lipschitz functions on a d-dimensional cube requires at least (L divided by 2 epsilon) to the d, minus one, queries.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm is deterministic and the objective class contains every real-valued \(L\)-Lipschitz function on \(X\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the objective class.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: covering-radius lower bound combined with the volume of infinity-norm balls

children.title: Noise-Floor Impossibility
children.top_down_role: Performance barriers caused by irreducible evaluation noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Floor Impossibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An additive accuracy floor under adversarially bounded function-value errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\), and let an oracle for \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) return \(y(x)=f(x)+e(x)\), where the unknown deterministic error satisfies \(|e(x)|\leq\delta\) for every \(x\in X\). For the objective class containing \(f_+(x)=\delta x\) and \(f_-(x)=-\delta x\), every oracle algorithm, regardless of its number of adaptive queries, has worst-case objective error at least \[\inf_A\sup_{f\in\{f_+,f_-\}}\sup_{e:\,|e|\leq\delta}\bigl(f(\widehat x_A)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\bigr)\geq\delta.\] Hence no uniform guarantee with objective error strictly below \(\delta\) is available in this oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With adversarial value errors bounded by delta, even one-dimensional linear objectives have a minimax objective-error floor of delta.
assumptions_latex: The deterministic error may depend on the query point and objective but obeys \(|e(x)|\leq\delta\).
The guarantee is uniform over the stated objectives and admissible error functions.

notation.meaning: Adversarial deterministic oracle error at x.
The two linear objectives used in the failure boundary.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

children.title: Nonidentifiability Impossibility
children.top_down_role: Performance barriers caused by observationally indistinguishable objectives or solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonidentifiability Impossibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General impossibility criterion based on overlapping oracle response sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each objective \(f\), let \(\mathcal Y_f(x)\) be the set of responses allowed at query \(x\). Suppose two objectives \(f_0,f_1\) satisfy \(\mathcal Y_{f_0}(x)\cap\mathcal Y_{f_1}(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every \(x\in X\), so an adversary can generate an identical transcript under both objectives. If their \(\varepsilon\)-solution sets \(S_i(\varepsilon)=\{x:f_i(x)-\inf_Xf_i\leq\varepsilon\}\) are disjoint, then no algorithm can guarantee an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal output for both. This impossibility persists with arbitrarily many adaptive queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two objectives always permit identical oracle responses but have disjoint epsilon-solution sets, no algorithm can guarantee epsilon-optimality.
assumptions_latex: The oracle may select any response in \(\mathcal Y_f(x)\) at each query.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No oracle algorithm uniformly guarantees \(f(\widehat x)-\inf_Xf\leq\varepsilon\) on \(\{f_0,f_1\}\).

notation.meaning: Set of oracle responses permitted for objective f at x.
Epsilon-optimal solution set of objective i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indistinguishable transcripts cannot support a decision between disjoint valid-output sets
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits and the criterion is valid for a set-valued adversarial oracle whose admissible responses depend only on the objective and query. A source is needed to certify those oracle semantics and the unlimited adaptive-query conclusion.

children.title: Degradation-to-Impossibility Transition
children.top_down_role: Boundaries separating deteriorating guarantees from complete loss of reliable identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Degradation-to-Impossibility Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates perturbative rate degradation from an irreducible oracle-noise floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a zeroth-order method has a robust guarantee \[f(\widehat x_q)-f^*\leq R_q+C\delta,\] where \(R_q\downarrow0\) is its noiseless optimization residual, \(\delta\) is the oracle-error scale, and \(C>0\) is independent of \(q\). For target accuracy \(\varepsilon>C\delta\), it suffices to choose \(q\) so that \(R_q\leq\varepsilon-C\delta\); noise merely degrades the required query count. If the oracle class also contains indistinguishable instances with minimax gap \(c\delta\), then every target \(\varepsilon<c\delta\) is impossible regardless of \(q\). The interval between these thresholds depends on model-specific constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Above the stability penalty, noise increases query cost; below an indistinguishability floor, the requested accuracy is impossible regardless of queries.
assumptions_latex: \(R_q\downarrow0\) and the displayed robust upper bound holds.
The oracle class has an indistinguishable-pair lower bound \(c\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon>C\delta\) is attainable once \(R_q\leq\varepsilon-C\delta\), whereas \(\varepsilon<c\delta\) is unattainable.

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Limitations of derivative-free optimization p. 5

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits and the upper/lower threshold distinction is internally correct. The cited general limitations section has not been shown to support the displayed model with constants C and c, so the record needs a directly aligned source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when polling directions have zero cosine measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(D=\{(1,0),(-1,0)\}\), \(f(x_1,x_2)=-x_2\), and \(x=(0,0)\). For every \(\alpha>0\), \(f(x+\alpha d)=f(x)=0\) for all \(d\in D\), so the poll is unsuccessful with zero forcing, although \(\|\nabla f(x)\|=1\). Here \(\kappa(D)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directions confined to a line can miss a nonzero descent direction, so an unsuccessful nonspanning poll cannot certify stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Polling uses only the displayed directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonspanning Poll Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which unsuccessful-poll bounds become asymptotically exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the unsuccessful-poll bound holds at \((x_k,\alpha_k,D_k)\), with \(\kappa(D_k)\ge\underline\kappa>0\), \(\alpha_k\to0\), and \(\rho(\alpha_k)/\alpha_k\to0\). Then \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\le\underline\kappa^{-1}(\rho(\alpha_k)/\alpha_k+L\alpha_k/2)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly well-spread unsuccessful polls become asymptotically exact certificates when radius and forcing-per-radius vanish.
assumptions_latex: The deferred immutable unsuccessful-poll bound holds for every k.

notation.meaning: Uniform lower bound on polling cosine measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Poll-Certificate Bound
Polling-Based Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gradient certificate obtained from an unsuccessful finite poll at a fixed step size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let \(D\) be a finite set of unit polling directions with cosine measure \(\kappa(D)=\min_{\lVert v\rVert=1}\max_{d\in D}v^\top d>0\). If a poll at \(x\) and radius \(\alpha>0\) is unsuccessful in the sense that \(f(x+\alpha d)\geq f(x)-\rho(\alpha)\) for every \(d\in D\), then \[\lVert\nabla f(x)\rVert\leq\frac{1}{\kappa(D)}\left(\frac{\rho(\alpha)}{\alpha}+\frac{L\alpha}{2}\right).\] Thus the unsuccessful poll is a verifiable approximate-stationarity certificate when its radius and forcing term are small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unsuccessful positive-spanning poll bounds the gradient norm using the poll radius, forcing term, smoothness constant, and directional cosine measure.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz near every polled segment.

notation.meaning: Cosine measure of the polling directions.
Permitted forcing decrease at poll radius alpha.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits, and the displayed stationarity bound is consistent with the descent lemma and the stated cosine-measure convention. An authoritative polling theorem or proposition locator is still required.

notation.meaning: Derivative-free local model centered at the current point.
Gradient of the model at its center.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order certificate from a fully linear trust-region model.

Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, and let \(m(s)=m(0)+g^{\mathsf T}s+	frac12s^{\mathsf T}Hs\), with \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}\), model \(f(x+s)\) on \(\{s\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|s\|\leq\Delta\}\). Suppose validated full linearity gives \(\|

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate second-order stationarity from validated model-gradient and Hessian errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in C^2\) near \(x\), and suppose a model \(m\) centered at \(x\) satisfies \(\|
