knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated fully quadratic errors convert model criticality into an approximate second-order stationarity certificate.
assumptions_latex: The displayed gradient and spectral-norm Hessian error bounds are valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Fully Quadratic Model Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unvalidated Model Criticality Is Not a Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of a true-model gradient-error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x=0\), let \(f(t)=t\) and \(m(t)=0\). Then \(\nabla m(0)=0\) while \(|\nabla f(0)|=1\). Thus a small model gradient certifies true stationarity only when accompanied by a valid model-gradient error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero model gradient can coexist with a nonzero true gradient, so model-accuracy validation is indispensable.
assumptions_latex: No bound relating \(\nabla m(0)\) to \(\nabla f(x)\) is assumed.
knowledge_statements.title: Unvalidated Model Criticality Is Not a Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous-confidence certificate for selecting the smallest mean from finitely many candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be finite and suppose intervals \([L_q,U_q]\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(\forall q\in Q:\mu_q\in[L_q,U_q])\ge1-\alpha\). If \(U_{q_*}<\min_{q\ne q_*}L_q\), then \(q_*\) is the unique minimum-mean candidate on the simultaneous-coverage event, and the probability of issuing this certificate when \(q_*\notin\arg\min_{q\in Q}\mu_q\) is at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate is certified best when its upper confidence bound lies below every competitor's lower bound under simultaneous coverage.
assumptions_latex: The intervals have simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Simultaneous confidence interval for candidate q's mean.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Candidate Selection Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample lower-mean selection under independent sub-Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q\in\{x,z\}\), let independent observations have mean \(\mu_q\) and be \(\sigma_q^2\)-sub-Gaussian. With \(n_q\) observations define \(\widehat\mu_q\) and \(r_q=\sigma_q\sqrt{2\log(4/\alpha)/n_q}\). With probability at least \(1-\alpha\), both means lie in \([\widehat\mu_q-r_q,\widehat\mu_q+r_q]\). Hence \(\widehat\mu_x+r_x<\widehat\mu_z-r_z\) certifies \(\mu_x<\mu_z\) with false-ordering probability at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separated sub-Gaussian confidence intervals certify a pairwise mean ordering at the prescribed error level.
assumptions_latex: The declared sub-Gaussian parameters are valid.

notation.meaning: Sub-Gaussian variance proxy at point q.

knowledge_statements.title: Sub-Gaussian Pairwise Selection Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for repeatedly inspected fixed-sample confidence intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A confidence interval proved to cover at one fixed sample size with probability \(1-\alpha\) does not thereby provide simultaneous coverage over a data-dependent sequence of sample sizes. Stopping at the first separation of ordinary fixed-sample intervals therefore need not retain false-selection probability \(\alpha\); that guarantee requires a confidence sequence, a valid alpha-spending construction, or another justified stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordinary fixed-sample intervals cannot be repeatedly inspected under unrestricted optional stopping while retaining their nominal selection guarantee.
assumptions_latex: The available coverage result is pointwise at a fixed sample size.
The stopping time depends on the observed intervals.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Sample Certificates Under Optional Stopping

assumptions_latex: For each \(q\in\{x,z\}\), the observations \(Y_{q,1},\ldots,Y_{q,n_q}\) are supported in \([a,b]\) and have common mean \(\mu_q\).
All observations used by the certificate are mutually independent.

notation.meaning: Hoeffding confidence radius at point q.
Maximum probability of issuing the stated certificate with the wrong ordering.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct application of simultaneous Hoeffding confidence intervals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample certificate for selecting the lower-mean point under bounded noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For points \(x\) and \(z\), let mutually independent observations \(Y_{q,i}\in[a,b]\), for \(q\in\{x,z\}\) and \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n_q\}\), have common mean \(\mu_q\) within each point. Define \(\widehat\mu_q=n_q^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_q}Y_{q,i}\) and \(r_q=(b-a)\sqrt{\log(4/\alpha)/(2n_q)}\). With probability at least \(1-\alpha\), both means simultaneously satisfy \(\mu_q\in[\widehat\mu_q-r_q,\widehat\mu_q+r_q]\). Consequently, the observed inequality \(\widehat\mu_x+r_x<\widehat\mu_z-r_z\) certifies selection of \(x\), and the probability that this certificate is issued when \(\mu_x\geq\mu_z\) is at most \(\alpha\). If the intervals do not have this ordering, the samples do not provide this certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonoverlapping bounded-noise confidence intervals select x with a false-ordering probability of at most the prescribed level; otherwise they do not certify an ordering.
knowledge_statements.title: Statistical Selection Certificates

children.title: Feasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence used to assess constraint satisfaction or infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Violation Is Not an Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limit of a pointwise constraint-residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x)=0\) hold exactly at feasible points. An observation \(h(x)>\varepsilon\) proves only that the evaluated point is not feasible to tolerance \(\varepsilon\); it does not prove that the feasible set is empty. For example, under the constraint \(x=0\), the point \(x=1\) has positive violation although \(x=0\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive residual rejects the evaluated point but cannot by itself certify global infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(h(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\) is feasible.
Only pointwise constraint information at the reported point is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Violation Is Not an Infeasibility Certificate
Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based certificate for nonlinear equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\leq0\), define the violation measure \(h(x)=\max\{\|c_E(x)\|_\infty,\|[c_I(x)]_+\|_\infty\}\), where the positive part is componentwise. A record containing \(x\), successfully evaluated constraint values, the evaluation context, and the computed residual \(h(x)\) is an \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\)-feasibility certificate precisely when \(h(x)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\). For exact evaluations and zero tolerance, this condition is equivalent to feasibility; for positive tolerance, it certifies only tolerance feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successfully evaluated constraint residuals certify feasibility when the largest equality or positive inequality violation does not exceed the declared tolerance.
assumptions_latex: All constraint values in the record are valid for the stated evaluation context.

notation.meaning: Componentwise positive part of a vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard residual definition for nonlinear constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual predicate is mathematically coherent and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this particular feasibility measure and its use in the DFO feasibility-restoration context.

children.title: Filter Acceptance Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting filter-based acceptance and progress classification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Margin-free predicate underlying biobjective filter acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When both violation \(h\) and objective \(f\) are minimized, \((h^+,f^+)\) is margin-free filter-acceptable relative to \(\mathcal F=\{(h_i,f_i)\}\) exactly when no entry weakly dominates it. Equivalently, \(\bigwedge_i(h^+<h_i\lor f^+<f_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without margins, every stored pair must be strictly improved in at least one of violation or objective.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is a finite set of valid violation-objective pairs.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Filter Acceptability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter Passage Is Not Complete Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between filter acceptability and a complete algorithmic acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_{\mathcal F}(x^+)\) denote filter acceptability and let \(G(x^+)\) collect any additional switching, trust-region, model-agreement, or evaluation-validity guards. If complete acceptance is \(A_{\mathcal F}(x^+)\land G(x^+)\), filter passage alone does not certify complete acceptance unless \(G(x^+)\) is separately verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Passing the filter does not certify complete acceptance when additional guards apply.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm declares at least one acceptance guard in addition to filter acceptability.
knowledge_statements.title: Filter Passage Is Not Complete Step Acceptance
Filter Acceptance Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Biobjective filter certificate using objective and constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=\{(h_i,f_i)\}_{i=1}^N\) be the current filter, with \(h_i\geq0\), and choose \(\gamma_h\in(0,1)\) and \(\gamma_f>0\). A valid trial point \(x^+\) has pair \((h^+,f^+)=(h(x^+),f(x^+))\). Its filter-acceptance certificate is the list of verified disjunctions \(h^+\leq(1-\gamma_h)h_i\) or \(f^+\leq f_i-\gamma_f h_i\), one for every filter entry. The certificate establishes that the trial lies outside every entry's margin-enlarged forbidden region; acceptance may still be subject to separately declared trust-region or switching conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial passes the filter when, relative to every stored entry, it sufficiently improves either constraint violation or objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is finite and contains valid objective-violation pairs.
The trial evaluations \(h^+\) and \(f^+\) are valid.

notation.meaning: Finite set of stored violation-objective pairs.
Constraint violation at the trial point.
Objective value at the trial point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard margin filter acceptance predicate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but the margin-enlarged filter predicate is variant-specific. An authoritative source is needed to confirm the exact inequalities, strictness conventions, and distinction between filter acceptability and complete trial-step acceptance.

children.title: Restoration-Phase Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence governing restoration progress, completion, or failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration-Phase Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate of successful constraint-violation reduction during restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^R\) enter restoration with finite violation \(h_R=h(x^R)>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\), and fix \(\rho\in(0,1)\). A restoration output \(x^+\) carries a success certificate when its constraint evaluation is valid and either \(h(x^+)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) or \(h(x^+)\leq\rho h_R\). The first alternative certifies restoration to the feasibility tolerance; the second certifies quantified restoration progress but not feasibility. If neither inequality holds, the evaluation record is not a successful restoration certificate, regardless of objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restoration step is certified by reaching the feasibility tolerance or reducing violation by the declared factor; objective decrease alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The constraint evaluation at \(x^+\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(x^+)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\;\lor\;h(x^+)\leq\rho h_R\;\Longrightarrow\;x^+\text{ has a successful restoration certificate}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but the disjunction between tolerance feasibility and a fixed contraction is an algorithm-specific restoration success rule. No source establishes this exact variant.

children.title: Cross-Phase Certificate Handoffs
children.top_down_role: Certificate compatibility across optimization, filter, and restoration phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Phase Certificate Handoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-preserving certificate for transfers between optimization and restoration phases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a phase state be \(S=(q,x,\mathcal D,\mathcal F)\), where \(q\in\{O,R\}\) denotes optimization or restoration. A handoff record \(H=(S^-,S^+,r)\) is valid when the incumbent and persistent records are preserved, \(x^+=x^-\), \(\mathcal D^-\subseteq\mathcal D^+\), and \(\mathcal F^+=\mathcal F^-\), and the receiving guard holds. For \(R\to O\), the guard is \(h(x^+)\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\). For \(O\to R\), the guard is \(h(x^+) > \varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\) together with a logged restoration trigger \(r\) from the algorithm's declared trigger set. Thus no phase change is certified without both state continuity and an applicable guard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phase handoff is certified only when persistent state is preserved and the receiving phase's declared feasibility or restoration guard is verified.
assumptions_latex: All retained database and filter records are valid in the unchanged evaluation context.
The restoration-trigger set is fixed before the handoff.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: phase transitions require guard verification and state continuity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed handoff certificate depends on method-specific guards and persistence rules, especially exact preservation of the filter and monotone extension of the database. These are not universal DFO restoration semantics and require an algorithm-specific source.

children.title: DFO Evaluation Management Interface
children.top_down_role: Implementation-facing navigation for sample reuse, concurrency, numerical geometry, diagnostics, and empirical assessment.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

children.title: Sample-Database Organization
children.top_down_role: Organization, indexing, provenance, and retrieval of accumulated sample records.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Database Organization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed representation of reusable derivative-free evaluation records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the sample database as a finite indexed family \(\mathcal D=\{R_j\}_{j=1}^N\), with \(R_j=(x_j,\theta_j,y_j,\sigma_j,t_j,m_j)\). Here \(x_j\) is the requested point, \(\theta_j\) is the evaluation context, \(y_j\) is the returned objective-constraint payload, \(\sigma_j\) is a status, \(t_j\) is provenance, and \(m_j\) is metadata. Define a canonical key \(K(x_j,\theta_j)\) and an index \(I(k)=\{j:K(x_j,\theta_j)=k\}\). Lookup first selects \(I(k)\), then applies compatibility predicates to its records; key equality alone does not assert semantic interchangeability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sample database stores typed evaluation records behind canonical keys, while a separate compatibility test determines whether a keyed record is reusable.
assumptions_latex: The key function \(K\) is deterministic for a fixed database version.
Every record retains its evaluation context and status.

notation.meaning: Index mapping keys to record identifiers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct content kind, but the six-field record, canonical key, and compatibility layer are an implementation design rather than a source-supported standard representation. An inspectable DFO implementation or interface source is required.

children.title: Evaluation Cache Semantics
children.top_down_role: Reuse policies for stored evaluation results across repeated requests.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation Cache Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic validity of deterministic and stochastic cache reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cache query \(Q=(x,\theta,u)\) requests point \(x\), evaluation context \(\theta\), and reuse mode \(u\). A stored record \(R\) is reusable exactly when its status is successful, its canonical key matches, and \(C(R,Q)=1\), where \(C\) checks objective version, constraint version, fidelity, precision, and noise policy. Under deterministic semantics, a reusable payload may replace a new evaluation. Under stochastic semantics, stored observations may update declared sufficient statistics, but a cache hit must not be labeled as a new independent replication. A miss returns no value and authorizes evaluation according to the calling policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A successful cache entry replaces work only under matching evaluation context; stochastic reuse cannot masquerade as a newly independent observation.
assumptions_latex: The query and every record contain explicit evaluation-context metadata.
\(C\) is deterministic within one cache version.
The caller declares deterministic or stochastic reuse semantics.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: deterministic cache hits and stochastic sample reuse have distinct semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role is plausible, and the warning about stochastic independence is sound, but the exact cache-hit predicate and context fields define a particular system policy. No source supports that complete semantic contract.

children.title: Cache Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Validity limits arising from changed environments, fidelity levels, or evaluation contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cache Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete compatibility boundary for reusing a cached evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v=(v_f,v_c,v_K)\) denote objective, constraint, and canonicalization versions, and let \(\theta=(\ell,p,\nu,s)\) denote fidelity, precision, noise policy, and seed policy. A record made at \((x_R,v_R,\theta_R)\) may answer a query at \((x_Q,v_Q,\theta_Q)\) only if \(v_R=v_Q\), \(\ell_R=\ell_Q\), \(p_R\) meets the requested precision, the noise and seed policies permit reuse, and \(x_R\sim_K x_Q\). Crossing any failed predicate is a cache-consistency boundary and forces a miss, re-evaluation, or an explicitly declared approximation; silent reuse is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Version, point identity, fidelity, precision, and noise-policy predicates form the boundary beyond which cached evaluations cannot be silently reused.
assumptions_latex: All versions and evaluation-context fields are recorded.
\(\sim_K\) is the declared canonical point-equivalence relation.
Precision and noise-policy compatibility orders are specified by the evaluator.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cache validity requires versioned semantic compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the leaf, but the record calls the listed predicates a complete compatibility boundary even though the precision and noise orders are evaluator-dependent and other context fields may matter. A source or explicit implementation specification is needed to establish the boundary.

children.title: Duplicate-Point Handling
children.top_down_role: Detection and disposition of repeated or numerically equivalent evaluation requests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distance-Tolerance Duplicate Tests Are Not Transitive
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of raw pairwise proximity as a cache identity relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), define \(x\sim_\tau y\) by \(|x-y|\le\tau\). With \(x=0\), \(y=3\tau/4\), and \(z=3\tau/2\), one has \(x\sim_\tau y\) and \(y\sim_\tau z\), but \(x\not\sim_\tau z\). Thus raw pairwise tolerance matching does not define order-independent duplicate classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Being within a numerical tolerance is not transitive, so naive tolerance matching can make duplicate grouping depend on insertion order.
assumptions_latex: Distance is absolute value on \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Distance-Tolerance Duplicate Tests Are Not Transitive

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition for unambiguous deterministic cache reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K(q)\) be a canonical key for an evaluation request \(q\), including every context field that may affect the response. Key equality partitions requests into equivalence classes. Deterministic reuse is semantically valid only when \(K(q)=K(q')\) implies equality of the certified oracle responses under the declared context.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic cache uses canonical contextual keys, and equal keys may be reused only when they guarantee the same certified response.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation context is included in the request domain.
Reuse substitutes a cached deterministic response for a requested response.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Duplicate-Key Requirement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Deterministic Reuse Is Invalid for Fresh Stochastic Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between duplicate-coordinate retrieval and independent stochastic observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If an oracle returns \(Y(x,U)\) with \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x,U)\mid x)>0\), returning a cached realization at a repeated point does not produce a fresh draw. Repeating one cached value produces empirical variance zero even though the conditional response variance is positive. A fresh stochastic replicate therefore requires new provenance and randomness unless retrieval or aggregation was requested.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached stochastic value is not a new replicate; counting retrievals as independent observations creates false precision.
assumptions_latex: A fresh replicate is intended to be conditionally independent of prior replicates.

notation.meaning: Random input and provenance for an evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Reuse Is Invalid for Fresh Stochastic Replication
Duplicate-Point Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate detection and reuse without fabricating evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a requested point \(x\), context \(\theta\), reuse mode \(u\), and database \(\mathcal D\). Compute \(k=K(x,\theta)\) and inspect all compatible successful records in \(I(k)\). If none exists, submit a new evaluation and append its record. If deterministic reuse is authorized, return one compatible cached payload with status \(\mathrm{cache\mbox{-}hit}\). If independent stochastic replication is requested, submit a new evaluation despite the duplicate key. If aggregation is requested, return statistics computed from the distinct stored replications. In no branch may a cache hit increment the count of independent evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicate requests become cache hits, new stochastic replications, or aggregations according to policy, and cache hits never count as independent evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Each stochastic replication has a distinct provenance identifier.
The requested reuse mode is explicit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{output}\in\{\mathrm{cache\mbox{-}hit},\mathrm{new\ evaluation},\mathrm{aggregate}\}\) and only a completed new evaluation increases the independent-evaluation count.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct kind, but the branching among deterministic reuse, replication, and aggregation and the associated accounting rules are interface-policy choices. No authoritative DFO evaluation-management source is provided.

children.title: Failed-Evaluation Handling
children.top_down_role: Classification and containment of unavailable, invalid, or aborted evaluations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety condition preventing failure metadata from being mistaken for numerical observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_v\) contain certified numerical observations and \(D_f\) contain failure records. A failure-aware manager maintains \(D_v\cap D_f=\varnothing\). A routine requiring numerical oracle values may consume a failure record only through a declared transformation \(\phi:D_f\to\overline{\mathbb R}^r\cup\{\mathrm{reject}\}\); without \(\phi\), failures may inform recovery but are not numerical samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid observations and failures remain disjoint; numerical routines may consume failures only through an explicit penalty, barrier, indicator, or rejection convention.
assumptions_latex: Every record has an unambiguous success or failure status.
Any interpretation of failure information is declared by the consuming method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_v\cap D_f=\varnothing,\qquad D_f\text{ enters numerical routines only through }\phi.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Containment Invariant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage representation for an unsuccessful evaluation request.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A failed request \(q\) is stored as a typed record \(R_f=(q,\sigma,e,c,t)\), containing failure status \(\sigma\), diagnostic provenance \(e\), incurred cost \(c\), and time metadata \(t\), but no value certified as an objective or constraint observation. Any numerical penalty later assigned to \(R_f\) is a separate method convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failed call is recorded with status, diagnostics, cost, and provenance, but without fabricating an optimization value.
assumptions_latex: The evaluator distinguishes certified numerical responses from failure metadata.

notation.meaning: Set of certified numerical evaluation records.

knowledge_statements.title: Typed Failed-Evaluation Record

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Evaluation Failure Does Not Imply Mathematical Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between unavailable evaluations and constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A failure status alone does not imply that the queried point violates a mathematical constraint: timeout, resource exhaustion, numerical breakdown, or transport error may occur at a feasible point. Treating every failure as \(+\infty\) or infeasibility is therefore valid only under an explicitly declared oracle convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failed call is not by itself evidence of infeasibility; failure-as-infinity requires an explicit semantic convention.
assumptions_latex: The failure status does not uniquely identify a violated mathematical constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation Failure Does Not Imply Mathematical Infeasibility
Failed-Evaluation Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed recording and safe exclusion of unsuccessful black-box evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an evaluation request \((x,\theta)\), execute the evaluator and validate termination, payload shape, and numerical finiteness. On success, store the payload with status \(\mathrm{success}\). On failure, store no fabricated objective or constraint value; instead append \(R_f=(x,\theta,\sigma,e,t)\), where \(\sigma\in\{\mathrm{transient},\mathrm{permanent},\mathrm{invalid}\}\), \(e\) is diagnostic provenance, and \(t\) is time metadata. A failed record is excluded from interpolation, regression, incumbent comparison, and filter acceptance. The algorithm returns the typed failure to a separate retry-or-exclusion policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failed evaluations receive typed, traceable records but no fabricated values, and they are excluded from models, comparisons, and acceptance tests.
assumptions_latex: The evaluator exposes success or a detectable failure condition.
Payload validation is fixed for the evaluation context.
Failure diagnostics contain no value declared valid for optimization.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unsuccessful evaluations must not be treated as valid numerical samples

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but unconditional exclusion of every failed record from modeling and acceptance is method-dependent; some black-box methods encode evaluation failures through barriers or other failure information. A source is required to delimit the intended policy.

children.title: Retry Versus Exclusion Policies
children.top_down_role: Structural choices between reevaluation, replacement, penalization, and permanent exclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Retry Versus Exclusion Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted decision rule following a typed evaluation failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a failed record with class \(\sigma\), retry count \(r\), retry limit \(R\), remaining evaluation budget \(B\), and exclusion radius \(\delta_f\geq0\). If \(\sigma=\mathrm{transient}\), \(r<R\), and \(B>0\), schedule one retry under the same semantic context, increment \(r\), and preserve all attempts. Otherwise mark the request excluded for the current evaluator version; when \(\delta_f>0\), suppress requests in \(\{y:\|y-x\|\leq\delta_f\}\) unless a declared override applies. Permanent or invalid failures are excluded immediately. A version or context change may invalidate the exclusion and permit a new request.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transient failures receive only budgeted retries; exhausted, permanent, or invalid failures create versioned exclusions, optionally covering a neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: Failure classes are assigned before this policy runs.
Overrides and exclusion invalidation events are explicitly logged.

notation.meaning: Current retry count and retry limit.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: typed failures support bounded retry and explicit exclusion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the retry threshold, immediate exclusion classes, neighborhood suppression, and version-based invalidation form a particular exception policy rather than a general DFO result. The exact policy and exclusion geometry require a source.

children.title: Warm-Start Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior points, samples, models, or solver state at initialization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent initialization from optional prior information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A warm-start interface augments current problem data \(P\) by optional prior information \(W\) and maps \((P,W)\) to an admissible initial solver state. A cold start is the case \(W=\varnothing\). Warm and cold starts must address the same objective, constraints, and required termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start converts optional prior information into an admissible initial state for the same current problem; a cold start supplies no prior information.
assumptions_latex: The solver declares its admissible initial-state set.
Current problem semantics and the required certificate are fixed independently of \(W\).

notation.meaning: Optional prior information supplied at initialization.
Admissible initial states for problem P.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Warm Starts Need Not Reduce Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting prior initialization information as an acceleration guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Admissibility alone does not imply that a warm start uses no more evaluations than a cold start. A prior point may lie farther from a useful basin, and imported information may require validation or geometry repair, so either initialization can require more work on a particular problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm starting preserves correctness when admissible but does not by itself certify fewer evaluations.
assumptions_latex: Both initial states are admissible for the same problem.
Work may depend on the initial state and initialization overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{warm}}\le N_{\mathrm{cold}}\quad\text{is not guaranteed without additional assumptions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm Starts Need Not Reduce Work

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Correctness Inheritance From Admissible Warm Starts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic inheritance result independent of the initialization payload type.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a DFO solver satisfies conclusion \(C(P)\) from every state in \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{adm}}(P)\), and the warm-start interface returns a state in \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{adm}}(P)\), then the warm-started execution also satisfies \(C(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start preserves a base solver's guarantee whenever it produces an admissible initial state.
assumptions_latex: The base guarantee holds from every admissible initial state.
The warm-start mapping returns an admissible state.

notation.meaning: Correctness or convergence conclusion for problem P.

knowledge_statements.title: Correctness Inheritance From Admissible Warm Starts

assumptions_latex: The black-box objective is a deterministic map \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
A prior run provides a finite evaluated archive \(\mathcal A_0=\{(x_i,f(x_i))\}_{i=1}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialized state reuses every compatible archived evaluation and requires no reevaluation of its archived points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic DFO warm start based on a compatible archive of exact evaluations.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal A_0\), discard entries incompatible with the current domain, objective version, or evaluation accuracy. Initialize the evaluation cache with the remaining entries, choose \(x_0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in\mathcal A_0}y\), and construct any initial model or geometry set solely from compatible cached points. When the optimizer requests \(x\), return the stored value if \((x,f(x))\in\mathcal A_0\); otherwise evaluate \(f(x)\), append \((x,f(x))\), and continue until the solver's stopping rule holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start imports compatible past evaluations, selects the best imported point as incumbent, and evaluates only previously unseen requests.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the interface leaf, but the cited introductory section does not specifically support this warm-start protocol. If all archived entries are incompatible, the stated argmin and incumbent are undefined.

children.title: Restart Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Fresh-run transitions triggered by stagnation, failure, or changed search conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing that admissible restarts alone do not preserve convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The base iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k/2\) converges to \(0\) from every initial point. If a restart resets \(x\) to \(1\) after every update, the observed post-update and reset states repeatedly equal \(1/2\) and \(1\), so the restarted execution does not converge to \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a globally convergent base iteration can fail when restarted infinitely often before progress accumulates.
assumptions_latex: A restart occurs after every base update.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite-Restart Convergence Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes full solver-state reinitialization from retention of validated persistent information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hard restart selects an admissible initial state without retaining mutable state from the interrupted run. A soft restart reinitializes transient search state while retaining a declared subset of persistent information, such as valid evaluations or an incumbent. The retained subset and its validity predicates are part of the restart interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hard restart discards mutable run state; a soft restart retains an explicitly validated subset while resetting transient search state.
assumptions_latex: The underlying solver declares its admissible initial-state set.
Every component retained by a soft restart has an explicit validity predicate.

notation.meaning: Admissible initialization states of the base solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Hard and Soft DFO Restarts

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence Preservation Under Finitely Many Admissible Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance of a tail-invariant base-method guarantee after finitely many restarts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a DFO method has a tail-invariant property \(P\) from every admissible initialization state. If an execution performs only finitely many restarts and every post-restart state is admissible, then the tail after the last restart is an ordinary execution of the base method and has property \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finitely many admissible restarts preserve any tail-invariant guarantee that the base method has from every admissible initial state.
assumptions_latex: The base method has tail-invariant property \(P\) from every admissible initialization.

notation.meaning: A tail-invariant conclusion of the base method.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence Preservation Under Finitely Many Admissible Restarts

assumptions_latex: A DFO run has incumbent \(x_k\), scale \(\Delta_k>0\), and compatible archive \(\mathcal A_k\).
A restart trigger and restart scale \(\Delta_{\mathrm r}>0\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restarted run preserves reusable evaluations while resetting transient search state and restoring a positive exploration scale.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation-preserving restart for a deterministic DFO run after a prescribed trigger.

source_refs.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When the trigger fires, retain all valid pairs in \(\mathcal A_k\), choose a restart center \(x_{\\mathrm r}\) from the archive or by a prescribed diversification rule, set the exploration scale to \(\Delta_{\mathrm r}\), and discard transient model, poll, and failure counters whose meaning depends on the previous run. Rebuild the initial geometry around \(x_{\mathrm r}\) using cached points when suitable; evaluate only missing points. The restarted process then applies the underlying DFO iteration and its original stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart keeps compatible evaluations but resets run-dependent models, counters, center, and search scale before rebuilding the DFO state.
knowledge_statements.title: Restart Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the chapter-level trust-region locator does not establish this restart interface. The expression for the restart center contains an erroneous doubled backslash, and the admissibility of a diversification-generated center is not specified.

children.title: Portfolio Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Coordination of multiple derivative-free solvers or search configurations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification of evaluation-budget allocation among multiple DFO solvers or configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A portfolio over solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\) is static when nonnegative budgets \(B_1,\ldots,B_p\) are fixed before observing outcomes, with \(\sum_{j=1}^pB_j\le B\). It is adaptive when the next solver and allocation may be measurable functions of completed portfolio history, while the cumulative charged evaluations remain at most \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static portfolio preallocates its budget; an adaptive portfolio reallocates it from observed history while respecting one global budget.
assumptions_latex: Charged-evaluation semantics are common across the portfolio.

notation.meaning: Charged evaluations allocated to solver j.

knowledge_statements.title: Static and Adaptive Solver Portfolios

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Uniform Dominance From Budget Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case limitation of fixed-budget portfolios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Without assumptions linking observed progress to future performance, splitting a budget among members cannot uniformly dominate every possible full-budget member run. If some member \(j\) receives \(B_j<B\), a permissible performance profile may have that member first improve at its \(B\)-th evaluation, which the split portfolio never reaches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed budget split has no assumption-free guarantee of beating every individual solver given the full budget.
assumptions_latex: At least one member receives fewer than \(B\) evaluations.
No structural restriction is imposed on member performance histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists\text{ fixed split that uniformly dominates every full-budget member run}.
knowledge_statements.title: No Uniform Dominance From Budget Splitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance relation for a portfolio aggregating member candidate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every member returns a nonempty candidate set \(A_j\) and the portfolio minimizes over \(A=\bigcup_{j=1}^pA_j\), then \(\min_{x\in A}f(x)=\min_{1\le j\le p}\min_{x\in A_j}f(x)\). This comparison alone gives no improvement guarantee over the best member under a different allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting the best candidate produced by any member is no worse than each returned member candidate, but does not prove that portfolio allocation improves the best solver.
assumptions_latex: All candidates use the same deterministic objective semantics.

notation.meaning: Candidate set returned by member j.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-of-Portfolio Performance Identity

assumptions_latex: There are \(p\geq 1\) DFO solvers sharing a deterministic objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
A total evaluation budget \(B\in\mathbb N\) and a deterministic allocation policy are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No point is evaluated twice through the interface, total new evaluations do not exceed \(B\), and the returned point is best in the shared archive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-cache portfolio interface with an explicit global evaluation budget.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\) and an archive \(\mathcal A\). Repeatedly select an active solver by the allocation policy and obtain its requested point \(x\in\mathcal X\). If \(x\) is cached, return its stored value without charging the budget; otherwise, when fewer than \(B\) new evaluations have been issued, evaluate \(f(x)\), store the pair, and return it to every interested solver. Stop when the budget is exhausted or every solver stops, and output \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in\mathcal A}y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portfolio coordinates several DFO solvers through one cache and budget, returning the best point evaluated by any solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Interfaces

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the portfolio leaf, but the cited general DFO section does not support the shared-cache portfolio policy. The final argmin is undefined when the archive is empty, and the no-duplicate guarantee requires coordination semantics not supplied here.

children.title: Cross-Run State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and validity of information transferred between runs or solvers.

assumptions_latex: Source and destination runs optimize the same objective version over compatible domains.
The source state contains an archive, incumbent, scale, and optional model data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transfer is admissible exactly when every imported component passes its compatibility predicate; otherwise that component is rejected or rebuilt.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for transferring reusable DFO state between runs.

source_refs.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transfer \(T:s\mapsto s'\) is compatible when imported evaluations have unchanged meanings and accuracies, imported points remain feasible, the incumbent is selected from valid imported points, the scale is positive and valid for the destination method, and any imported model has the basis, center, scaling, and interpolation set expected by the destination solver. Components satisfying these predicates may be copied. An incompatible evaluation must be reevaluated, while incompatible model or geometry data must be discarded and rebuilt from compatible evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-run transfer is valid only when evaluation semantics, feasibility, scale, geometry, and model conventions remain compatible with the destination solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Run State Transfer

source_witnesses.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but the source does not establish this transfer schema. The conclusion requires every imported component to pass, whereas the statement permits componentwise rejection or rebuilding, so the asserted iff condition conflicts with the stated partial-transfer behavior.

children.title: Parallel Polling
children.top_down_role: Concurrent evaluation of polling directions or direct-search candidates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incomplete Polls Cannot Certify Poll Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on declaring failure or shrinking the poll scale while concurrent responses remain unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a strict-improvement poll declares failure while some \(z\in P_k\) is unevaluated or unresolved, the available responses do not imply \(f(z)\ge f(x_k)\) for every \(z\in P_k\). An unresolved point may satisfy \(f(z)<f(x_k)\). Therefore a complete-poll failure certificate requires rejection or valid completion of every required poll point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel poll with unresolved points cannot certify that the full poll set contains no improvement.
assumptions_latex: Poll success means strict objective improvement.
At least one required poll response is unresolved when failure is considered.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Polls Cannot Certify Poll Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information equivalence between completed synchronous parallel and serial complete polls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_k\) be a finite deterministic poll set and suppose every \(f(z)\), \(z\in P_k\), completes before the iteration decision. Concurrent evaluation reveals the same indexed value set \(\{(z,f(z)):z\in P_k\}\) as serial complete polling. Any deterministic selection rule depending only on that completed set therefore returns the same incumbent; only execution timing differs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A completed synchronous parallel poll is information-equivalent to complete serial polling under the same deterministic selection rule.
assumptions_latex: Every poll evaluation completes before selection.
Both executions use the same poll set and selection rule.

notation.meaning: finite poll set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Parallel Poll Equivalence

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), \(x_k\in\mathcal X\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and \(D_k\) is a finite positive spanning set.
At least \(|D_k|\) workers can evaluate the deterministic objective concurrently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful poll accepts a strict decrease; an unsuccessful completed poll certifies that no tested poll point strictly improves \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of a positive-spanning direct-search poll set.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7
4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the feasible poll set \(P_k=\{x_k+\Delta_k d:d\in D_k\}\cap\mathcal X\) and submit all uncached members concurrently. After the prescribed synchronization point, if some completed \(z\in P_k\) satisfies \(f(z)<f(x_k)\), select a prescribed improving point as \(x_{k+1}\) and update \(\Delta_k\) by the success rule. Otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and update \(\Delta_k\) by the failure rule. Stop according to the method's scale, budget, or target criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel polling evaluates a positive-spanning poll set concurrently, accepts a prescribed improving point, and otherwise records a failed poll.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Polling

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7
4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and positive-spanning poll construction fit the leaf, but neither locator specifically supports parallel DFO polling. The failure branch must require completion of every tested poll evaluation; a merely prescribed synchronization point does not ensure the claimed no-improvement certificate.

children.title: Parallel Model Sampling
children.top_down_role: Concurrent acquisition of points used to construct or improve local models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent acquisition of model-building observations with explicit batch and terminal policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At model epoch \(k\), fix center \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), model class, requested batch size \(b_k\), admissible unevaluated candidate set \(C_k\), completion threshold \(c_k\leq b_k\), and a finite epoch decision deadline. Select \(b_k\) distinct candidates when \(|C_k|\geq b_k\); otherwise invoke the declared insufficient-candidate fallback. Dispatch selected requests with epoch tag \(k\). Fit only when at least \(c_k\) valid responses pass the model class's eligibility test; by the decision deadline, otherwise cancel outstanding work, use a permitted lower-order model, or declare sampling failure according to the prespecified rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel model-sampling epoch fixes its model region and batch size, tags requests, and has explicit finite fallbacks for insufficient candidates and incomplete responses.
assumptions_latex: C_k\text{ excludes completed, pending, invalid, and duplicate requests}.
A finite epoch decision deadline and deterministic terminal fallback are declared.
The model class supplies a separate eligibility test for completed samples.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each epoch reaches either an eligible completed model set or a declared non-fit outcome}.

notation.meaning: requested batch cardinality at epoch k
minimum valid completions before fitting may be attempted
sampling radius attached to epoch k

knowledge_statements.title: Epoch-Tagged Parallel Model Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for responses completed after their sampling epoch changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A response requested for epoch \(k\) does not automatically satisfy the eligibility conditions of a later epoch \(\ell\). If the model center, radius, admissible domain, noise treatment, or model class changes, the observation may remain in the historical store but may enter the epoch-\(\ell\) fit only after the epoch-\(\ell\) eligibility and geometry tests are reapplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Late observations remain data but are not automatically eligible model samples after the model region or class changes.
assumptions_latex: Requests carry their originating model-epoch metadata.
At least one model-defining condition may change between epochs \(k\) and \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{completion during epoch }\ell\not\Rightarrow\text{eligibility for the epoch-}\ell\text{ model}.
knowledge_statements.title: Late-Sample Eligibility Boundary

assumptions_latex: A deterministic objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) has a finite evaluated set \(Y_k\).
A model class and a geometry criterion for selecting interpolation or regression points are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next model is built from completed evaluations only and satisfies the prescribed geometry criterion whenever the collected sample set permits it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel geometry-improving sampling for interpolation or regression DFO models.

source_refs.locator: 6 Ensuring well poisedness and suitable derivative-free models p. 89
4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose distinct unevaluated points \(Q_k=\{q_1,\ldots,q_b\}\subset\mathcal X\) by maximizing or greedily improving the prescribed geometry criterion relative to \(Y_k\). Evaluate all \(f(q_j)\) concurrently, augment \(Y_k\) with completed pairs, and select a model set satisfying the required cardinality and poisedness or rank condition. Fit \(m_k\) by the prescribed interpolation or regression equations. If insufficient evaluations complete, defer the fit or use a lower-order model explicitly allowed by the model class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel model sampling chooses a geometrically informative batch, evaluates it concurrently, and fits a model only from completed data.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Model Sampling

Unique interpolation when \(s=q\), or unique least-squares coefficients when \(s\ge q\), holds exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=q\).

The chosen model basis has dimension \(q\).
Only completed valid evaluations enter the fit.

children.title: Shared-Budget Coordination
children.top_down_role: Allocation of limited evaluation capacity across polling and model-building workloads.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting condition for concurrent polling and model-sampling admissions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb N\) be a hard budget measured in charged physical evaluations. At every time let \(C\) be the number completed, \(R\) the number admitted and still reserved, and \(U=B-C-R\) the unreserved balance. Budget feasibility is equivalent to preserving \(C\ge0\), \(R\ge0\), and \(U\ge0\), or \(C+R\le B\). Admission atomically changes \((R,U)\) to \((R+1,U-1)\), and completion changes \((C,R)\) to \((C+1,R-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared evaluation budget is safe when completed plus reserved evaluations never exceed the budget and every admission reserves capacity atomically.
assumptions_latex: Budget units count charged physical evaluations.
Every admitted unfinished evaluation holds one reservation.
Completion transfers one reserved unit to the completed count.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Budget Conservation Invariant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Budget Safety Does Not Imply Workload Fairness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Starvation boundary for coordination between polling and model-building queues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The invariant \(C+R\le B\) imposes no positive allocation guarantee on either workload. A strict-priority coordinator that always admits model-sampling requests while such requests exist can consume all \(B\) reservations and admit no poll request. Hence budget safety does not imply starvation freedom or a positive allocation share.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Never exceeding the shared budget does not prevent one workload from starving the other.
assumptions_latex: Polling and model sampling draw from the same finite budget.
The admission rule may give strict priority to one nonempty queue.
knowledge_statements.title: Budget Safety Does Not Imply Workload Fairness

assumptions_latex: All workers share a global budget \(B\in\mathbb N\) of newly issued black-box evaluations.
The cache identifies duplicate requests before budget reservation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coordinator issues at most \(B\) new evaluations and charges each distinct newly issued point exactly once.

notation.meaning: number of reserved or completed new evaluations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomic budget reservation for parallel black-box requests sharing one cache.

source_refs.locator: 4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(N=0\). For each requested point \(x\), atomically inspect \(\mathcal C\). If \(x\) is completed, return its value; if it is pending, attach the requester to that evaluation. Otherwise reserve one unit only if \(N<B\), then set \(N\leftarrow N+1\), mark \(x\) pending, and issue the evaluation. On completion, store the result and notify attached requesters. Reject or defer an uncached request when \(N=B\), and terminate after all reserved work is accounted for.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A shared coordinator atomically deduplicates requests and reserves budget, ensuring that concurrent workers never exceed the global evaluation limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Budget Coordination

children.title: Batch Surrogate Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous evaluation sets selected from non-Bayesian surrogate models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-candidate deterministic surrogate selection with explicit exclusion state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_k\) be a finite set excluding completed, pending, invalid, and already selected queries. For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), minimize a declared deterministic score \(s_{k,j}\) over the current nonempty candidate set, add a minimizer to \(Q_k\), and remove it from further selection. Dispatch \(Q_k\) concurrently and refit from valid completed observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite exclusion-aware candidate set makes greedy deterministic surrogate batching well posed.
assumptions_latex: C_k\text{ is finite and initially contains at least }q\text{ admissible points}.
Each score \(s_{k,j}\) is real-valued on the remaining finite set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |Q_k|=q\text{ and its members are distinct and admissible}.

notation.meaning: deterministic selection score at batch position j

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posed Greedy Surrogate Batch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic model-based batch combining predicted improvement with model maintenance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose one admissible point approximately minimizing the current deterministic surrogate over the region of interest. Choose remaining points using a declared geometry-improvement criterion, excluding completed, pending, invalid, and already selected points. Evaluate concurrently and refit only from valid completed observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic batch can combine a model-descent point with points chosen to improve future model geometry.
assumptions_latex: The descent and geometry subproblems have declared exact or approximate solution rules.
knowledge_statements.title: Descent-and-Geometry Batch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of independent pointwise surrogate ranks to coordinate a batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Selecting the \(q\) smallest values of a pointwise score controls only individual ranks. Without an interaction, separation, or geometry term, it gives no positive lower bound on pairwise separation and no rank or poisedness guarantee; arbitrarily many top-ranked candidates may occupy an arbitrarily small neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individually best surrogate scores can form a redundant cluster and fail to improve model geometry.
assumptions_latex: The selection score has no interaction, exclusion-radius, or geometry term.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Top-q Redundancy

assumptions_latex: A surrogate \(m_k:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is fitted from completed black-box evaluations.
A batch size \(q\geq1\) and an admissible candidate set \(C_k\subseteq\mathcal X\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns \(q\) distinct surrogate-selected points when at least \(q\) admissible candidates exist.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy batch selection from a deterministic DFO surrogate and admissible candidate set.

source_refs.locator: 10 Trust-region methods based on derivative-free models p. 173
4.2 Parallel computing p. 101
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(Q_k=\varnothing\). For \(j=1,\ldots,q\), choose \(x_{k,j}\) minimizing the prescribed surrogate acquisition score over \(C_k\setminus Q_k\), optionally updating that score to penalize points near previously selected batch members, and set \(Q_k\leftarrow Q_k\cup\{x_{k,j}\}\). Submit all members of \(Q_k\) concurrently, append completed evaluations to the data set, and refit the surrogate before constructing the next batch. Stop when the global budget or solver criterion holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch surrogate evaluation greedily selects distinct model-favored candidates, evaluates them concurrently, and refits after results become available.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Surrogate Evaluation

Having at least q candidates does not ensure that each prescribed score attains a minimum, and the candidate set is not required to exclude completed or pending evaluations.

children.title: Batch Bayesian Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Simultaneous evaluation sets selected through Bayesian optimization criteria.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential approximation to a joint Bayesian batch decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose one point by the current acquisition, condition temporarily on a specified sampled or deterministic fantasy outcome there, choose the next point under the fantasy-updated posterior, and repeat until \(q\) points are selected. Discard fantasies after dispatch and update the true posterior only with actual observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fantasy batching constructs a Bayesian batch by temporarily conditioning on imagined outcomes at already selected points.
assumptions_latex: Each sequential acquisition problem has a declared exact or approximate solution rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_k\text{ is selected before any actual outcome from the batch is observed}.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Fantasy Sequential Batch Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous selection by a continuous joint posterior acquisition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q_k\subseteq\mathcal X^q\) be nonempty and compact and let \(\alpha_k\) be continuous on \(\mathcal Q_k\). Select \(Q_k\in\mathcal Q_k\) with \(\alpha_k(Q_k)\geq\max_{Q\in\mathcal Q_k}\alpha_k(Q)-\varepsilon_k\), evaluate its members concurrently, and update the posterior after all required batch results are resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact feasible batch set and continuous acquisition make approximate joint Bayesian batch selection well posed.

notation.meaning: feasible set of ordered q-point batches

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Posed Joint Bayesian Batch Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint posterior acquisition for noiseless Bayesian minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: q\mathrm{EI}_k(x_1,\ldots,x_q)=\mathbb E_k\!\left[\left(f_k^{\min}-\min_{1\leq i\leq q}F(x_i)\right)_+\right].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch expected improvement is the posterior expected improvement obtained from the best member of the batch.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with incumbent \(f_k^{\min}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence boundary for noiseless joint batch expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The value of \(q\mathrm{EI}\) depends on the joint posterior law. In the noiseless latent-value model, duplicating a query does not change the minimum inside the improvement: \(q\mathrm{EI}_k(x,x,x_3,\ldots,x_q)=q\mathrm{EI}_k(x,x_3,\ldots,x_q)\), with the right side interpreted as the acquisition of the duplicate-collapsed batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint Bayesian selection uses posterior dependence, while a duplicate noiseless query adds no improvement.
assumptions_latex: Repeated noiseless queries share the same latent value.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Dependence and Duplicate Redundancy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior value-of-information acquisition for a concurrently observed batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Bayesian minimization, let \(\mu_k(x)\) be the current posterior mean and let \(\mu_{k,Q}(x)\) denote the posterior mean after observing the random outcomes at a proposed batch \(Q\). The batch knowledge gradient is \[q\mathrm{KG}_k(Q)=\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu_k(x)-\mathbb E_k\!\left[\min_{x\in\mathcal X}\mu_{k,Q}(x)\right],\] whenever the minima and expectation are well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch knowledge gradient measures the expected improvement in the best posterior-mean decision after observing a proposed batch.
assumptions_latex: The displayed posterior minima exist or are replaced by consistently declared infima.
All outcomes in Q are incorporated jointly in the hypothetical posterior update.

notation.meaning: Posterior mean after hypothetical batch observations

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Knowledge-Gradient Acquisition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian concurrent evaluation using independently sampled posterior objective functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditional on data \(\mathcal D_k\), draw posterior sample functions \(F_k^{(1)},\ldots,F_k^{(q)}\). For each \(i\), choose \(x_{k,i}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal X}F_k^{(i)}(x)\), applying a declared tie-breaking or duplicate-resolution rule. Dispatch the resulting batch concurrently and update the posterior with the completed observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch posterior sampling forms concurrent candidates from minimizers of independently drawn posterior functions.
assumptions_latex: Posterior sample functions and their optimization rule are well defined.
A duplicate-resolution policy is declared when distinct evaluations are required.
Every sampled-function minimization enforces the feasible domain.

notation.meaning: The i-th objective function drawn from the current posterior.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Posterior Sampling

assumptions_latex: Conditional on data \(\mathcal D_k\), the objective has a specified posterior distribution.
A batch size \(q\geq1\) and measurable batch acquisition functional \(\alpha_k:\mathcal X^q\to\mathbb R\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected batch is a maximizer of the prescribed joint posterior acquisition criterion, up to the declared numerical optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-acquisition formulation of synchronous batch Bayesian black-box evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute a tuple \((x_{k,1},\ldots,x_{k,q})\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in\mathcal X^q}\alpha_k(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), subject to distinctness and any feasibility constraints, and set \(Q_k=\{x_{k,1},\ldots,x_{k,q}\}\). Evaluate the black box at all points in \(Q_k\) concurrently. After the synchronous batch completes, augment \(\mathcal D_k\) with the observations, update the posterior, and repeat until the evaluation budget or posterior stopping criterion is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch Bayesian evaluation jointly maximizes a posterior acquisition function, evaluates the selected points concurrently, and updates the posterior after completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Bayesian Evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits batch Bayesian evaluation, but no source is supplied. Measurability alone does not ensure an acquisition maximizer, a feasible distinct q-point batch, or a meaningful numerical tolerance guarantee.

children.title: Batch Diversity Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coverage, redundancy, and interaction concerns within a concurrent candidate batch.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric diversity selection from a finite candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_1\in C\). For \(j=2,\ldots,q\), choose \(x_j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C\setminus\{x_1,\ldots,x_{j-1}\}}\min_{i<j}d(x,x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy maximin repeatedly selects the candidate farthest from the points already chosen.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Maximin Batch Coordination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact existence condition for a minimum-separation batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(C,d,\delta)\) be the maximum cardinality of a \(\delta\)-separated subset of \(C\). A \(q\)-point \(\delta\)-separated batch exists if and only if \(M(C,d,\delta)\geq q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separated batch exists exactly when the candidate set's packing number reaches the requested batch size.
knowledge_statements.title: Packing-Number Feasibility Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric diversity convention for a simultaneous candidate batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\), define \(\operatorname{sep}_d(Q)=\min_{i<j}d(x_i,x_j)\). The batch is \(\delta\)-separated when \(\operatorname{sep}_d(Q)\geq\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch is diversity-feasible when every distinct pair is separated by at least the declared distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Separation Diversity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating distinctness and coverage heuristics from global batch optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=\{0,2,3,5\}\subset\mathbb R\) with Euclidean distance and \(q=3\), greedy maximin initialized at \(2\) selects \(5\) and then \(0\), giving separation \(2\). The batch \(\{0,3,5\}\) also has separation \(2\); more generally, the greedy rule's output depends on initialization and tie-breaking and carries no exact global-maximin certificate without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy maximin guarantees distinct selections but not initialization-independent or certified globally optimal diversity.
assumptions_latex: The initial point and tie-breaking rule are not globally optimized.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Maximin Is Initialization Dependent

assumptions_latex: A candidate batch is \(Q=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in\mathcal X^q\) with \(q\geq2\).
A metric \(d\) on \(\mathcal X\) and separation threshold \(\delta>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A batch is diversity-feasible if and only if every distinct pair satisfies \(d(x_i,x_j)\geq\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum pairwise-distance condition for diversity within a simultaneous evaluation batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the batch separation by \(\operatorname{sep}_d(Q)=\min_{1\leq i<j\leq q}d(x_i,x_j)\). The batch diversity constraint is \(\operatorname{sep}_d(Q)\geq\delta\). Equivalently, the feasible batch set is \(\mathcal Q_{q,\delta}=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in\mathcal X^q:d(x_i,x_j)\geq\delta\text{ for all }i<j\}\). A batch-selection objective may be optimized only over \(\mathcal Q_{q,\delta}\); if this set is empty, the interface must reduce \(q\), reduce \(\delta\), or report infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch diversity requires every pair of selected points to be separated by at least a prescribed distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Batch Diversity Coordination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the diversity leaf and the pairwise-separation equivalence is internally correct, but no source supports adopting this particular diversity convention. The mandated responses to an empty feasible set are interface design choices rather than consequences of the definition.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimizer-neutral dispatch and completion protocol without a global batch barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Whenever a worker is idle and stopping has not fired, dispatch an admissible uncached request or attach to an identical pending request. On each completion, validate the result, perform its permitted terminal state transition, incorporate a valid observation at most once, update the optimizer immediately, and dispatch newly available work. After stopping, issue no new requests and apply the declared cancel-or-drain policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Results update the optimizer as they arrive, and new work is dispatched without waiting for all outstanding evaluations.
assumptions_latex: The admissibility, cache-key, validation, stopping, and cancel-or-drain policies are declared.
Request transitions obey Asynchronous Request-State Semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No global completion barrier is required, and no new request is issued after stopping.}
knowledge_statements.title: Event-Driven Asynchronous Dispatch

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical state model for event-driven black-box requests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each request has a unique identifier \(r\), query \(x_r\), submission version \(v_r\), and one state in \(\{\mathrm{queued},\mathrm{running},\mathrm{completed},\mathrm{failed},\mathrm{cancelled}\}\). Only a valid completed result may enter the optimization archive, and each identifier is incorporated at most once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous evaluation tracks identity, optimizer version, terminal status, and at-most-once incorporation.

notation.meaning: optimizer-state version used to create request r

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Request-State Semantics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schedule-dependent trajectory boundary for adaptive asynchronous optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If subsequent queries depend nontrivially on the archive at individual completion events, two executions having identical pointwise oracle values and random seed but different completion orders can generate different later queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different completion orders alone can change an adaptive asynchronous optimization trajectory.
assumptions_latex: At least two outstanding requests can complete in different orders.
The query generator updates after individual completions and depends nontrivially on the current archive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{same oracle values and seed}\centernot\Longrightarrow\text{same query sequence}.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Order Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Utilization invariant under an ideal instantaneous-dispatch model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scheduler is work-conserving when it leaves no worker idle while admissible unassigned work is available. Before stopping, if \(I(t)\) is the idle-worker count and \(A(t)\) the available-request count, then \(I(t)A(t)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eligible work and idle workers cannot coexist under a work-conserving asynchronous policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Work-Conserving Dispatch

assumptions_latex: There are \(w\geq1\) workers and a deterministic black-box objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
The scheduler maintains pending, completed, and cached request states under a global stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted result is incorporated without a global batch barrier, and no uncached request is issued after the stopping rule fires.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven black-box scheduling without synchronous batch barriers.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

source_refs.locator: 1.4 How derivative-free algorithms should work p. 7

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P=\varnothing\) and archive \(\mathcal A\). Whenever a worker is idle and stopping has not occurred, generate a request \(x\) from the current optimizer state; return a cached value, attach to an identical pending request, or issue \(x\) and add it to \(P\). Whenever an evaluation of \(x\) finishes, remove \(x\) from \(P\), append \((x,f(x))\) to \(\mathcal A\), update the optimizer immediately, and dispatch further work. At stopping, issue no new requests and apply the declared cancellation or drain policy to \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous evaluation updates the optimizer and dispatches new work whenever any result arrives, without waiting for an entire batch.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Black-Box Evaluation
