children.title: Uncertainty Assessment
children.top_down_role: Characterization of variability in stochastic benchmark outcomes and solver comparisons.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample confidence certificate for independently replicated binary outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iid \(S_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\), let \(X=\sum_{i=1}^nS_i\). Set \(L=0\) when \(X=0\), otherwise \(L=B^{-1}(\alpha/2;X,n-X+1)\); set \(U=1\) when \(X=n\), otherwise \(U=B^{-1}(1-\alpha/2;X+1,n-X)\). Then \(\Pr_p\{p\in[L,U]\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(p\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Clopper–Pearson interval is a conservative exact confidence interval for an independently replicated success probability.

notation.meaning: Quantile of the beta distribution with parameters a and b.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Binomial Success-Probability Interval

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mean-Interval Failure Under Heavy Tails or Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of iid standard-error and central-limit summaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard error \(s_n/\sqrt n\) and iid central-limit interval are not generally valid for dependent replicates. Moreover, if \(Y_i\) are iid standard Cauchy, then \(\bar Y_n\) has the same Cauchy distribution for every \(n\); the population mean and variance do not exist and averaging does not concentrate at a finite mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependence invalidates iid standard errors, while Cauchy responses show that replication alone need not stabilize a sample mean.
assumptions_latex: The heavy-tail counterexample uses iid standard Cauchy responses.
knowledge_statements.title: Mean-Interval Failure Under Heavy Tails or Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-sample uncertainty assessment for an iid scalar response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1,Y_2,\ldots\) are iid with mean \(\mu\) and variance \(0<\sigma^2<\infty\), then, with \(\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\) and \(s_n^2=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(Y_i-\bar Y_n)^2\), \(\sqrt n(\bar Y_n-\mu)/s_n\Rightarrow N(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For iid finite-variance responses, the studentized sample mean is asymptotically normal and gives a large-sample confidence interval.

notation.meaning: q-quantile of the standard normal distribution.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Mean-Response Assessment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample uncertainty certificate for a matched comparison of two solver configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(D_i=Y_{A,i}-Y_{B,i}\). If \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\) are iid \(N(\delta,\sigma_D^2)\), \(n\geq2\), and \(s_D^2=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(D_i-\bar D)^2\), then \(\left[\bar D-t_{n-1,1-\alpha/2}s_D/\sqrt n,\bar D+t_{n-1,1-\alpha/2}s_D/\sqrt n\right]\) has exact coverage \(1-\alpha\) for \(\delta=\mathbb E[Y_A-Y_B]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under iid normal paired differences, the Student-t interval exactly covers the mean matched performance difference.

notation.meaning: paired performance difference in replicate i
sample standard deviation of the paired differences

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Paired-Normal Mean-Difference Interval

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample uncertainty certificate for the variance of independently replicated normal responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(\mu,\sigma^2)\), \(n\ge2\), and \(s_n^2=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(Y_i-\bar Y_n)^2\), then for \(0<\alpha<1\), \[I_{\sigma^2}=\left[\frac{(n-1)s_n^2}{\chi^2_{n-1,1-\alpha/2}},\frac{(n-1)s_n^2}{\chi^2_{n-1,\alpha/2}}\right]\] satisfies \(\Pr_{\mu,\sigma}\{\sigma^2\in I_{\sigma^2}\}=1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under iid normal replication, chi-square quantiles give an exact confidence interval for response variance.

notation.meaning: q-quantile of the chi-square distribution with ν degrees of freedom

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Normal-Variance Confidence Interval

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-free mean-response uncertainty certificate for independent bounded replicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are independent with common mean \(\mu\) and satisfy \(a\le Y_i\le b\) almost surely, then for \(0<\alpha<1\), \[\Pr\!\left\{\left|\bar Y_n-\mu\right|\le(b-a)\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\alpha)}{2n}}\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hoeffding's inequality gives a finite-sample confidence interval for the mean of independent bounded benchmark responses.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are independent and have common finite mean \(\mu\).
\(a\le Y_i\le b\) almost surely for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sample Bounded-Mean Confidence Interval

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distribution-Free Order-Statistic Interval for a Quantile
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample uncertainty certificate for a continuous response quantile under independent replication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be iid with continuous distribution function \(F\), let \(q_p=F^{-1}(p)\) for \(0<p<1\), and write \(Y_{(1)}\le\cdots\le Y_{(n)}\). For integers \(1\le l<u\le n\), \[\Pr\{Y_{(l)}\le q_p\le Y_{(u)}\}=\sum_{j=l}^{u-1}{n\choose j}p^j(1-p)^{n-j}.\] Hence any \((l,u)\) for which the displayed sum is at least \(1-\alpha\) gives a distribution-free confidence interval \([Y_{(l)},Y_{(u)}]\) for \(q_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binomially calibrated order statistics give a finite-sample confidence interval for a continuous response quantile without a parametric response model.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are iid with continuous distribution function \(F\).
knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Free Order-Statistic Interval for a Quantile

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cluster-Level Mean Uncertainty Under Within-Cluster Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic mean-response uncertainty when within-cluster dependence is absorbed into independent scalar cluster summaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Z_1,Z_2,\ldots be iid scalar summaries of independent replicate clusters, where observations within a cluster may be dependent. If \mathbb E[Z_g]=\mu and 0<\operatorname{Var}(Z_g)<\infty, define \bar Z_G=G^{-1}\sum_{g=1}^G Z_g and s_{Z,G}^2=(G-1)^{-1}\sum_{g=1}^G(Z_g-\bar Z_G)^2. Then \frac{\sqrt G(\bar Z_G-\mu)}{s_{Z,G}}\Rightarrow N(0,1), so \bar Z_G\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}s_{Z,G}/\sqrt G has asymptotic coverage 1-\alpha.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent cluster summaries permit asymptotically valid mean uncertainty even when observations within each cluster are dependent.
assumptions_latex: Clusters are independent and identically distributed.
Each declared cluster summary Z_g has common mean \mu and finite positive variance.
The estimand is the equally weighted mean of the declared cluster-summary distribution.

notation.meaning: Declared scalar summary of cluster g.
Sample standard deviation of the cluster summaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Cluster-Level Mean Uncertainty Under Within-Cluster Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Familywise confidence certificate for several benchmark estimands, allowing arbitrary dependence among their intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_M\) be benchmark estimands and suppose intervals \(I_j\) satisfy \(\Pr\{\theta_j\notin I_j\}\le\alpha_j\). Then \[\Pr\{\theta_j\in I_j\ \text{for every }j=1,\ldots,M\}\ge1-\sum_{j=1}^M\alpha_j.\] Consequently, choosing \(\sum_j\alpha_j\le\alpha\) gives simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), without requiring independence across intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocating a total error budget across marginal intervals gives a simultaneous familywise confidence guarantee even when the reported statistics are dependent.
assumptions_latex: Each marginal noncoverage bound \(\Pr\{\theta_j\notin I_j\}\le\alpha_j\) is valid.

notation.meaning: Noncoverage budget assigned to estimand j.
Marginal confidence interval for estimand j.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Long-Run-Variance Assessment for Stationary m-Dependent Responses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic mean uncertainty for serially dependent benchmark responses with finite dependence range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((Y_t)_{t\ge1}\) be strictly stationary and \(m\)-dependent, with \(\mathbb E[Y_t]=\mu\), \(\mathbb E|Y_t|^{2+\delta}<\infty\) for some \(\delta>0\), and \[\tau^2=\gamma_0+2\sum_{h=1}^m\gamma_h>0,\qquad \gamma_h=\operatorname{Cov}(Y_t,Y_{t+h}).\] Define \(\widehat\gamma_h=n^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{n-h}(Y_t-\bar Y_n)(Y_{t+h}-\bar Y_n)\) and \(\widehat\tau_n^2=\widehat\gamma_0+2\sum_{h=1}^m\widehat\gamma_h\). Then \(\widehat\tau_n^2\to_p\tau^2\) and \[\frac{\sqrt n(\bar Y_n-\mu)}{\widehat\tau_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For stationary finite-range dependence, uncertainty in the mean uses the long-run variance rather than the iid variance.
assumptions_latex: \((Y_t)\) is strictly stationary and \(m\)-dependent for a fixed finite \(m\).
The dependence range \(m\) used in \(\widehat\tau_n^2\) is correctly specified.

notation.meaning: Long-run variance of the sample mean.

knowledge_statements.title: Long-Run-Variance Assessment for Stationary m-Dependent Responses
Uncertainty Assessment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample confidence certificate for an independently replicated mean response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given independent responses \(Y_1,,,Y_n\) with \(n\geq2\), define \(\bar Y_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\) and \(s_n^2=(n-1)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n(Y_i-\bar Y_n)^2\). If the responses are normally distributed with unknown mean \(\mu\) and variance \(\sigma^2\), then for \(0<\alpha<1\), \[I_{1-\alpha}=\left[\bar Y_n-t_{n-1,1-\alpha/2}\frac{s_n}{\sqrt n},\;\bar Y_n+t_{n-1,1-\alpha/2}\frac{s_n}{\sqrt n}\right]\] is an exact two-sided \((1-\alpha)\)-confidence interval for \(\mu\). The tuple \((n,\bar Y_n,s_n,\alpha,I_{1-\alpha})\) is verifiable from the replicate data and stated distributional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under independent normal replicates, the Student-t interval gives an exact confidence certificate for the protocol-specific mean response.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are independent and identically distributed as \(N(\mu,\sigma^2)\).

notation.meaning: q-quantile of Student's t distribution with ν degrees of freedom.
Two-sided confidence interval for the mean response.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Student-t interval is standard under the stated iid normal model, and certificate is a defensible role for the reported interval. However, no source is supplied, and the opening sequence \(Y_1,,,Y_n\) is malformed and must be corrected to \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\).

children.title: Replicate-to-Uncertainty Calibration
children.top_down_role: Adequacy of replicate coverage for the intended uncertainty summaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed replicate count guaranteeing an absolute sample-mean error bound for independent bounded responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be independent responses with common mean \(\mu\) and \(Y_i\in[a,b]\) almost surely, where \(a<b\). Hoeffding's inequality gives \[\Pr\{|\bar Y_n-\mu|\geq\varepsilon\}\leq2\exp\!\left(-\frac{2n\varepsilon^2}{(b-a)^2}\right).\] Therefore \[n\geq\left\lceil\frac{(b-a)^2}{2\varepsilon^2}\log\frac{2}{\alpha}\right\rceil\] ensures \(\Pr\{|\bar Y_n-\mu|<\varepsilon\}\geq1-\alpha\). The guarantee need not hold without independence or a valid almost-sure range bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent bounded responses, Hoeffding's inequality converts a desired absolute mean error and confidence level into a distribution-free replicate count.
assumptions_latex: \(a\leq Y_i\leq b\) almost surely for known \(a<b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated replicate count guarantees absolute sample-mean error below \(\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Free Bounded-Response Calibration
Replicate-to-Uncertainty Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replicate-count condition for a prescribed confidence half-width under known variance, with an explicit boundary for unknown-variance planning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) be independent normal responses with mean \(\mu\) and known variance \(\sigma_0^2>0\). For \(0<\alpha<1\) and desired half-width \(\varepsilon>0\), the exact known-variance two-sided normal confidence interval has half-width \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sigma_0/\sqrt n\). Therefore the least admissible replicate count is \[n_{\min}=\left\lceil\left(\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}\sigma_0}{\varepsilon}\right)^2\right\rceil.\] If the variance is unknown and estimated from the same replicates, a calculation that replaces the unknown scale by a prespecified planning value and uses a Student-t critical value is only a sample-size planning rule; it does not guarantee that the realized Student-t interval has half-width at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With known response variance, choose the smallest replicate count making the normal confidence half-width no larger than the target. When variance must be estimated, a planning standard deviation cannot provide an exact guarantee on the realized Student-t half-width.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\) are independent and identically distributed as \(N(\mu,\sigma_0^2)\), with \(\sigma_0>0\) known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integer \(n\geq n_{\min}\) gives known-variance normal-theory half-width at most \(\varepsilon\); no analogous fixed guarantee follows from merely treating \(\sigma_0\) as an unknown-variance planning value.

notation.meaning: Known response standard deviation, or only a planning value in the explicitly qualified unknown-variance case.
q-quantile of the standard normal distribution.
Least integer replicate count satisfying the known-variance half-width condition.
